author: xmoon
body:
## Summary

TSP-7 PR-A: the experimental TSP renderer now paints two read-only **native** status rows inside its existing `dock`, fed from the ONE application `StatusStore`. Before this PR the dock carried a single text banner (`DSH TSP renderer · experimental composer · working · plan · …`); that banner is retired and its facts become real `ui.status` + `ui.seg` nodes so the client owns layout, priority and clipping.

A new getter-only `StatusSnapshotReader` port is handed to `SurfaceRendererMount.mount` at its single binding point. The renderer can sample a committed snapshot but gains **no** update or subscribe authority, and it samples only at the formal display commit — the display-completion half of the same `SurfaceRuntime.commitStatus` transaction.

## Scope

- **Changed:**
  - New `src/tui/tsp/statusline-view.ts`: pure projection of six existing builtin footer items onto two `ui.status` rows.
  - `SurfaceRendererMount.mount` gained a second read-only `statusReader` parameter; the one TSP mount site passes `{ snapshot: () => status.snapshot() }`.
  - `renderer-selection` binds the reader (then the image binding) in its mount wrapper, on both renderer shapes.
  - `TspRenderer.bindStatusReader` (one-time, refuses after disposal); `commitDisplaySubject` samples the reader behind a `disposed` fence; `beginSessionHydration` clears the presented snapshot.
  - Dock: duplicate banner removed, draft count becomes its own short `Draft N` line, session title / todo count / compaction phase stay as short legacy lines, the two native rows follow the editor.
  - `docs/tsp/foundation.md`: the draft-count paragraph, a status-facts ownership row, and invariant 9 (the read-only mount reader).
  - Two manual real-pane evidence scripts (`scripts/tsp7-statusline-pane.mjs`, `scripts/tsp7-statusline-subject.mts`), same class as the other pane flows and not part of `pnpm test`.
- **Not changed / deferred:**
  - `StatusStore` remains the only writer; `commitStatus` / `resetSubjectStatus` ordering and the PiTui branch (`buildOptions.statusStore`, `TuiApp.commitDisplaySubject`) are untouched.
  - The controlled `ui.editor`, its submission controller, paste, undo, the modal seat, pickers, the Work Hub/Reader, `setTranscript` source fencing and image/visual lifecycles are untouched.
  - No `StatusSnapshot` schema, JSON persistence, writer or SDK pin change. No `/footer` config read or write.
  - **Deferred by plan:** PR-B (richer Attention/Performance items, responsive richness), G-H (short-pane height adaptation), PR-C (OMP-style composer controls), PR-D (custom/extension footer).

## Related work

Related: N/A — this PR is self-contained. PR-A is one slice of TSP-7; it is **not** stage closure and says nothing about PR-B/C/D or G-H.

## Verification

All results below were produced on base `2c3ff441` (latest `origin/main`) plus this PR's tree.

| Check / environment | Result | Evidence / limitations |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `node --test test/app/tern-tsp-statusline-view.test.ts` | PASS | 24 / 24. Pure projection, port contract, and L6 chains. |
| Same + 9 affected suites (`tern-tsp-live-mount`, `-live-projection`, `-renderer-selection`, `-port-isolation`, `status-display-subject`, `status-ownership`, `tern-tsp-interaction`, `-image-lifecycle`, `footer-command`) | PASS | 195 / 195 |
| `pnpm typecheck:bundle` | PASS | exit 0 |
| `pnpm build` | PASS | exit 0 |
| `node scripts/application-architecture-gate.mjs` | PASS | dependency direction clean |
| `node scripts/client-boundary-gate.mjs` | PASS | no new Host coupling, baseline not stale |
| `node scripts/naming-gate.mjs` | PASS | |
| `node test/architecture/host-keybindings-gate.test.mjs` | PASS | |
| `node scripts/run-test-lane.mjs tooling` | PASS | 737 / 737 |
| new-test fixed-wait guard | PASS | 0 unreasoned fixed waits in the new test file |
| `git diff --check` (unstaged + staged) | PASS | exit 0 |
| Real Tern headless pane, **production** `mountTspRenderer` (`tern 0.9.7 (c2f7563)`) | PASS | 18 checks + 11 measurements, 0 failed. Two native status groups; right side laid out right of left by measured rects; composer laid out above row 1; both rows fully readable at 400×600 through every clipping ancestor; priority drop asserted with a positive control (git painted at 400px, gone at 260px, higher-priority segments survive, same run); dark and light appearances resolve. |
| A-23 short panes (400×160 / 400×120) | NOT_APPLICABLE as PASS | Measured, **not** claimed: 160px row 1 readable but **row 2 clipped**; 120px neither readable. PR-A adds no height-adaptive collapse; G-H stays open. |
| `REAL_TERN_GUI` (live window) | NOT_RUN | Not attempted in this environment. Recorded as `NOT_RUN`, not `GUI_BLOCKED` — no blocking cause was established. |
| Owner visual acceptance (design-language §11.2 / plan G8) | NOT_RUN | A human decision; deliberately not claimed. |
| `scripts/run-test-lane.mjs product` | NOT_RUN | Not re-run on this final tree. An earlier run's 8 `submit-hot-path` timeouts (135/135 in isolation) are old-tree evidence; the contention explanation is an inference, not profiled. |

### Source → decision → sink (L6)

The chain proven end-to-end is `StatusRuntime` derivation → `SurfaceRuntime.commitStatus` → the ONE `status.update` → `SurfaceDisplaySeam.commitDisplaySubject` → `statusReader.snapshot()` → `nativeStatuslineRows` → the ONE `surface.render` → SDK wire:

- **Direct branch**: a real `createStatusRuntime` over the real surface; the live Agent header supplies the cwd and the in-process Host `permissionPresets` supplies `danger-full-access` ⇒ row 1 reaches the wire as `AGENT_CWD` + `yolo` with tone `warning`.
- **Remote-equivalent branch**: no live Agent, so the official `sessionStatus` projection supplies cwd/permission/context, with a real `StatsFolder` `request/context` event for the window ⇒ row 1 `ro` + `REAL_SOURCE_WS`, row 2 `ctx 25%`, and no fabricated `yolo`.
- Neither branch is fed a hand-built `StatusPatch`.

### Negative witnesses

A bare store `update()` with no display commit emits **no frame at all** (the half-applied state is unobservable — there is no subscription). A disposed renderer performs no further snapshot read (1 read live, still 1 after two post-dispose commits). An unbound reader fails the display commit instead of painting a substitute. A real binder throw propagates unchanged and the production `releaseUnmounted` accessor closes the SDK session exactly once (one close frame; inert on the second call). Hydration paints zero status rows. A child subject paints its own cwd/permission and **no** parent cwd, parent permission, plan or row 2. A Remote session with no token projection paints the context seg and **no** `↑0 ↓0`.

### New tests

`test/app/tern-tsp-statusline-view.test.ts` (24 cases) — the only new test file. Its failure-detection value: no existing test covered a native status row, the read-only port boundary, the dispose-after-commit path, the production binder-throw release path, or the child/parent status isolation.

## Risks and compatibility

- **Ownership:** the mount gains one extra argument; a renderer that ignores it is unaffected, and the surface stays the only store writer. No second store, subscription, renderer or surface is introduced.
- **Lifecycle:** the reader is installed once and the renderer refuses a rebind or a post-disposal bind. The display commit is the only sampling point, so no cross-scope frame and no render storm are possible; an identical repeat commit adds no node and no frame (tested).
- **Behavioural:** the retired banner is the only user-visible removal; its `working`/`plan` words are native facts now, and the run phase lands in PR-B. Draft count text changed from a `Draft N · …` prefix to its own `Draft N` line — `docs/tsp/foundation.md` says so.
- **Short panes:** unchanged and still limited (measured above). No CSS/media-query workaround was added.
- **Rollback:** revert the commit; nothing persists, no migration and no config write

body:
Makes the Aspire local stack HTTPS end to end and moves Aspire to its latest patch.

- **HTTPS with the .NET development certificate.** The standalone Vite surfaces (`mgmt`, `playground`,
  `conformance`) opt into `WithHttpsDeveloperCertificate`, so Aspire runs Vite under a wrapper config that sets
  `server.https` from the ASP.NET Core development certificate the OP hosts already use. They now serve
  `https://localhost:5173`–`5175`, and the browser trusts one certificate across the stack. The OP already registers
  the `https://…/callback` redirect URIs and CORS origins. The API is an Aspire evaluation API, so
  `ASPIRECERTIFICATES001` is suppressed in the never-packed AppHost project, with a comment giving the reason.
- **The AppHost's `http` launch profile is removed.** It could not start without `ASPIRE_ALLOW_UNSECURED_TRANSPORT`;
  F5 already used `https`.
- **Aspire 13.6.1 → 13.6.4** (`global.json` SDK and the four `Aspire.Hosting.*` pins), which brings the 13.6.3/13.6.4
  resource-startup reliability fixes. Aspire 13.6.2+ pulls `MessagePack` 2.5.307 itself, so the transitive pin that
  cleared GHSA-qhrr-8q5h-9q3h is removed; it still resolves 2.5.307, and `dotnet list package --vulnerable` finds none.
- ADR-0071, the frontend README and `CHANGELOG.md` are updated.

**Verified:** `./build/dod.ps1 -Fast -Affected` passed. Ran the full stack on 13.6.4: both OPs return 200 from
`/health/ready`; the three Vite apps serve their pages and the proxied `/config/bootstrap.json` over HTTPS, and their
certificates validate without skipping checks (the same dev certificate as the OP, TLS 1.3); plain HTTP on 5173 no
longer answers; CORS echoes each `https://` origin; and `/authorize` accepts `https://localhost:5173/callback` for
`mgmt-spa`, redirecting to the sign-in page. Sign-in with the seeded `admin` account also worked in the browser.

**Not in this change:** `pnpm dev` run outside Aspire still serves plain HTTP, so the seed keeps the
`http://localhost:517x` redirect URIs and CORS origins; #402 tracks serving HTTPS there and dropping them. #401 tracks
making the AppHost fail fast when the pinned Node or the workspace install is stale, which is what broke local runs
before this change.

author: pradyumna0222
body:
## Summary of Changes

This pull request completes the end-to-end migration of **CampusShare X** from SQLite to **PostgreSQL**, targeting free hosting via **Render Free** (Web Service) and **Neon Free** (Serverless PostgreSQL database), with zero persistent disk charges and support for subsequent custom `.xyz` domain mapping.

### 1. SQLite to PostgreSQL Migration
- Replaced `better-sqlite3` and `@types/better-sqlite3` with `pg` (`pg.Pool`) and `@types/pg`.
- Configured secure SSL connection pooling (`ssl: { rejectUnauthorized: false }`) suitable for Neon Serverless PostgreSQL with PgBouncer connection pooling (`?sslmode=require`).
- Created versioned SQL migrations (`server/db/migrations/001_initial_schema.sql`) and a transactional, idempotent migration runner (`server/db/migrate.js`) that runs safely on startup and via `npm run migrate`.
- Converted all SQL queries, placeholders (`$1, $2, ...`), and data types to PostgreSQL standards.
- Preserved JSON data modeling via PostgreSQL `JSONB` with automatic fallback parsing.

### 2. Concurrency & Conflict Prevention
- Enforced transaction-safe booking conflict prevention using PostgreSQL row-level locks (`SELECT id FROM resources WHERE id = $1 FOR UPDATE`) and transaction boundaries (`BEGIN` / `COMMIT` / `ROLLBACK`).
- Prevents race conditions when multiple users simultaneously attempt to book or approve overlapping slots.

### 3. Core Feature Preservation
- Verified 100% preservation of:
  - Multi-role RBAC: Student, Resource Owner, Campus Administrator.
  - Authentication, password hashing (`bcryptjs`), and HTTP-only sessions.
  - Resource listing, discovery, and SmartMatch intent matching with deterministic fallback.
  - Verified training certifications and institutional profile verification.
  - Booking requests, owner decisions, waitlisting, and FairShare quotas (max 3 active bookings).
  - Handover check-in and return condition reports (good, minor, damage).
  - Extension requests and owner decisions.
  - Damage/incident reporting and resolution workflows.
  - Resource maintenance blocks and schedule availability snapshots.
  - In-app notifications and scheduled overdue return reminders.
  - Tamper-evident audit logs and role-authorized CSV export (`/api/audit.csv`).

### 4. Render Free & Neon Configuration
- Updated [render.yaml](render.yaml):
  - Configured `plan: free`.
  - Removed obsolete persistent disk block (`disk:`) to eliminate hosting costs.
  - Configured health check path to `/api/health`.
  - Configured `DATABASE_URL` with `sync: false` to allow setting database credentials safely in the Render dashboard.
  - Maintained single-origin serving for both React frontend and Express API.

### 5. Automated Testing & Verification
- Embedded PostgreSQL (`@electric-sql/pglite`) was added to `devDependencies` to provide zero-config, fully isolated, reproducible local test execution without requiring Docker or a local PostgreSQL installation.
- Created comprehensive integration test suite in [tests/api.test.js](tests/api.test.js) covering:
  - Health check & unauthorized access restriction
  - Authentication, sessions, and RBAC
  - Training verification and eligibility blocking
  - Booking workflow, owner decision, waitlist, and simultaneous conflict locking
  - FairShare quota limits
  - Check-in, extension, and return condition reports
  - Resource maintenance blocks
  - Admin profile verification & training granting
  - Audit trail & CSV export
  - Persistent data recovery across database pool restarts
- Test Results: **10 passed, 0 failed (100% pass rate)**.
- TypeScript check (`tsc -b --pretty`): **0 errors**.
- Production build (`vite build`): **Succeeded**.

---

## Remaining Deployment Steps

1. **Create Free Neon Database:**
   - Sign up at [neon.tech](https://neon.tech).
   - Create a project (e.g., `campushare-x-db`) on PostgreSQL 16.
   - Copy the Pooled connection string (`postgresql://neondb_owner:...@ep-...neon.tech/neondb?sslmode=require`).

author: truong14042004
body:
## Why
With the new RSVP ("register as many as come"), an invitation answering Yes for fewer people than invited, or No, leaves its empty places UNUSED. Seating only skipped declined people, so those empty places were still seated by auto-seating, counted by the table estimate and kept by "release declined seats".

## Rule (`PlanningSeatingRules.NeedsSeat`)
- A declined person needs no seat (a checked-in one can still be seated).
- An empty place needs no seat once the invitation has a firm answer (Yes / No).
- Unanswered and MAYBE invitations keep every place planned from the import, as before.

## Changes
- Auto-seating and the table estimate use the rule; the scoring and strategies are unchanged.
- Move party seats only the people who come; release declined seats also frees empty places of answered invitations.
- RSVP never moves seats already given: the snapshot warns `UNUSED_PLACE_SEATED` instead.

## Tests
- `SeatingUnusedPlacesTests`: unanswered / MAYBE = 4 seats, Yes 2 of 4 = 2, No = 0, auto-seating exclusions.
- Unit tests: 362 passed. Integration tests not run locally (Docker unavailable).

author: irmirumi
body:
백업 A를 확인한 뒤 텍스트를 B로 바꿔도 A가 복원되는 문제와, 목록 한도를 넘는 백업을 조용히 잘라 일부만 복원하고 성공으로 표시하는 문제를 고칩니다. 독립 검토의 전체 발견·근거·미검증 범위·후속 로드맵은 `dev/CRITIQUE.md`에 정리했습니다.

## 변경과 이유

- 백업 텍스트를 수정하면 이전 요약/확인 결과를 무효화하고 `확인` 단계로 돌아갑니다. 사용자가 보고 있는 내용과 실제 쓰는 데이터가 일치하도록 합니다.
- 기존 목록 한도를 넘으면 쓰기 전에 전체를 거부합니다. 카테고리 40/소분류 60, 반복·고정 각 200, 세부 항목 100, 시간대 14, 쉼·변경 400 한도는 늘리지 않습니다. 큰 정상 백업을 완전 복원하는 작업은 후속 과제이며, 이번에는 부분 누락을 성공으로 숨기지 않는 것이 목적입니다.
- 복원 중에는 텍스트/버튼을 잠그고 실패 시 확인한 내용을 유지한 채 재시도할 수 있습니다. 오류에 role=alert를 추가합니다.
- 새 오류 문구: `복원 한도를 넘는 항목이 있어요. 복원을 중단했어요. 원본 백업을 보관해 주세요`.
- `dev/HANDOFF.md`에 검토 문서와 협업 경계를 연결했습니다.

## 검증

- 기존 코드에서 201개 반복 항목이 조용히 잘리는 것을 회귀 검사로 확인(실패), A 확인→B 교체 후 A 복원도 브라우저로 재현했습니다.
- 신규 test_backup.py: 모바일 390px/PC 1280px에서 총 30개 assert 통과. 목록/중첩 한도, 200개 경계, 수정 후 재확인, 잘못된 JSON, 중복 실행 방지, 실패 후 재시도, 실제 전달 데이터 검사.
- Python 빌드 통과. 전체 run_all.sh 실행: Node 3/3, Python 화면 스크립트 20/21 통과. 기존 test_views.py:42는 모바일 시간표 이동 후 숨겨진 오늘 버튼 클릭 대기 초과로 실패하며 전체 종료 코드는 1입니다. 변경 전 온보딩에서도 같은 실패가 반복됐고 개별 및 모션 축소 진단 실행은 통과했습니다. 이를 전체 테스트 성공으로 간주하지 않습니다.
- 브라우저 화면과 스크린샷을 직접 검토했습니다. 시스템 Chromium 사용, 가상환경과 테스트용 메모리/Firebase fake 사용.
- 운영 Firebase 로그인·두 기기 동시 수정·푸시 실기기·Android/iOS·화면 낭독기는 미검증입니다. 실제 운영 데이터에 쓰지 않았습니다.

## Claude가 중점적으로 볼 부분

- 한도 초과 백업을 이제 차단하는 의도적인 동작 변경. 기존 목록 한도를 유지하면서 안전하게 실패하도록 했습니다.
- 이번 변경은 복원 전체를 원자적으로 만들지 않습니다. 기존 다중 배치 부분 실패, 잘못된 ID 필터링·문자열 정규화, 닫힌 시트의 비동기 완료 처리는 남아 있습니다.
- 검토 문서에 자동 묶기의 최신 편집 경합 위험(실제 서버 재현 전), 1MiB 초과 문서 합성 재현, 여러 배치 복원, 알림 중복, 접근성과 테스트 문제를 구분해 기록했습니다. 큰 구조 변경은 포함하지 않았습니다.
- Firestore 문서 필드/스키마 변경·마이그레이션·의존성 추가 없음. 루트 배포본, 실제 firebase-config.js, VERSION/CACHE, Worker는 변경하지 않았습니다. 자동 배포되지 않는 Worker 변경도 없습니다.
- 리뷰 후 합치기·버전/캐시 갱신·배포는 Claude가 담당합니다. 이 PR에서 배포하지 않습니다.

body:
The embedding LRU cache (`_EmbeddingLRUCache`) and the webhook replay guard (`DeliveryLRUCache`) kept their keys in an `OrderedDict` with their own eviction. They now keep them in a `cachetools.LRUCache` of the same size, under the lock each one has. Their interfaces, the hit and miss counters, and the replay refusal stay the same.

The memory cache of `CloudflareRadarClient` was a `dict` with no bound and no expiry, so a long-running process kept each record and never asked Radar again. It is now a `cachetools.TTLCache` of at most 1,000 records that expire after the client's threat-intel TTL (`valkey.threat_intel_ttl`, 24 h by default). It reads time through the clock seam, so its test moves time with the `clock` fixture.

cachetools 7.1.8 is already a pinned dependency. The `OrderedDict` of the OSV client stays for #1146.

author: blueberrycongee
body:
## Changes
Follow-up to the intermittent lifecycle failures found after #929, #934 and #936.

- Confirmed forced archive stays pending through its owned runner's physical settlement instead of failing after a fixed two-second deadline. Reuse the existing per-session ingress ordering so unrelated conversations remain responsive while same-session mutations cannot overtake it.
- Recheck the original principal/resource authorization and operation cancellation before the durable archive write. Preserve execution ownership, mutation leases and durable-settlement checks.
- Distinguish uncertain commit, committed-but-view-unavailable and pre-commit cancellation. A canceled post-commit view refresh can respond promptly, but its owner joins the physical refresh before releasing the lease and ordered lane. Desktop transport loss uses the existing unknown-outcome error and does not replay the mutation.
- State authority records its own admitted probe cleanup and completes it through its legitimate Close context and original provider binding. Reconcile durable pending outcomes, retain failures/recovery evidence, reject ordinary calls after retirement, and drain execution registrations.
- Require the actually selected state authority to prepare successfully, preserving the original provider preparation error rather than masking it as a retired downstream dependency.
- Exercise quota changes through the real serialized server refresh path, preserving watchers and all account/quota assertions.
- Keep failure-only core stack capture in the isolated confirmed-archive E2E; all four original scenarios and assertions remain intact.

## Local validation
- Deterministic before-fail/after-pass archive tests: slow settlement, request cancellation, revocation before commit, unrelated-session progress, same-session order, shutdown and committed-view cancellation. Focused race suite repeated three times passed.
- Full internal/runtime race suite passed (252.682 seconds). Twelve targeted lifecycle cases passed, including real process delegates, lost probe/cleanup requests and replies, permanent cleanup failure/reopen, required-authority diagnostics and registry drain.
- Desktop targeted unknown-outcome checks and typecheck passed; a broader local renderer run passed 4713 tests but is not represented as the entire unit command.
- Test policy, documentation policy, syntax and diff checks pass.
- The quota fixture was race-tested against unmodified production authority before the product fix. The original CI quota error was not reproduced locally; the fixture's concurrent manual preflight/publication violated the documented serialization requirement. The production authority cleanup defect was independently reproduced deterministically.

## Hosted acceptance and limits
The initial diagnostics/fixture-only checkpoint passed hosted CI, including all confirmed-archive modes, but produced no new failure stack. That did not establish that the two-second contract was correct. `Request("https://example.com/path#section", data={"a": "two words"}, method="GET")` currently appends the encoded data after `#section`. Its request selector is then just `/path`, so the parameters never reach the server.

author: siddiqueirshad
body:
## Description
Bounds-check \ ield->id() < field_to_id_map.size()\ before writing into the field-id-to-index mapping in:
- \src/reflection.cpp\ (\ForAllFields\)
- \src/bfbs_gen.h\ (\FieldIdToIndex\)

Fixes #9426.

## Motivation
\ForAllFields()\ and \FieldIdToIndex()\ build a field-id-to-index table by writing \ ield_to_id_map[field->id()]\, where the vector is sized to \object->fields()->size()\. If a schema buffer has a field whose \id()\ exceeds \ ields()->size()\, direct array subscripting triggers an out-of-bounds heap write. Adding a bounds check ensures safe indexing without writing past the allocation.

author: colaberryintern
body:
## Gov sync: publish the gov build plan on the sync path

**The bug (found diagnosing a live gov intern).** A government build publishes its BuildPlan only when the gov cockpit view is opened — `ensureGovBuildPlanPublished` runs from `getStudentGovProjectView`, never from the repo-sync path. So a gov student who connects a repo, adds ColaberryIntern as a collaborator, pushes, and clicks **Sync from GitHub** gets `no_plan` forever: `build_plans` stays empty, `refreshRepoDocuments` short-circuits, and the platform never writes `.colaberry/plan.json` / manifest / docs into their repo — even though push access is granted and the build is fully materialized.

**The fix.** `refreshRepoDocuments` now publishes the gov plan itself before reading it, via `ensureGovPlanPublishedForSync`:
- **Gated to gov builds** (`project_variables.kind === 'gov'`) — regular SBP builds also carry STORY tasks, so an unconditional call would fabricate a gov plan for a non-gov project.
- **Idempotent** — the publisher is a no-op once a plan exists.
- **Best-effort** — never throws; a non-gov project or a failure falls through to the normal `no_plan` path.

**Evidence (read-only prod diagnosis).** The affected intern's `github_connections` row was writable (`platform_can_push:true`), her build had 14 materialized STORY tasks, but `build_plans` for her project was empty and no `Colaberry Build Bot` commit ever ran. This removes that `no_plan` short-circuit. Also fixes a second symptom — `verifyBuildFromRepo` reads `getPublishedPlan` directly too, so gov commit→story evidence was never recorded on hand-sync.

**Scope.** One new service + its test + a 2-line wiring change in `refreshRepoDocuments`.

**Tests.** `govPlanForSync.test.ts` (the gov-build gate). Backend typecheck authoritative in CI.

**Operational note.** The already-stuck intern also needs her plan published once (a separate one-shot, noted in the handoff); this PR is the code fix so it never recurs.

author: shakeb03
body:
## What changed

Experiment completion and the deterministic analysis (TRD phase 4). No LLM is involved.

- **`POST /api/experiments/{id}/complete`**: checks ownership and that the experiment is `active`, requires enough check-ins, runs the analysis, saves the report, then marks the experiment `completed` (atomic active -> completed update). Completing twice returns 409, and completed experiments already reject check-ins.
- **`GET /api/experiments/{id}/report`**: returns the stored report. The AI-written fields (`interpretation`, `learnings`, `next_experiment`) are null until the report-generation step.
- **`experiment_reports` table** (migration `20261028000500`): one report per experiment, RLS read-only for users, writes backend-only, grants included.
- **Analysis engine** (`backend/app/services/analysis.py`, pure Python): per-metric baseline vs intervention (mean, median, sd, absolute and percent change, effect size, direction consistency, outliers), adherence and coverage, prediction vs observed (error, in-range, direction, 0-100 accuracy), and the signal classification (`likely_signal` / `possible_signal` / `unclear` / `probably_noise`) with machine-readable reasons. All thresholds are named constants at the top of the file.
- Small refactor: `owned_experiment` moved into `api/deps.py` so check-ins and reports share it.

## Things for the reviewer

- **"Enough data"** means at least 2 baseline and 3 intervention check-ins, capped at the configured phase length. It does not require the days to have elapsed, so a user can finish early.
- **Accuracy formula**: `100 * (1 - |observed - midpoint| / scale)`, floored at 0, with `scale = max(|midpoint|, range width, 10)`. A result just outside the predicted range can score low (seeded run: +10.9% against a 3-10% prediction scored 55.8). Scoring distance to the range edge instead is a possible follow-up.
- **Likely signal** needs: change meets the success threshold in the predicted direction, >= 70% of intervention days beat the baseline mean, |effect size| >= 0.8, >= 5 intervention days, adherence >= 60%. A strong move *against* the prediction is `unclear`, not a signal.
- All intervention-phase days count in the intervention mean, including skipped-habit days; adherence is reported separately.
- The report write is idempotent, so a retry after a partial failure rewrites the same report. There is no cross-table transaction.
- **Migration is not applied by CI.** Run `supabase/migrations/20261028000500_create_experiment_reports.sql` in the Supabase SQL editor.
- Pair rule: this change is backend and `supabase/` only, so it does not touch the frontend files Nazmul owns.

## How it was tested

- `uv run pytest` in `backend/`: 168 tests, including the analysis on a realistic seeded shape (3 baseline + 7 intervention days, ~+11%), all four signal classes, a strong opposite move, zero variance, the 1 + 2 day demo shape, the accuracy formula, and the completion flow (ownership, not-enough-data, double completion, race, database outage).
- By hand against the real Supabase project, from a signed-in session: seeded 10 realistic check-ins on a test experiment, completed it via the real endpoint (200, `completed`, `likely_signal`, +10.9%), read the report back (identical), and confirmed a second completion, a late check-in, completing a `proposed` experiment (all 409) and a request with no token (401).
- Not tested live: a second user's isolation, and direct browser access to the new table under RLS.

author: flux-gs
body:
Adds ee(1), FreeBSD 2.2.8's easy editor: a modeless screen editor with key help on screen and an ESC menu, for anyone who does not want vi. It builds from the vendored `ee.c` unchanged. Getting there took three toolchain changes, each fixed in the toolchain rather than in ee:

- **fcc: a fn-ptr struct field takes any null pointer constant.** ee's menu tables initialize unused handlers with `NULL`. fcc accepted only a bare `0` there (K&R A.6.6). Fixture `M22/fnptr_null`.
- **curses: keypad mode, after NetBSD 1.5.** `keypad()` and the `KEY_` values, with `wgetch` matching the termcap key sequences that 4.3BSD curses already reads (ku kd kl kr kh k0-k9). An unfinished sequence comes back a byte at a time after a 0.2 s `select(2)` timeout, so a lone ESC is still ESC. Also `fixterm()` and `wnoutrefresh()`, the two System V names ee uses. The NetBSD sources are vendored under `vendor/netbsd-1-5`.
- **ld: a program file too big for a bank is packed function by function.** ee is 118 KB of C in one file. The new manifest key `split` compiles it with `--sections` and links each function as its own pack unit, which works because every call between functions is already linker-resolved.

The PR also commits the `dirty_root` harness key, which boots a MAME test with the root not marked clean, as a power cut leaves it.

`/bin/ree` is the restricted-mode hard link upstream installs. The man page has a BUGS section listing what FGX lacks: message catalogs, lp, spell and ispell.

**Testing**
- `tools/gate.sh` green: 44 tests, multibank sweep, and 232/232 runtime fixtures.
- In MAME, ee opened a new file, took typed text, moved with the Up and Right arrows through the real keyboard path, inserted at the cursor, and saved with ^C `exit`. `cat` showed `aX` / `bc`.
- A lone ESC opened ee's main menu.

Ticket 17 (`.scratch/ios-sdk/issues/17-ios-size-budget.md`): iOS size budget gate.

- `scripts/check-ios-size-budget.sh`: runs `scripts/measure-ios-sdk.sh --size-only` on a fresh ZIP of HEAD (or a given ZIP), prints the SDK deltas, and fails when a delta is above its budget, not positive, or not an integer.

body:
## Problema confirmado (Supabase oficial)
- Un pago Wompi sandbox APPROVED del plan BASIC terminó en `REVIEW_REQUIRED / contract_review`.
- La organización ya tenía una suscripción `TRIAL` de PRO con periodo vigente.
- La creación del checkout y la conciliación del webhook trataban cualquier diferencia de plan vigente como un cambio de **contrato pagado**, incluso con `status=TRIAL`.

## Corrección contenida
- Autorizar `TRIAL -> BASIC/PRO` bajo firma Wompi, conciliación de proveedor, moneda y monto ya existentes.
- Mantener revisión para `ACTIVE` pagado y plan diferente, y bloqueos `SUSPENDED/CANCELLED/LIFETIME`.
- Impedir checkout si la licencia es no SaaS o está suspendida/cancelada/terminada.
- Impedir un segundo checkout si ya hay un pago `APPROVED/REVIEW_REQUIRED` pendiente de conciliación; reintentar la misma clave sigue siendo idempotente.
- El periodo pagado de una prueba comienza en el momento del pago aprobado; las renovaciones de contratos ACTIVE preservan el periodo pagado.
- Sin rebajar aislamiento sandbox, seguridad de webhooks, idempotencia, permisos SQL ni controles tributarios.

## Pruebas
- Integración CI existente `billing_activation_assertions.sql` actualizada para permitir compra desde TRIAL.
- Nuevo `billing_trial_to_paid_assertions.sql`: compra desde PRO TRIAL de BASIC, evento validado a nivel RPC, idempotencia, importe erróneo, suscripción/licencia, rechazo cambio de plan pagado, licencia suspendida y bloqueo de doble cobro ante una revisión pendiente.
- Prueba de concurrencia trasladada a un tenant de fixture independiente para no eludir la regla de conciliación.
- Ejecutar CI y ensayo con PostgreSQL 17 antes de cualquier despliegue.

## Limitaciones / despliegue
- **DRAFT**: no merge ni despliegue hasta superar CI y ensayo de staging.
- No modificar el pago histórico APPROVED / REVIEW_REQUIRED con replay: eventos aprobados son inmutables. Requiere conciliación **separada, autorizada y auditable** tras verificación de Wompi.
- Mantener `production_enabled=false`; Wompi sigue en sandbox.
- Revisar snapshot/contrato anterior a aplicación de migración y comprobar `pg_get_functiondef` y privilegios en destino.

author: rafael-sanchezf
body:
The listing reader agent in `services/agent/` (HIQ-13, HIQ-14, HIQ-15; epic HIQ-2). A renter pastes a listing and its photos. Muse Spark reads the address, unit, floor and side, plus what the photos show (view, windows, AC units, wall material). Every fact is tied to a quoted line or a photo, and "can't tell" is allowed. Then the code places the address with NYC GeoSearch and scores it: `/v2/score`, falling back to `/v1/score` while v2 is not deployed. Each turn streams from `POST /read` as a server-sent event. The website and eval code against [`services/agent/CONTRACT.md`](services/agent/CONTRACT.md).

## Live results (muse-spark-1.3, Oct 28)

All 7 fixtures match `fixtures/expected.json` on every score field. The photo fixture also got all four observed fields right.

| Fixture | Address, unit, floor, side, expected | Read live | Turns | Refusals | Model time | End to end |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 01 stated rear | 315 West 86th Street, 11C, 11, rear | all 4 match ("eleventh floor", "face the rear of the building") | 1 | 0 | 6.7 s | 10.9 s |
| 02 silent | 201 East 87th Street, can't tell ×3 | match: adjectives ignored, floor and side can't tell | 1 | 0 | 5.0 s | 9.2 s |
| 03 street front | 155 Ludlow Street, 2A, 2, street | all 4 match ("Both bedrooms face Ludlow Street,") | 1 | 0 | 3.7 s | 7.1 s |
| 04 corner | 305 East 24th Street, 14G, 14, corner | all 4 match ("Corner unit") | 1 | 0 | 3.9 s | 6.7 s |
| 05 courtyard, unit only | 235 East 10th Street, 3F, can't tell, courtyard | match: "Apt 3F" not taken as a floor | 1 | 0 | 4.9 s | 8.3 s |
| 06 photos (new) | 520 East 81st Street, 3D, can't tell, street (from the photo) | match: side from `photo:0`; observed view street, windows double-hung and operable, AC window unit, wall brick | 2 | 0 | 1.9 + 6.3 s, plus 9.4 s for 2 photos | 20.7 s |
| 07 tempting (new) | 222 West 14th Street, 9F, can't tell, can't tell | match: "quiet side", "away from the avenue", "high-floor" and "Apt 9F" all left as can't tell | 1 | 0 | 4.5 s | 6.6 s |

- **Calls:** 17 Meta API calls in total, under the 50-call budget:
  - 1 probe
  - 10 agent turns
  - 4 photo reads
  - 2 `muse-image-1.0` generations, for the two synthetic photos in fixture 06
- **Tokens, agent turns:** 28.6k in and 10.9k out, of which 8.8k were reasoning. Photo-call tokens were not recorded in this run; readings carry them from 453afda on.
- **Refusals: none live.** Muse Spark quoted exactly and chose can't tell on its own, including on fixture 07, which was written to tempt it. So the refuse-and-retry path has only run in the mock tests (invented quote, adjectives, unread photo, wrong photo value), not live.

**Fixed from the live run:**

1. **GeoSearch put fixture 06 in Brooklyn.** Canarsie also has a 520 East 81st Street, and GeoSearch ranked it first for an Upper East Side listing. It also ranks "235 West 10th Street" next to "235 East 10th Street". `locate` now matches the street as well as the house number. It then picks the borough the listing names (a borough, a ZIP after "NY", or a neighborhood), or else takes Manhattan and adds a note listing the alternatives. The result carries `borough_from` and `alternatives`. After the fix, all 7 fixture addresses place on the right Manhattan building, and 06 was rerun live end to end.
2. **Token headroom.** Every call is capped at `max_output_tokens=4096`. A live agent turn spent 574 to 1,483 reasoning tokens. A reply with no tool call and no text is asked again within the same turn (`retries` in the trace) instead of costing a turn. Photo calls get the same cap, and an empty reply there is retried as invalid JSON.

## How it holds rule 2 (the model cannot invent a source)

The checks are in `reader/evidence.py`, called from inside the tools, so no prompt can skip them:

- `submit_listing` refuses a field marked read unless every quote is in the text sent. The match is exact; only whitespace is normalized.
- The quote must also state the value. The floor number has to sit next to the word floor, the side needs a side word, and the address and unit need every one of their own tokens. Adjectives get their own refusal, and "Apt 3F" is not a floor.
- A photo citation must name a photo that exists, that `read_photo` looked at, and whose reading shows the same value. The `what` is copied from that reading. Live, the model once put the photo's description in `quote`; the check ignores it and uses the reading.
- A refusal goes back to the model with the reason, within 8 turns. When the turns run out, or the API fails, the result is still clean.

The loop follows the AgentKit pattern in meta-models/legal-agent-workshop: the OpenAI SDK's Responses API, one tool per turn, the checks inside the tools, and an offline transport so tests use the real SDK path.

## Verified

- **71 tests pass in mock mode, offline, in about 1 s.** New since the first push:
  - empty-reply retry for agent turns and for photo reads
  - borough picked by the listing, with the Manhattan default and its note
  - street mismatch refused
- **Live:** the 7 fixtures above.
- **Earlier, against the mock:** `POST /read` streams locally, the v2 query shape matches the engine v2 code, and the v1 fallback works on the hosted API.

## Fixtures

Seven synthetic listings, written for this repo, for real Manhattan buildings checked in GeoSearch and PLUTO. The two photos in `fixtures/photos/` were generated by `muse-image-1.0` (a bedroom window onto a street with a window AC, and a galley kitchen) and downscaled to 768 px. Nothing was taken from a listing site. Mock mode skips 06, because it cannot see.

## Defaults taken (override any)

- **A unit number is not a floor.** Filed as HIQ-57 for Rafa, due Oct 30.
- **An address in two boroughs:** the listing's own borough, ZIP or neighborhood decides. Otherwise Manhattan, with a note naming the other borough.
- **`observed` comes from photos only.**
- **A cant_tell `side` has value `"unknown"`;** every other cant_tell field has `null`.
- **Placing an address needs a house number** and the same street in GeoSearch.
- **Scoring goes over HTTP** (hosted by default). The v1 fallback sends `day_bothers` as `wfh`.
- **`/read` takes an optional `answers`.** Evidence quotes carry `start` and `end` offsets.
- **Budget:** 8 turns, `max_output_tokens` 4,096 per call, up to 6 photos per `read_photo` call.

## AI switch and caller keys (HIQ-75, Oct 29, 9a048a0)

The Meta reading now sits behind a switch, and a caller can bring their own OpenAI or Anthropic key. Contract: `services/agent/CONTRACT.md`, "The AI switch and caller keys".

- **Headers on `POST /read`:** `X-HushIQ-AI` (on|off), `X-HushIQ-Provider` (meta|openai|anthropic), `X-HushIQ-Key`, `X-HushIQ-Model`. `make_client(provider, key, model, ai)` builds the client per request, and the eval calls the same function in process (`from_env` reads `OPENAI_API_KEY` / `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`).
- **`HOUSE_AI=on|off`** on the server. With AI off, no key, or the house key off, the **basic reader** runs (today's heuristic model: regular expressions, no model call).
- **A provider failure runs basic, with a reason.** 401/402/403 is `key_rejected`, 429/529 is `provider_busy`, and a timeout, 5xx or 404 is `provider_error`. The failed turn stays in the trace, then the basic reader reads the listing from the start. **No path leads from a caller's key to the house key.** This also changes the house path: a Meta failure used to end the reading as `partial`/`model_error`, and now the basic reader takes over.
- **`ai` on every result:** `{mode, provider, model, key, reason, message}`, next to `mode` and `model`, which stay.
- **Anthropic:** `reader/anthropic_adapter.py` answers the loop's Responses calls through the Messages API with the Anthropic SDK. It handles tools, base64 images and tool results, and replays Claude's thinking blocks unchanged on the next turn. The loop does not change.
- **OpenAI:** the same SDK at api.openai.com. Each request adds `include: ["reasoning.en

_Requested by **Maxwell** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01WizQJXFFg3WDaZ46YPE8cM?thread=cmsg_01WizQJXFFg3WDaZ46YPE8cMDYU9Bbeyiubgia5PhwQwhm)_

From going through the admin page's crash list:

- **`The object can not be cloned.` (7×, iPhone app)**: the stack runs `campfire.js use` → LiveKit `onSetEncryptionKey` → `postKey` → `worker.postMessage`. In the iPhone app (WKWebView), a `CryptoKey` can't be sent to a worker, so the room key never reached the encryption worker. Now `RoomKeys.use` hands over `{ raw }` bytes, and a short wrapper added to the worker's Blob imports them as the same HKDF key LiveKit's `createKeyMaterialFromBuffer` makes. Messages that arrive while a key is being imported wait, so they stay in order. The derived keys are unchanged, so new clients and older ones still hear each other. I checked this in Chromium: the worker gets `setKey` with raw bytes, then an encrypt/decrypt round trip with the real worker and `BaseKeyProvider` options works, the same as the old path. **It reaches the iPhone app only with a new app build.**
- **`state.messages.at is not a function` (14×)**: `Array.prototype.at` and `findLast` only exist from Safari 15.4 / Chrome 92 on. `core.js` now adds both (non-enumerable) when they're missing.
- **`The operation was aborted.`**: an `AbortError` is a request we cancelled on purpose, so `reportError` skips it.

Not changed: `X is not defined` (1× each) come from partly loaded pages (one was Googlebot), and `Unexpected token '='` is a browser too old to read `||=` (Safari before 14).

`node scripts/check-client.mjs` is clean.

author: sebakhi
body:
Phase 4 of the accounts sign-in pages feature (stacked on #117, phase 3). Owner decision Q6: three steps and a custom number for the height of every control, and the same for the table row height.

## Problem

Every control in both apps is 36px (`h-9`) and every table row 44px, fixed in the primitives. The administrator can choose colours, corners and the menu accent in Platform settings › Appearance, but not how dense the interface is. Phase 5 will reuse `PlatformTheme` for a per-application appearance, so the heights have to be part of that value object, not side settings.

## Change

**Model and API**
- `PlatformTheme` gains `ControlSize` and `TableRowHeight`: a step (`compact`, `default`, `comfortable`) or `custom` with whole `px`. Controls 32/36/40px, custom 28–56. A one-line table row 40/44/48px, custom 32–72, never lower than the controls. The lowest row step equals the tallest control step, so every pair of steps is valid. Validated in `PlatformTheme.Create` like the colour choices; pixels sent with a step are dropped. Constants in `ThemePresets.cs`, held equal to the TS copy by the parity test.
- Reading never fails: a theme stored before these fields reads with both at `default` and keeps its colours; an invalid stored size costs only the sizes. Proven on the exact JSON the previous `Write` produced.
- `PUT /api/v1/admin/platform-settings/theme`, the DTOs, `GET` settings, the branding payload and the audit record carry both. New codes: `SystemSettings.ThemeUnknownSize`, `ThemeCustomSizeOutOfRange`, `ThemeRowHeightBelowControlHeight` (`error-codes.json`, `DomainErrors.resx` ×7). `schema.d.ts` regenerated from this build; only this feature's hunks are kept (the regeneration also showed `ui_locales`/`ui_theme` params missing since #112, left out of this PR).

**Tokens and engine**
- `preset.css`: `--control-height: 2.25rem` and `--table-row-height: 2.75rem` beside `--radius`; `@theme inline` adds `h-control`, `control-sm` / `control-lg` (−/+0.25rem) and `py-cell-y`. `inline`, so a scoped element (phase 5 preview) recomputes its own sizes.
- `build-theme.ts` writes both on the root block. `THEME_ENGINE_VERSION` 3 → 4, fingerprint re-recorded. The shipped heights still download no registry (browser test with a floor).
- `cn` registers the new names with tailwind-merge, so `h-8` passed by a caller still wins over `h-control`.

**Primitives**
- Read the token: `button` (default/sm/lg and icon/icon-sm/icon-lg), `input`, `input-group` (and its `icon-sm` button), `native-select`, `select` (default/sm), `toggle` (default/sm/lg incl. min-width), tabs list, `menubar`, pagination ellipsis. `command`'s input group and the DataTable sort button lost their pinned heights.
- Fixed on purpose: `xs` (24px, not a control-row size); the sidebar (menu rows and its collapse control fit the 56px icon rail, so `SidebarTrigger` is pinned to 32px).
- `TableCell` pads by `(row − 20px) / 2`: a one-line row is exactly the row height, the default is today's `p-3`, and a row with an avatar or a button grows by the difference as before.

**Console** (Platform settings › Appearance)
- «ارتفاع عناصر التحكّم» / Control height and «ارتفاع صفوف الجداول» / Table row height: a ToggleGroup of «مضغوط / افتراضي / مريح / مخصّص», Custom opening a px number field (InputGroup). The whole console previews the draft; the preview tiles gain an input group beside a button and a two-row table. Save stays disabled, and the field says why, while a custom value is out of bounds or the rows are lower than the controls. Strings in all seven locales.

## Deploy

No schema change: the theme is a JSON column and old rows read as default. API and both front ends together (the console sends the two fields and the API requires them).

## Verification

author: professorzhi
body:
Refs #515 (W19 独立发布门禁). This PR adds the independent gate and its evidence; it merges nothing and closes nothing.

## Two verdicts, because #515 separates them

| verdict | value | why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `LANDING_VERDICT` | **READY (SIGNED_PASS)** | #519 over `main @ 99c06fab`: 20 added files, 0 modified, `git merge-tree --write-tree` rc=0 with no conflicts, exact-head hosted CI 4/4 green with `0 new` |
| `RELEASE_VERDICT` | **BLOCKED** | `REAL_DEVICE = NOT_RUN` (0/3 devices), two release-scoped defects, and the artifact pins reproduce only at #518's unmerged head |

A development merge is not a release; a gate with one verdict would have to be wrong about one of them.

## The retire map is measured

`w19_measure.py` compares blob-level trees and commit ancestry — no row is typed by hand, so every classification can be re-derived:

- **3 SUPERSEDED_ANCESTOR** — #506 → #513, #509 → #518, #516 → #519 (each head is literally an ancestor of its successor's head)
- **2 BLOCKED_OWNER** — #507/#508 rewrite 74 files `main` already has
- **6 OWN_DELTA_PENDING** — #512/#513/#514/#517/#518/#519 add only files they declare
- **1 RELEASE_NOT_RUN** — #483

The fact that separates these is `touched`: a file `main` moved on that a branch never edited is not that branch's delta.

## The red `pull_request` jobs, measured rather than inferred

`refs/pull/506|512|513|514|518/merge` each have a **first parent older than `dd5919a9`** (the card-window fix, landed 2026-10-27), so the tree CI ran still carries the pre-fix `tests/test_direct_lark_notify.py` — a file none of those branches touches. Merging #513/#514/#518 into the *current* main is conflict-free and resolves that file to the fixed copy, so the `1 new` does not survive a retarget.

## Re-verifications with their negative controls

- #509's five digests rebuild under ambient `core.autocrlf=true`; the control (old expectations) exits 3 on exactly one digest
- #506's mid-upgrade trap does not reproduce on #513's writer across 18 separate processes; the control proves a *successful* upgrade does move the fingerprint
- #508's transcript P1 is live on `main`; both positive controls agree, so the readers are not simply true/false
- #483's legacy suite is 70/70 identical node ids and outcomes before and after

## What this does not do

No merge, no PR closed, no branch deleted, no install, no service/OAuth/Tailscale change, no real Feishu/IM, no paid model, no device or production gate. Full record: `docs/integration/FLEET-NEXT-W19-RELEASE-READINESS-20261029.md`.

`eval_gate._defined` accepted any `int | float` that was not NaN. JSON `true`/`false` load as Python bools, which are ints, and `json.loads` reads `Infinity` as a float. So:

- a run mean of `true` or `Infinity` passed its check (and `render` showed `1.000` / `inf`);
- a baseline lower bound of `false` or `-Infinity` let any run pass that check.

That is the same class of malformed input as #163 and #175, except this one fails open. Now `_defined` requires a finite number that is not a bool, and `compare` uses it for the run mean. author: craigpestell
body:
Michelle's main work is multi-day house and pet sitting where she stays at the client's home and charges for the stay, not by the hour. This adds continuous-period bookings, off by default.

## What changes when `FEATURE_STAYS=on`
- **Booking calendar**: a "Visit or stay?" choice. For a stay the client taps the arrival day and the day they're back; the calendar greys out days that are booked or marked off and won't let a stay cross them. Address and notes prompts switch to the home and pets. Picking a stay starts on "Pets & plants" (or "Home checks") when she offers it.
- **Pricing**: per night (nights = return day minus arrival day), from a new optional **nightly rate** on her profile. No rate means no stays on her page.
- **Availability**: a stay blocks every day it touches (local midnight to midnight), so hourly visits can't land on those days, and stays can't overlap visits or time off. Weekly hours don't apply to stays. Stays start tomorrow at the earliest, end inside the 8-week window, max 30 nights (`brand.maxStayNights`). Re-checked in the same serializable transaction as visits.
- **Schedule, admin, account pages and emails** show stays as "Tuesday, November 3 to Thursday, November 12 (9 nights)" with "Overnight stay · service". Booking, cancel and "finished" emails use stay wording.
- Home page and `/book` mention the nightly rate.

## Flag
`src/lib/features.ts` reads `FEATURE_STAYS` at request time. With it off, nothing is shown, `/api/concierges/[slug]/stays` 404s and `/api/bookings` rejects stay requests. On the droplet it comes from the repository **variable** `FEATURE_STAYS` via `deploy.yml` → `.env` → `docker-compose.yml`.

## Database
Additive migration: `BookingKind` enum, `Booking.kind` (default `VISIT`), `Booking.nights`, `ConciergeProfile.nightlyRateCents`. Existing rows are unaffected. `prisma migrate diff` against the schema is empty.

## Testing
- New unit tests (`src/lib/stays.test.ts`): night counts, DST-safe stay bounds, blocked days, overlap checks, request validation, the flag.
- Locally with Postgres: booked a 9-night stay end to end in the browser (emails, $810 at $90/night), confirmed those days drop out of hourly availability, saved the nightly rate from `/concierge`, checked admin and home page. With the flag off, the stay UI is gone and the API refuses stays.

author: renovate-wibrow[bot]
body:
This PR contains the following updates:

| Package | Update | Change |
|---|---|---|
| [jdx/mise](https://redirect.github.com/jdx/mise) | patch | `v2026.10.21` → `v2026.10.22` |

---

### Release Notes

<details>
<summary>jdx/mise</summary>

### [`v2026.10.22`](https://redirect.github.com/jdx/mise/releases/tag/v2026.10.22): : Project-scoped uninstall, JSONC dotfile merges, and node@lts moves to Node.js 26

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/jdx/mise/compare/vfox-v2026.10.21...vfox-v2026.10.22)

You can now uninstall only the tools the current project requests, and new `--no-global` and `--project` flags replace the two different meanings `--local` had. Dotfiles can merge into JSONC files like VS Code's `settings.json` and can seed a file once without overwriting later edits. `node@lts` now resolves to Node.js 26. The rest of the release adds an `ipv4_only` setting, JSON output for `mise vars`, and fixes for Windows, lockfiles, pruning and GitHub release listing.

#### Added

- **`mise uninstall --project` and `mise ls --project`.** `mise uninstall --project` removes the installed versions requested by the nearest project's config files: `mise.toml`, `mise.local.toml`, `conf.d` fragments, `.tool-versions` and idiomatic version files in that directory. Config in parent directories and global config is not included. It lists each version with the file that requests it and asks before removing anything. `--yes` skips the prompt, and `--dry-run` only shows the list. `mise ls --project` lists the same scope. Installs are shared between projects, so another project using the same version will need to reinstall it. [#​15079](https://redirect.github.com/jdx/mise/pull/15079), [#​15081](https://redirect.github.com/jdx/mise/pull/15081) ([@​jdx](https://redirect.github.com/jdx), [@​httpete-broadcom](https://redirect.github.com/httpete-broadcom))

  ```console
  $ cd ~/work/app            # ~/work/mise.toml also exists
  $ mise ls --no-global      # app's config and ~/work's, not the global config
  $ mise ls --project        # app's config only
  $ mise uninstall --project # removes the versions app's config names, after asking
  ```

- **`--no-global` on `ls`, `outdated`, `upgrade` and `tasks ls`.** It selects tools or tasks from all non-global config, including parent directories, and does what `--local` did on these commands. [#​15081](https://redirect.github.com/jdx/mise/pull/15081) ([@​jdx](https://redirect.github.com/jdx))

- **Dotfile merges into JSONC files.** A `merge` entry can now edit files that contain comments and trailing commas, such as VS Code's `settings.json`. It keeps the file's comments, indentation and any keys the source doesn't set. `.jsonc` targets are detected automatically. For other files, set the new `format` key (`json`, `jsonc`, `toml` or `yaml`). A `.json` target without `format` is still parsed as strict JSON. Merge sources that fail to parse now report the file path and the parse error. [#​15077](https://redirect.github.com/jdx/mise/pull/15077) ([@​jdx](https://redirect.github.com/jdx), [@​TimonLukas](https://redirect.github.com/TimonLukas))

  ```toml
  [dotfiles]
  "~/.config/Code/User/settings.json/shared" = { source = "vscode/shared.json", merge = true, format = "jsonc" }
  ```

- **`create_if_missing` for dotfiles.** `copy`, `template` and inline `content` entries with `create_if_missing = true` write the target only when nothing exists there. After that, local edits are left alone and do not count as drift in `mise dot status` or `mise dot diff`. If you delete the target, the next apply creates it again. This works for files that are filled in on each machine, such as local tokens. [#​15080](https://redirect.github.com/jdx/mise/pull/15080) ([@​jdx](https://redirect.github.com/jdx), [@​thernstig](https://redirect.github.com/thernstig))

  ```toml
  [dotfiles]
  "~/.config/mise/conf.d/private.local.toml" = { source = "templates/private.toml", mode = "copy", permissions = "0600", create_if_missing = true }
  ```

- **`permissions` on dotfile `merge` entries.** The mode is applied only when the merge creates the file. Files that already exist keep their mode. Merge entries for the same file must not set different modes. [#​15087](https://redirect.github.com/jdx/mise/pull/15087) ([@​jdx](https://redirect.github.com/jdx), [@​thernstig](https://redirect.github.com/thernstig))

- **`ipv4_only` setting.** Set `ipv4_only = true` (or `MISE_IPV4_ONLY=1`) for networks where a host fails over IPv6, for example `dl.google.com` returning 404 or Sigstore TUF fetches failing. This applies to mise's own HTTP connections: downloads, version lookups, GitHub API calls, attestation verification and vfox plugins. External programs such as `git`, `npm` and the `npm:` backend's package manager still use the system resolver. The default is `false`. [#​15057](https://redirect.github.com/jdx/mise/pull/15057) ([@​jdx](https://redirect.github.com/jdx), [@​Alby02](https://redirect.github.com/Alby02))

- **`mise vars --json` and `--json-extended`.** Prints vars as JSON. `--json-extended` also includes the file each value comes from. Redacted values stay `[redacted]`. [#​15069](https://redirect.github.com/jdx/mise/pull/15069) ([@​jdx](https://redirect.github.com/jdx), [@​artemklevtsov](https://redirect.github.com/artemklevtsov))

- **`mise shell --unset --all`.** Removes every `MISE_<TOOL>_VERSION` override from the current shell in one command, including ones you exported by hand. [#​15088](https://redirect.github.com/jdx/mise/pull/15088) ([@​jdx](https://redirect.github.com/jdx), [@​wfouche](https://redirect.github.com/wfouche))

- **Bootstrap hook descriptions.** A hook table can set `description`, and `mise bootstrap` prints it instead of the hook's script. Without a description, mise prints `$` followed by the command's first line, cut to the terminal width. `--verbose` and `--dry-run` still print the full script. [#​15106](https://redirect.github.com/jdx/mise/pull/15106) ([@​jdx](https://redirect.github.com/jdx), [@​owpac](https://redirect.github.com/owpac))

  ```toml
  [bootstrap.hooks.final]
  description = "Remove the root copy of pam_reattach if Homebrew removed the module"
  run = "..."
  ```

- Debian packages from the mise APT repository now include Bash, Zsh and Fish completions. [#​15074](https://redirect.github.com/jdx/mise/pull/15074) ([@​gilesw](https://redirect.github.com/gilesw))

- Registry: added an aqua backend for `oxfmt`. [#​15092](https://redirect.github.com/jdx/mise/pull/15092) ([@​scop](https://redirect.github.com/scop))

#### Changed

- **`node@lts` now resolves to Node.js 26**, which entered Active LTS on 2026-10-28. It used to resolve to 24. `lts/lithium` (also `lts-lithium`) selects the 26.x line. Aliases for older lines, such as `lts/krypton`, are unchanged. To stay on Node.js 24, pin `node@24` or `node@lts/krypton`. [#​15105](https://redirect.github.com/jdx/mise/pull/15105) ([@​jdx](https://redirect.github.com/jdx))
- Setting `system_packages.elevate_with = ""` now means "never elevate": package manager commands run as the current user. This helps on hosts without root, such as Termux. Before, an empty value fell back to `sudo`, `run0` or `doas`. If the setting is unset, mise still picks an elevator from `PATH`. [#​15049](https://redirect.github.com/jdx/mise/pull/15049) ([@​jdx](https://redirect.github.com/jdx), [@​iliqiliev](https://redirect.github.com/iliqiliev))

#### Deprecated

- `--local` on `ls`, `outdated`, `upgrade` and `tasks ls` is deprecated in favor of `--no-global`. It still works and prints no warning for now. Warnings start in 2027.1.0, and the flag is removed in 2027.7.0. `settings --local` and `lock --local` are not affected. [#​15081](https://redirect.github.com/jdx/mise/pul

body: ## Overview The thread title is what you scan the sidebar for, but the project line, branch line and time had nearly the same weight. The project line's icon also sat in the same leading column as the provider icon, so each row read as two list items. - The title gets full `sidebar-foreground`. Project, branch and time drop to `muted-foreground/75`. - The PR number and checks keep their status colors, so they stay brighter than the branch next to them. - The time moves to the right of the project line. The Threads tab has no project line, so the time stays on the branch line there. - The provider icon moves from in front of the title to the end of the branch line. Every line now starts at the same edge, and the title gets the full width. ## File tree renders blank Also fixes the Files view, which often opened with its top rows blank until you scrolled. To reproduce: select a row far down the tree, switch to another view, then switch back to Files. The view remounts on every switch, and the tree scrolled to the selected row on mount. LegendList moved its rendered rows to the selection before the scroller had its height. The scroll then clamped to 0 and fired no scroll event. `initialScrollIndex` hits the same race, so the tree now follows the selection only when it changes after mount. A reopened tree starts at the top. The next arrow key moves on from the old selection and scrolls it into view. | Before, reopened | After, reopened | | --- | --- | | ![blank tree](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/060a3ad0-d658-4836-ba59-74c4c8d2c700) | ![tree from the top](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0dc6ad5a-af2e-447b-b900-a2e420083a4f) | ## Tradeoffs - Resting and attention rows now share one title color. author: 0xleathery
body:
## Summary

Adds a native macOS build for Apple Silicon. Almost every Mac change in shared source is inside
`#ifdef CANE_GL41` or `#ifdef __APPLE__`, with the existing code unchanged in the `#else` branch; running
`unifdef -UCANE_GL41 -U__APPLE__` on those files gives master's file back.

What does reach Windows and Linux:

- **Null checks in `coin.cpp` (#57).** These change behaviour on every platform: entering a level door while a
  charm is still swirling no longer dereferences the null charm pointers of the default PZI that is used when there
  is no player. See "Shared-code fixes".
- **Build files, no effect on existing builds:** new `if(APPLE)` blocks in `CMakeLists.txt` (plus an argument
  list that is empty elsewhere), new macOS presets in `CMakePresets.json`, and an `embed-shaders.cmake` step that
  only runs when the macOS shader folder is passed in.
- **`File Extractor GUI/Views/MainWindow.axaml.cs`:** compiled everywhere, but the added block only runs on macOS
  (`RuntimeInformation.IsOSPlatform(OSPlatform.OSX)`).

Closes #55.

## Building and running on a Mac

```bash
brew install cmake ninja ffmpeg sdl2-compat sdl3
cmake --preset macos-release && cmake --build --preset macos-release
build/macos-release/bin/ProjectCane --data-dir <folder with Worlds, Cutscenes, extraction_manifest.json>
ctest --test-dir build/macos-release          # data tests skip unless CANE_TEST_DATA_DIR is set
packaging/macos/build-app.sh                  # dist/ProjectCane.app
packaging/macos/build-extractor-app.sh        # dist/ProjectCane File Extractor.app (needs the .NET SDK)
```

Details are in `packaging/macos/README.md` and `tests/README.md`. The top-level README is not changed (it still
describes Windows and Linux only); happy to add a macOS section if you want one.

## What's in it

- **Build:** `macos-release` and `macos-asan` presets (Ninja, arm64). The deployment target is macOS 27 because
  Homebrew's FFmpeg and SDL bottles are built for it; a lower target would need FFmpeg/SDL built for that target.
- **Platform layer:** executable directory via `_NSGetExecutablePath`; saves and settings in
  `~/Library/Application Support/ProjectCane`; inside a `.app`, game data is looked up in Application Support, then
  beside the app (`--data-dir` still wins).
- **Renderer on OpenGL 4.1:** macOS only offers OpenGL 4.1 core, and the game targets 4.3. Under `CANE_GL41`:
  - a 4.1 forward-compatible context, with shaders' `#version 430` rewritten to 410 at load time;
  - shader storage buffers replaced by buffer textures (bones, poses, warp state, cel-border edges, shadows,
    lights), and the SSBO writes + `glMemoryBarrier` of the material cache replaced by a transform-feedback bake;
  - sampler and uniform-block bindings set from C++ instead of `layout(binding = N)`;
  - `glTexStorage2D/3D` loaded directly from the driver (glad only loads them for 4.2+), and the base-instance blip
    draws replaced by re-pointing the instance attributes;
  - placeholder textures bound where 4.1 needs a complete texture unit.
- **GL 4.1 shader copies:** seven shared shaders have 4.1 copies in `Sly1-Release/gl41/` (about 2,000 lines).
  `gl41/ORIGINS` records the SHA-256 of the shared shader each copy was derived from, and `cane_shader_source_tests`
  fails when a shared shader no longer matches. That test only builds on macOS and no CI runs it, so a change to a
  shared shader made on Windows or Linux won't warn anyone. The procedure is: port the change into
  `gl41/<name>`, run `cane_shader_source_tests`, and record the shared file's new hash in `ORIGINS`.
- **Cel outlines:** macOS's forward-compatible 4.1 core context only allows 1 px lines, so outlines are expanded in a geometry shader
  (`gl41/celborder.geom`) to match how GL draws wide lines: minor-axis bands rounded to whole pixels without MSAA,
  perpendicular rectangles with MSAA.
- **macOS window behaviour:** Fullscreen uses a borderless window at the display's current mode and hides the menu
  bar and Dock while the game is active. Exclusive fullscreen through GLFW picks the nearest mode from its own list
  and can change the display mode; the fullscreen test saw a 1920x1200 framebuffer on the built-in Retina panel.
  `imgui.ini` is kept in the user folder (Application Support unless `--user-dir` is given). A bundled app with no
  game data shows an alert saying where to put it, instead of an empty window.
- **Packaging:** `packaging/macos/build-app.sh` builds a self-contained, ad-hoc-signed `ProjectCane.app` (bundled
  FFmpeg/SDL dylibs, rewritten install names) and `check-app.sh` verifies nothing loads from outside the bundle.
  `build-extractor-app.sh` builds `ProjectCane File Extractor.app` (self-contained .NET single-file publish, native
  tools beside the executable, no `.csproj` change). On macOS the extractor's output folder defaults to Application
  Support. The bundles take their versions from upstream: 0.4.0 from `CMakeLists.txt` for the game and 0.4.1 from
  the `.csproj` for the extractor.
- **Tests (data tests are opt-in and skip cleanly without data):** `cane_platform_tests`, `cane_shader_source_tests`,
  `cane_shader_tests`, and `cane_world_sweep` — loads every level, cutscene and sound, save round-trips,
  display/fullscreen and a simulated Retina (2x drawable), determinism, and scripted unlock tours, with 0 GL errors
  required. Sanitizer suppressions for the undefined behaviour reported in #58 and #66–#69.

## Shared-code fixes

- `coin.cpp`: null checks for the charm swirl crash when a door is entered mid-swirl (#57). Not guarded: it
  changes behaviour on all platforms (the prize is dropped instead of crashing). Found on macOS; the crash path
  is timing-dependent, so it was not reproduced on Windows or Linux.
- `basic.cpp`: sidebag alignment check that rejects valid libc++ allocations (#61) — macOS only.
- Cel borders drawn with no vertex array bound after a cane swing (#62) — applied under `CANE_GL41` only. #62 notes
  that #48 may be the same bug on Windows, where the same two-line bind in `DrawCelBorder` would fix it.

Other bugs found while porting are filed separately (#58–#60, #63–#72) and not fixed here.

## Testing

- Apple Silicon (M4 Pro), macOS 27: full suite with extracted NTSC-U data — every level (46/46), every cutscene
  (18/18), all audio, save round-trip, display/fullscreen — 0 GL errors, 0 driver warnings.
- Played through the first level natively on an earlier build of this branch (keyboard, Xbox controller incl.
  vibration, music, cutscenes).
- File Extractor `.app`: NTSC-U extraction byte-identical to an extraction made with the extractor run directly
  (1583 files); a Sly 2 ISO is rejected cleanly.

Not tested: PAL and Japanese extraction on macOS; Intel Macs (not supported).

## Known limitations

- Apple Silicon and macOS 27 only; ad-hoc signed, not notarised (the README explains removing the quarantine flag).
- With MSAA on or off, outline width follows the GL specification; it has not been compared pixel-for-pixel with a
  Windows driver.
- Fullscreen hides the menu bar on every display while the game is active.

author: kiendle
body:
## ELI5

Scrolling through a large combined diff was doing work for thousands of lines that were not on screen. Each file now draws only the visible slice, reducing stutters while keeping the same code and one outer scrollbar.

## What Changed

Workspace combined diffs, the PR page, and the PR dialog now keep Monaco's rendered surface bounded to the viewport while preserving each section's full logical height. Cursor movement, Find matches, and note navigation move the outer scrollbar; edits and the reading position survive tab switches. The editor reserves the measured sticky-header height so Find controls and upward cursor navigation stay visible.

## Why

File-level virtualization was already present, but a visible file could still create an approximately 18,000px editor inside an 852px viewport. Bounding that editor addresses host rendering work without changing Electron or Monaco versions.

### Performance evidence

Local macOS arm64 profiling of the viewport change, using the production Electron renderer through hidden-window Playwright CDP. Workload: `createIsolatedManyFileStagedDiffRepo(20, 1200)`, 240 wheel steps of 180px with a scheduled 16ms delay. Both runs ended at `scrollTop=43200`, with the same `scrollHeight=56702` and one mounted diff editor.

| Measurement | Before | After |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Median frame interval | 8.3ms | 8.3ms |
| p99 frame interval | 49.2ms | 17.6ms |
| Largest frame interval | 133.7ms | 83.4ms |
| Frame intervals over 33ms | 12 | 1 |
| Long tasks | 7 | 0 |
| DOM elements | 19,531 | 4,689 |

Tail latency and DOM size improved; median timing did not change, and one long frame remained. These captures were made during implementation. They are local evidence, not a cross-platform statistical benchmark or a CI performance gate.

<details>
<summary>Capture data and reproduction workload</summary>

The existing fixture generator is in `tests/e2e/large-diff-repro-fixtures.ts`. It creates 20 staged 1,200-line files with a change every twelfth line. Open Staged Changes, let Monaco settle, then capture animation-frame intervals while issuing the wheel sequence above. The screenshots below show the same file and lines at the same outer scroll offset.

```json
{"before":{"label":"prod-tall","wallMs":8651.302875,"frames":957,"p50":8.3,"p95":9.3,"p99":49.2,"max":133.7,"over33":12,"longTasks":7,"domElements":19531},"after":{"label":"viewport-final-warm","wallMs":9323.380959,"frames":1083,"p50":8.3,"p95":9.2,"p99":17.6,"max":83.4,"over33":1,"longTasks":0,"domElements":4689}}
```

</details>

## Linked Issue

Related: https://github.com/stablyai/orca/issues/26541

Related: https://github.com/stablyai/orca/issues/28074

These are non-closing links: the broader Windows loading/jumping and single-file reports are not claimed resolved, and the exact original split-mode ArrowDown report was not separately validated against the original baseline.

## Visual Proof

Static captures demonstrate preserved content and layout, not frame timing; the measurements above cover scrolling.

**Before**

![Before: full-height editor, module-0002.ts at outer scrollTop 43200](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b35ec8a0-e723-42de-a65e-759bcb998f0e)

**After**

![After: viewport-bounded editor showing the same lines at outer scrollTop 43200](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/aff8f10b-8ed9-412e-8ed9-61c5301e7c31)

## Testing

- [x] Manually exercised the rendered workspace diff on macOS arm64 using hidden Electron/CDP, including Find and upward navigation after the header fix. Both PR surfaces were inspected in light and dark fixtures during implementation.
- [x] Automated regression tests added/updated.
- Full-project `pnpm tc` and `pnpm lint` (38 steps) passed during implementation. After integrating main and the review fix, `ORCA_BACKGROUND_LAUNCH=1 pnpm check:changed --maxWorkers=2` passed all 23 checks; post-commit verification reused that passing result.
- Seven selected Electron scenarios passed: restore; far-line navigation/edit retention/Find/note reveal; clipped Find in a partly visible file; sticky-header Find and upward cursor visibility; note draft; note layout; and combined word wrap.
- New coverage failed before the corresponding fixes: full-height rendering exceeded the viewport bound; deep-scroll Find and clipped Find matches were not visible; the sticky header obscured Find controls.
- Windows, Linux, SSH latency, and mobile were not exercised locally. Full unit/build/platform coverage is left to CI; no claim that the complete E2E suite is green.

## AI Disclosure

OpenAI GPT-6.1-Sol through OMP was used for investigation, implementation, and validation, with native-agent correctness and simplification reviews.

## Review

Code review: harness-native fallback — the standalone CE orchestration protocol conflicts with this session's native-only orchestration policy. Native correctness and five simplification lenses completed; retained findings were addressed. Greptile's sticky-header finding was fixed with a failing-before/passing-after rendered regression; [resolution and visual proof](https://github.com/stablyai/orca/pull/35739#discussion_r4409550975).

- **Cross-platform:** standard DOM, ResizeObserver, animation-frame, and sticky-layout APIs; no new platform-specific production branch. Test Find shortcuts use Playwright's `ControlOrMeta`. macOS was exercised; other platforms depend on CI.
- **Local/SSH/remote and folder workspaces:** renderer-only sizing and scrolling; no new git-worktree assumptions, server messages, persisted formats, or mixed-version client/server requirements. Remote behavior was considered, not manually tested.
- **Agents/integrations/providers:** no agent, integration, or git-provider protocol changes.
- **Performance:** per-scroll-root frame batching and geometry-read-before-render ordering retained; owned observers, listeners, subscriptions, and pending frames are cleaned up.
- **UI quality:** existing fonts, themes, wrap, whitespace, and editing behavior retained; workspace and both PR surfaces checked.
- **Security:** no new HTML rendering, privilege boundary, IPC, or network capability.

## Agent skill upstream boundary

- [x] Not applicable, or this change copies or mechanically translates no upstream skill-installer source, tests, fixtures, registry entries, path tables, comments, or documentation.

## Notes

Three unrelated single-file E2E failures also reproduced with the original renderer modules from `b685340243` through a baseline build overlay: the two `diff-note-line-range.spec.ts` note-highlight counts (expected 6/1, received 0) and `diff-word-wrap.spec.ts`'s missing single-file Word Wrap menu item after narrow layout. They were left unchanged rather than weakening tests or expanding this PR.

body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"dichhead"} -->
_Requested by **Matus** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01RMfnmT3hVaNRapok1aVuVD?thread=cmsg_01RMfnmT3hVaNRapok1aVuVDNwWPnkfzjKuLLnHwcKfBdm)_

## Description

The organisation's Actions runners are shared by every repository in it, and the queue is backed up on concurrent jobs. This makes pm's CI look at what a change touches first. It is the pm half of losos-project/desktop#374.

- New `.github/changes` script. It compares a pull request with the base it merges into, or a push with `github.event.before`. It prints `code=false` when every path is text or other CI: `.github/`, `docs/`, `README.md`, `CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md`, `CONTRIBUTING.md`, `SECURITY.md`, `LICENSE` or `.gitignore`. A change to the calling workflow or to the script, any other path, or any other event runs everything.
- `ci.yml` has a `changes` job first. `lint`, `test` and `sandbox` skip when it says `code=false`. If `changes` fails they still run (`!cancelled() && code != 'false'`), so a broken detector can never become a green skip.
- `rust-clippy.yml` gets the same job, plus a concurrency group, so a newer push to a pull request cancels the analysis already going. `ci.yml` already had one.

## Screenshots

No visible change.

## Reviewer notes

- master's ruleset has no required status checks (deletion, non-fast-forward and Copilot review only), so a skip can't hold up a merge.
- `actionlint` and `shellcheck` pass. The script was tried on a text-only commit (`code=false`) and on a `plugins/Cargo.toml` change (`code=true deps=true`).
- `examples/` and `editors/` count as code: the tests mirror examples, and lint builds `editors/zed`.

body:
## What changed

- **Backup progress in two stages.** A backup job now reports a *snapshot* stage (copy, drop the search index, compress) and an *upload* stage per target. Each fills the bar once in its own colour, with percent, bytes done and speed (`internal/backup/progress.go`, `Job.Stage`/`Job.Speed`). Messages name the target readably ("Data server host:9696/app").
- **Backup card at the top of the dashboard.** While a backup runs the card becomes the progress row, so a second backup cannot be started. The generic job list hides the backup job on the dashboard.
- **File search in the files pane.** New `GET /api/projects/{pid}/tree/search?q=` (path contains every word, case-insensitive incl. Cyrillic, folders first, 100 results) served from the cached file tree. The collapsed rail's two duplicate buttons are now one, with a dot and tooltip when a scope is active.

## Why

Backups of a large corpus took long with no visible progress, the card was easy to miss and could be triggered repeatedly, and the Cyberpunk project has thousands of files that the lazy tree made hard to reach.

## For reviewers

- The upload body is now wrapped in a counting reader. `DataServer.Put` reads its length from that wrapper (`Len()`), so the data server still gets a `Content-Length` rather than a chunked upload; a test covers this.
- The 40/25/35 split of the snapshot bar (copy / index / compress) is a rough guess at where the time goes, not a measurement. The copy step is polled by watching the temp file grow, which is approximate.
- No schema changes in this PR.

## Testing

`go build`, `go vet`, `go test ./...`, `gofmt -l`, `tsc --noEmit` and `eslint` pass. New tests: stage order and ranges of the progress reports, `Content-Length` with progress, `Progress.Update`, target labels, and tree search matching/limit. The UI was checked in the browser on a throwaway demo DB (never the real corpus); the live progress swap was too fast to observe on that DB, so check it on a real backup.
