## Task

ORB-19752 — Private source text reaches the orchestrator's hosted model via source-show and search

### Description

## Problem
`private` means "inference only on the user's chosen private endpoint". The office tools enforce that for their own model calls, but `office.source-show` and `office.search` return private bodies and snippets to the MCP caller unchecked (only media reads are gated, `specs/models-and-privacy.md` ~122-135). The orchestrator is the user's agent CLI, usually on a hosted model, so reading a private source sends its text to that hosted model. `specs/selection-sharing.md` (Safety) already drops quotes from private selections for exactly this reason, so the two surfaces disagree.

Found while writing the office-orchestrator skill references; `references/library.md` currently only tells the agent not to copy private text onward, which does not stop the read itself.

## Fix
Make an explicit decision (4_decisions.md) on what private content the MCP surface returns to the orchestrator — e.g. withhold bodies/snippets of private documents from MCP callers (metadata, ids and anchors only), optionally with a summary produced on the private route — and apply it consistently to source-show, search, knowledge-show/artifact-show for private items, and attach. Update models-and-privacy.md, selection-sharing.md and the skill's library reference.

### Acceptance Criteria

- The decision on what private content MCP callers receive is recorded in docs/design/office/4_decisions.md
- office.source-show and office.search follow that decision for private documents, consistently with office.selection-get's private handling
- Regression tests through the tool entry points show a private source's body text is not returned to an MCP-scoped caller (or is returned only as the decision allows), failing before the fix
- specs/models-and-privacy.md and the orchestrator skill's references/library.md describe the enforced behaviour

## Execution Summary

<details>
<summary>Click to expand</summary>

Decision (4_decisions.md, Private content is withheld from MCP-visible read tools, ORB-19752): uniform metadata-only withholding — no MCP-vs-app caller key exists in-repo and an input key would be spoofable, and no private-route summary is substituted. For private documents, source-show/search/knowledge-show/artifact-show return id/kind/title/path/sensitivity/provenance/anchors with content_withheld:true and no body/text/span/snippet/summary-sidecar/chapter-frame-gotcha text/page body/artifact body. (4) models-and-privacy.md (replaced source-text-display sentence with Read tools withhold private bodies), selection-sharing.md Safety, and skill references/library.md (Search hits + Sensitivity) describe the enforced behaviour — verified by rg. App: uniform withholding also reaches the app (same tools), so contracts SourceView gains content_withheld, server sources feature passes it through (new server test), and web source/library screens show a withheld notice instead of an empty document. ## Summary

### 1. 2D (top-down) board view, toggled in Settings (`4bcf0ff`, fixed in `1181d43`)
- New **Board view** setting (3D / 2D) in the lobby's Settings and the game menu's Settings. It's saved in `tuktuk-settings`, defaults to 3D, and switches immediately, including mid-game.
- 2D is the **same scene** seen straight down through a long lens (`src/scene/camera/view.ts`), so it looks like a flat printed board. Every 3D feature keeps working: thrown dice, tokens stepping tile by tile, drawn cards, the spotlight on a hovered player's holdings, floating amounts, tile highlights and the space picker.
- Camera in 2D: every shot is top-down with the board's front at the bottom. It never swings round to a lane, dragging pans instead of rotating, and wheel/pinch zooms. Distance limits scale with the lens.
- Height doesn't show from above, so in 2D a hop briefly enlarges the token (`liftScale`), and floating labels drift up the screen instead of rising toward the camera.
- **Fix (`1181d43`):** on some GPUs the 2D view showed only the board's green frame. The printed board sits 0.002 above the slab's top, and with the 2D camera ~3.5× farther away on the same near plane (0.1), the depth buffer could no longer separate the two surfaces. The near/far planes now move with the view (`VIEW_CLIP`: 2D uses 2 / 700), and the printed board has a polygon offset so it always draws over the slab.

### 2. The board gets the whole middle; collapsible log (`dde9bff`)
- **Wide screens:** the turn bar moves to the top of the left column (above the players) and the action bar to the bottom of the right column (under the log). The board gets the whole middle at full height.
- **Tablets:** the players stay a strip on top, and the turn bar, the right-hand panels and the action bar share the right column. **Phones are unchanged.**
- The docked bar's buttons share the column's width in one row, or in two rows (Manage/Trade, then the icons) when the column is narrow.
- **Log:** a chevron folds it to its header, remembered in this browser. The Log button or `L` shows it again.

### 3. Trade dialog in the middle (`1181d43`)
- The trade builder is now centred over the lightly dimmed board instead of sitting against the right side. The camera no longer re-frames around it.
- On wide screens the action bar stays in its place (bottom right), above the backdrop, so Roll / End turn still work mid-trade. On tablets the bar moves under the board while trading, in one row, so the dialog keeps its full height.

## Testing
- `npm run typecheck`: passes. `npx vitest run`: 88 files, 1,354 tests pass. This includes new tests for the 2D view maths and the setting.
- New Playwright specs: `e2e/board-view.spec.ts` (choosing 2D in the lobby and mid-game, desktop and phone, kept after a reload) and `e2e/log.spec.ts` (collapse, kept after a reload, `L` and the chevron).
- After the last commit, these offline Playwright specs pass, 17 tests in all: solo, local-hotseat, heroes-hotseat, board-view, log, touch, smoke and settings. That includes trading with a bot and sending the offer at 960×540.
- `solo.spec.ts` "Play now vs bots …" (asserts exactly 3 rolls with three bots playing) failed in an earlier full run. It also failed one run in two on the code without these changes, so it's an existing timing flake.
- Layout and the trade dialog were checked with screenshots at 1920×968, 1280×720, 960×540, 900×700 and phone size, in 3D and 2D.
- **Not run here:** the online specs, which need the database emulator.

## Known limitation
At 960×540 the trade dialog's Cancel / Send offer buttons are partly clipped at the bottom, as they were before this PR.

author: ghywel
body:
Adds `Rule30UniversalStart`, a core-Lean catalog module about the right diagonals `D j t = x_t (t − j)` of `Rule30Realization.evol`, read from a start whose rightmost black cell is at `0`. They satisfy `D j (t+1) = D j t xor (D (j−1) t || D (j−2) t)` for every start (`rightDiag_step`).

- `universal_start`: let `m ≥ 2` be the first index with `x (−m) = x (−(m − 1))`. Then `D (m+1), …, D (m+6)` have individual least periods `4, 8, 8, 16, 32, 32`, and `D (m+7)` has least period `32` or `64`, whatever the other start bits.
- `universal_start_finite`: every nonzero finitely supported start, after this normalization, has such an `m`, so the conclusion holds for every finite seed.
- `universal_start_profiles`, `cert`: up to `m` each diagonal alternates. A running XOR of a `P`-periodic forcing repeats after `2P` (`run_double`), so the seven new diagonals repeat within `256` ticks and depend only on the common feeder phase and seven start bits. The `256` assignments are a kernel-checked certificate in sixteen `decide +kernel` declarations of sixteen cases each (`cert_0000` … `cert_1111`, assembled by an explicit match), with no `native_decide`. Least periods are decided by cyclic rotations of bit masks, rejecting every smaller positive period.

This complements `Rule30RightPeriods` (the doubling criterion and the single cell's right periods) by showing that the opening of the period sequence after the alternating prefix is the same for every finite seed. Nothing is claimed beyond `D (m+7)`, about later period growth, or about the centre column.

Checked on Lean 4.35 against the kit's core catalog as an isolated module: `Check.lean --claim partial` with the headlines `universal_start`, `universal_start_finite`, `universal_start_profiles` and `cert` passes, replaying 258 constants. All 122 declared constants use standard axioms (`cert`: propext; the others: propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound). The full certificate check takes about 40 s and peaks at about 1.3 GB per process. The companion portal essay embeds the same proof in submission form.

body:
Задача: tasks/T-0259-secrets-tree-and-rift.md

Поток: claude-13 / sonnet-5.5 / high
Запустил: владелец

**Черновик с вопросами:** поведение реализовано и проверено, но в нескольких местах спецификации я выбрал толкование сам — они в разделе «Вопросы». Если ответы совпадут с моим выбором, достаточно вывести из черновика; если нет — правка небольшая.

## Что сделано

- **Виды.** `SECRET_KINDS`: `tree` и `rift` (перед `wisp`); `SecretsDef.tree` и `SecretsDef.rift`; числа и веса — `content/secrets.ts`: древо — радиус 120, лечение 2 % максимума здоровья в секунду, щит раз в 60 с; разлом — радиус 50, шесть элит кольцом 300, сундук 5. Веса: древо 1 во 2-м и 3-м кольцах, разлом 1 только в 3-м; в 1-м кольце по-прежнему одно капище.
- **Древо-оберег.** Пока игрок в круге: лечение долей максимума за тик (не выше максимума) и щит на одно попадание (`player.shieldHits`, тот же, что у «Эгиды») раз в период по непрерывному стоянию; щит не копится сверх одного. Отошёл — лечение прекращается, отсчёт щита идёт с нуля. Древо не исчезает и «использованным» не становится.
- **Разлом Нави.** Вход в круг → волна из `elites` элит кольцом `ringRadius` вокруг разлома, **мимо потолка живых** (упирается только в ёмкость пула); тип каждой берётся из потока тайников (`STREAM_SALT.secret`), `world.rng` не тронут (тест сверяет состояние генератора с миром без тайников). Убиты все — `openChest(world, chestSize)`, исход `cleared`; игрок ушёл дальше кольца, не добив, — разлом закрыт без награды, исход `left`; повторный вход ничего не делает.
- **Правила.** `findSecretsProblems` называет поля `tree.*` и `rift.*` (в том числе «кольцо волны дальше круга разлома»); огонёк ведёт и к древу, и к разлому.
- **Документы.** `CLAUDE.md` («Шесть видов», пример настройки), `docs/32-balance.md` §3.2.

## Эталоны

Не сдвинулись: на этой ветке тайники ещё не подключены к забегу (T-0352, #577), а бот калибровки по тайникам не ходит и после подключения (замер в T-0352 — свод до и после совпал). Раскладка колец от новых весов меняется, но её поток отдельный (`STREAM_SALT.secret`) и golden-прогоны не затрагивает. Обновлять в `test/golden/**` нечего.

## Вопросы

1. **«6 элит из пула элит текущей минуты»** (раздел «Решения», разлом). У мира нет таймлайна — он у директора спавна, и «минута» мира в `World` не лежит (`world.difficulty.segment` — только номер). Сейчас пул — **все типы с `rank: "elite"` из контента** (сегодня их два: `elite_ghoul`, `elite_grave_knight`), выбор по каждой элите — из потока тайников. Как задумано: элиты, которые таймлайн уже выпускал к текущему моменту (тогда директору нужно передавать в мир список `eliteSeen` при смене отрезка, а он войдёт в снимок), или любой элитный тип достаточно?
2. **«Ушёл или не добил — сундука нет»** (разлом). Что считать «ушёл»? Круг входа — 50, а волна выходит на 300 вокруг игрока, стоящего в нём, так что от круга игрок отходит сразу. Сейчас «ушёл» = **дальше `ringRadius` (300) от разлома**, пока жива хотя бы одна элита волны. Нужен другой порог или условие (например, «время вышло», «все элиты отстали»)?
3. **«большой сундук (размер 5) у разлома»**. Сейчас — **тот же путь, что у клада**: `openChest(world, 5)` (награды выданы сразу, окно сундука по `pauseOnChest`). Альтернатива — уронить подбор-сундук на месте разлома, чтобы к нему дошли (потребует нового источника в `ChestSource` и размера у `dropChest`). Какой вариант?
4. **Щит древа и уже стоящий щит.** Сейчас щит **не копится**: если у игрока уже есть непотраченный щит, древо ничего не добавляет. Нужно «+1 до потолка» (какого)?
5. **Волна не поместилась в пул врагов.** Выходит столько элит, сколько нашлось слотов; если ни одной (нет элит в контенте или пул полон) — разлом закрывается без исхода и без сундука. Устраивает?
6. **Снимок прерванного забега.** Состояние разлома (`opened`, элиты волны) и отсчёт щита древа — поля `SecretSite`. В снимок забега их внесёт та же работа, что подключает тайники к снимку, — T-0352 (#577); в этой ветке снимка тайников ещё нет. После вливания #577 нужно будет добавить `opened` и `wave` в `capturedSecrets` / `restoreSecrets` (я могу сделать отдельным коммитом в этом PR после #577).

## Отступления от спецификации

- В `shared` шапки добавлены (по Р176 п.2): `secrets-rules.ts`, `secrets-layout.ts`, `world.ts` (поля `SecretSite.opened` и `wave`), `create-world.ts` (запасные правила), `secrets.test.ts`, `secrets-content.test.ts`. Два последних закрепляли «в дальних кольцах только клад и камень» — это правило задача меняет, тесты обновлены.
- `docs/32-balance.md` §3.2 — абзац рядом с замером T-0352 (при вливании возможен небольшой конфликт текста; смысл не пересекается).

## Проверка

- Тесты первым коммитом (`secrets-tree-rift.test.ts`, 17 случаев); `typecheck`, `lint`, `vitest run packages scripts` (289 файлов), сборка web-telegram, `pnpm budget`, `pnpm docs:check`, `pnpm task diff-check` — зелёные.
- Аналитика: `secret_used { kind: "rift", outcome: "cleared" | "left" }` — через `usedLog` движка, как в спецификации; уход в аналитику — T-0260.

📋 **СВОДКА: В DEV ВЛИТ PR #578 — ДРЕВО-ОБЕРЕГ И РАЗЛОМ НАВИ**

Ещё два тайника на дальних кольцах: древо-оберег лечит и даёт щит рядом с собой, разлом Нави выпускает волну из шести элит и даёт большой сундук, если выстоять.

There is consequently no old-to-new published result to report. The new cases do not recompute or replace the paper's validation counts or maximum differences. P08's external reproducible archive is absent from this tree and was not replayed; the relationship between these new discrepancies and its documented differences is unverified.


## Codex report
# rpar-P08: meta-regression R-parity coverage

Final status, pass 4: FEEDBACK.md confirms the complete recursive unit set ran through the named quick-gate runner: **82 tests, 80 PASS, 0 FAIL, 2 TODO, exit 0**, across all six unit-test files. Within that run, P08 has **25 PASS, 0 FAIL, 2 TODO**. Both experimental location-scale assertions still execute and report the original discrepancies, as required by CXTASK.md; neither their assertions nor the absolute 1e-6 tolerance changed. The initial P08 run was **25 PASS, 2 FAIL, 0 TODO**. The missing constant-scale diagnostic evidence has now been received. This final pass updates the job documents only; no additional runs are needed.

No application code or pre-existing tests/references/corpora have been changed. All new code is under `wt/hub/shared/tests/`; job documents are alongside CXTASK.md.

## Inventory before adding tests

| Surface | Existing R comparison | Missing or limited coverage |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Single moderator, PM + floored HKSJ | `meta-regression/tests/test_against_metafor.py:10` compares a hard-coded Python dictionary to R on mr-tiny, **not the JS engine**. Its R script uses unfloored `knha`. `hub/shared/tests/meta-regression-sanity.spec.mjs:197` compares the JS intercept, slope and tau2 to R at 1e-6. | Python test alone cannot catch a JS defect; the mr-tiny browser test deliberately excludes inference. |
| PM exported-script fixtures | `hub/shared/tests/meta-regression-features.spec.mjs:137` and `fixtures/features/meta-regression/rscript/r-results{,-tight}.json` cover six cases, R 4.6.0/metafor 5.2.1. Coefficients, SEs, CIs, tau2, QE/p/df, R2, slope t use scaled 1e-6 (tau2=0: 1e-9). | Slope p and HKSJ q are stored/displayed but omitted from R comparison pairs. No k=1/2/3 tests. Not in the Node quick gate. |
| PM prediction intervals | `hub/shared/tests/meta-regression-pi.spec.mjs:14` checks one heterogeneous k=8 example against rounded knha numbers. | Prediction uses 5-decimal matching, SE 4 decimals, bounds 3 decimals: no 1e-6 PI check; no floor-active or df=1 case. |
| Permutation inference | `meta-regression-permtest.spec.mjs:19` checks one exact p; `meta-regression-features.spec.mjs:89` compares 365 exact k=4..7 p-values at 1e-12; fixed-seed MC at 3 binomial SEs. | MC is intentionally not an exact 1e-6 comparison. Already broad exact coverage, so not selected for this job. |
| Experimental location-scale ML | `hub/shared/tests/location-scale-parity.spec.mjs:19` compares one rounded BCG example. | Existing checks use 2–5 decimal places, not 1e-6; covariance matrices, per-study tau2, and additional regimes are absent. |
| Multivariable ML, 2/3 moderators, optional interaction | `meta-regression/validate/reference.R:2`, `validate/plus/reference.json`, `validate/numeric.test.mjs:11`, and `meta-regression-plus.spec.mjs` cover full/reduced beta/SE/z/p/CI/tau2/logLik/AIC/BIC, LRT/df/p, 41-point prediction mean/SE/CI and weights. 194 configurations, k=4..80; 32 refusals and 32 accepted full fits with tau2 exactly zero in the supplied files. | Iterative values use **scaled** 1e-6, p-values absolute 1e-9 (`validate/contract.js:9`); not uniformly absolute 1e-6. No k=1/2/3 corpus cases. The extension does not offer new-study PIs. Existing rank-refusal policy differs intentionally from metafor dropping redundant columns. |
| Shared parity/rchecks/quick gate | rchecks contains p0cnma.R and p0share.R, neither for this app. No pre-existing P08 unit test in `hub/shared/tests/unit`. GOSH, network, and RVE meta-regression parity files exercise other apps. | No browser-free quick-gate regression coverage of this app. |

All estimators actually offered are PM/floored HKSJ, multivariable ML/z, and experimental location-scale ML/z. There is no FE/DL/REML selector to cover. Inputs are effect sizes and strictly positive SEs, not raw binary 2x2 tables: zero-cell corrections are not an app estimator and are not applicable. Zero SE/variance, constant moderators, and location-scale small-k/rank/boundary behavior remain additional gaps. The supplied tree does not include the paper's external reproducible archive; its reported counts in README-plus are not independently replayed here.

## Root causes and selected work

1. PM inference coverage: `meta-regression-features.spec.mjs:140` omits slope p and HKSJ q. Add full unrounded comparisons on heterogeneous and floor-active input.
2. Boundary coverage: no native-R unit case exercises q flooring with zero tau2, zero null tau2/R2, or k=1/2 refusal versus k=3/df=1. `meta-regression/index.html:251` and `:277` are the implementation under test.
3. PI coverage: old browser tolerances at `meta-regression-pi.spec.mjs:25` cannot enforce 1e-6. App source `meta-regression/index.html:521` explicitly claims t(k-2), with an explicit df argument at `:529`; `shared/ma-core.js:450` defaults to t(k-1) for a simple pool. The new R fixture records `predict(adhoc)`, explicit t(k-1), and `predict(z)` separately. Do not silently replace the app's claimed convention.
4. Location-scale coverage: loose single-example assertions at `location-scale-parity.spec.mjs:30` leave ML covariance/heterogeneity behavior untested at 1e-6. Add constant-scale, varying-scale and existing rounded-BCG inputs against native metafor with recorded optimizer controls.

New files: `hub/shared/tests/r/p08-meta-regression-input.json`, `p08-meta-regression-reference.R`, `p08-meta-regression-reference.json`, `p08-meta-regression-diagnostic.mjs`, `p08-meta-regression-sensitivity.R`, `p08-meta-regression-quick-gate.mjs`, and `hub/shared/tests/unit/p08-meta-regression-{harness.mjs,parity.test.mjs}`. The helper executes the actual inline PM/parser/render/export code in a Node VM with DOM/UX stubs and loads the actual shared PI and location-scale modules. No statistical engine is reimplemented in the assertions. It exposes private PM helpers solely to inspect unrounded values. DOM styling, browser integration and permutation execution are outside this numeric harness.

## Native reference and pass-2 changes

The wrapper ran `p08-meta-regression-reference.R` successfully with R 4.6.0 (2026-04-24 ucrt), metafor 5.2.1, jsonlite 2.0.0, and numDeriv 2016.8.1.1. It produced six PM cases and three LS cases. P

author: jems-chawin
body:
## Owner's brief (29 Oct 2026)

Subtle, optional ambient audio during longer processing on the website call; calm, not distracting; configurable delay; no lyrics or beat; low and faded in; stopped at once when Dory speaks, the person speaks or interrupts, or the turn completes, fails, times out or is cancelled; a clearly labelled "Waiting sounds" toggle, off by default, remembered; accessible operation-specific status text; no repetitive spoken fillers; respect browser audio permissions; never trigger the mic's speech detection; no overlapping loops; clean up at the end of the call.

## What (`center.html` `liveCall`)

- **The sound**: no audio file. A quiet pad built in the call's own Web Audio graph: four oscillators (A2 sine, A3 + a detuned twin, E4 triangles) through a low-pass filter whose cutoff breathes slowly (0.08 Hz LFO), gain faded from silence to 0.035 over 1.5 s. It runs through the call's output gain, so the existing Speaker button silences it too, and it needs no extra permission: the AudioContext already exists for the call. One pad at a time (`S.wait`).
- **When**: `waitArm()` on the `thinking` event starts a `WAIT_DELAY_MS` (2500) timer; the pad starts only if the turn is still thinking and no audio has been queued.
- **Stops, immediately**: Dory's first audio chunk (`enqueue`), the person's own mic level (`tick`, level > 0.3), `heard`, `interrupted`, `turn`, `error` (through `end`), switching the toggle off, and `end()` before the AudioContext closes (200 ms fade, nodes stopped and disconnected).
- **Toggle**: a fourth round button in the call controls, "Waiting sounds", `aria-pressed`, label "Waiting sounds: on/off", off by default, remembered in localStorage `dory_wait_sound`; disabled when the call ends like the others.
- **Status text**: the state line (already a polite live region) now says what she is doing when the question tells: "Searching flights…", "Checking hotel options…", "Looking at expenses…", "Checking the calendar…", "Checking tasks…", "Searching…" (TH + EN, `opLabel` keyword rules), else the existing "Dory is checking: {q}". Spoken fillers were handled in #35 / #37.
- **Mic**: the browser call already uses echo cancellation, and the pad is both quiet and tonal; if any leak reaches the mic the person's level stop fires first. Not measured with speakers.

## Verified

`tests/test_center_page.py` (new static test: keys in both languages, default off, delay constant, every stop hook present, operation labels) and the inline-script parse under node: 47 passed. Not yet heard or clicked in a browser; the Playwright smoke (`-m e2e`) was not run.

## Browser check (Playwright against the page in mock mode, 29 Oct 2026 06:24 UTC)

With the 2.5 s delay shortened by a test patch so the mock's short turns reach it: the control renders as "Waiting sounds: off" next to Mute / End call / Speaker; one click makes it "Waiting sounds: on" and stores `dory_wait_sound=1`; a typed "check hotel options near Marina Bay" showed "Checking hotel options…" in the status live region while thinking; the pad started once (5 oscillators created, gain ramped to 0.035) and stopped the moment Dory's first audio chunk arrived (ramp to 0.0001, all 5 oscillators stopped); End call cleaned up; the console stayed empty. Second commit: the status live region is written only when its text changes (it was rewritten every frame, which can make screen readers re-announce it).


## The filler window (third commit)

A real tool turn with #37's timing: `thinking` at 0 s, pad at 2.5 s, Dory's acknowledgment line at 4.5 s (its audio stops the pad), the answer at 9-11 s. Before this commit the first audio chunk also ended the page's "thinking" state (a pre-existing line in `enqueue`), so the 3-5 s after the acknowledgment showed "I'm listening…" with no pad, the longest silence of the turn. Now "thinking" ends only on `turn`, `interrupted` or `error`, the status keeps naming the operation, and `tick` re-arms the pad once nothing is playing, so it returns 2.5 s after the acknowledgment ends. Judgment call left as is: the second delay equals the first; a shorter one is one number (`WAIT_DELAY_MS`) if the gap feels long. The mock has no filler, so this path is covered by the static test, not the browser check.

author: kd100100
body:
## What

Milestone 1 of the Pipelines 2.0 plan (`docs/plan/pipelines-2.md`, from the journeys proposal in `docs/proposals/pipelines/journeys.html`). After this, a fresh install can take a repository from a push to a running Cloud Run service in a project the company already has, then to Prod and back. Before it, shipping worked only on demo data.

**Server and runner**
- **Attached connections.** A Google Cloud connection can use projects that already exist ("Use projects I already have") and creates none, so it needs no organization or billing account.
  - Attaching a project checks, as the identity Pipelines will deploy as, that the project is visible, Cloud Run is on and the deploy permissions are held. Each gap becomes a sentence saying what to grant.
  - Pipelines acts as the deployer an account names, or as itself; services run as the named account, or as Cloud Run's default.
  - Detaching is refused while an environment still deploys there, and the landing zone refuses attached connections.
- **Laptop sign-in.** Bemmoly can use the person's own gcloud application default credentials, sending their quota project. A service account key is still refused.
- **Environments and paths you can create.** Platform admins create, edit and archive environments and set each tier's path. Only the seed did this before.
- **Image push.** When a connection names a registry, runners build for the deploy platform (so an ARM Mac builds an image Cloud Run can start), push with the machine's own Docker credentials and report the registry digest. The release points at that repository and keeps the deploy settings.
- **Cloud Run revisions** take the port, CPU, memory, startup probe and public access from the release. An image that never left the runner is refused with what to do instead.
- **Auto-promote works.** Paths stored the switch but nothing acted on it. The minute sweep now promotes each application's newest release to auto-promote steps: the first at once, later ones after the stage before has baked. These promotions are asked for by nobody, go through the same code as a person's request, and are held by the same gates and approvals. Production is never promoted to this way.
- **Private repositories check out** with a read-only token minted for that one repository and job (GitHub App installation token narrowed to contents read). Forks get none, a personal token is never handed out, and the runner fetches with the URL so the token never lands in `.git/config`. This adds `readToken` to the kernel's code-host module contract.

**Web**
- Connect a cloud offers "Create projects for me" (unchanged) or "Use projects I already have".
- Attached connections show sign-in, region, registry (edit or clear with undo) and their projects. Each project has status, problems, Check again and Detach, and there is an Attach a project dialog.
- Platform › Environments: New environment, Edit, Archive, an empty state, and a path editor per tier with "Use the same path for every tier". Auto-promote is disabled on production steps.

**Docs:** the journeys proposal, the 2.0 plan, and `docs/pipelines/your-own-project.md`, a step-by-step guide to test with a real project.

## Why

An audit on 29 October found every check green but no way to ship on a real install: no environment writes, no image push, no attached projects, auto-promote stored but ignored, and private repositories unreadable by runners.

## How it was tested

- `pnpm format:check`.
- `turbo typecheck lint`: 46/46 tasks.
- Unit tests for module-pipelines, pipelines-web, runner, pipelines-cli, core and server: all pass.
- Pipelines integration: 38 files, 135/135, up from 123. New coverage:
  - the attached journey over HTTP;
  - environment and path writes, including a zod 4 trap where partial schemas kept defaults and an edit reset fields;
  - auto-promote to Dev, then to Staging after bake, never to Prod.
- Server code-host integration: passes.
- Replayed Google Cloud answers for the attach check and an attached deploy, with port, size, public access and no impersonation.
- The runner's push command run against a stand-in docker CLI.
- The read token on the GitHub App, the clone URL and the checkout.
- `turbo build`, then the Pipelines walkthrough: 9/9, including the new `6-attach-a-project` spec.
- Light and dark screenshots of the new screens were taken locally during the e2e run and checked by eye. They are not attached here.

**Not tested against a real cloud.** Nothing in this pull request has called real Google Cloud or real GitHub. Before merge it should be run by hand with `docs/pipelines/your-own-project.md` on a sandbox project; the guide says what to send back. Also not checked in a browser: a failed attach's problem list (the simulator cannot be made to report problems) and the workload identity file upload (unit-tested only).

**Known gap:** an install that GitHub's webhooks cannot reach never syncs `.bemmoly/application.yaml` and never starts runs on push. The guide uses a tunnel; a "sync now" action is left for later.

## Schema and configuration

- Changeset `0020-pipelines-attached-accounts` adds `origin`, `config`, `problems` and `last_checked_at` to `cloud_accounts`. It is quick and reversible.
- No new environment variables. The release note is `.changeset/pipelines-attach-project.md` (minor).

## Interaction notes

- **Attached card.** Primary job: see whether Bemmoly can reach your projects and what each still needs. Actions: Attach a project, Check again, Detach (confirms). Keys: Enter saves and Esc cancels the registry edit. States: loading, no projects yet, load error with Try again, refusal, failed connection, checking, phone layout.
- **Environments.** Primary job: decide where releases go and in what order. Actions: New environment, Edit path per tier, Edit or Archive per row. Keys: Mod+Enter submits the dialogs. States: loading, empty (with Connect a cloud when no project is ready), load errors, the server's sentence on 409 and 400, tiers without a path.

author: betterclever
body:
Multi-precision arithmetic needs the upper half of a product and its carries. This adds `U32.mul_hi`, `U32.add_hi`, `U32.mac_hi`, and `U32.mac64` so workloads such as cryptographic field arithmetic can express these operations in Bend.

The Base definitions give the operations their mathematical meaning; compiler intrinsics provide C and JavaScript implementations, including device-specific wide multiplication. `U32.mac64` returns a selected 32-bit word of a 128-bit multiply-accumulate result, and returns zero for indices outside 0–3.

This branch also includes a compiler simplification intended to make room for the additions. It is based on an older upstream revision and needs its merge conflicts resolved and its size brought within the repository gate before submission.

**Validation on this branch**
- The existing `U32.mac64` test and the new out-of-range index regression pass on native CPU and JavaScript. Reinstating the old out-of-range behavior makes the regression fail.
- GPU execution and the full cluster test gate have not been run in this environment.
- The repository gate fails because `bend2/comp.ts` exceeds its 66,000-token cap; this needs to be addressed.

body:
**fix(timescale): ignore non-finite viewport inputs**

Invalid values from chart options and synchronized views could poison the time scale and panic during edge clamping. Retain valid state at the shared setters and preserve configured live offsets when invalid options arrive.

**fix(scales): bound maturity whitespace expansion**

A last maturity from host data could allocate without limit or never return. Cap its contribution at 12,000 months, fall back to the minimum for non-finite values, and preserve larger explicitly configured ranges.

**docs(progress): point the maturity scale row at its widget entry point**

Chart::set_horizontal_scale lives in src/widget/time_scale.rs; src/widget/mod.rs does not reference the maturity scale.

**test(scales): drop whitespace rows that repeat other cases**

A negative infinity already fell back to the minimum before the bound, and an infinite last maturity with a large minimum repeats the infinite and large-minimum rows, so neither guards a regression the remaining rows miss.

**fix(widget): retain finite time scale options**

Keep configured spacing and offsets when replacements are non-finite so reapplying options preserves a scrolled viewport at runtime and after construction.

**fix(timescale): clamp retained spacing to new bounds**

Ignoring an invalid spacing must still honour bounds supplied with it. Clamp the retained spacing after substituting it so a raised minimum or lowered maximum takes effect immediately.

**docs(changelog): explain time scale input migrations**

Hosts need an explicit minimum range for longer maturity whitespace and finite limits for scrolling or zooming to an edge now that invalid inputs are ignored.

**test(timescale): remove duplicate non-finite cases**

The state table already checks invalid widths and spacing with stronger assertions, so the bounds table can focus on distinct constraint changes.

**fix(widget): reject non-finite box zoom inputs**

Reject invalid corners and widths before saving history or changing scales so a discarded offset cannot leave half a zoom applied.

Closes #1306
Closes #1307

author: grigabyte
body:
## What and why

Arch-based systems, Omarchy among them, install apps from the AUR (`yay -S …`, `omarchy pkg aur add …`). This PR adds the files for an `octopus-ai-bin` package. It is built from the `.deb` of a GitHub release, the one the `linux-x64` job of `release.yml` (#45) produces, laid out the Arch way:

| `.deb` | package | why |
|---|---|---|
| `/usr/bin/octopus-ai`, `/usr/bin/omp` | `/usr/lib/octopus-ai/{octopus-ai,omp}`, `/usr/bin/octopus-ai` → link | The app finds the engine next to its executable (`locate_omp`, `/proc/self/exe` resolves the link). `omp` is too generic a name for `/usr/bin`: one installed through mise or bun would clash. |
| `Octopus.desktop` | `octopus-ai.desktop` | Named after the window class, so docks and launchers match the window to its entry. |
| `hicolor/256x256@2/apps` | `hicolor/256x256/apps` | No icon theme reads the `@2` folder the `.deb` uses. |
| engine licenses | `/usr/share/licenses/octopus-ai-bin/` | The engine is MIT; Apache-2.0 is in Arch's common licenses. |

Other details:
- Dependencies are what the binaries link against, as `namcap` lists them. Optional:
  - `libayatana-appindicator` for the tray (#50);
  - `gnome-keyring` or `kwallet` for provider keys (#44).
- `!strip`: the engine is a Bun single-file executable, and stripping cuts off its bundled code.
- The built-in updater stays off, as for every system package (#46).

Files:
- `packaging/aur/octopus-ai-bin/PKGBUILD`, `.SRCINFO`;
- `scripts/aur-bump.sh <version> [deb]`: sets the version and the `.deb`'s sha256, and regenerates `.SRCINFO`. Until a release carries a Linux `.deb`, the checksum is `SKIP`.
- `packaging/aur/README.md`: publishing to the AUR (an account and three commands) and testing in a clean container.

## How to check

On Omarchy 4.0.6, with a `.deb` built from `main` the way `release.yml` builds it:

- `scripts/aur-bump.sh 0.2.1 <local .deb>` set `pkgver` and `sha256sums` and regenerated `.SRCINFO`.
- Clean `archlinux:latest` container: `makepkg -d` builds the package (146 MB). `pacman -U` pulls in only the declared dependencies.
  - `ldd` finds every library of `octopus-ai` and `omp`.
  - `namcap` on the package and on the PKGBUILD reports nothing except, for `omp`, the expected notes of a prebuilt Bun binary: unstripped, no PIE, no full RELRO.
- Installed on the desktop itself with `pacman -U`:
  - `octopus-ai` from `PATH` runs `/usr/lib/octopus-ai/octopus-ai` and opens a window. The engine process is `/usr/lib/octopus-ai/omp`.
  - The same through the desktop entry (`gtk-launch octopus-ai`).
  - `desktop-file-validate` passes, and GTK finds the icon in `hicolor/256x256`.
  - `pacman -R` leaves none of the package's files behind.

Not checked:
- the download from a release: there is no Linux `.deb` in a release yet;
- `omarchy pkg aur add` and `yay`: the package is not on the AUR yet.

## Checklist

- [x] `npm run build` and `npm test` pass — no app code changed
- [x] `cargo test --manifest-path src-tauri/Cargo.toml` passes (if Rust changed) — no Rust changed
- [ ] Tests added or updated for changed behaviour — packaging only; checked by hand as above
- [x] No secrets or personal data in code, fixtures or screenshots
- [ ] Discussed in an issue first, if this adds a feature or changes behaviour — new files only

author: heidar
body:
Closes #1.

## What changed
- **`plan-feature`**
  - Feature doc's `slices` entry now includes which slices can be built together.
  - Shared rules (how a value is parsed, shown or checked) are settled in the feature doc before slicing, asking per `risk` (AC3).
  - Prefer the cut that lets more slices be built together only between equally vertical cuts; no layer-only slices (AC2).
  - Each slice records its dependencies and what it touches (screens, tables, modules, rules); the feature doc shows which slices can be built together, with an example line (AC1). Issues note both.
- **`drive-feature`:** by default builds the slices the doc marks as buildable together in parallel, in isolated worktrees; dependency order and human limits still apply (`one at a time` added to the examples); unmarked plans fall back to today's "different parts of the code" rule (AC4).
- **README:** principle 4, `/drive-feature` usage, and the one-ticket-per-session advice describe the new default (AC5).

## Decision ledger
| Decision | Cost if wrong |
|---|---|
| Slices that share only a *settled* rule still count as buildable together; shared screens, tables or modules don't. Without this, settling rules (AC3) would never unlock parallelism. | If a settled rule is still read differently by parallel builders, run 1's conflict comes back; visible in review. |
| The marking is free text with one example ("1 first; then 2, 3 and 4 together; 5 after 3"), not a fixed format. | A driver might misread an odd marking; low, since the planner and driver are both strong models. |
| Kept the existing meaning of limits: any limit stops after each batch (README already says so). | `at most 2 at once` stops after every 2 slices rather than only capping concurrency. Unchanged from before. |

## Verification
No smoke run (owner's decision): skill text only. Independent review (omp `reviewer`): all five criteria pass. One finding fixed (shared-rule wording above). One inherited ambiguity left unchanged: drive-feature's limit bullet treats concurrency caps (`at most 2 at once`) as batch stops. Confirmed on the next real run in `runs/`.

## Flagged
- #3 edits the same sections; land this first.

author: oe5sos
body:
Drei Befunde vom Gerät, gemessen am 2026-10-29 im Protokoll 07:00–07:05 (FLEX-8400, 40 m, fünf FT8-Sendungen).

## 1. Der Sendetaktgeber war grob — 0,79 s zu früh

Qt gibt jedem Taktgeber ab 20 ms von sich aus `Qt::CoarseTimer` und erlaubt sich dabei bis zu **fünf Prozent Vorlauf**. Bei FT8 wird auf die nächste Fenstergrenze gewartet, bis zu 17,8 s — fünf Prozent davon sind 0,89 s.

Gemessen, fünfmal hintereinander dieselbe Größe:

| Sendung | MOX an | soll | Vorlauf |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 07:02:30,215 | :30,000 | 0,779 s früher als bestellt |
| 2 | 07:02:59,213 | :00,000 | 0,787 s |
| 3 | 07:03:29,221 | :30,000 | 0,786 s |
| 4 | 07:03:59,214 | :00,000 | 0,786 s |
| 5 | 07:04:29,214 | :30,000 | 0,786 s |

Das Signal lag damit bei der Gegenstation um −0,8 s versetzt, und der Empfang brach 0,8 s vor dem Fensterende ab. Betreiber: *„die empfangs und sendezeit stimmt nicht."*

Die Rechnung in `Ft8Tx::bisZumNaechsten` war dabei **richtig** und ist geprüft (`derZeitplanStimmt`); der Taktgeber hat sie verworfen. Die Systemuhr war es nicht — `sntp time.apple.com` meldete im selben Augenblick **+37 ms**.

Jetzt `Qt::PreciseTimer`, und ebenso für das Abschalten am Ende der Sendung (dort wären bis zu 0,65 s Vorlauf möglich gewesen und hätten den Schluss des Signals abgeschnitten).

## 2. Je Sendung war nicht zu sehen, was *wir* hinausgeschickt haben

Die Maschine meldete:

| Durchgang | MICPEAK | CODEC | FWDPWR |
|---|---|---|---|
| 4 (:03:59) | **−150 dBFS** | −150 dBFS | 11,4 dBm = 14 mW |
| 5 (:04:29) | −5,98 dBFS | −12,9 dBFS | 38,5 dBm = **7,1 W** |

Bei ihr kam im vierten Durchgang also nichts an. Ob Longpath nichts geschickt oder sie nichts angenommen hat, war **nicht zu entscheiden**: `m_flexFt8Spitze` ist ein Höchststand über die ganze Laufzeit und meldet sich nur, wenn er steigt — nach der ersten Sendung nie wieder.

Neu, je Sendung zurückgesetzt und je Sendung gemeldet: Zahl der Proben an die Maschine, Spitze nach der Dämpfung, und wie oft die Pumpe am Mikrofon statt an FT8 hing. Der nächste Durchgang entscheidet die Frage.

## 3. Die Leistung ging beim Anmelden nie an die Maschine

Die beiden Bänder hängen an `powerChanged` / `tunePowerChanged` — sie feuern **nur, wenn der Regler bewegt wird**. Beim Anmelden blieb die Maschine auf dem Wert, den ein anderer Client zuletzt gesetzt hatte; am 2026-10-29 war das 1 %. Der Betreiber sah „Power 1" und „POWER 0 W" in einer Oberfläche, die 10 W anzeigte, und jede Erklärung dafür lag am falschen Ende (Ton, Verriegelung, Pegel) — die Zahl war einfach nie hinausgegangen.

`verdrahteFlexSenden` zieht beide Werte jetzt einmal nach. Nichts entschieden, nur gesagt, was Longpath schon führt.

## Was dabei bestätigt wurde

Die Behebungen von heute Nacht halten: der Empfang kommt nach dem Lösen in **15 / 29 / 25 / 44 / 39 / 20 ms** zurück, und während des Sendens laufen 2429–2443 Tonpakete durch.

## Noch offen (nicht in diesem PR)

- **Der Driftausgleich jagt:** −1851 → −2173 → +1222 → −348 → **−5543 ppm** über fünf Minuten. Eine echte Quarzabweichung liegt bei ~4 ppm. Gemessen, Ursache offen.
- **Die Flex schickt kein `tx_allowed`:** ihre Verriegelungsmeldung enthält nur Zubehör-Verzögerungen (`acc_tx_delay`, `tx1_enabled`, …), weder `state` noch `tx_allowed`. Darum steht in jeder Sendung „getastet, OHNE je eine Verriegelungsmeldung gehoert zu haben".

## Prüfstand

`tst_ft8_senden` +1 Fall (`derSendetaktgeberIstGenau`), mit der Gegenprobe **im Lauf selbst** (ein frischer Taktgeber bekommt Qts Vorgabe `Qt::CoarseTimer`) und einer Gegenprobe gegen die alte Fassung gefahren: ohne die Zeile im Sendeweg **rot**, mit ihr **grün**. 39/39.

Fünfzehn Compliance-Skripte grün; `discover-thetis-author-tags --drift` und `generate-contributor-indexes --check` sind lokal rot, weil `../Thetis` hier auf `852bf0e` statt dem CI-Pin `501e3f5` steht — belegt vorbestehend, dieselben zwei sind auch auf unverändertem `origin/main` rot.

author: balint245
body:
## Summary

First of three pull requests for milestone 3 ("First render loop", `docs/adr/README.md`): `fosscut-media` can now write files, read audio and check what it wrote. Text layers (part 2) and the export job with the round 1 exit check (part 3) build on this.

- **`FfmpegWriter`** writes MP4, QuickTime and WebM:
  - exact frame timestamps: frame `n` at `n / rate`, including 30000/1001;
  - BT.709 limited-range tags;
  - video from Y'CbCr frames (`push_frame`) or from the renderer's non-linear RGBA (`push_rgba`, converted with BT.709 coefficients rather than swscale's BT.601 default);
  - AAC or Opus audio pushed in any chunk size and re-chunked to the encoder's frame size.
- **Encoder policy (ADR-0009):**
  - H.264 and HEVC come only from hardware encoders: VideoToolbox with `allow_sw=0`, NVENC, Quick Sync, AMF, Media Foundation;
  - ProRes 422 uses `prores_ks`, AV1 uses SVT-AV1, libaom or rav1e, and VP9 uses libvpx;
  - `libx264` and `libx265` are never used, even when the linked FFmpeg has them (the Homebrew and conda builds do).
- **`encoder_capabilities()`** test-opens every candidate once per process, so an encoder that is compiled in but unusable, such as a hardware encoder in a virtual machine, is not offered. An unavailable codec fails with `fosscut.media.encoder_unavailable` and lists what this machine can encode, never a silent substitute (the round 1 regression). Impossible requests fail with `fosscut.media.unsupported`: wrong container, odd size, no streams, mismatched audio format.
- **`probe_output`** reports container, brand, codec, profile, size, exact rate, frame count (counted when the container does not record it), stream durations, pixel format, color tags, audio format and file size. These are the "agent eyes" for exports.
- **`FfmpegAudioDecoder::read(start, duration)`** returns exactly `duration` of interleaved `f32` at the requested rate and channel count, resampled with swresample and placed to the sample, with silence before the start and after the end.
- **Fix:** frame lookup in containers that round timestamps returned the previous frame for some frames. WebM stores milliseconds, so frame 17 at 30 fps is stored at 567 ms. Lookup now allows half a tick of slack, and only when ticks cannot represent the frame duration.
- **Housekeeping:**
  - the FFmpeg backend is split into `ffmpeg/{mod,audio,writer,report}.rs`;
  - FFmpeg logs only errors;
  - `cargo xtask coverage` ignores report entries for files that no longer exist (stale local objects made a moved file count as uncovered).

## Architecture

- ADRs this implements or relies on: ADR-0005, ADR-0006, ADR-0009, ADR-0016
- [x] Architectural adjustments are included as ADR edits: ADR-0009 implementation notes (encoding, encoder policy, capabilities, verification, audio decoding, rounded timestamps)

## Checklist

- [x] Title follows conventional commits
- [x] Every commit is signed off
- [x] Tests added or updated at the right level (ADR-0016); each behaviour change has a test that fails without it (the WebM fix has a lossless WebM decode test)
- [x] No test was weakened, skipped or deleted, and the coverage minimums were not lowered
- [x] New capabilities are reachable from CLI and MCP and listed in `capabilities`: not yet. Export reaches the CLI in part 3 and MCP in milestone 4.
- [x] Writes follow the agent safety contract: no project writes
- [x] Schemas, snapshots and docs regenerated or updated where public behaviour changed (ADR-0009)
- [x] User-facing skills in `skills/` updated if the API they use changed: none exist yet
- [x] No material copied from CapCut or other products; test media is generated by FFmpeg `lavfi` sources and in code

## AI assistance

- [x] AI tools were used: Claude Code wrote the code, tests and docs under the maintainer's direction.

## Verification

Run locally on macOS (Apple M3 Pro), Rust 1.99, FFmpeg 8.1.1:

- `cargo fmt --all --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings`, `cargo doc` with `-D warnings`: clean
- `FOSSCUT_REQUIRE_FFMPEG=1 FOSSCUT_REQUIRE_GPU=1 cargo nextest run --profile ci --workspace --all-features --locked --no-tests=fail`: 139 tests pass, none skipped, three runs in a row. The 21 new tests check:
  - every available encoder (here H.264 and HEVC with VideoToolbox, ProRes, AV1 with SVT-AV1, VP9 with Opus) writes 30 frames plus audio, probes as the requested codec with exact frame count, rate, duration and BT.709 tags, and decodes frame 17 back as frame 17;
  - 30000/1001 timestamps;
  - 75% red RGBA lands at Y 51, Cb 109, Cr 212;
  - audio stays within 0.01 of the exact sine after resampling 44.1 to 48 kHz from 0.75 s;
  - mono output, AAC sources, silence outside the stream, and every typed error.
- `cargo xtask coverage`: workspace 93.85%, `fosscut-media` 92.97%. Every crate is above 85%.
- `cargo deny --all-features check`, schema check, wasm build of the portable crates, ADR index, Markdown lint and link check: clean

Not verifiable locally: encoders on the CI runners. Linux and Windows (LGPL FFmpeg) are expected to encode ProRes, AV1 and VP9 and to refuse H.264 and HEVC, which exercises the `encoder_unavailable` path. Windows' Media Foundation H.264 encoder and VideoToolbox on the macOS runner may behave differently from this Mac.

Known limits:
- Encoding speed and quality settings are tuned for correctness tests, not for final exports; presets come with the export job in part 3.
- Audio is AAC or Opus at a fixed bit rate, and there is no HDR or 10-bit output other than ProRes.

body:
## Qué

Integra el análisis de SonarQube Cloud (`atareao_id3cli`) en el job `test` del CI existente, sin workflow paralelo y sin tocar el job `musl`.

## Cambios

- **`sonar-project.properties`** (nuevo): `sonar.projectKey=atareao_id3cli`, `sonar.organization=atareao`, cobertura vía `sonar.rust.lcov.reportPaths`, exclusiones de `target/`, `scripts/` y `tests/fixtures/`, y `src/tests.rs` fuera de duplicación (los tests repiten estructura por formato a propósito).
- **`ci.yml`**: `fetch-depth: 0` en el checkout; `cargo test` pasa a `cargo llvm-cov --lcov` (ejecuta la suite y emite el informe); scan con `SonarSource/sonarqube-scan-action@v8`.
- **`.gitignore`**: `lcov.info`.

## Decisiones

- `SONAR_TOKEN` a nivel de job y guarda `if: env.SONAR_TOKEN != ''`: `secrets` no se puede evaluar en un `if`, y así un PR desde fork sin secretos no rompe el CI.
- Quality gate **no bloquea**: `sonar.qualitygate.wait` se queda por defecto en `false`. Primero se observa, luego se decide.
- El analizador de Rust relanza `cargo clippy` internamente; el `clippy -D warnings` existente sigue siendo el gate duro.

author: rileytheriler
body:
### 💡 What:
Replaced `canvas.getBoundingClientRect()` and dimensions assignment inside the `PitchOrb` `requestAnimationFrame` loop with an asynchronous `ResizeObserver`.

### 🎯 Why:
Calling `getBoundingClientRect()` inside a high-frequency animation loop (running ~60fps via `RenderCoordinator`) causes the browser to perform synchronous layouts (layout thrashing). Combined with reassigning `canvas.width` and `canvas.height` on every single frame, it was forcing unnecessary repaints, increasing CPU utilization, and risking stutter.

### 📊 Impact:
*   Significantly reduces the number of layout calculations per second when `PitchOrb` is mounted.
*   Prevents clearing and recreating the canvas drawing context on every single frame unless the physical container size actually changes.
*   Improves overall animation smoothness and reduces GC pressure.

### 🔬 Measurement:
1.  Open the application to a view containing the `PitchOrb` component (e.g. Practice Mode -> Pitch tab).
2.  Open Chrome DevTools -> Performance tab.
3.  Record a profile for a few seconds.
4.  Observe that "Recalculate Style" and "Layout" events are no longer continuously triggered during the animation loop, yielding a cleaner framerate.

author: anirudhkumar-nanonets
body:
**Issue:** Until its hooks were trusted in `/hooks`, Codex never heard how to save a learning. Asked to save one, it edited a teammate's learning file by hand. In Claude Desktop worktree sessions, editing a file never brought its learnings, and neither app was counted as its own host.
**Why:** AGENTS.md only covered code search, and `trail note` wrote to `~/.trail` (which Codex's sandbox can't write) before the repo. Desktop's hooks get the main checkout as the project, so a worktree file's path never matched a learning. `agent_host` had no value for either app, and hook events from Codex said `cli`.
**Fix:** AGENTS.md gets a Learnings part. A repo learning saves even when `~/.trail` can't be written. Touch learnings take the file's path in its own checkout. A hook puts all its events, and the trail commands it starts, down to the payload's host, now including `codex` and `claude-desktop`.

Moves: active users by host, PostHog Postgres (Metabase db 11, `posthog_event_full_view`), distinct installs over the last 7 days with a `repo_seen`, `query`, `note_saved` or `learnings_committed` event, `cli_name = 'trail'`, by `agent_host`. On 2026-10-29: claude-code 1,157 · cli 677 · mcp 262 · claude-desktop and codex 0 (the values don't exist before this PR).

## What works where (checked with real sessions on 2026-10-30)

| Host | Learnings at start | Saving one | Reusing one | `agent_host` |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Claude Desktop Code tab (worktree session) | works (from the main checkout's branch) | works | **partly → works** | `claude-code` → `claude-desktop` |
| Codex, hooks trusted | works | **no → partly** (saves when asked; never unasked) | works | `cli` → `codex` |
| Codex, hooks not trusted (right after `trail init`) | **no → partly** (AGENTS.md) | **no → partly** (same) | works (`trail ask`) | none |
| Claude Desktop chat (Trail connector, trail-cloud) | partly | partly (saves to the workspace, not the repo) | works | not in this repo |

### Codex: five real sessions
Codex 0.162 (the CLI inside ChatGPT.app, which the app runs as its app-server), default model, `workspace-write` sandbox, each run in its own home outside `/tmp` so the sandbox can't write it. "Before" is trail 0.26.0 as installed; "after" is this branch. The repo had one committed learning (money stays in integer cents). Prompt: add `applyDiscount` with a test; "half-cents always round down".

| Run | Reached the model about learnings | Used the learning | Saved the rule unasked | Then asked to save |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A before, untrusted | nothing | yes, via `trail ask` | no | edited the teammate's learning file by hand |
| B after, untrusted | AGENTS.md Learnings part | yes, via `trail ask` | no | `trail note`: turned away for naming no file, then saved inside the sandbox |
| C after, trusted (`--dangerously-bypass-hook-trust`) | session-start text, prompt learnings, save directive, AGENTS.md | yes, credited | no | not asked |
| D before, trusted | session-start text, prompt learnings, save directive | yes, credited | no | not asked |
| E after, trusted | every queued event from the session says `codex` (hook_ms ×3, prompt-hook `ask`, stop-hook `check`, `repo_seen`, `learnings_committed`); in D they said `cli` | | | |

Codex's shell sets `CODEX_THREAD_ID`, `CODEX_SESSION_ID`, `CODEX_SANDBOX` (seen), so `detectHost` reads those. But a trail command Codex runs itself can't write the event queue under `~/.graft`, so those send nothing either way.

### Claude Desktop: this session
The transcript and trail's state files show SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit, PostToolUse, PostToolUseFailure, PreToolUse on Bash and Stop all ran; the trail skill and MCP server loaded. PreToolUse on Edit ran but never found a learning: in a worktree session `CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR` is the main checkout, so `learningsOnTouch` saw `.claude/worktrees/<name>/src/...` (same cause #738 fixed for overlap warnings).

## Changes
- `src/hosts/instructions.ts`: under trail, the AGENTS.md block (also GEMINI.md, Copilot) ends with `### Learnings`: where they are, read them via `trail ask`, save with `trail note`, commit them, run `trail check`. Graft's text is unchanged.
- `src/notes/notes.ts`: `writeNote` falls back to `repoPlace` when `ensureRepoHome` throws and the learning goes in the repo. `--personal` still needs `~/.trail`.
- `src/claude/hooks.ts`: `learningsOnTouch` takes the file's path relative to `checkoutRoot(dirname(file))`; learnings and session state still come from the project dir, so nothing is shown twice. The hook sets `TRAIL_AGENT_HOST` from the payload's host.
- `src/telemetry/track.ts`, `contract.ts`, `TELEMETRY.md`: `agent_host` adds `claude-desktop` (`CLAUDE_CODE_ENTRYPOINT === 'claude-desktop'`) and `codex` (Codex's shell variables, or `TRAIL_AGENT_HOST` from a hook). Every env value is only compared against fixed names; none travels.
- A learning on what each host does and how to test Codex for real (replaces yesterday's, which said every hook worked in Desktop).

## Tests
- New: host detection per env and from `TRAIL_AGENT_HOST`, a Codex `learnings_committed` carrying `codex`, the trail AGENTS.md text, `writeNote` with an unwritable home, and a learning reaching an edit in a linked worktree while the project dir is the main checkout (fails without the fix).
- 829 telemetry, hosts, hooks, trail and upkeep tests with a scratch HOME: 5 fail, all of which also fail on `origin/main` here (they depend on a real `trail` on this machine's PATH). `tsc --noEmit` clean.

## trail check
Two flags, both word matches: `TELEMETRY.md:40` against "Claude ran with the real HOME…" (Oct 27, about tests loading the real `~/.claude/settings.json`), and `src/claude/hooks.ts:177` against the `replaces:`-holds-ids learning (Oct 22): that line has `.replace(` and the words "file" and "name", and touches no learning field.

## Follow-ups
- Codex never saved a learning unasked, with the directive in context. Claude Code gets a Stop-hook ask after real digging; Codex needs its own nudge.
- In a Desktop worktree session, session-start and prompt learnings come from whatever branch the main checkout has.
- Trail commands Codex runs itself send no telemetry (queue under the home folder).
- Desktop chat learnings land in the workspace, not `.trail/learnings/` (trail-cloud).
- Overlap: #738 adds the same `checkoutRoot` import to `hooks.ts`; #724, #727, #728 edit `TELEMETRY.md`/`contract.ts`/`track.ts` in other hunks.

author: alimarchal
body:
## Problem
A user whose role grants a module (e.g. File Management via the division role) saw its Product card and could open it, even though their own permissions did not include it. Role permissions could not be switched off for a single user.

## Change
- New table `user_denied_permissions` (migration `2026_10_29_112116_create_user_denied_permissions_table`). Nothing is stored until an admin revokes something.
- Settings > Users > Edit: each permission that comes via a role has a **revoke** checkbox. Saving stores only revokes that a selected role really grants; un-ticking gives it back. The profile page no longer lists revoked permissions as granted.
- `User::hasPermissionTo()` denies a revoked permission, which is what `can()`, `@can`, the permission middleware and direct checks all use, so Product cards, module routes (403) and dashboards follow. Other users of the same role are unaffected.
- Role permissions can still be removed for everyone from Settings > Roles; nothing re-adds them.

## Server
Run `php artisan migrate`. Existing users are unchanged until something is revoked.

## Testing
- New `UserRevokedRolePermissionTest` (4 tests): revoke is per user, card hidden and module 403 for that user only, form save stores/clears revokes, edit form renders the checkbox. Related suites pass.
- Checked locally in Chrome as a division user with File Management and Account Opening revoked: both cards gone, the module URL shows 403. Restored afterwards.

author: ngonie69
body:
## What changes

The Route Checklist export (Retail Sales Orders → Route checklist → Export):

- **Items fold under their order.** The Checklist sheet has one row per order, with its item lines in a collapsed Excel row group beneath it. Click **+** beside an order to see its items, or **2** at the top left of the sheet to open them all.
- **Invoice # column.** Each order row shows the SAP invoice it became, and there's a new **Invoiced** count card. The Order Lines sheet also gets an Invoice # column, after Status.

## Where the invoice number comes from

Mobile Orders only asks SAP about the orders on its current list page (10 by default), so most checklist orders had no answer. On export, the checklist now asks SAP (`validate-bulk`, through the shared `SalesOrderPodStatusCache`) about approved orders the page has no invoice for. That's at most one call per 100 orders. Status follows the same answer, so an order SAP has invoiced reads Invoiced (or Delivered). If SAP fails, the export still downloads and the subtitle says invoice numbers may be missing.

## ClosedXML outline fix

ClosedXML 0.105 puts `collapsed` on the hidden detail rows and writes the row outline depth to `outlineLevelCol`. With that output, Excel can show "−" over groups that are already shut. The saved workbook is post-processed with the OpenXML SDK, which moves `collapsed` to the order row and sets `outlineLevelRow`. This follows the pattern the Vendor Performance export already uses.

## Verification

- 59 workbook tests pass, including new ones for the folded groups, the raw `collapsed`/`outlineLevelRow` XML, and invoice numbers on both sheets.
- Opened a generated sample in Excel: **+** opens an order's items, **−** closes them, and the Invoice # and Invoiced card show.
- Not checked against live SAP: the export-time invoice lookup is only covered by tests.

author: nehagslab
body: ## Summary Some Glue views are ingested with a single `dummy` column instead of their real columns, while their lineage is correct. When an Athena/Presto view has an output column whose type Hive cannot represent — for example `timestamp with time zone` (from `AT TIME ZONE`) or `char` longer than 255 — the Glue Data Catalog stores a single placeholder column named `dummy` in `StorageDescriptor.Columns`. The connector ingested that placeholder as the view's schema. Lineage was unaffected because it is parsed from the view SQL, which Glue stores intact in `ViewOriginalText`. The real output columns, with their Trino types, are also present in that base64-encoded Presto view definition. This PR reads them from there when the column list is the placeholder. ## Changes - **`presto_view_decoder.py`**: add `trino_type_to_hive_type`, which converts Trino types to the closest Hive type so recovered columns go through the existing Hive schema path and get the same v2 field paths as regular Glue columns. - `timestamp(p) [with time zone]` → `timestamp`, `real` → `float`, `varbinary` → `binary` - `row(...)` / `array(...)` / `map(...)` → `struct<...>` / `array<...>` / `map<...>`, recursively, including quoted row field names - Types Hive cannot represent (`time`, `json`, `uuid`, `ipaddress`, anonymous `row` fields) → `string`, so the column is kept - **`glue.py`**: add `_get_placeholder_view_schema_fields`, used by `_get_glue_schema_metadata`. It applies only when the table is a `VIRTUAL_VIEW` whose column list is exactly one column named `dummy`. - Keeps the original Trino type as `nativeDataType` (e.g. `timestamp(3) with time zone`) - Applies Lake Formation column tags to the recovered columns - Report counters: `num_view_schema_from_view_definition`, and `num_view_placeholder_schema_unresolved` plus a warning when the columns cannot be recovered (the `dummy` column is kept in that case) - **Docs**: new "Views with a `dummy` Column in Glue" section in `glue_post.md`. Because the view now has real columns, column-level lineage parsed from the view SQL attaches to them in the UI. Raw Spark/Hive views (not Presto-encoded) are unchanged. Tables with a real column named `dummy` are unchanged. ## Testing - **Unit tests**: - A placeholder view recovers its real columns, with the correct type and the original Trino native type - A placeholder view with an undecodable definition keeps `dummy`, increments the unresolved counter and warns - A table (not a view) with a column named `dummy` is left untouched - Parametrized tests for `trino_type_to_hive_type` - **Without the fix**, the recovery test fails (schema is only `dummy`). - **Glue and decoder test suites**: `tests/unit/glue`, `tests/unit/test_presto_view_decoder.py` — 295 passed. - **Manual**: against a real Glue catalog with views using `AT TIME ZONE` (single and multiple columns) and `char(256)`, plus a control view with only Hive-compatible types. Before the fix, the three affected views showed only `dummy`. After the fix they show all their columns with correct types, and column-level lineage to the base table appears. The control view is unchanged. Before: After: ## Checklist - [x] The PR conforms to DataHub's [Contributing Guideline](https://github.com/datahub-project/datahub/blob/master/docs/CONTRIBUTING.md) (particularly [PR Title Format](https://github.com/datahub-project/datahub/blob/master/docs/CONTRIBUTING.md#pr-title-format)) - [ ] Links to related issues (if applicable) - [x] Tests for the changes have been added/updated (if applicable) - [x] Docs related to the changes have been added/updated (if applicable) - [ ] For any breaking change/potential downtime/deprecation/big changes an entry has been made in [Updating DataHub](https://github.com/datahub-project/datahub/blob/master/docs/how/updating-datahub.md) — not a breaking change: affected views gain their real columns in place of `dummy` 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) --- ## Summary by cubic Fixes the Glue ingestion source converting Athena/Presto views with Hive-unrepresentable output types (e.g. `timestamp with time zone` from `AT TIME ZONE`, or `char(256)`) into a single placeholder `dummy` column. Views whose column list is exactly that placeholder now recover their real columns from the base64-encoded Presto definition in `ViewOriginalText`, so schemas and column-level lineage are correct. - Converts Trino types to the closest Hive type so recovered columns get the same field paths as regular Glue columns; keeps the original Trino type as `nativeDataType`, and falls back to `string` when a type has no Hive equivalent. Row, map, and array types are translated recursively, with positional names for anonymous row fields (including multi-word types like `interval day to second` or `timestamp with time zone`) and case-preserved quoted field names. - Validates the recovered columns via a typed helper, which also fixes a crash on malformed `columns` values that previously aborted the run. - Caps type nesting depth and length, and rejects deeply nested view definitions before parsing — on Python 3.12+ `json.loads` can segfault the whole process on such input — so pathologically nested or oversized definitions can't crash or stall the run. - Applies Lake Formation column tags to recovered columns and adds `num_view_schema_from_view_definition`, `num_view_placeholder_schema_unresolved` (with a warning stating whether the definition could not be decoded or had no valid `columns` list), and `num_view_columns_type_unresolved` (for recovered columns ingested without a type or as `string`). A failed decode is reported once per view rather than from both the schema and view-definition paths. - Tables with a real column named `dummy`, and Spark/Hive views or views without `ViewOriginalText`, are unchanged. Written for commit 23f841a1df396c17b9926c5377f0ffbd13643f83. Summary will update on new commits.

body:
Yukon submission `54e31bc8-5da2-46f9-8f79-e405f2240960` against https://github.com/Layr-Labs/labinius-fast-challenge at `48f2a6d36f6a4828dffd515eb84dd6959adac17f`.

Current best score: 214.184103999287. This PR's own benchmark run scores the head commit;
Improving submissions stay open until Yukon promotes them, after owner review when enabled. Other results are closed.

---

**Submitter note**

Model: Claude Opus 5.5
Harness: Claude Code

# Page faults out of the commitment, a sorted fold schedule, a fold that writes the proof, a commit kernel fed batch by batch

## The change

Four files: `solution/proof_generate/src/main.rs` (allocator, setup phase, where the folded witness goes), `solution/labinius/crates/pcs/src/simd/sms_commit.rs` (two dead stores, the staging buffer, the prefetch distance), `solution/labinius/crates/pcs/src/simd/ntt/bin_asm.rs` (the commit kernel's order) and `solution/labinius/crates/pcs/src/fold.rs` (the fold's schedule and output). No arithmetic, bound or format changes.

1. **Large blocks are kept for reuse.** A freed block of 1 MiB or more used to be unmapped at once. Now up to four of at most 16 MiB stay mapped, tagged with their span in 2 MiB pages, and the next uninitialised allocation of that span takes one; zeroed ones get a fresh mapping.
2. **Medium size-class fallback.** Blocks of 64 KiB to 1 MiB come from quarter-octave free lists; an empty list now falls back to the next four classes, at most twice the size, before new memory is carved, so the commitment's freed blocks serve the fold's.
3. **Spare chunks.** Five fresh 2 MiB chunks are mapped early and handed to the medium allocator once faulted in, so the commitment's worker scratch lands on present pages.
4. **Prefault in the matrix phase.** The phase faulting in the witness table's pages also faults in, one 2 MiB piece per task, a block of exactly the commitment rows' size (dropped right after, so the rows take it), the spare chunks, the commitment buffer and the first pages of the three switch planes, one zero byte per 4 KiB.
5. **Two dead stores removed.** At a chunk's first lockstep step the digit accumulators start from the fold bias broadcast from one word, so filling the seven digit streams at the group's start was overwritten before any read; only stream 0 is still filled, and the zero stored back into it after the row writer read it is dropped too.
6. **Sorted fold schedule.** Each term adds its column's bit planes to every slot pair its 128-slot run meets. The plan wrote one offset per term per pair, padded to even length per sign. Now a term gives one entry, plus one of opposite sign when its run wraps past slot 243, counting-sorted by run start, so a pair's entries form one contiguous window.
7. **The fold writes the proof encoding.** When the proof file is mapped and its folded span holds exactly the fold's elements, each task writes its elements straight into the file as one little-endian `i32` per coefficient, so no element buffer is allocated and the final write skips that span; otherwise the old path runs.
8. **Commitment kernel batch by batch.** A quarter used to run all eight batches' lookup stages first, into eight 162-vector blocks (83 KB), then the 48 tails; the sink rows of each block but the last ran in eighths after the next eight tails or lookup stages. Now one batch's lookup stage writes one 162-vector block (10.4 KB) that stays in L1, its six tails read it back at once and stage the quarter's 48 outputs in one 83 KB buffer, and the sink takes the six blocks whole after the last tail. The sink prefetches key lines 6 slots ahead instead of 3.

## Why it is faster

A first write to a fresh anonymous page makes the kernel allocate and clear it, 2 MiB at a time under huge pages. Workers reach their first writes into fresh commitment buffers together, so they stall on page clears at once and the phase ends with the slowest; the matrix phase already faults in page-cache pages, so those faults run there instead. The dead stores cost seven 648-slot fills per group, the sorted schedule replaces ~64 scattered writes per term with two counting passes, and the direct write removes a 5.3 MB buffer and an encode.

In the kernel the lookup stage is memory-bound, not port-bound: its 34 vector operations per row position retire in 17 cycles, but eight batches' 83 KB of output cannot share a 48 KB L1 with the index rows it reads, so each store missed L1. With one block per batch the output stays in L1 until its six tails have read it; the same bytes reach L2 from the tails, whose ~700 vector operations per 27 stored vectors cover their misses. The key prefetch distance was timed on this order: 6 tied the best, 3 was slower.

## Why the proof cannot change

- **Kept and fallback blocks.** Only uninitialised allocations take a kept block, and every such large buffer is filled before it is read: each commitment row's 648 entries are written first. A fallback block counts as reused, so a zeroed request clears it.
- **Prefault writes.** Every touch writes a zero byte. The rows-sized block and spares are fresh mappings receiving only zeros, and the commitment buffer was allocated zeroed. The plane pages are written before any read, and the touched prefix is capped.
- **Removed stores.** Stream 0 is overwritten with its fold bias at each group start before any load, and digit streams are never loaded at a chunk's first step.
- **Schedule.** A run starting at slot `m` meets pair `q` exactly when `2q - 127 <= m <= 2q + 1`, the old range, and its wrapped part is the same window for `m - 243` with the opposite sign. Entries read the same planes as before and the counters are exact integer sums, so order changes nothing; an odd window's extra input reads zero planes as the old padding entry did, and a 63-entry tail plus it adds at most 64 to a six-bit counter holding at most 63.
- **Direct encoding.** The fold writes the same 16-bit sums sign-extended to little-endian `i32` as the encoder did: 648 coefficients of 4 bytes per element, every element of every block, and only when mapped with the layout's folded span equal to that size.
- **Batch order.** Each batch's lookup stage reads its own index rows and writes its own block with the same operations, each of its six tails reading 27 vectors of that block into its own slot. No step reads another batch's data, and every tail follows its own stage, so reordering batches cannot change a transform output.
- **Sink order.** The sink still takes blocks 0 to 23 and their rows 0 to 26 in the old order. The tail writing block `j` of batch `h` and the sink reading it share an offset, and all of a quarter's tails finish before its first sink call, so every row sees the same values. A prefetch reads no value.
- **Same arithmetic.** No reduction, chunk partition, transcript input or field encoding changes; addresses, fault timing and entry order enter no value.

## How validity was checked

- Built with the challenge's own setup script (sandboxed native release build), the benchmark ran three times, five proofs each on fresh seeds, and the trusted verifier accepted all fifteen. They took the mapped-file path, so the witness checked is the one the fold wrote.
- The commitment is compared bit for bit against the reference commitment at both test shapes, and the crate's whole test suite passes, 221 tests with nothing failing.
- The kernel was timed against a block-by-block order of the same tails and rows in paired, alternating rounds with both hyperthreads of each core busy, at two key-stream sizes including the scored one; every round went the same way, and a second core family at one thread agreed.
- All four changed files are under `solution/`, none a symlink or special file, below the size and file-count limits.

## Caveats

- **Memory held.** Up to four kept blocks of at most 16 MiB and five 2 MiB spares stay mapped until reused, at most ~74 MiB.
- **Kernel order.** Its gain depends on the core's L1 size, on how two hyper

author: rdhafiz
body:
The mobile menu stuttered and froze while opening and closing on phones.

**Menu**
- The portal used to grow three full-screen `clip-path` circles. Phones repaint those on the main thread every frame, along with the menu content.
- It now grows three discs with `transform: scale`, each sized to reach the farthest corner from the menu button.
- The links sit on a panel that fades in after the navy disc and fades out before it shrinks.
- Only `transform` and `opacity` animate, so the GPU runs it even while the page is busy. The look stays the same.
- The dock no longer uses a backdrop blur.

**The page never rested**
- The hero slider dots and the steps section rails were filled from a `requestAnimationFrame` loop, which re-rendered the whole page every frame.
- They are now CSS animations, paused while held (hover, focus, pause button, off screen, hidden tab). When one ends, the next slide or step shows.
- The steps section's icon ring spins only on the shown step while the section is on screen, and not at all on phones and low-end devices. The browser can't hand that spin to the GPU.

**Measured** on a simulated phone (390 px, CPU slowed 6×):

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Menu open | ~18 fps | ~57 fps |
| Menu close | ~20 fps (one 1 s freeze) | ~56 fps |
| Idle home page, style recalculations | ~60 a second | 0 |

Checked:
- Slider and steps still advance.
- Hover and the pause button hold them.
- A clicked step stays.
- Focus returns to the menu button on close.
- No console errors.
- 207 tests pass.
