author: avrabe
body:
## Why

The first real `check-tasks` run with cppcheck 2.22.0 failed "C reference has zero F1 findings" on both C tasks. `misra-c2012-8.7` fired on every public function in `rb.c` and `q15.c`. cppcheck only saw the solution file, so each external function looked as if it was used from one translation unit. The hidden tests do call them from another TU.

## What

**The caller TU (owner decision).** Each C task gets a fixed public caller, `tasks/<id>/c/api_use.c`. It calls exactly the functions the header declares and defines only `main`.
- `friction_cppcheck` is the one cppcheck call. F1 friction (what models see), the post-hoc MISRA measure and `check-tasks` all go through it, and it now gets the answer and `api_use.c` together. References and agent answers are therefore judged the same way.
- The MISRA rule set is unchanged, and rule 8.7 stays on.
- The caller is shown at F0 and F1 alike, with a neutral label. A self-test check makes sure F0 names no checker.
- The caller is never in the oracle's directory. The hidden suite is unchanged, and so are its hashes and their claim pins.
- **Drift check** (self-test in CI, and `check-tasks`): the caller calls exactly the header's functions. Probes show it fails on a dropped call, an extra call and a new header function.
- **8.7 negative control** in `check-tasks`: an exported helper outside the header must be reported under 8.7 on its own lines and nowhere else. It goes through `friction()`, the same path the agent sees. The existing "F1 can fail" probe still fails as intended (2 findings).
- **Disclosed limit:** misra.py's 8.7 counts name references. An exported helper with a prototype and one call, or with no prototype and two calls, gets no 8.7, with or without the caller. This was measured, and it is written into the amendment.
- **Pre-registration:** a dated amendment section ("2026-10-29, before any data collection: …"), plus a pointer from the F1 definition.
- **`claims.yaml`:** pins for the amendment sentence, both caller hashes, the cppcheck argv and the negative control.

**`matrix --wait-on-limit` (owner addition).**
- On a usage limit, it sleeps until just after the reset. The reset time comes from `rate_limit_info.resetsAt` (the field name was checked against a live CLI event), else from "resets at …" text, else it waits 30 minutes. One wait is capped at 6 h.
- It then starts a new gated pass. That pass skips the cells that are already ok and re-runs the cell the limit cut off.
- A login failure ("Not logged in", HTTP 401, an invalid or expired token) gives exit 4 and is never retried. A structured rejected limit is checked first, so a limit is never mistaken for a login failure.
- With `FXM_NOTICE` set, it posts one factory notice per wait and one when it finishes or stops.
- The README documents the manual restart after a reboot. There is no launchd job, because of macOS privacy controls on external volumes.
- Self-tests use the stub model and a fake sleep. They cover: limit, then wait, then resume with done cells skipped and the cut-off cell re-run and counted once; a login failure stopping after one call with no wait; reset-time parsing; the wait cap.

## Verified locally (cppcheck 2.22.0, misra.py sha256 at the pin)

- `fxm.py self-test`: exit 0
- `fxm.py self-test --with-tools`: exit 0
- `fxm.py check-tasks`: 0 failed, 2 skipped (exit 3). Both skips are Miri, which is not installed locally. Every C check is ok, including the two that failed before and the new 8.7 control.
- `claim-check.py claims.yaml`: 50/50 claims hold

The full gate (`check-tools`, `self-test --with-tools`, `check-tasks` with 0 skipped) runs on the bench machine after merge.

## Add training to your calendar (MAJOR 39)

Train → **Add to calendar** exports the next planned sessions as an `.ics` file (share sheet where available, download otherwise): start time + reminder pickers, exercises with sets×reps and an estimated length in each event.

author: ajaykr089
body:
## What and why

New package `@editora/paste-cleaner`. Content pasted from office apps arrives with broken structure, not just extra styles:

- **Word** sends lists as flat paragraphs with `mso-list` styles and fake `·` bullets.
- **Google Docs** wraps the whole paste in `<b style="font-weight:normal">`, uses inline styles for bold and italic, places nested lists directly inside the parent list, and routes links through `google.com/url?q=`.
- **Pages and TextEdit** mark headings only by font size, in a `<style>` block.
- **Spreadsheets** send tables full of widths, number formats and stylesheet classes.

TinyMCE (PowerPaste, Professional tier) and CKEditor (enhanced Paste from Office, Productivity Pack) charge for fixing this. The open-source cleaners are small or unmaintained.

**`cleanPaste()`** has no dependencies (about 11.5 kB gzipped) and works in any editor or on a server. It:
- detects the source app,
- reads the clipboard's stylesheet, including class styles and Word's `@list` definitions,
- rebuilds real nested `<ul>`/`<ol>` lists,
- turns inline styles into `strong`/`em`/`u`/`s`/`sup`/`sub`/`code`,
- recovers headings, and turns a bold first table row into a header row,
- unwraps Google redirect links and accepts Word tracked changes,
- turns VS Code copies into one `<pre><code>` block,
- converts plain text that is clearly Markdown into headings, lists, tables and code,
- sanitizes everything against an allow-list,
- reports images it had to drop, such as Word's `file:///` paths.

**Other entry points:**
- `attachPasteCleaner()`, for any contenteditable. It splits the paragraph when blocks are pasted mid-sentence, keeps the browser's native undo, makes Shift+Ctrl/⌘+V paste plain text, and takes an optional image-upload hook.
- `@editora/paste-cleaner/editora` (`PasteCleanerPlugin()`): one undo step per paste, a replacement for `smartPaste`.
- Tiptap and ProseMirror plug in with one line through `transformPastedHTML`.

It starts from `smart-paste`'s sanitizing rules. A demo is in `packages/paste-cleaner/demo` (`node packages/paste-cleaner/demo/server.mjs`), with one-click samples per source.

## How it was checked

- 35 unit tests (vitest + jsdom), with one clipboard sample per source plus an XSS sample. The Pages/TextEdit sample is a real capture (macOS `textutil`). The Word, Word for the web, Google Docs, Sheets, Excel, Chrome and VS Code samples are written to match those apps' documented clipboard markup, because no Office or Google login was available. The README says this.
- The XSS sample caught a real bug while building: with `keepColors` on, a `background:url(javascript:...)` value was kept as a "colour". Only plain colour values pass now.
- Chromium (browser pane), with real `ClipboardEvent('paste')` events carrying each sample:
  - in an Editora editor, each paste was one Undo step and one Redo step,
  - in a plain contenteditable, native undo worked and Chrome's `insertHTML` added no style spans,
  - pasting blocks mid-paragraph split it correctly.
- Repo gates: lint clean, typecheck clean, build OK. The `npm ci` typings step was replayed from a clean `dist` (the PR #86 lesson: `tsconfig.json` emits declarations into `dist`).
- Not tested: Firefox and Safari; real Word and Google Docs clipboards.

## Checklist

- [x] Tests pass (`npm test`, plus the package's own tests) and the build succeeds
- [x] New behaviour has a test, and a bug fix has a test that fails without the fix
- [x] A changeset is added for any published package you changed (`npx changeset`; patch for a fix, minor for a feature). Documentation-only changes do not need one
- [x] Commit messages follow [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/)

Merge note: this PR and #86 both append a package to the root `test:packages` script and touch `package-lock.json`. Whichever merges second needs a trivial rebase. `package-lock.json` also catches up stale workspace version numbers, which npm rewrote when the new workspace was added.

Closes #33.

**New `src/secrets.ts`** — pure, no I/O:
- `maskSecrets(text, config?, env?)` and `maskValue(value, …)` (recursive for objects, arrays, Maps, Sets and `Error` fields).
- Mask format `[label:first3…last2]`; never more than 5 characters of a secret survive, values ≤ 5 chars are fully hidden.
- Patterns: Telegram bot tokens, GitHub (`gh[pousr]_`, `github_pat_`), `sk-` / `sk-ant-` / `gsk_`, AWS `AKIA…`, `Authorization: Bearer` and bare `Bearer`, JWTs, PEM private-key blocks, `https://user:pass@host`, plus **exact values of secret-named env vars** (`TOKEN|SECRET|PASSWORD|PASS|KEY|CREDENTIAL`, value ≥ 8 chars) — that last one is the safety net for provider keys with unknown formats.

author: tristan-stoltz-erc
body:
Closes #8909.

## Why this benchmark

A confidence sequence for one fixed policy does not imply safe winner-selection across 4, 8 or 32 policies. This benchmark separates optional stopping from portfolio multiplicity and measures selection quality only alongside familywise validity.

## Methods

- **Reused pointwise Wald:** diagnostic baseline; not anytime-valid.
- **Independent Hoeffding CS:** alpha=0.05 per policy, time-valid per fixed candidate but not portfolio-corrected.
- **Bonferroni Hoeffding CS:** alpha/M per policy, controlling simultaneous coverage across all policies.
- **Independent empirical-Bernstein CS:** bounded empirical-variance radius with telescoping anytime alpha-spending, alpha=0.05 per policy.
- **Familywise empirical-Bernstein CS:** same variance-adaptive radius with alpha/M per policy.
- **Shared cell-mean Hoeffding CS:** four primitive context/action reward-mean sequences, each allocated alpha/4. For this tabular DGP with known context probabilities, policy values are nonnegative weighted sums of those four means; simultaneous cell coverage therefore covers every candidate without an extra M correction.

The two per-policy CS families use per-tail Hoeffding spending alpha_policy/[2t(t+1)] and running intersections. The empirical-Bernstein sequence allocates total interval error delta_t=alpha_policy/[t(t+1)] and uses the SCOPE-RL bounded empirical-variance radius; its familywise guarantees are gated separately.

A best-policy certificate requires one lower bound to strictly exceed every other candidate’s upper bound. Empty/reversed intervals fail closed.

## Frozen DGP and pairing

Two equally likely contexts, two actions, and reward means:
- context 0: (A=0, A=1) = (0.10, 0.90)
- context 1: (A=0, A=1) = (0.95, 0.15)

There are six portfolios (healthy/weak-support logger × M={4,8,32}). Each policy uses a deterministic stochastic-policy vector; exact true values and policy-specific maximum importance ratios are emitted as 88 POLICY rows. Each logger/replicate seed is shared across portfolio sizes, so action/reward prefixes are identical; all candidate policies receive the same logged sequence.

Healthy logging has h(A=1|x)=(0.50,0.50). Weak-support logging has (0.95,0.05). The benchmark runs 1,024 replicates to horizon 4,096 and reports looks at 256, 1,024 and 4,096.

## Metrics and gates

At each look: familywise point coverage, familywise sequence coverage, probability of any false best-policy certificate by that horizon, certificate rate and conditional median/90th-percentile time, average/max policy interval width, empty-interval rate, IPS-argmax top-1 accuracy and simple regret.

The exact-head workflow checks 1,008 full metric rows (672 smoke metric rows), 6 portfolios and 88 explicit policy definitions; deterministic statistical replay excludes wall-clock rows. It verifies per-policy importance scores remain within their computed W_j, and gates sequence-coverage Wilson lower bounds above 0.90 and false-certificate Wilson upper bounds below 0.10 for the Bonferroni Hoeffding, familywise empirical-Bernstein, and shared-cell methods. It records source/output/summary/seed SHA-256 receipts.

These are synthetic regression checks—not proofs beyond the stated confidence sequence/union-bound construction and assumptions, and not SOTA evidence. The objective is a validity–regret–decision-time frontier. The shared-cell result is specific to this finite tabular setting; unknown context distributions or learned reward models require additional uncertainty accounting.

- Adds `backupFile`, which copies the existing file to `~/.harness/<prefix>-backup-<timestamp>` with mode 0600. It skips missing or blank files and never overwrites an earlier backup.
- `configure` aborts before writing if the backup fails, and prints the backup path.
- Backup location matches hc, not `.npmrc.bak` beside the file, so old tokens don't end up in a project directory.

Not included: restoring from a backup.

author: highskore
body:
## Summary

On phones the UPGRADES sheet had no height limit: it was anchored above the bottom bar and grew upward. With 15+ cards (ascend unlocked) on a short screen, the top rows ran past the top of the game card. The card has `overflow: hidden`, so they were cut off under the links bar, and the sheet couldn't scroll. Now the sheet stops 10px below the top of the game card and scrolls inside itself.

## Changes

All changes are in `page.html`, inside the `max-width: 760px` block, so desktop is untouched.

- `.shop` (phone): `max-height: calc(100% - 60px)`, `overflow-y: auto`, `-webkit-overflow-scrolling: touch`, `overscroll-behavior: contain`, `touch-action: pan-y`, `align-content: start`. It also gets a 4px padding, and the same 4px comes back off `bottom` and `width`. The cards stay exactly where they were, and the focus rings stay inside the scroll box.
- `.menu-body`, `.asc-body` (phone): the same scroll containment (`overflow-y: auto`, `overscroll-behavior: contain`, `touch-action: pan-y`). The ascend box used to clip any overflow instead of scrolling.
- `.menu` overlay (phone): padding is now `max(16px, env(safe-area-inset-*))`, so the achievements, characters, ki tree, angels and ascend cards keep clear of the notch and home indicator.

## Testing

Headless Chromium (`isMobile`, touch) and WebKit, at 390x844 and 375x667, with `#mui#kaio#galick` (15 cards plus the goal):

- **Before, 375x667:** the sheet's top was at y=16 (Chromium) or y=25 (WebKit), but the game card starts at y=40. The goal bar was clipped under the links bar, and `scrollHeight == clientHeight`, so it couldn't scroll.
- **After, 375x667:** the sheet starts at y=50 and the first card at y=54. The sheet scrolls by 38px (Chromium) or 29px (WebKit) to show the last card (God Ki) fully above the bottom bar. A touch scroll gesture in Chromium (CDP `synthesizeScrollGesture`) and a wheel gesture in WebKit both scroll the sheet. The page doesn't scroll (`scrollY` stays 0) and doesn't zoom (`visualViewport.scale` stays 1).
- **390x844:** the sheet fits, and the cards sit at the same pixels as before.
- **Menu, characters, ki tree, angels and ascend at both sizes:** the cards are in the same places as before. The scrolling bodies now report `overscroll-behavior: contain` and `touch-action: pan-y`.

## Notes

- The bottom bar (sound / upgrades / share) is still at `bottom: 12px`, with no safe-area offset. I didn't move it here. The sheet tracks the bar, so it can never sit under it.
- WebKit on macOS has no touch input, so the WebKit check uses a wheel gesture. The touch-drag check ran in Chromium.
- Pixel baselines: none changed. CI's visual job passes against the existing desktop and phone baselines. The phone `shop` state (`#form4#kaio`) has few enough cards to fit, and the cards sit at the same pixels, so no baseline update was needed.

body:
## La règle

`GET /evaluations`, la liste générale des évaluations de l'établissement (brouillons et questions compris), est **réservée au personnel reconnu**. `ListEvaluationsRequest::authorize()` vaut `isStaff()` : la liste est fermée par défaut.

C'est la règle sœur de #941 (portée fermée par défaut). Le prédicat est `isStaff()`, en correspondance exacte, et non le middleware `role:`, qui ignore la casse (#949). Une variante de casse d'un rôle à privilège n'ouvre donc pas la liste.

## Ce qui ne change pas

- Les consommateurs de cette liste sont des écrans du personnel : le calendrier côté enseignant, coordinateur et admin, les évaluations de l'enseignant, les résultats de l'admin et les évaluations du coordinateur.
- L'élève a sa propre route, `/evaluations/student`, inchangée. Le calendrier de l'élève passe par elle.
- Le détail d'une évaluation (`GET /evaluations/{id}`) n'est pas modifié ici.

## Ce qui change

| Fichier | Changement |
|---|---|
| `app/Http/Requests/ListEvaluationsRequest.php` | `authorize()` : `isStaff()` au lieu de `true`, avec sa docblock |
| `app/Services/Evaluation/EvaluationListService.php` | le commentaire qui disait la route « sans garde de rôle » ; aucune logique |
| `tests/Feature/Evaluation/EvaluationListStaffOnlyTest.php` | nouveau |
| `tests/Feature/Evaluation/Student/CorrigesEtCopiesExposesTest.php` | la propriété « la liste ne recopie aucune copie, `submissions_count` conservé » est rejouée par un ENSEIGNANT, vrai jeton ; nouveau test de refus pour l'élève |

## Tests

Vrai jeton porteur, deux volets (école reliée à KLASSCI, école autonome).

- **Refus hors personnel**, pour `etudiant`, `Etudiant`, `eleve`, `SuperAdmin`, `Supradmin`, `ADMIN`, `Enseignant` et `''` : 403, avec un corps qui porte EXACTEMENT `{success, message}`, sans donnée ni titre. Rôle NULL : impossible en base (`users.role` est NOT NULL, avec le défaut `student`) ; `''` en est l'équivalent admis.
- **Personnel** (`enseignant`, `coordinateur`, `admin`, `superAdmin`) : la liste reste servie, brouillons compris.
- **ROUGE sans le correctif** : 17 échecs, tous attendus (16 cas de refus et le refus de l'élève).
- **Falsification** : avec `with('submissions')` réintroduit dans la liste, le test rejoué par l'enseignant rougit.

## Preuves

- Tests ciblés : Evaluation OK (104), Requests OK (401), Architecture OK (7) ; puis Security (172) et Docs (9) à 0 échec.
- PHPStan ciblé : No errors. Baseline 288/443. Gardes de taille et de longueur de méthode : 0 violation ; OCP : 0 violation neuve.
- **PHPStan complet non exécuté en local** (mémoire) ; le run ciblé est vert. La CI tranche.

## Limites connues

- Les alias `teacher` et `student` et le supradmin ne sont pas couverts par des cas dédiés.

author: linusnorton
body:
Fixes the `trap: line 2: unexpected EOF while looking for matching ')'` failure that has taken out roughly one build in two in this repo, on a different case each time — `claude-md-missing`, `azure-restored`, `atlassian-fails`, `hai-installed-off-path`, `claude-md-error`.

## It was never the handler

`trap:` is bash's label for re-parsing a signal handler's string, and the line number is **handler-relative** — a one-line handler reports `line 2`, a two-line handler `line 3`. The handler is `trap shutdown TERM INT`: one line, nothing interpolated, unchanged since the file was added.

Up to and including **bash 5.2**, the parse of a `$( … )` or `<( … )` body is not reentrant. When a signal lands inside one, `run_pending_traps` parses the handler with the enclosing `(` still open, so the handler hits EOF and **never runs** — the signal is lost outright. Whole reproducer:

```bash
h() { echo HANDLED; exit 0; }
trap h TERM
while :; do read -r a b < <(echo 1 2); done
```

Measured on an isolated hammer, 300 runs per arm: bash 5.2.37 loses **7**, bash 5.3.20 loses **0**. Handler content is provably irrelevant — `trap 'exit 0'` loses 5/300, a function 12/300, a multi-statement handler 1/300. Loss rate by construct: `read < <(awk …)` 12/300, `printf "$(…)"` 4, `: "$(…)"` 2, `x=$(…)` 2, backquotes 0.

Why it looked load-sensitive: the window is the few microseconds of that re-parse, so what matters is the fraction of each loop pass spent expanding substitutions. The suite fakes `sleep` to 0.05s, compressing the 5s poll cadence about a hundredfold.

## The change

Since no handler is safe, the only fix is for the loop that waits for SIGTERM to stop expanding substitutions on every pass. One file, in the repos-progress and reporting block:

- `write_repos_state` — `printf … "$(date -u …)"` becomes a `{ printf …; date -u …; }` group redirected to the temp file.
- `fallback_count` — `read … < <(awk …)`, the worst construct measured, becomes awk to a file then `read` from it.
- `report_running` — `detail=$(repos_detail)` becomes a variable set by `set_repos_detail` (one caller), and `at=$(date +%s)` becomes `$SECONDS`, with `reported_at` initialised to `-REPORT_EVERY` so the first report is still never rate-limited.
- `repos_verb` becomes `set_repos_verb` setting a variable (two callers).
- `poll_repos` — `repos_finished "$(cat "$REPOS_RC")"` becomes `read -r rc`.

Substitutions that run once per session or per logged state change are left alone; removing those would need bash ≥4.2 `printf '%(…)T'` and the suite must run under bash 3.2. **The `gateway` route arm is untouched, so there is no overlap with #155.**

## Evidence, since a green run proves nothing about an intermittent failure

Interleaved before/after hammers under identical conditions, same machine, baseline byte-identical to `git show HEAD:…/entrypoint.sh`:

| arm | runs | lost SIGTERM |
|---|---|---|
| master | 7200 | **15** |
| fixed | 7200 | 0 |
| master | 7200 | **17** |
| fixed | 7200 | 0 |
| fixed (final file) | 7200 | 0 |

Plus 6048 case-runs across every case post-fix with no trap-signature failure, and 3024 pre-fix case-runs reproducing it three times.

**No regression test, deliberately.** The window is microseconds wide and cannot be widened — a 400k-token substitution did not help, because time in the child is not time in the parse. A 7200-run hammer does not belong in CI and a static "this loop contains no `$(`" assertion would be brittle, so the invariant is stated in a comment at the trap.

## Why it matters beyond CI

In the suite a lost signal is a case failing on teardown. In a pod it is the kubelet reaching the termination grace period and SIGKILLing the container with Claude, the bridges and the clone step all still running.

## Gates

`yarn typecheck`, `yarn test` (4380 + 1375), `yarn biome check src test packages` (669 files) and `bash -n` on the entrypoint, all exit 0 with codes read directly. `yarn test:integration` not run — no TypeScript changed, and three other sessions are using the shared Postgres.

## Two unrelated harness races found, not touched

Both reproduce on master as well and neither carries the trap signature: `entrypoint.test.sh:898` greps for a line without a `wait_for`, and `:414` reads `hai.env.1` after waiting only for `hai.argv.1`, which the fake hai writes three processes earlier.

Fix TypeError and token leakage risk when redact_stderr receives None

Utilities like redact_stderr must handle None inputs gracefully (e.g. using `stderr or ''`) because subprocess.run might fail before standard error is returned, yielding None for result.stderr. Failing to handle None causes TypeErrors that crash the script and undermine defensive logging.

author: mick340
body:
Four ledger and invoice gaps (G20 to G23). Every change is additive: configs that set none of the new options behave as before, except that purging an organization with a ledger now works instead of failing.

## Data lifecycle: purge an organization with a ledger (G20)

The ledger's `ledger_append_only` trigger refused every delete, so `purge_organization` failed with `LEDGER_APPEND_ONLY` for any organization with one ledger transaction (invoices, leave, inventory and credits all post there).

- `purge_organization` sets the transaction-local `better_supabase.purge_tenant` to the tenant's id around its deletes and clears it afterwards.
- With data-lifecycle installed (the ledger now lists it in `integrates`), the guard lets a row through only when the operation is a `DELETE`, the setting names the row's tenant (the trigger takes the tenant column as an argument), the caller is the service role, and the tenant has a due deletion that is neither cancelled nor purged. Everything else, including any `UPDATE`, still fails with `LEDGER_APPEND_ONLY`.
- Tests: an integration test that purges a tenant with a ledger and keeps another tenant's rows, and a pgTAP file (`ledger_purge.test.sql`) for the denials: the setting without a due deletion, an update during a purge, another tenant's rows, and a non-service caller.

## Subjects: the configured tenant column (G21)

`withBlockSubjects` named the tenant column `tenant_id` even when `database.sql.tenantColumn` renamed it on the block tables, so `open_conversation` and `can_subject` failed on first use once the ledger (or any block with a subject) was installed. Block subjects now name the column the way the SQL context does: a `columns.<table>.tenant` mapping first, then `sql.tenantColumn`. The fix covers every block subject, not only `ledger_account`.

## Invoices: payments after a write-off (G22)

`options.paymentsAfterWriteOff: true` lets `record_invoice_payment` book a payment on an `uncollectible` invoice, such as a provider payment that arrives after the write-off. The invoice stays `uncollectible` while a balance is left and moves to `paid` once nothing is owed, which records `invoice.paid`. The write-off posts nothing to the ledger, so there is nothing to reverse, and the write-off reason stays. The default still refuses the payment with `INVOICE_NOT_PAYABLE`, and the rendered SQL is unchanged.

## Actors on payment reads (G23)

- Invoices: `payments(invoiceId)` calls the new `list_invoice_payments(invoice)`. It is `security definer`, checks the read key, returns `INVOICE_NOT_FOUND` to a caller who can't read the invoice, and is revoked from `anon`.
- Ledger: `entries(accountId)` returns the transaction's `actorId` on each `LedgerAccountEntry`.

## Checks

`pnpm verify`, `pnpm supabase:test` and `pnpm test:integration` pass locally. The migration is `20261029110518_ledger_invoice_gaps.sql`, and a second `supabase:diff` reports no changes.

author: kassemshdy
body:
**Why Google indexes almost nothing.** The pages are rendered in the browser from `/api/...`, and `robots.txt` said `Disallow: /api/`. Googlebot obeys robots.txt when it renders, so every page it rendered was empty: the served HTML for `/products` has **0 characters** of body text, only the head, which the server fills in.

**Changes**
- `robots.txt`: `Disallow: /api/` is replaced by the private API only: `/api/admin`, `/api/my`, `/api/me`, `/api/auth`. `/dashboard`, `/admin`, `/login`, `/cart` and `/favourites` stay closed.
- **Views stay honest.** Once crawlers can render the API, their fetch of a shop, product or profile would have counted as a view. `ViewCounterService.record(..., crawler=...)` now skips crawlers and link-preview fetchers (Googlebot, facebookexternalhit, WhatsApp, Twitterbot, TelegramBot, …). The check reads the user agent through a `Crawler` dependency and never stores it. The counter table is unchanged, and `test_the_counter_table_stores_nothing_about_a_visitor` still passes.

**Tests**
- `test_a_crawler_or_link_preview_is_not_counted`, parametrized over 5 agents.
- `test_robots_disallows_private_areas` now also asserts the public API is open and the private API closed.
- `test_views.py`, `test_search.py` and `test_i18n.py`: 74 passed. ruff and mypy are clean.

**Follow-up:** issue #258, putting the listing text into the served HTML so crawlers that don't render still see content.

Separately, Search Console reports "Blocked due to access forbidden (403)". That's Cloudflare's challenge, not this code. The site now answers a challenge (`cf-mitigated: challenge`) to every page load; verified bots must be exempted there.

author: joshp123
body:
Rewrites the text of the video skill (SKILL.md, the six role files, the seven tool files) so that a frontier model given a new recording can make the cut without working out the rig, the pipeline or Josh's intent for itself. No code changed; `pipeline/`, `private/` and `looks/` are untouched.

## Why

The last run (codex-switch, run 4) took 673 tool calls, 1.3 million output tokens, 34 builds and three judge rounds for one short. The role files were procedures: do this, run that, check this number, repeat at every edge. That turned the model into a slow interpreter of a hand-written loop. The tool files listed steps without explaining the mechanism. Several rules carried one recording's numbers, and the gate and fix loop were written in four or five places with small differences. Josh's steering on how these skills must be written: goal-driven, specific, high detail, roles explained, bitter-lesson-pilled, ZFC (code does mechanical steps, models judge).

## What changed

- **SKILL.md:** ten invariants at the top. The mission and what a good demo video is. What is Josh's and what is the crew's. The roles and why they run in this order: professional hand-overs, a fresh context per role, cheap work before lock and expensive work after. The two timelines and tidy rules. The edit list and its primitives. The loop, written once. The Resolve changelog check now runs at the end of a video, only when Resolve's version is newer than the one recorded in tools/resolve.md.
- **Roles** are briefs to a top professional: the role's outcome and how it serves the video, the raw material, the craft as opinion with its reason (weak and strong pairs where a distinction is easier to show), the tools explained by how they work, what proves the work right, and the hand-over. Per-edge loops, numbers from one recording stated as rules, and stories of past runs are gone. The editor file now says to decide the whole cut, measure in batches, place once and gate once.
- **Tools** are mechanism documents:
  - faults.md explains how the gate measures, what it cannot see, and how to run it. The commands now include `--subtitles` and `--video-folder`.
  - resolve.md covers what scripting reaches, what only the timeline file reaches, and why. It adds the verified API calls `CreateMagicMask`, `PerformMulticamSmartSwitch`, `CreateSubtitlesFromAudio` and `ApplyFairlightPresetToCurrentTimeline`, each with its limits; untested ones are marked as leads.
  - remotion.md describes what `render-graphics.mjs` actually reads (`graphics/spec.json`, field by field), replacing the stale claim about the old format.
  - checking.md shows how to take frames straight from the camera files.
  - transcription.md no longer names a path on Josh's drive.
- **"Nobody can hear"** is written as a gap, with the test a listening model would have to pass, not as a law.
- **history.md:** only its citations of renamed headings were updated.
- **After Astra's cold review:**
  - **Changes made in Resolve.** The skill no longer claims that the timeline reads back into the list. `readback.py` prints what the timeline holds in its own terms. SKILL.md now states the real path: which readback fields become which list rows, and what cannot be recovered (a CDL, hand work on a colour group, the Dialogue Leveler). It also says what `finish.py` and `place.py` will undo if the translation is skipped.
  - **The gate finds; the model decides.** A measured row is fixed at its source by default, or overridden in writing with its frame, evidence and reason. Every override reaches the cold judge and the director, who may reinstate it. A fault the gate missed is fixed now, and the instrument's gap is logged for the end of the video. faults.md now states beside each number what it rests on, including where that is only one or two judged cuts.
  - **The closing card.** The where-was-i treatment is now an example of a choice Josh made for that video, not a rule.
  - **The examples.** examples/README.md says the pairs are private and live only on Josh's Mac.

## My reading, not Josh's words

The split of the edit list between roles is my reading of the role files, not something Josh said: the editor owns `segments`, `audio`, `sound`, `captions` and graphic timing; the colourist owns each camera's grade and group; the motion designer owns how titles and panels look. So is `graphics/spec.json` as the home of the terminal graphics' timing.

## Mechanical work the model still does by hand

- `frame.py` returns one frame per call and holds the Resolve lock while it works.
- `envelope.py` measures one span per call, and its output is every 5 ms step. One call that reports quiet and onset for every join would remove most per-edge turns.
- `readback.py` does not produce the list. Bringing a change made in Resolve into the list is a manual translation (SKILL.md, "A change made in Resolve comes back into the list by hand").
- `align.py` is not wired into `captions.py` or `qc.py`, so caption word times are carried across by hand, and the gate still writes "look" rows for highlights inside connected speech.

## Code findings, not fixed here

- `skill/scripts/devenv.nix` hard-codes `HF_HOME` to Josh's SSD, and `verbatim_transcript.py` hard-codes its vendor path there.
- `qc.py`'s top-controls check uses its own 200 px constant rather than the look's `fusion.safeArea.top`. Same value today.
- `captions.py` assumes Futura Bold for caption width, and `qc_vision.swift` assumes white letters on an orange pill to recognise captions. Both need a stated boundary when the look changes.
- `remove_range.py` and `replace_media.py` were tested only on plain clips, never on a cut timeline holding the multicam and the one-track dialogue.

author: ankit1324
body:
- Fixes #3001

With terrain enabled, fill, line, raster, background, hillshade and color-relief layers are drawn into cached per-tile textures by `RenderToTexture`. `setPaintProperty` fires a style data event, and `Map._handleTerrainDataEvent` releases all textures. That happens in the first frame of the transition, where the layer still evaluates to the old value. On the following frames the RTT fingerprint (source tiles, source revision, zoom, visible layers) does not change, so `renderLayer` keeps reusing those textures. The map shows the old value until something else invalidates the tiles, such as a zoom or a source reload. With `transition: {duration: 0}` it already works.

`RenderToTexture.prepareForRender` now re-renders, on every terrain tile, the render stacks that contain a layer whose paint is transitioning. It does this on each frame of the transition and once more on the frame after it. The extra frame is needed because `TransitioningPropertyValue.possiblyEvaluate` clears `prior` in the frame that first evaluates the final value (`src/style/properties.ts:309-311`), so `hasTransition()` is already false there; the previous frame's set of transitioning layer ids covers it. Only the affected stacks are released, through the per-stack release from #8782.

The same applies to paint values that transition after `setGlobalStateProperty` (a paint property reading `global-state`) and after `setStyle(..., {diff: true})`, since both go through `StyleLayer.setPaintProperty`. I checked both with a map test: on main the drawn opacity stays at 1, with this change the last frame draws 0.25. I did not add those as tests.

Behaviour change for throttling: a tile keeps one fingerprint per source for all its stacks, and re-rendering a stack overwrites the fingerprints of the sources it draws. So if another stack draws one of those sources and its texture is stale for that source (for example kept at the old zoom while the map moves, or waiting for its turn in the one-stale-tile-per-frame budget), it is released together with the transitioning stack. Otherwise it would be marked up to date and keep the stale content. During a transition such stacks therefore skip both the per-frame budget and the keep-while-moving rule. Stacks that are stale only for other sources keep their textures and their throttling. Outside transitions nothing changes apart from one `hasTransition()` call per draped layer per frame.

Tests:
- `map_terrain.test.ts`: transitions `fill-opacity` from 1 to 0.25 on a map with terrain and records the value each terrain-tile render uses. On main the only values drawn are `[1, 1, 1, 1]` and the test fails with `expected 1 to be 0.25`. With the fix the last render uses exactly 0.25.
- `render_to_texture.test.ts`, four new tests that all fail on main: the transitioning stack is re-rendered during the transition and on the frame after it while the other stack keeps its texture; a stale stack sharing the source is re-rendered with it while the map moves; a stale stack on another source keeps its texture while the map moves; a stack that shares the source but is stale only for another source keeps its texture.
- Render test `terrain/fill-set-paint-property`: `setPaintProperty` changes a draped fill from blue to red with the default 300 ms transition.
- `npm run test-unit`: 3826/3826. `npm run lint`, `npm run typecheck` and `npm run build-dev && npm run build-css` pass. Terrain render tests: 85/85. Run on Node 22.23.2, because the Node version in `.nvmrc` was not available locally.

Open question: this re-renders the affected stacks on every terrain tile on each frame of a transition (300 ms by default). The cheaper alternative is to re-render once, when the transition ends: the final value still shows, but on terrain the change jumps instead of fading. I went with the smooth version and can switch if you prefer the other.

author: cursor[bot]
body: ## Bug and impact Two concurrent `DELETE /sheets/{id}` calls on a drawing with exactly two sheets could both pass the "keep at least one sheet" check and each delete one sheet, leaving the drawing with **zero sheets** (total content loss; release/BoM then operate on an empty husk). ## Root cause `delete_sheet` loaded the drawing without `SELECT … FOR UPDATE` and trusted `len(drawing.sheets)` from that unlocked snapshot. Under READ COMMITTED, both writers could observe two sheets, both pass the gate, and both commit. ## Fix - Lock the parent drawing with `_lock_drawing_for_update` before the count check. - Expire and re-read `drawing.sheets` after the lock so a sibling delete that committed while waiting is visible; 404 if this sheet is already gone, 409 if it would be the last sheet. ## Validation - Reproduced the unlocked race with two SQLAlchemy sessions: both passed `len == 2`, both committed → final sheet count `0`. - Confirmed lock + expire + recount leaves one sheet and refuses the second delete. - `pytest tests/test_drawings.py` — 6 passed, including `test_delete_sheet_rechecks_count_after_drawing_lock`.

The `agreement` relation reported only the first place webpack's tree differs from the reference (css-tree, parse5, `@rgrove/parse-xml`). In a source whose first difference is an `EXPECTED` reference gap, nothing after it was ever checked.

The trees are now aligned with Myers' diff (the algorithm behind `git diff`), and each run of differing events is its own finding. A node one side lacks costs one difference, not one per node after it. The parse table's column shows the first difference and how many more follow.

`RELATION=agreement node tooling/compare-<lang>-tools.js --invariants --require-corpus`, over the installed corpora:

| this PR | 0 findings (12 `EXPECTED` matched) | 0 findings (3 matched) | 0 findings |

None of the differences that became visible is a webpack bug:

- **The css-tree reader had a gap of its own.** When a nested block opens with a rule, it read the rest of the block as rules, so in `.baz-1 {…} max-inline-size: 1024px; .baz-2 {…}` the declaration ran into the next selector. It now reads on from such a rule, recognized by a `;` in its selector.

  - parse5 8 has no declarative shadow roots; with aligned trees, the `<a>` it places differently shows as one removal and one insertion.

author: mkrueger
body: Improves what users see during long-running ingestion and documents expectations and limitations for customers. ## Progress reporting `import` previously only printed a final summary, and `bulk` printed progress only when an operation completed, so it went silent during slow writes or SDK retry waits. Both now share an `IngestionProgress` heartbeat that reports about every two seconds: - **import:** items processed, imported/failed, elapsed seconds, items/s, observed write RU charge. Dry runs report offline validation counts instead. Because input is streamed without a counting pass, there is no total, percentage, or ETA. - **bulk:** processed/total operations, succeeded/failed, elapsed seconds, operations/s, observed RU charge. Progress starts after validation, confirmation, and journal verification. Progress is human-readable output only. Quiet mode, structured output (`json`/`csv`), redirected stdout, and MCP calls emit nothing extra, and final result shapes are unchanged. Reporting failures never abandon in-flight writes. ## Sizing guidance and measurements New [docs/ingestion.md](docs/ingestion.md) covers pilot sizing, how to read progress, limits (2 MB per item, stateful bulk caps, temporary spool disk, no rollback, retry safety), and local emulator measurements. The opt-in `IngestionBenchmarkTests` (skipped unless `COSMOSDB_SHELL_INGESTION_BENCHMARK_CSV` is set) ran the full matrix of import and bulk create with 1K/10K/100K 1 KiB items at concurrency 1/16/32. All 18 cases verified their final container counts (666,000 writes). Concurrency 16 was about 3x faster than 1; 32 showed no consistent gain: | Items | Import (c=16) | Bulk (c=16) | |---:|---:|---:| | 1,000 | 5.2 s | 5.3 s | | 10,000 | 51.8 s | 51.7 s | | 100,000 | 8.6 min | 8.7 min | These are local emulator command-path numbers, **not** Azure throughput promises. **Azure (real account, West Europe):** the opt-in `AzureIngestionBenchmarkTests` (`LiveAzure` category, skipped unless configured) ran the same matrix against a single-region provisioned account. It used Entra ID (Azure CLI identity), Direct mode, and one `/pk` container at 4,000 RU/s manual. All 18 cases verified their item counts (666,000 writes), with no 429s (peak normalized RU 83%): | Items | Concurrency | Import | Bulk create | Rate (items/s) | RU charge | |---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | 1,000 | 1 | 24.99 s | 23.54 s | 40–43 | 7,000 | | 1,000 | 16 | 6.55 s | 3.21 s | 153–312 | 7,000 | | 1,000 | 32 | 4.00 s | 3.59 s | 250–278 | 7,000 | | 10,000 | 1 | 224.03 s (3.7 min) | 225.47 s (3.8 min) | 44–45 | 70,000 | | 10,000 | 16 | 27.17 s | 25.65 s | 368–390 | 70,000 | | 10,000 | 32 | 26.44 s | 25.43 s | 378–393 | 70,000 | | 100,000 | 1 | 2,189.28 s (36.5 min) | 2,209.65 s (36.8 min) | 45–46 | 700,000 | | 100,000 | 16 | 256.65 s (4.3 min) | 255.23 s (4.3 min) | 390–392 | 700,000 | | 100,000 | 32 | 256.22 s (4.3 min) | 255.95 s (4.3 min) | 390–391 | 700,000 | RU charge is for import; bulk adds 2 RU per case for reading target metadata. All times are single measured runs on 2026-10-29, client in Europe (~55–60 ms HTTPS round trip to the account). Each 1 KiB insert cost 7.0 RU. Sequential ingestion is latency-bound at about 45 items/s; concurrency 16 reaches about 390 items/s (about 1.4M items/hour), and 32 adds nothing. That plateau (~2,730 RU/s) is below the provisioned 4,000 RU/s, so raising RU/s alone isn't guaranteed to help. Details and reproduction steps are in [docs/ingestion.md](docs/ingestion.md#azure-measurements-west-europe). ## Local emulator timeout Commands connected to a localhost emulator were canceled after 10 seconds in total, even while making progress. That broke long imports, `rm *`, exports, queries, and piped scripts, and disconnected the shell. The limit is now an **inactivity** timeout: - Every emulator response restarts it (via a custom `RequestHandler`). Completed import/bulk writes and locally validated bulk operations also restart it. Request timeouts and 503s do not count, because the SDK synthesizes them when the emulator doesn't answer. - It is paused during confirmation prompts and the sproc/trigger/udf editors, which used to abort after 10 seconds of user input. - A stalled or unreachable emulator still times out and disconnects. ## `rm` progress and in-place progress line Pattern-based and piped `rm` now report items scanned and deleted. In a terminal, progress for `import`, `bulk`, and `rm` is redrawn on a single line (truncated to the console width), cleared before mid-run warnings, and erased when the command finishes. Progress appears only when stdout is a terminal; pipes and OS or shell redirection suppress it. ## Validation - `dotnet build` for the shell and test projects: 0 warnings, 0 errors - Offline suite (`Category!=Emulator`): 4,927 passed - Emulator suite: all new tests pass; 2 existing failures (`Info_Container_FormatTable_RedirectsGrid`, `Sproc_Exec_WithoutResponseBody_ReturnsNull`) also fail on unmodified `main` - End to end against the emulator with the default limit: 3,000-item import (23.9 s), 1,000-pair piped script (22.5 s), and `rm *` on 3,000 items (48.5 s) all complete; previously each stopped at about 10 s - `l10n/CosmosDBShell.json` regenerated with the new and changed strings Example:

author: aymen2518
body:
## Summary
`cloudRun.auth: googleToken` makes a Cloud Run agent reachable from outside the VPC while keeping two checks:

1. **Cloud Run IAM (unchanged guarantee):** the invoker check stays on and `allUsers` / `allAuthenticatedUsers` are still rejected. Callers send their ID token in `X-Serverless-Authorization`.
2. **The container:** it verifies the Google token in `cloudRun.googleToken.header` (default `x-google-token`) against `allowedPrincipals` / `audiences`, injected as `AGENTLESS_*` env vars. `agent.environment` and `agent.secrets` can't set those names.

- `invoke` and agent card reads send both headers, and a custom `rebuild_auth` drops them on a cross-host redirect (requests only strips `Authorization`). `invoke --app-token` overrides the app token.
- Validation: exclusive with `iap` and `ingress: internal`; reserved and hop-by-hop headers rejected; principals lowercased; no commas in principals or audiences.
- `plan` states both layers and warns when there are no invokers, when the impersonated deployer isn't an allowed principal, and when Gemini Enterprise is set.
- README: config and a FastAPI middleware (hd claim for `domain:`, cached certs, verification off the event loop, agent card exempt), tested locally against stubbed tokens.
- `auth: iam` is unchanged: no spec diff for existing services.

An independent review found no path to an anonymous service; its findings (redirect leak, env/secret override, header validation, middleware fixes) are addressed here.

**Not verified live:** that Cloud Run forwards `x-google-token` unchanged (Google's front end strips some `X-Google-*` headers on other products). The README says to check with a header-echo service.

Release **0.9.0**.

body:
## What

Story: [`BITB-251`](docs/BACKLOG_STORIES/BITB-251-emergency-critical-path-hotlines.md). This PR also adds the BITB-252 spec and the follow-up stories BITB-253 and BITB-254.

**Emergency critical path.** A message that threatens self-harm or someone else now gets a crisis card with local emergency and crisis-line numbers. The card is the **first stream event**, sent before retrieval or the LLM runs, so the numbers never depend on the model.

**What triggers the card**
- All three trigger cases: help-seeking self-harm (allowed, with a compassionate LLM reply), blocked self-harm, and blocked violence or threat. Before this change, a threat against someone else got no contacts at all.
- Excluded: `directed_harm` (abuse aimed at the bot), hate, sexual and generic blocks.

**Country selection**
- Precedence: an override the user picked on the card, then Cloudflare `CF-IPCountry`, then the locale region, then a per-language default, then international only.
- `XX` and `T1` are ignored.
- A country with no registry entry gets international help plus a "call your local emergency number / 112" hint. It never shows another country's numbers.

**Hotline registry**
- Self-curated, in `api/utils/crisis_resources.json`: 22 countries with crisis lines, plus emergency-only entries for EG, SA, AE, LB, MA and JO.
- Every entry must have a `source_url` on an official (non-aggregator) host, plus `verified_on` and `verified_by`. A test enforces this.
- Where the police number differs, threat cases dial it (e.g. DE 110, BR 190).

**Cards on web and Android**
- `tel:` and `sms:` links. Android uses `ACTION_DIAL` / `ACTION_SENDTO` only, so no call permission is needed.
- RTL support, `role=alert` / a live region, and 44px / 48dp tap targets.
- A "Not in {country}?" picker. Picking a country re-renders the card in place via `POST /api/v1/crisis-resources`. It is a POST so the picked country never lands in URLs or App Insights telemetry.
- The card is saved with the conversation, on the device only.

**Old clients.** Requests that don't send `supports_crisis_card` get the numbers as deterministic markdown, on blocked replies and appended after the LLM text. The compassionate addendum is capability-aware and never asks the LLM to write numbers.

**Content filter.** When a message contains crisis wording, the route-level profanity and repeated-characters filter no longer returns 400. The URL and spam checks still re-run and still block.

**Android history.** Room goes from v1 to v2 with an explicit `MIGRATION_1_2` that adds a nullable `crisisJson` column, so the app's destructive fallback doesn't wipe saved chats.

**Ops**
- A weekly `crisis-resources-staleness.yml` workflow fails on any entry that is unverified, older than 180 days, or has a dead source URL. It is not a PR gate.
- `docs/HOW-TO-VERIFY-CRISIS-RESOURCES.md`.
- The Cloudflare IP Geolocation step in `deployment/README.md`.
- A privacy-policy line in all 11 languages.

## Test plan

- [x] **Tests added or updated** for the changed behaviour:
  - **Backend:** ~700 new tests across the registry, country resolution (×11 languages), chat path, routes and lookup endpoint. They cover:
    - stream first-event ordering;
    - all 5 blocking return paths;
    - the card surviving search, intent and LLM failures;
    - the old-client fallback (×11);
    - the profanity / URL bypass;
    - Bible narrative phrasing through the real keyword fallback (×11).
  - **Web:** Vitest for the card, the picker refresh, history round-trip, RTL and accessibility.
  - **Android:** JVM parser and mapper tests, a v1→v2 migration test, ViewModel tests and `CrisisResourcesCardComposeTest`.
- [x] `cd api && python -m pytest tests/ -q`: 10178 passed, 8 failed locally. The same 8 fail on the base commit and are sandbox or network related: `test_security` 422 ×4, `test_translations` URL ×2, `test_client_errors` oversized, and `test_db_backup_restore_script`. They pass in CI.
- [x] ruff, black and mypy are clean in CI.
- [x] `cd frontend`: vitest 1556 passed, lint has 0 errors, and tsc and build pass.
- [x] **Android, verified in this PR's CI** (the sandbox couldn't resolve AGP 9.0.1): Kotlin compile, unit tests, Compose UI tests, instrumented UI tests, API 24/25 compatibility, lint and artifact build all pass.
- [x] Three independent verify passes; the last one PASSED with nothing blocking. Full CI is green on the head commit.

## Notes

**Owner steps**
1. Cloudflare → Network → **IP Geolocation: On**. Until then, the country comes from the locale.
2. **Verify every hotline number** (all are `verified_on: null`), following `docs/HOW-TO-VERIFY-CRISIS-RESOURCES.md`, and sign off the table. The weekly staleness workflow stays red until then, by design. Points to check:
   - RU 8-800-2000-122 is a children's and teens' line; an adult line is probably needed.
   - AR 135 covers the Buenos Aires area only.
   - Several lines have no hours listed.

**Known gaps (stories filed)**
- **BITB-253:** the keyword fallback (used when ML safety is down) blocks "Why did Cain kill Abel?" in en and ar as violence. These cases are strict `xfail` in the tests.
- **BITB-254:** Llama Guard S11 combined with S6 or S10 maps to a non-self-harm reason, so no card is shown.

**Non-blocking follow-ups**
- The lookup endpoint shares the per-IP chat rate-limit budget.
- An old stream client loses the fallback numbers if the LLM fails mid-stream.

author: francescok
body:
Probed at master `d4e804c62`, macOS, Apple clang 21.

```ruby
class U
  begin
    X = zz
  rescue NameError => e
    puts e.message
  end
  def self.zz = 5
end
p U.zz
```

| Program | CRuby | Spinel master | This PR |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| the class body above | `undefined local variable or method 'zz' for class U`, `5` | `5` | as CRuby |
| `zz(1)`, `self.zz`, `U.zz` in the body before the def, rescued | `undefined method 'zz' for class U` (each) | calls the later def | as CRuby |
| `zz; def self.zz = 5` in a module body | `... for module M` | calls the later def | as CRuby |
| `foo(1)` at the top level before `def foo(a) = a`, not rescued | NoMethodError `undefined method 'foo' for main`, the program stops | calls the later def | as CRuby |
| `[1].each { early }` before `def early` | `undefined local variable or method 'early' for main` | calls the later def | as CRuby |
| `y = qq` in `class V`, no `qq` anywhere, rescued | `... 'qq' for class V` | `... 'qq' for main` | as CRuby |
| `puts "a"`, `rand(3)`, `format("%d", 1)`, `sleep(0)` or `p name` in `class U` before the body's own `def self.<same name>` | Kernel's or Module's answer (`a`, an Integer, `"1"`, `0`, `"U"`) | calls the later def | as CRuby |
| `X = zz + 1`, `W = zz ? 1 : 2` in the body before `def self.zz`, rescued | NameError | the write runs with the later def's value | as CRuby |
| `xx` and `xx(1)` in `class Integer` before its `def self.xx`, rescued | NameError, NoMethodError `... for class Integer` | calls the later def | as CRuby |
| `zz` in `Class.new do ... end` before its `def self.zz`, rescued | `... 'zz' for class #<Class:0x...>` | calls the later def | as CRuby |

Root cause:
- `call_target` asked the load record about a call's point only for a method with several versions (`ct_version`), and took the record's "not defined here" as unknown. A method defined once was the target of every call naming it, before its def too.
- `desugar_class_body_self_calls` rewrites a class body's bare call to `U.zz` with no regard to where the def stands, so the call kept that target.
- The NameError and NoMethodError arms of `emit_unresolved_call` named self from the class being emitted, which is none in a class body: they said "main" there.

**The record answers whether a call finds its method where it runs.** `elab_call_method` gives ELAB_YES, NO or UNKNOWN for a call on a class's chain, its class side or main's top-level functions. A NO is meant to be acted on. The query also searches main's singleton side (`def self.solo`, `class << self`), a reopened Class's instance side and, for a class's class side, Object's and BasicObject's singleton methods, since the plan's tables hold those under the same name. The record keeps the program's reopenings of Object, BasicObject, Module and Kernel by the header that opens each, rather than asking the class table by name. It answers UNKNOWN wherever the record cannot prove that nothing supplies the method yet:
- a def, mixin or call a pass made or copied, or one from the builtin prelude, builtins/ or a pre-installed package (`set` and `pathname`, which CRuby has loaded at boot while the program's own `require` puts them later). The parser's file table now keeps each file's tier, where `require` found it, set when the file gets its id (the splice marker and the load graph's file flags carry it), and the node table takes it per file beside its defer-refusals flag (`nt_file_tier`), so the record reads where `require` found the file, not its path;
- a point after code the record cannot follow (`send(:define_singleton_method, ...)`) has run on the chain;
- a call in a block of a call the record does not know, which may keep the block and run it later (such statements are now marked `kept`);
- a chain through a class whose superclass the record does not hold (`Struct.new`, `Data.define`, `< Struct.new(:a)`, a core class);
- an undef or removal of an earlier definition, which its own arm answers;
- a program that defines `method_missing` or `respond_to_missing?`, which answers a call no method does.

A call under a condition is still answered from the record's own may and sure facts: `p zz if true` before the def raises, and a def under a condition before the call makes the answer UNKNOWN. With this commit alone no program's C changes; the next commit reads it. Layer: the load record.

**The plan states the raise.** `call_target` asks the record for a class's class methods and main's functions, for every method rather than only versioned ones, and answers no target when the record proves none is defined where the call runs. A constant receiver's class is the one the record resolves the reference to where the call stands (`elab_class_ref_at`), through one helper that `cplan_missing` and `cplan_self_builtin` share. A call on an instance keeps its tables' target, which its dispatch arms are built on, and so does an explicit receiver's call of a name a builtin answers on any self (`U.format`).

Where no program method answers, a builtin may, as in a class with no def of the name. A Kernel module function (`puts`, `rand`, `format`, `sleep`, `load`) is private, so `route_self_builtin_calls`, a rewrite step after the record like `rewrite_builtin_cm_alias_calls`, makes the desugared `U.rand(2)` bare again (`cplan_self_builtin`). A builtin the class itself answers (`U.name`) keeps its receiver and reaches the builtin through `call_target`'s answer. A Kernel call Spinel refuses in a class with no def of the name is refused here too: `load("missing.rb")` before `def self.load` (master called the later def; CRuby raises LoadError). `builtin_self_method_known`, a `builtin_names.c` predicate, says whether a builtin answers a name on any self: Kernel's module functions, Object's surface, and a sorted index of the arity facts' Object, BasicObject, Kernel, Module and Class names, searched by binary search. `builtin_object_method_known` moves beside it.

Otherwise `cplan_missing` states the run-time raise: NameError for a vcall, NoMethodError otherwise, and the receiver's description ("class U", "module M", "main"). An anonymous class names itself at run time through the existing `anon_class_text`. `cplan_missing` tests the cheap facts first, so a name no program scope defines answers at once. One codegen arm at the head of `emit_call_body` renders that answer after evaluating the arguments; `emit_call_body_ordinary` does not change. A constant write whose value runs such a call raises there rather than dropping the write: `missing_call_in_order` follows CRuby's order for a call (the receiver, then the arguments left to right, into nested calls; operators are calls too) and runs the operands ahead of the missing call for their effects, then the call (`A = id(zz)`; `B = snd(noisy, zz)` prints noisy's line first). An operand whose order it does not follow (an Array, a Hash, an interpolation, a `&.` call, a call with a splat, keyword, block argument or literal block) runs whole when it holds the missing call (`cplan_subtree_missing`), and raises inside (`L = noisy&.then { zz }`, `I = kw(1, k: zz)`). Self, a pure read and a constant receiver the record resolves to a program class run nothing and are skipped. This is evaluation order, which the value-position walker does not answer; and a condition that is such a call evaluates it for the raise. The vcall, missing-self-method and rescued-as-missing arms of `emit_unresolved_call` take their self text from the plan (`cplan_self_text`) and share one raise placeholder. `desugar_class_body_self_calls` is left as it is: it only spells the class body's self as the class constant, and the plan decides from the call's point. Layer: the call plan and a builtin-names predicate, one renderer.

**Cost.** `--timing` on `test/scale/call_shapes.sh 100`, three runs each: `cg_methods` takes 1122-1130 ms on master `ecf9dfe86` and 1127-1145 ms with this PR.

## Problem / user outcome
Protect DallasCircle's canonical entity graph and ensure public sitemap/entity identifiers never leak a personal-name URL.

## Decision
Extend the existing live-route verifier to require stable JSON-LD `@id` values matching the canonical profile/guide URL, verify `mainEntityOfPage` parity where present, and reject personal-name URLs in sitemap entries and entity IDs.

## Discoverability impact
Keeps the canonical page URL, structured-data entity ID, and sitemap aligned. This is a guardrail for the agreed brand-first URL policy, not a claim about rankings or indexing.

## Risks
Low-risk test-only change. No runtime behavior, database schema, DNS, or production configuration changes.

## Acceptance criteria
- Guide and place routes have JSON-LD `@id` equal to their canonical URL.
- `mainEntityOfPage`, where present, matches the same canonical URL.
- Sitemap URLs and structured entity IDs do not contain `praveenyadav`.
- Existing lint, production build, local HTTP route checks, and Cloudflare Worker build pass in CI.

## Verification
CI will run the repository's existing quality workflow. Live production and browser behavior remain separate from CI evidence.

## Rollback
Revert this test-only change if it exposes a false positive; no data migration or deployment rollback is required.

author: mk-aify
body:
This follows up [HyFib/HyFib-HealthCare360-NanaHospitals#163](https://github.com/HyFib/HyFib-HealthCare360-NanaHospitals/pull/163), India compliance fix **C5**, part 1. That PR merged with 365 days before the fix for [its review comment](https://github.com/HyFib/HyFib-HealthCare360-NanaHospitals/pull/163#discussion_r4410996308) was pushed. This PR is that fix. It also fixes the same shortfall in the logs HC360 keeps in its database.

## Problem

The Digital Personal Data Protection Rules 2025 have logs kept for at least a year (rules 6 and 8). Two kinds of log fell short of that whenever the year held a 29 February:

- **Log files.** The file sink dates each day's file from that day's midnight, and deletes the file once that midnight is older than the retention limit. A day's last events are almost a day younger than its midnight. With 365 days they went a day before they were a year old, and two days early in a leap year.
- **Database logs**: the message log, the integration log and the sign-in records. The nightly clean-up deleted each row 365 days after it was made. A year that holds a 29 February has 366 days, so rows went a day early. A hospital could not set less than 365.

## Change

- **Log files:** `HospitalLogging.RetentionDays` is **367**, a leap year's 366 days plus the day the file holds. Its comment says why.
- **Database logs:** kept **366 days**, which is both the default and the minimum (`RetentionSchedule.LogDays`).
  - A year has at most 366 days, so every row is kept a full year.
  - A period stored lower before is read as 366, because the period in force is clamped to the minimum. There is nothing to migrate.
- **Staff app:** *Privacy › Retention* shows "366 days (1 year)".
- **Docs:** `SECURITY.md` and the retention table in `privacy.md` give the new periods and the reason.

## Tests that fail on `main` and pass with the change

**`ObservabilityTests.A_log_file_is_kept_until_its_last_event_is_a_year_old_in_a_leap_year_too`** (integration) puts log files dated 200, 366, 368 and 400 days ago in a logs folder. It then writes an event with the server's log configuration, which opens the day's file and applies the retention.

- **On `main`** (6e543a5, 365 days) it fails. The file from 366 days ago, whose last events are not yet a leap year old, is deleted:

  ```
  File.Exists(DaysAgo(366))
      should be
  True
      but was
  False
  ```
- **With the change**, the files from 200 and 366 days ago are kept, and those from 368 and 400 days ago are deleted.

**`RetentionTests.Logs_are_kept_a_full_year_across_a_leap_day_too`** (unit, once for each of the three database logs). It takes every day of 2027 to 2029 and the shortest period a hospital can set. On each day, the clean-up's cut-off must be no later than a year before.

- **With 365 days** all three fail, from 29 February 2028 onward:

  ```
  days
      should satisfy the condition
  (rule.Cutoff(now, shortest) <= now.AddYears(-1))
      but
  [02/29/2028 09:00:00 +00:00, 03/01/2028 09:00:00 +00:00, …]
      do not
  ```
- **With 366 days** all three pass.

## Checks

- **Unit:** the privacy module's tests, 75 passed.
- **Integration:** `ObservabilityTests`, 5 passed. `PrivacyTests`, 6 passed: the portal's privacy summary now gives 366 days for the message log.
- **Staff app:** the privacy rules' tests (37) pass, including "366 days (1 year)". Typecheck, ESLint and Prettier are clean.
- **Formatting:** `dotnet format whitespace` is clean on the changed C#.

## For the hospital

- The server keeps two more days of log files, and its database one more day of log rows. There is nothing to do.
- **Patients see the change.** The privacy notice in the patient portal gives the message log's period, which becomes 366 days.

author: amazing-source
body:
## What and why

The owner could not find reverse: it sat behind the downshift paddle (Q twice at a standstill). In automatic, the brake held on its own for 0.3 s at a standstill now selects R. In R the pedals swap, so the brake key backs the car up and the accelerator brakes it. The accelerator held on its own at a standstill selects first again. Manual is unchanged. Reverse also tops out at 40 km/h now; before, only the rev limiter stopped it, at about 90 km/h after 4 s.

Closes #67
Closes #70

## Agentic provenance

- **Built by:** systems agent (one agent, no sub-agents).
- **Brief:** in automatic, select reverse by holding the brake at a standstill and drive backwards on it, as in GTA or Forza; drive again by holding the accelerator; nothing while moving; manual Q/E unchanged; show R on the HUD, the cluster and the reversing lamps; a controls-screen row and the README. Then the owner's 40 km/h cap (#70).
- **Decisions taken on the way:**
  - **Owner:** the gesture (approved design), and the 40 km/h cap (#70, 2026-10-29).
  - **Our gesture, not the real car's.** The real Aventador selects R with a button on the centre console and returns to first with the right paddle (research note 2026-10-29, section 3: Parkers, Autocar, Gulf News, CarsGuide). The held brake is our gesture for a keyboard and a pad. No R key: R is the start key.
  - **Agent:**
    - **0.3 s hold.** Longer than a tap (Drive Lab's tap limit is 0.25 s, `Config/ControlsHelp.TAP_SECONDS`), so a dab of the brake at a standstill selects nothing. Shorter than the exit's 0.35 s hold, so reversing is not slower than getting out. The owner's to tune.
    - **"On its own".** A pedal selects only while the other is under 10 %, so brake and full throttle together (a launch) never select R.
    - **Neutral is left to the paddles.** The pedals move only between a forward gear and R.
    - **It is input help, not the car.** It sits in `Config/InputHelp.reverseHoldTime` for the keyboard and pad presets. The `direct` preset (robot drivers, DriveSim's default, the calibration) drives the pedals as they are, so no physics spec changed meaning.
    - **How the cap acts.** The driver's throttle fades to zero over the last 4 km/h below 40 (`Gearbox.reverseCut`), as a limiter cuts: it never brakes the car. A limit on engine rpm was rejected. At the cap the engine turns about 3,160 rpm in R, under the 5,000 rpm the launch clutch aims for, so a rev limit there would have kept the clutch from ever closing. The cut applies in both gearbox modes. The real car's reverse limit is undocumented (research note §3), so the cap is our design choice.
    - **Controls screen.** A `keysOf` field on `Rules/ControlsHelp` rows lets the Reverse row show the brake's keys without "explaining the brake twice", which the screen's check forbids.
  - **Coordinator:**
    - The reversing lamp stays as #41 built it. The lamp lit in R is the existing `Light_Rear*_Reverse` piece, identified on an Aventador S photo (cited in `Config/CarLights`). The SVJ's own reversing-lamp position is unsourced (research note §3). This PR changes no lamp code.
    - **Upcoming exception (deviation from the approved gesture, decided by the coordinator, to go in the launch-control PR):** while launch control is available (Corsa, ESC off, first gear, standstill, automatic), the brake will not select R, and R stays on the Q paddle there. Reason: a player waiting on the brake before flooring the throttle would otherwise get R and back up instead of arming. The owner has been told and can overrule it.
- **Mistake owned:** while building the mutation script I overwrote the audio agent's scratch `mutate.py` (same scratchpad path, 11:47). I reported it to the coordinator. The results here come from my own script, `docs/evidence/car-reverse/mutate.py`.

## Evidence

- [x] Gates green locally: format, lint, types, unit tests (64 spec files, 517 passed), build.
- [x] Every new rule shown failing on a deliberate break: 20 breaks, each failing at least one spec, then 517 passing once restored. `docs/evidence/car-reverse/mutate.py` applies each break and runs the full suite; its output is in `mutation_run.txt`. Examples:
  - no hold: `Selector.spec:42 expected 1, got -1`;
  - R while rolling: `Selector.spec:55`;
  - R with both pedals: `Selector.spec:71`;
  - pedals swapped in manual: `Selector.spec:121`;
  - Model skips the selector: `Selector.spec:152`;
  - Model skips the cut: `Selector.spec:207`;
  - hard cut with no band: `Gearbox.spec:194`;
  - `define` accepting an empty cut: `Cars.spec:54`;
  - the Reverse row losing the brake's keys: `ControlsHelp.spec:151`.
- [x] Studio:
  - **Edit mode:** both `Light_RearLeft_Reverse` and `Light_RearRight_Reverse` are MeshParts with a SurfaceAppearance in `Workspace.CarImport`.
  - **Functional Play check** (solo, simulated keyboard, no network simulation): `docs/evidence/car-reverse/play_check.md`, with every result and the log line behind it.
    - R at 0.00 m/s about 0.3 s after S went down. S backs the car up; W brakes it, and D comes back at 0.07 m/s.
    - S from 19.1 m/s only brakes; R comes after the stop, at -0.03 m/s.
    - Manual: S at a standstill only brakes, and Q/E step 1, N, R and back.
    - HUD and cluster show R/N/1. The reversing lamps glow in R (emissive 8 by day) and are dark otherwise. Capture: `play_manual_R_reversing_lamps_hud.jpg`.
    - Cap (second session, synced with the barrier branch too): reversing on S held 39.2 km/h for about 10 s and never went above it; braking from 105 km/h with S held selected R only at -0.04 m/s.
- [x] Performance: per frame, the selector adds a few comparisons and one table write in `Model.step`, and the cut one clamp per substep. Not profiled in Studio; the claim is from the code.
- [x] No key printed or committed; nothing published; no DataStore written.

## Changes stored in the place

author: spheceo
body:
## Why
A footage build takes 5–7 minutes, and almost all of it is one Opus call: Oct 26's builds spent 5 min 14 s and 6 min 10 s in it, producing 28–38K output tokens, mostly thinking (no single reply was over 719 tokens). Research and speakers take ~30 s; Writer's checks are instant. The aim is about 1½–2 minutes without losing quality.

## What
A **fast build** (`steps::build_fast`) in three phases, on Writer's existing MCP tools and checks:
1. **Outline**: Opus plans the whole script and calls `set_outline`, giving up to 8 sections. Each section gets its moments (`[m:ss]` and word IDs), what its cut-ins tell, and its seconds.
2. **Sections at once**: one Opus call per section, each on its own draft. Items are checked as they arrive, exactly as today. A section after the first is checked as coming after a cut-in.
3. **Finish**: the sections are joined in order. Opus runs `review_plan`, fixes what it reports, smooths the seams between sections (repeated facts, cut-ins that don't follow on) and calls `finish`. Off-target handling is the same as today.

Every phase gets the same system prompt, tool list, evidence and effort. That way the sections and the finish read the outline's prompt from the cache instead of re-reading 100–600 KB each. Effort is `medium` by default (`WRITER_FAST_EFFORT` changes it); `effort` is now passed through `agent::Question` and the sidecar. With no outline, the build falls back to today's build in steps.

**The fast build is everyone's default** (decided Oct 29). `WRITER_SCRIPT_BUILD=steps` brings back the build in steps, for comparisons; the switch isn't `WRITER_BUILD`, which already names a release's tag at compile time.

## Comparing
`scripts/ab/run.py <dir> [engines]` now compares `sdk,fast` by default, through the debug route's new `fast` engine. `page.py` makes the blind page, with the time split (outline, sections, finish), and time and cost hidden until the reveal. Worth running after merging: if the blind reviews favour the build in steps, raise `WRITER_FAST_EFFORT` or switch back.

## Checks
`just check` passes; new tests cover the phases' tool gating, the outline, `finish_section`, the section and finish prompts, and the shared tool list.

The live A/B builds haven't been run yet: they need `just dev`, which shares port 1421 with the Writer that's open now.

author: nikophil
body:
`FakerSeedIsNotResetDuringRunKernelTest` randomly fails with a unique constraint violation on `WithUniqueColumn.uniqueCol`, see [this run on 2.x](https://github.com/zenstruck/foundry/actions/runs/40393226390/job/121819376825) or [this one on #1192](https://github.com/zenstruck/foundry/actions/runs/40844483756/job/123348923564).

Faker relies on the global `mt_rand()` state, and Symfony consumes it as well in some cases (`ServicesConfigurator` when the container is built, cache pools namespace versioning...). So the kernel reboot triggered by the browser request can shift the sequence: forcing a container rebuild between both requests is enough to change the third generated word. That word then lands anywhere in a list of ~180 words, and sometimes on one which is already persisted.

With a uuid, such a collision becomes negligible, while the value stays deterministic for a given seed: the test still catches a seed reset.

author: dan-petty
body:
## What

`split_record` reads only the comment at the end of the issue body as the job record. It parses the body with markdown-it-py. The last block must be an `html_block` that holds the record comment.

## Why

The old regular expression matched the record format anywhere in the body. A quote of the format in a code span or a code block read as the record, gave a warning, and the next write of the record deleted the quote. A comment in the middle of the body was taken as the record too.

A quote in a code span, a fenced code block or an indented code block now stays in the body, reads as no record and gives no warning. The removal of every regular-expression match is deleted.

Closes #2538
