author: danielutsch85
vinayakss007
body:
Closes #3277.

## The drift

`validatePassword()` in `lib/auth/session.ts:38` is the check that actually
enforced the rule — **12 characters, one uppercase, one digit, one special**. Five
schemas declared their own minimum beside it and disagreed:

| field | declared | route then said |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `signupSchema.password` | `min(8)` | refused at 12 |
| `resetPasswordSchema.password` | `min(8)` | refused at 12 |
| `inviteMemberSchema.password` | `min(8)` | refused at 12 |
| `changePasswordSchema.new_password` | `min(12)` — length only | refused on class |
| `createAdminSchema.password` (route-local) | `min(8)` | refused at 12 |
| `auth/reset-password` schema (route-local) | `min(8)` | refused at 12 |

So `Ab1!` + nothing was a *valid* signup payload that returned 400 one screen
later, and which message arrived depended on which check fired. The bootstrap
case is the sharp one: `POST /api/setup/create-admin` is provisioned by a
scripted caller that reads the schema as the contract, and the first-run flow has
no second attempt to fall back to.

## The fix

`newPasswordSchema` in `lib/api/schemas/auth.ts` is **derived by calling**
`validatePassword` (a `superRefine` — the shape #1173 already used in
`password-reset/confirm`), so there is no second number to drift, plus the
`max(128)` bcrypt cost ceiling the schemas already carried. Adopted at every
field whose request path already runs the policy:

- `signupSchema.password`, `resetPasswordSchema.password` (`lib/api/schemas/auth.ts`)
- `inviteMemberSchema.password` (`lib/api/schemas.ts`)
- `changePasswordSchema.new_password`
- the route-local schemas in `setup/create-admin` and `auth/reset-password`
- `password-reset/confirm` now reuses the shared schema instead of its own copy of
  the derivation — same behaviour, one fewer place to be wrong

Two consequences worth naming, both intended:

- **The route-level `validatePassword()` calls in `create-admin` and
  `auth/reset-password` are gone.** Once the schema calls the same function they
  cannot fire, and leaving them would keep the two response shapes (`{error: msg}`
  vs `Validation failed` + `details`) that this issue is about. A weak password now
  has exactly one answer shape.
- **Existing-password fields stay lenient** (`loginSchema`, `setup2faSchema`,
  `disable2faSchema`, `changePasswordSchema.current_password`) — raising them locks
  out accounts whose valid password predates the rule, which is #1286's finding.
  The comment that said so now points at `newPasswordSchema` instead of `min(12)`.

`setup/create-admin` also gets `.trim().min(1)` on `full_name` / `workspace_name`:
`"   "` passed `min(1)` and the slug derivation (`route.ts:93-96`, strips
non-`[a-z0-9-]`) then produced an empty workspace slug.

## Deliberately not touched

- `updateMemberSchema.password` (`lib/api/schemas/admin.ts:58`, `min(8)`) and
  `createTenantSchema.owner_password` (`lib/api/schemas/superadmin.ts:109`, `min(8)`)
  — **neither path calls `validatePassword()` at all**, so they are not a drift,
  they are an absent check. Adding enforcement where none exists is a different
  change than the one claimed here.
- `superadminInviteMemberSchema` (`superadmin.ts:90`) has **zero importers** (`grep
  -rn superadminInviteMemberSchema app lib tests` → only its own definition) — dead
  schema, not a live contract.
- `lib/auth/api-handlers.ts:277` keeps its route-level `validatePassword` call
  after `signupSchema`. It is unreachable for the same reason the other two were,
  but that file's lines are cited by `docs/BASECRM/03-RBAC-AUTHZ.md:292,427` and
  `docs/BASECRM/05-BUSINESS-FLOWS.md:137,138`, so deleting two lines there would
  re-pin four doc coordinates in files this PR is not about. Recorded here so the
  next pass can do it with the doc edits in the same change.
- The signup form's client rules (`app/auth/signup/page.tsx:57-60`) check length
  only, not the three character classes, so a 12-char lowercase password still
  reaches the server before being refused. The message is now the only one there
  is; making the client pre-check the classes needs `validatePassword` extracted
  into a leaf module, because `lib/auth/session.ts` imports `next/headers`,
  `bcryptjs` and `jose` and cannot enter a client graph.

## Tests

`tests/unit/password-schema-single-source-3277.test.ts` (new) asserts the thing
that stays true rather than the number that drifted: over a table of passwords,
`newPasswordSchema` accepts **exactly** the strings `validatePassword` accepts and
refuses with the same message; the ceiling holds; `signup`/`reset`/`invite`/
`change` all refuse what the policy refuses and name the `password` field; the
four existing-password fields stay lenient.

Two fixtures asserted the *old wrong* contract and were updated, not deleted —
`schemas.test.ts:18` (`'12345678'` → policy-valid) and `:170` (`'newpassword'` →
policy-valid). `create-admin-route.test.ts` mocks `@/lib/auth/session`, so its
`validatePassword: () => null` stub is what the schema now sees: the too-short
case drives the refusal through the mock, and a new case covers the
whitespace-only names.

- `npx vitest run tests/unit tests/dashboard` → **941 files passed**, 1 failed:
  `register-drift-screen-2416.test.ts`, which is red on `main` for 8 citations
  (`lib/ai/gateway.ts:143`, `backup-verify/route.ts:313,181,351,322`,
  `process-sequences/route.ts:36`, `cleanup-tenant-sweep.test.ts:372`) none of
  which is a file this PR touches. #3361 re-pins them.
- `npm run typecheck` clean; `npx eslint` clean on the 8 changed files.
- `guard:schemas`, `guard:coords`, `guard:boundaries`, `guard:filesize`,
  `guard:any-suppressions` green. `guard:register-drift` reports the same 8
  pre-existing pointers.
- No client component imports these modules (`grep` over `use client` files for
  `@/lib/api/schemas` → only `schemas/billing`), so `validatePassword` cannot
  reach a browser bundle; the CI `build` job is the authority, because the
  local `prebuild` gate refuses a symlinked `node_modules` in a worktree.

No migration, no DDL (#3246), no schema-shape change.

## What

New snippet in both locales: **grain on the gradient**.

- Explains the cause of banding: 8 bits per channel, a slow transition stretching each step over several pixels, and Mach bands making the edge worse. No gradient syntax fixes it; dithering does.
- `feTurbulence` rendered into a data URI background: no image file, no request, no decode.
- The knobs: `fractalNoise` over `turbulence` (which clumps and reads as dirt), `baseFrequency` 0.6–1.2, `numOctaves` capped at 3, `stitchTiles` for tiled layers.
- The escaping that breaks the declaration (`#` to `%23`, `%` to `%25`), and why not base64.
- Useful opacity range, `mix-blend-mode: overlay` when the grain should follow luminance, and the cost on a phone.

The preview shows the same gradient twice, with and without the layer.

body:
## 卡：P3-7 MCP 注册、Agent Skill 与文档

> **Stacked on #33**（P3-6）。依赖 P3-4 已在 #31。

### 改动

- `crates/cormex/src/install/mcp_register.rs`：`ClaudeCodeMcp`（`mcpServers` 条目）、`CodexMcp`（`[mcp_servers.cormex]`）。
- `cmd/init.rs`：把 MCP 注册接进 `init`。
- `skills/cormex/SKILL.md`。
- `README.md`：「Connect an agent over MCP」一节（roadmap B 的欠账）。

### 验收

- [ ] Skill 文件通过 `npx skills add weironz/cormex` 能装上（或在 PR 里说明验证方式）

**没有跑那条命令** —— 它需要访问 skills registry 与一个已发布的仓库。本 PR 能说明的是：文件在 `npx skills add` 会找的路径上（`skills/cormex/SKILL.md`），frontmatter 有该格式要求的 `name` 与 `description`。

```
$ cargo test -p cormex --lib mcp_register
running 4 tests
test the_claude_registration_is_idempotent ... ok
test a_trailing_slash_does_not_double ... ok
test the_codex_registration_preserves_the_existing_file ... ok
test a_path_with_a_quote_is_escaped ... ok
test result: ok. 4 passed
```

`cargo fmt --all -- --check` 无输出；`cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` 通过；`cargo test --workspace --locked -- --include-ignored` 无 FAILED。

### 三处值得读的

1. **Codex 的条目是追加的，不是重新序列化整个 `config.toml`。** 那个文件里有用户自己的模型设置和注释，TOML 往返会丢掉注释。

2. **`SKILL.md` 写的是「用最便宜的那一层」**：search → brief → digest → transcript → raw。直接跳到 transcript 会为一个索引就能回答的问题花掉几千 token。

3. **`as_of` 与 `at` 的区别写清楚了**：今天采集、三个月前发生的会话，`at` 找得到、`as_of` 找不到 —— 那是对的，不是 bug。

### 顺带发现

1. **MCP 注册的安装器要和其它安装器分开规划**：Claude Code 的条目里嵌着设备密钥，没有凭据时「注册 Cormex」是一个无法应用的变更。
2. **设备密钥会以明文进宿主的配置文件**（Claude Code 的 `mcpServers` 条目里）。那是宿主自己的存储决定，不是我们的 —— 但值得知道，`doctor` 应该提一句（未做，记在这里）。

### 与设计不一致之处

无。

author: simonvanlaak
body:
## What changes

For macOS **Window** recording, use a real-time H.264 writer for ScreenCaptureKit image samples and a fresh, owner-checked stop image on the same timeline. Validate coded packet reach and decoded stop pixels before replacing the original MP4. A failed or timed-out candidate keeps the original; a rejected window cannot silently become a Display capture. Timed CLI microphone input now stops concurrently with screen finalization, rather than recording during a potentially 26-second writer wait. Display and Region retain their existing movie path. This is the proposed fix for #99, not a release.

## Verification by head

The **current** remote head `55b69dca0473562572e3d746c4234f9e7fd3e429` (documentation-only follow-up to the Mac-tested runtime head `0872c51cd9131a58ac4a9b6a953e6dbb361d4534`) integrates main through `27b7a8e3a96c59e254acb9cae13aecd30778bfe1`, repairs a review finding in timed CLI audio stop, and adds two missing Mac-only fields to a test fixture. It passed Linux **579 tests, 3 ignored**, an offline build and 22 Python checks before the fixture-only follow-up; that focused fixture test passed afterward. Its concurrent-stop regression failed before the repair and passed after it. On an isolated macOS arm64 VM the runtime head `0872c51` built, passed the full Mac suite (**522 passed, 3 ignored**), passed the native production-ABI Swift fixture (three decoded frames, fresh green stop pixel at 6.0 seconds), and installed/launched with `codesign --verify --deep --strict`. Independent read-only reviews accepted the integration and staged audio repair for a draft push, not a merge.

On the **earlier** head `d5eae998fccbfa258775c28cd3cbafe892f6ee17`, installed-app Finder CLI captures: static six seconds yielded 49 coded packets, 5.678-second MP4, 6.012-second bundle; moving/resizing/changing Finder yielded 88 packets, 6.032-second MP4, 6.097-second bundle. Both decoded; the moving recording showed the original NoMac view at the beginning and Applications after the action at the end. DTS packet order was strictly increasing and the final moving frame decoded at approximately 6.015 seconds. An explicit ambiguous `--window Finder` with two visible Finder windows and an unmatched query both failed without making bundles. A default Display capture created a movie.

On the **current head**, an installed-app six-second static Finder Window yielded 42 strictly ordered packets from 0.102 to 5.898 seconds; its decoded final frame visibly showed only Finder. A moving/resizing six-second Window yielded 62 ordered packets from 0.070 to 5.953 seconds, with visibly changed Finder geometry and clean decoded start/end frames. Explicit `--window Finder` with multiple selectable Finder windows refused ambiguity. An installed GUI Window picker capture yielded 105 ordered packets through 30.792 seconds of a 30.877-second bundle and visible resized Finder pixels at the start/end. A GUI Region captured a chosen Finder rectangle for 23.779 seconds; its 74-frame movie decoded with the expected crop. Default CLI Display also decoded, though its three-second bundle produced only a 0.85-second legacy movie; this path was intentionally unchanged, not certified as fixed by #99. Bundle manifests, summaries and private decoded images were inspected. The ad-hoc VM signature does **not** establish production TCC persistence. A disposable BlackHole microphone produced 3.915 seconds of silent WAV for a four-second CLI capture; a synthetic tone routed to BlackHole still yielded all-zero samples, so real microphone signal and slow-finalization audio remain unproved. The owned NoMac VM was explicitly stopped with confirmed cleanup, 25 billed minutes, $0.33. Private capture images and footage are not attached to this public PR.

## Still blocked before ready for review

- `ffprobe` infers `r_frame_rate=600/1` from a 600 Hz VFR timestamp grid; the saved H.264 stream does **not** declare 600 fps. Actual average frame rates are much lower and packets are strictly ordered. The earlier 5.678-second static MP4 was unavailable, but the new exact-head static MP4 and decoded end frame were retained privately and inspected.
- Native callback/encoder failure, owner replacement, rejected/slow stop image, finish timeout and original-file retention still need exercised failure-path proof. The Rust tests establish guards, not a live native failure. The VM's BlackHole input proved WAV creation and approximate stop timing but no nonzero samples, even while a tone was routed to it; verify signal and slow-finalization audio on a working input. Preserve privacy exclusions and screenshot-only fallback checks before any wider claim.
- The PR remains **draft**. GitHub reports no CI checks for this branch, so no CI pass is claimed. The published head currently merges cleanly into main, but mergeability is not platform proof. No merge, release or issue closure is requested.

author: julesopp
body:
File ▸ Open, the CLI, drag-and-drop and the workspace tree now read SHELX `.res` and `.ins` files. Each non-zero PART becomes an atom group (*PART 1*, *PART 2*, *PART -1*), as it already does for a CIF that carries its SHELX file.

## What the reader does (`xtal/io/shelx.py`)
- **Space group** from `SYMM`, `LATT`'s centring, and the inversion a positive `LATT` implies, looked up the way a CIF's operation loop is.
- **Occupancy**: SHELXL's sof includes the site symmetry (`10.125` for Zr on Fm-3m), so it is multiplied back by the order of the site's stabiliser, at the 0.05 Å special-position tolerance, and rounded to the places the five-decimal sof supports.
- **Fixed values and free variables** (`10.5`, `21.0`, `-21.0`) resolved against `FVAR`.
- **U**: anisotropic read; riding hydrogens (`-1.2`) take their parent's U_eq.
- Short and long `SFAC`; nothing after `HKLF`/`END` is an atom.
- PARTs left in `meta["shelx_parts"]`, so the Document makes the groups exactly as for a CIF.

Read-only: SHELX is not offered in Export. Zeo++'s `diameters.res` is refused with a message saying it has no CELL.

## Also: the workspace chooser's keys
Cmd+N (New workspace…), Cmd+O (Open Other…) and Cmd+Q (Quit) now work in the Choose a Workspace window, which comes up before any menu bar. Tested by `test_the_file_menus_keys_work_before_there_is_a_file_menu`.

## Tests
- `tests/test_shelx_reader.py`: group construction, special-position occupancy, free variables, riding U, peaks, registry, Zeo++ `.res` refusal, and UiO-67's embedded `.res` read against its own CIF (sites, occupancies, PARTs).
- `tests/test_atom_groups_ui.py`: the `.res` opens with the same PART groups over the same atoms as the CIF.
- Full suite: 6047 passed, 5 skipped. That run was on the earlier base; the targeted tests pass on current main.

author: intech
body:
## What

Past 1440px the body now follows the top bar instead of sitting in a centered 1440px island: the sidebar anchors the left edge, the outline anchors the right edge, and the article keeps a readable measure between them.

VitePress caps the whole layout at `--vp-layout-max-width: 1440px`, which on a 2560px display put the sidebar's first column 592px in from the edge and left 560px of nothing on the right.

| At 2560px | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Sidebar | 0–832, text from 592px | 0–272, text from 32px |
| Article | 944–1632 (688px) | 886–1686 (800px) |
| Outline | 1712–1968 | 2268–2528 (right edge) |
| Empty band on the right | 560px | 32px |

## Why the article stays at 800px

The empty bands were a composition fault, not a reason to set 100-character lines. 800px is already around 95 characters. The width is a single token, `--connectum-content-width`, if it needs to move.

`!important` on the dimensions is deliberate: VitePress compiles its own `.VPDoc.has-aside .content-container[data-v-…]`, and a plain override of the same class silently loses to it.

- `pnpm docs:build` and `pnpm docs:validate` pass.

author: wolf31o2
body: Genesis snapshots can place multiple pools behind one relay endpoint, leaving bootstrap without independent witnesses. Add trusted operator groups and canonical network relay defaults. Configured groups supply the exclusive corroboration identities. Aliases count once, conflicting origins fail closed, and retained peers cannot change operators. An explicit empty list restores ledger-based identities. Startup and replacement governors receive owned configuration without modifying canonical network files. --- ## Summary by cubic Adds trusted relay operator groups (`controlGroups`) to Genesis bootstrap so corroboration witnesses are declared independent of topology valency and stake snapshot pool grouping. When configured, only these operator identities can corroborate Genesis sources. All aliases of one identity count once, conflicting declarations fail closed, and a retained peer cannot be renamed to a different operator while its frontier is tracked. Nil config selects canonical IOG and Blink Labs relay defaults for Dijkstra (and Musashi in Genesis mode), gated on matching every canonical genesis hash so private networks don't inherit public trust; an explicit empty list restores ledger-based identity selection. **Peer governor integration** - Startup and replacement governors receive owned copies of the group set without modifying canonical files. - One local root is overlaid per operator group, without assigning stake. Written for commit 13287346e892f7e8319074a7641897b5702fc000. Summary will update on new commits.

author: jwilleke
body:
Builds [#2130](https://github.com/jwilleke/ngdpbase/issues/2130) (part of epic [#1979](https://github.com/jwilleke/ngdpbase/issues/1979)). The commit message has the details; in short:

- `/import` offers one name field for a single file (not a zip, not several files), pre-filled with the file's own name (for a page, without the extension).
- The name travels as the upload's `givenName` and reaches receivers that declare `names: 'title' | 'file'` as `ReceiveInfo.givenName`. `core.pages` uses it as the title and `core.files` as the file name. A receiver without `names` never gets one.
- There is one rule (`src/ice/givenName.ts`), checked by the route (400) and again in the run (the file is refused). If the location already has the name, that file is refused and nothing is replaced.
- The report, the ledger, recent imports and the audit (`importedFrom` on page-create and asset-upload) keep both names. Private pages and sealed stores stay by id.
- No catalogue (permission/role/policy) changes. One new config key: `ngdpbase.import.engine.name-max-length` (200).

Tests: `npm test` 821 files, 15041 passed, 10 skipped. `npm run lint` is clean. On a throwaway instance, import-screen and admin-import E2E: 7/7 passed.

author: livecodelife
body:
## Fix: check reports false PROV024 for specs outside a nested config directory (#32)

With the config in a subdirectory of the git top level, `check --staged` built its staged tree with `git checkout-index -a` run from the config directory, and `checkout-index -a` exports only the files under the current directory. A spec outside the package (for example `../../spec/x.sh`) was missing from the staged tree, so it hashed as missing and every record with such a spec got PROV024 (plus PROV018). `lint` reads the real working tree, so it passed.

The same bug existed on `--commit` and `--range` (and the pre-push hook): `commitTree` ran `git archive` from the config directory.

### Fix

- `stagedTree` (prov-2026-28d0e0c4, v7) runs the checkout against the git top level (`git -C <top level> checkout-index -a`); the returned path is still the config's directory inside the temporary tree.
- `commitTree` (prov-2026-d741e072, v3) archives the whole commit from the git top level and returns the config's directory inside it.
- Both edits are hand-written inside the marked regions; the markers' stale body hashes go with the marker sweep. The new test file is added to both records' scope and specs.
- Audit of the other subdirectory-cwd uses: `stagedPaths`, `commitFiles` and the merge-exemption diff use `--relative` on purpose (files outside the package are not governed); `git show/cat-file <rev>:./path` resolve `../` correctly from a subdirectory; the rest do not depend on the cwd.

### Tests (new file `check_staged_subdir_test.go`, written first; they failed before the fix)

- `--staged` with a `../../` spec outside the package: no PROV024, and agrees with lint
- a changed spec inside the package and a changed outside spec are still reported
- `--commit` and `--range` with the outside spec
- config at the repo top level, specs beside and below it, for `--staged`, `--commit` and `--range` (no regression)

`go test ./...` all ok, `provenance lint` 0 errors, `provenance stale` none, `provenance check --range origin/main..HEAD` clean.

The records stay open for completion in a clean clone. The 3.0.1 version bump follows as a second PR.

author: ljachymczyk
body:
An app that signs in with passkeys through the [webauthn](https://github.com/cedarcode/webauthn-ruby) gem did not build on spinel. This is the controller shape a Rails app writes for it (the gem's README does the same):

```ruby
class SessionsController < ApplicationController
  def auth_options
    options = WebAuthn::Credential.options_for_get(allow: Credential.pluck(:external_id), user_verification: "preferred")
    session[:auth_challenge] = options.challenge
    render json: options.as_json
  end

  def auth
    credential = WebAuthn::Credential.from_get(params)
    stored = Credential.find_by!(external_id: credential.id)
    credential.verify(session[:auth_challenge], public_key: stored.public_key, sign_count: stored.sign_count)
    stored.update!(sign_count: credential.sign_count)
    render json: { ok: true }
  rescue WebAuthn::Error => e
    render json: { error: e.message }, status: :unprocessable_entity
  end
end
```

`roundhouse --target spinel` on main refuses each `WebAuthn` constant ("constant of an unknown gem: `WebAuthn::Credential` belongs to the webauthn gem, which the Spinel tree does not carry (no façade, no spin package)", plus "constant not supported (all targets)") and `options.as_json` ("Object extension not supported (all targets): as_json lacks a shared runtime/lowering implementation"). On Ruby and JRuby the gem is neither declared in the Gemfile nor required.

## Change

The same seam bcrypt, rqrcode and nokogiri use, plus the catalog entries the jwt gem has:

- `src/catalog/gems.rs`: the gem's surface (`WebAuthn`, `WebAuthn::Configuration`, `WebAuthn::Credential`, the creation and request options, the two credential classes). The options type as the gem's classes, so `as_json` is their own method (`PublicKeyCredential::Options#as_json`, the browser's options JSON with Symbol keys in camelCase), not ActiveSupport's Object extension. The gem's errors are rescuable exceptions (`src/analyze/registry/stdlib.rs`).
- `src/gems.rs`: webauthn is Modeled, and Ruby and JRuby declare and require it (`RUNTIME_GEMS`, `GEM_REQUIRES`), as jwt.
- `src/project.rs` `spin_shape`: when app code names `WebAuthn`, `runtime/webauthn_facade.rb` (a raising façade, the write-path rule every gem façade follows) becomes `require "webauthn"`, its sidecar drops, the manifest declares `webauthn = { git = "https://github.com/sology/spinel-webauthn", ref = "v3.4.3" }` and the binary builds through `spin build`. The package is the gem 3.4.3's relying-party half for Spinel, in the gem's class names; its tests compare each answer with the gem's under CRuby.
- `src/lower/ruby_family_gems.rs`: every other target refuses each reference, as it does for jwt.
- `docs/pipeline/runtime.md`: a section next to rqrcode's.

Not in this change: an initializer's `WebAuthn.configure do |config| ... end`. The initializer ledger already reports it as unconsumed, and the emitted program runs with the gem's default relying party (no `rpId`, and `verify` raises "Unspecified expected origin"). The runtime.md section says so.

## Regression tests

- `spin_shape_swaps_webauthn_facade_for_the_package` (`src/project.rs`): the swap, the dropped sidecar, the manifest line under `[dependencies]`, the `spin build` recipe; a comment that mentions WebAuthn, or no mention, keeps the façade and adds no dependency.
- `webauthn_runs_as_the_real_gem_on_ruby` (`tests/emit_and_run.rs`): on real-blog, options JSON, a registration and an assertion from the gem's `FakeClient` verify, a stale challenge raises `ChallengeVerificationError` and a sign count that went backwards `SignCountVerificationError`; the Gemfile declares the gem. CI's gem install line gains `webauthn`, next to `jwt`.
- `webauthn_is_refused_off_ruby_jruby_and_spinel` (`tests/emit_and_run.rs`): clean on Ruby, JRuby and Spinel (façade swapped, manifest line), refused on the ten other targets.

## What I verified

- `cargo test --locked --lib -- spin_shape gems catalog ruby_family`: 38 passed.
- `cargo test --locked --test emit_and_run -- webauthn jwt`: 4 passed (a deliberately wrong expectation in the Ruby script fails the test, so the script runs).
- `every_runtime_method_body_is_fully_typed`, `runtime_frozen_string_literal`, `spin_dependencies_header`, `real_blog`, `docs_references`, `external_gem_includes`: pass.

author: shehjaddev
body:
Closes #976.

### Problem
fetchNextJob counts a group's active jobs and claims in one statement. Under READ COMMITTED a concurrent fetch's uncommitted claim is invisible, so concurrent fetchers can claim past `groupConcurrency`.

### Change
After the claim commits, `#fetch` counts the claimed groups again in a new statement and gives back the jobs over the limit through the existing `restore()` path (the one `localGroupConcurrency` uses), before any handler, `wip` event or tracking sees them. Of two racing fetches, at least the later count sees both claims. If every job was given back, it retries after a random pause of up to 50 ms (at most 3 tries) so fetches that raced don't keep giving back in lockstep. If a policy index refuses the give-back (23505), the job runs as before. No advisory locks, no schema change.

Caveat (documented): `fetch()` with `db` inside your own transaction isn't covered. Other fetches can't see its claim until that transaction commits.

Known limits, unchanged from the `localGroupConcurrency` path: a given-back retry job returns as `created`, and the job given back follows `RETURNING` order, not priority.

### Tests
- New test forces the race with two connections. It fails on master (the second fetch returns the job) and passes with the fix. Skipped on pglite, Yugabyte and distributed mode.
- Full suite passes with TZ=UTC. The groupConcurrency tests pass with DISTRIBUTED=true.
- Repro (2–4 instances, limits 1–3): handlers never exceeded the limit; master reached 8 at limit 2.
- Benchmark, 8 fetchers, 2000 jobs, limit 5: 651–734 ms vs master 594–668 ms. Sequential fetch+complete 2.0 vs 1.7–1.9 ms/op.

body:
PR 3 of `docs/plans/SCHOOLOGY_QUIZ_IMPORT.md`. It builds the "From Schoology" review screen for the quizzes and question banks the Chrome extension puts in the server inbox (PR 2, #4851).

## What it does
- **Inbox listener** (`hooks/useSchoologyInbox.ts`). It listens on `users/{uid}/schoology_import_inbox` only while the flag is on. Discarding an entry deletes it, and PR 2's trigger then removes its pictures. Pictures are downloaded from Storage with `getBlob`; only the owner can read them.
- **Review modal** (`SchoologyInboxModal.tsx`). It follows the `.imscc` checklist.
  - Each row shows the title, the course or folder it lands in, the question count, "N to check", "N answers missing", the picture count, and Schoology settings that come across.
  - Rows expand to list the questions and can be discarded.
  - Ticks, Select all/none, a shared-pictures checkbox, progress, and Retry failed.
- **Saving.**
  - New copies go into a folder named after the Schoology course or Resources folder, created with `ensureFolderPath` (Q9).
  - Quizzes use `saveQuiz` then `moveQuizItem`; banks use `saveBank` with the bank folder.
  - Pictures go through `attachDocumentImages`, same as every other import.
  - The inbox entry is deleted only after the save succeeds.
- **Provenance and Update / Keep both (Q10, Q11).**
  - `QuizData.source` and `QuestionBankData.source` record where the copy came from. Library metadata gets a matching `sourceKey` (`schoology:{kind}:{itemId}`), written in `useQuiz.saveQuiz` and `buildBankMetadata`, so a re-send finds the earlier copy without a Drive read.
  - **Update** keeps the copy's id, folder and saved settings, and replaces its questions and pictures. Learning-target tags stay on every question whose prompt didn't change. The old order and sections are dropped because they point at question ids that no longer exist.
  - **Keep both** saves a new copy.
- **Settings (Q12).** Schoology's time limit, attempts and shuffle become a new quiz's saved settings (`timeLimitMinutes`, `attemptLimit`, `shuffleQuestions`).
- **Entry points.**
  - A "N from Schoology" button in the Quiz library toolbar; it shows only when something is waiting.
  - `?schoologyImport=1`: the first Quiz widget on the board opens the review and strips the parameter.
  - With no Quiz widget on the board the parameter does nothing yet. PR 4 (the extension buttons) decides what tab the extension opens.
- **Tour anchors.** The new controls have anchors, the `quiz.import.schoology` surface is registered, and the generated anchor lists are refreshed.

## Not in this PR
- The suggested learning targets step. Schoology sends no targets to suggest, so it has nothing to offer.
- The "From Schoology" Import-menu entry and folding in the `.imscc` flags (PR 5).
- Extension buttons (PR 4).

## Flag
Gated by `schoology-quiz-import` (PR 2), starting at access level **admin**: admins only, so Paul plus the other `/admins`. To open it: Admin Settings > Access > Previews > "Send quizzes from Schoology" > Public. Nothing shows for teachers until then.

## Tests
- `utils/schoologyInbox.test.ts`: parsing (blank answers unpacked, unknown types dropped, bad sources refused), row planning and provenance match, settings, tag keeping, and the URL-parameter claim.
- `SchoologyInboxModal.test.tsx`:
  - a new quiz saves into its course folder with its settings and the inbox entry is cleared;
  - Update keeps the old id and creates no folder;
  - a failed bank save stays for retry and its folder isn't created twice;
  - discard.
- Locally, `Widget.docCam.test.tsx` (Webcam) fails in this worktree with an undefined-component error. This PR doesn't touch the Webcam widget; CI will show whether that failure is real.

author: jencryzthers
body:
## Problème

Un bot Claude Code qui faisait un travail outillé (vérifier les ports d'une VM, chercher des clés) s'arrêtait avec une carte d'erreur rouge : « Autocompact is thrashing … use /clear to start fresh ». La personne ne doit jamais voir ça.

## Cause racine

Le CLI arrête le tour quand le contexte se remplit à nouveau jusqu'à la limite dans les 3 appels de modèle qui suivent sa compaction, 3 fois de suite (`api_error: autocompact_thrashing`, raison `rapid_refill_breaker`). Sagax choisit une fenêtre de 200 000 jetons (`--autocompact`).

Les serveurs MCP du bot passent par `mcp-gate.ts`, qui coupe à 8 000 caractères. Les outils machine que Sagax sert lui-même étaient exclus parce que jugés « déjà bornés ». Leurs bornes étaient pourtant celles du transport :

- `run_command` sur l'ordinateur de la personne : 512 Ko ;
- `read_file` : 256 Ko par défaut, 1 Mo sur demande ;
- `run_command` dans l'environnement serveur : 256 Ko ;
- `exec` de l'ordinateur cloud : sans borne côté Sagax.

Chaque résultat pouvait donc peser entre 60 000 et 250 000 jetons. Le CLI coupe un résultat MCP vers 25 000 jetons, mais plusieurs résultats dans un même appel (des balayages de ports et des recherches de clés en parallèle) suffisent à remplir la session juste après chaque compaction.

Ce que Sagax réinjecte après une compaction est déjà borné : le résumé fait au plus 6 Ko et seuls 2 digests sont renvoyés. Ce n'est pas la cause.

## Correctif

**1. Sorties bornées à la source** (`server/tool-output-bound.ts`)
- Chaque réponse est limitée à 30 000 caractères, la même borne que le Bash de Claude Code.
- On garde le début et la fin, coupés sur des fins de ligne. La coupe indique combien de lignes manquent et comment demander la suite (grep, head, tail, sed -n, offset pour un fichier).
- C'est appliqué sur l'ordinateur de la personne, dans l'environnement serveur, sur l'`exec` de l'ordinateur cloud et sur un ordinateur prêté.
- Un fichier base64, les images et les catalogues d'outils restent entiers.

**2. Reprise automatique (Claude Code)**
- Sur le thrashing, ou sur un `prompt is too long`, le pilote ferme le processus et poursuit le même tour logique dans une session neuve.
- Cette session reçoit la reconstruction du fil et une note bornée des étapes déjà faites : la commande, le résultat et le début de la sortie de chacune. Le modèle ne refait donc pas ce qui a réussi.
- Le chat n'affiche rien. Une ligne s'ajoute dans les événements (règle des avis techniques de `shared/chat-notices.ts`).
- Le coût de la session pleine reste compté dans le tour.
- Si la session neuve déborde aussi, la personne lit un message en mots simples, sans « /clear » à taper. Le bouton Réessayer repart alors dans une session neuve au lieu de rouvrir la session pleine.

**3. Autres moteurs**
- Codex : `contextWindowExceeded` est dit en mots simples, et le tour suivant démarre un fil Codex neuf à partir du fil de discussion.
- Grok (ACP) : l'erreur passe en mots simples par `engine-errors`.

## Tests

- `server/tool-output-bound.test.ts` : une sortie énorme est bornée (ordinateur de la personne, environnement serveur), un fichier base64 reste entier.
- `server/drivers/claude.test.ts` : le thrashing simulé par le faux CLI (`[fake:context-thrash]`) déclenche la reprise automatique. Le tour finit OK, aucun runtime.error, aucun texte brut. La session neuve est lancée sans `--resume` et porte le fil et l'étape déjà faite. Un second débordement donne le message simple, et le tour suivant repart à neuf.
- `server/context-renewal.test.ts`, `claude-auth.test.ts`, `codex.test.ts` : les formulations, et le fait que le message n'est jamais classé comme une panne transitoire.
- Tests des fichiers touchés : 39 fichiers, 1257 OK. `pnpm verify:merge` suit en commentaire.

author: brianboti
body:
## What

A new package, `appdelivery`, beside `cloudinfra`. It takes an image that already exists (by digest) and will run it on machines a `cloudinfra` request already created. This PR builds steps 1 to 5 of the phase 1 plan in `docs/DELIVERY-SPEC.md` section 14: everything up to the machine session. **Nothing runs on a machine yet**; the service can plan a release end to end:

```
app-delivery plan release.yaml --config appdelivery.local.yaml --as shop-team
```

| File | Role |
|---|---|
| `models.py`, `errors.py` | Strict release contract: digest required; each env value from a literal, a request endpoint or a request secret; credential-looking literals refused; no field that could run or build anything |
| `config.py`, `appdelivery.example.yaml` | Environments with their own service accounts, allowed registries, trusted signers, approval; teams mapped to a `cloudinfra` owner |
| `infra.py` | Reads `GET /infrastructure/{id}` over HTTP only; ignores fields `cloudinfra` adds later |
| `planner.py` | Owner, READY, the team's `admin` grant on every machine, Container-Optimized OS, IAP SSH, registry and Artifact Registry reachability, bindings; every problem at once |
| `google.py`, `bindings.py`, `attest.py` | Host and per-environment tokens (IAM Credentials, 15 min), Secret Manager reads, Cosign attestation per trusted signer |
| `remote.py` | The only module that runs commands, and only `gcloud` and `cosign` |
| `cli.py` | `token`, `check-config`, `plan` |

## Why

Deploying onto what the infrastructure layer built is a separate small service, not a `cloudinfra` kind, so `cloudinfra` keeps its guarantee that it runs nothing on a company's machines. `docs/RESEARCH-2026-10-29-delivery-layer.md` checks that choice against Cloud Deploy, Google's enterprise application blueprint, the CNCF Platforms white paper, OpenGitOps and AWS's deployment pipeline reference architecture. `docs/DELIVERY-SPEC.md` is the specification, the facts checked before building (section 13) and the build plan (section 14).

`labdeploy` is not used and will be removed later, so this package has no dependency on it.

## For the reviewer

- **No `cloudinfra` code changes.** Phase 1 needs only configuration there: one read-only principal per delivery environment, and a `container-host` profile on Container-Optimized OS.
- **Boundary tests** (`tests/appdelivery/test_delivery_boundaries.py`): no import of `cloudinfra` or `labdeploy` in the package and none of `appdelivery` in either; `labdeploy` named nowhere in the package or its tests; no shared test helper or `conftest.py`; commands only in `remote.py`; and the whole delivery test directory rerun in a fresh interpreter where importing `labdeploy` fails.
- **Contract test:** the fake `cloudinfra` answer every delivery test uses is validated against `cloudinfra`'s own `InfrastructureResponse` model.
- **Google's container startup agent** (`gce-container-declaration`) stopped working on 2026-07-31; nothing here uses it.
- **Not yet proven:** four facts no Google page confirms (section 13): `gcloud compute ssh` passing stdin as an impersonated service account, sudo for that account's OS Login user on Container-Optimized OS, `base64` and bash `/dev/tcp` on the host, and the container restarting after `cloudinfra` stops and starts the machine. They are step 0, a spike on the company's project; step 6 waits on them.
- Outside the new folders: the `app-delivery` script and package in `pyproject.toml`, and two links in the README.

## Tests

- `python -m pytest tests/appdelivery -q`: 104 passed
- `python -m pytest tests -q`: 1555 passed, 5 skipped
- `python -m ruff check .`: clean

author: wjarka
body:
Closes hearsay-tools/cezarion#2194

## Summary
Move wake admission retries, delivery backoffs and retained-note memory into `workflows/run/wake-retries.ts`. Keep RunManager as the facade and preserve behavior.

## Design decision
Direct track, approved by the coordinator. No departure from the issue plan. This is a verbatim move with named operations replacing the specified inline statements in place; no test or call order changes.

## Moved names
- Fields: `wakeRetries`, `wakeBackoffs`, `retainedNotes`.
- Methods: `retryWaitAdmission`, `clearWakeBackoff`.
- Inline operations: `stopRetry`, `backoff`, `inBackoff`, `noteRetained`, `clearRetained`, `forget`, `dispose`.
- No extra helper or constant moved. Backoff calculation imports move with their only use. `wakeRetryBackoff` stays on the manager.

## Seams kept
- `wakeRetries` getter returns the same Map: `ci-wait.test.ts`, `waits-parity-cells.testkit.ts`.
- `wakeBackoffs` getter returns the same Map and native timers: `waits-wake.test.ts`, `waits-parity-cells.testkit.ts`.
- `wakeRetryBackoff` stays writable on the manager and is read through the host at use: those tests, `ci-wait.test.ts`, `ci-wait-failure-parity.test.ts`.
- `retryWaitAdmission` and `clearWakeBackoff` remain delegators. Timer callbacks reach `queueWaitWake` and `retryWaitAdmission` through manager callbacks. `run-states.test.ts` still finds the named retry.
- `owesWake` routes through the manager as the issue requires; disposed reads the shared context at use.
- No moved method reads active state; all operations work without a live session.

## Orders preserved
This is a verbatim move. The side-effect orders remain:
- Admission retry: read row, guard, create timer, unref, register; on fire remove retry, queue through manager, retry through manager on throw (`ci-wait.test.ts`; U9, U13).
- Backoff: clear previous timer, create timer using current manager setting, unref, register; on fire check identity, remove, queue through manager, retry through manager on throw (`waits-wake.test.ts`; U14, U14m, U22c).
- Clear/stop: cancel timer before map deletion. Failure cap resets delivery before stopping retry; spending admission stops retry before unpark; empty-wake retirement retains its preceding line operations (`waits-wake.test.ts`, U13/U14).
- Retained note: compare message, save changed message, then append event in facade; success removes note before marking wake (`waits-wake.test.ts`).
- Forget: cancel admission timer, remove retry, remove retained note; facade then resets delivery and removes queued/admitted wake (U9, U13, U14).
- Dispose: retry timers then retry map, backoff timers then backoff map; retained notes remain. Called after wait-watch retries and before remaining wait-watch disposal. Kept comment: “Wait records stay as they are: a later manager re-arms them from their deadlines.”

Reader sweep: searched tests and testkits for all moved fields and methods, plus docs, protocol, guards and comments for moved method names. Existing readers retain their seams. The run-state guard already scans run modules. No reader needed edits. Lowered run.ts pin to 5,991 lines (349,780 bytes).

## Experience
N/A — no user-facing UI.

## Verification
- `npm run build -w @wjarka/cezarion` → pass.
- From packages/cezar: `npx tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit`, `npx tsc -p tsconfig.test.json --noEmit`, `npx tsc -p tsconfig.scripts.json --noEmit` → pass.
- `FILE_LENGTH_UPDATE=1 npm test -- packages/cezar/src/file-length.test.ts` → 7 tests pass.
- `git fetch origin; node .github/scripts/check-clones.cjs --base origin/main --head HEAD` → no new clone.
- `node .github/scripts/check-citations.cjs` → pass.
- `npm test -- packages/cezar/src/workflows/waits-wake.test.ts packages/cezar/src/workflows/ci-wait.test.ts packages/cezar/src/workflows/ci-wait-failure-parity.test.ts packages/cezar/src/workflows/run-states.test.ts` → 4 files, 131 tests pass.
- Full local parity run skipped under the approved verbatim-move rule. CI Vitest shards passed core and workflows parity, including waits rows U9, U13, U14, U14m and U22c.
- No test or guard changed; regression-proof gate does not apply.

## Left undone
Nothing.

The coordinator merges this PR.

body:
## O que muda

Publica a aula interativa **Miocardiopatia Hipertrófica** (cardiologia) em
`vethis.com.br/Aula/Cardiologia/Miocardiopatia-Hipertrofica`.

Segue o padrão já usado por `/plano-mkt` e `/guia-gravacao`: HTML autônomo em `apps/site/public/` servido em URL limpa por um `rewrite` no `next.config.mjs`.

- `apps/site/public/Aula/Cardiologia/Miocardiopatia-Hipertrofica/`
  - `index.html` (9 slides: capa 3D, classificação, anatomia 3D com marcadores, camadas internas, histologia, fisiopatologia, crescimento assimétrico, obstrução da via de saída, revisão)
  - `img/` (4 ilustrações do professor)
  - `models/heart.txt` (modelo GLB em base64, ~10 MB, "Realistic Human Heart", CC BY 4.0)
- `next.config.mjs`: rewrite `/Aula/Cardiologia/Miocardiopatia-Hipertrofica` → `.../index.html`
- `.prettierignore`: ignora `apps/site/public/Aula` (conteúdo importado pronto, não editado no repo)

Ajustes no HTML em relação ao arquivo original: caminhos de `img/` e `models/` viraram absolutos (a URL limpa sem barra final quebraria os relativos), `lang="pt-BR"` e `charset="utf-8"`. O restante é idêntico.

## Verificação

- `pnpm format:check`, `pnpm lint`, typecheck e `next build` passam.
- Servidor standalone local: a URL responde 200, `/img/*.jpg` e `/models/heart.txt` 200, `/guia-gravacao` segue funcionando.
- Renderizado em Chromium headless: modelo 3D carrega (16 marcadores anatômicos), as 4 imagens carregam, simulações desenham, sem erros de console.

## Observações

- A página carrega `three.js` do jsDelivr e fontes do Google Fonts (CDNs externos), como no arquivo original.
- Sem `noindex`: é conteúdo de aula público. Não foi adicionada ao sitemap.

author: civilwarinfrance
body:
`build_msg('/v', '')` currently produces a message with no arguments. Both synchronous and asynchronous TCP clients use that helper, so an explicitly supplied empty string is silently dropped. The UDP client already sends it correctly. This can prevent an OSC receiver from clearing a string-valued control.

Use an empty tuple for omitted values and let explicit strings follow the normal scalar path. Update both TCP defaults together so omitted values still produce argument-free messages. Add API documentation, a changelog entry and regression tests covering literal OSC bytes, both TCP clients, the existing UDP behavior, omitted values, empty iterables, zero, false, nil and generators.

Validation:
- Original revision: 3 new tests fail; 5 tests and 7 subtests pass as controls.
- Final source and installed-wheel suites: **189 tests and 9 subtests pass**, with 92% source coverage.
- Locked Ruff lint/format and Mypy checks pass across the project and examples. The installed wheel includes its typing marker and passes the published-package type check.
- All installed pre-commit hooks pass for the changed files, including the hook's older Mypy version. Running every hook on every repository file still reports eight existing Mypy errors because its isolated environment lacks pytest; those exact errors also occur on the original revision. The project's prescribed `uv run mypy pythonosc examples` passes with its locked dependencies.
- Wheel and sdist build successfully; installed runtime and test files match the tested checkout.

Related: #95 established support for empty OSC strings; this fixes their handling in the newer shared message helper and TCP clients.

AI assistance was used to investigate, implement and test this change.

author: dovvnloading
body:
The engine's particles were one CPU emitter of flat-coloured points: a cone, a rate, a burst and five presets. This replaces them with an effects system on the same **Particles** component. Components saved before keep their look: old presets and their Rate, Burst and Loop, and Custom's own fields, all resolve to the new model.

## What an effect can do (`runtime/particleEffect.ts`)

- **Emission:** a rate, a rate per metre moved (trails laid along the path), timed bursts each cycle, loop or run once, prewarm, a start delay and a cap.
- **Shapes:**
  - point, sphere, hemisphere, cone (opening outwards), box, disc and line;
  - the **object's own model surface**, sampled by triangle area and launched along face normals;
  - surface-only to full-volume fill, random direction mixing, and a launch axis (rain and snow fall down it).
- **Start values:** lifetime, speed, size, rotation and spin ranges; a colour picked between two; inherited emitter velocity; world or local simulation space.
- **Over life:** a colour/alpha gradient and size and speed curves, baked to 64 samples.
- **Forces:** gravity, drag, wind, turbulence (a cheap swirl field) and orbit around the object's up axis.
- **Collision with the world** through physics rays, capped at 384 per emitter per step: bounce with friction, or die on hit.
- **Sub-emitters:** another Particles component on the same object fires where particles die or hit. Examples: rain that splashes, sparks that smoke.
- **Light:** an optional point light that follows how busy the effect is, with flicker. It stays in the scene, dark while idle, so lit materials never recompile.

## Simulation and rendering

- **Simulation** (`particleSimulation.ts`): flat typed arrays, live particles packed at the front, deterministic for a given random source.
- **Rendering** (`particleRenderer.ts`):
  - one instanced quad per particle, in camera-facing, stretched-along-motion, flat or upright modes, or a **ribbon** through the particles oldest first;
  - flipbook sampling, alpha or additive blending, fog that additive particles fade into, and back-to-front sorting;
  - world-space meshes that keep an identity transform under any parent.
- **Built-in sprites** (`particleSprites.ts`), drawn once on a canvas: soft, smoke (4 variants), spark, glow, ring, star, an animated 16-frame flame, droplet, snowflake, leaf, square and debris. Project textures work too, as flipbooks.
- **Eighteen presets:** smoke, fire, sparks, dust, explosion, embers, magic, rain, snow, steam, leaves, confetti, fireflies, waterfall mist, muzzle flash, shockwave, trail and debris.

## Editing and control

- **ParticlesInspector:** a preset picker that writes the full effect, and sections for every module, with gradient and curve editors and sub-emitter targets chosen among the object's other emitters.
- **Level-script nodes:** **Play**, **Stop** (optionally clearing), **Emit** (a burst) and **Get Particles**. Script commands: `ctx.particles(objectId?).play() / stop(clear?) / emit(count?)`.
- Tyre smoke and dust now run on the same simulation and renderer.

## Verified in the engine

Verified in a new **Effects Lab** level built for this. It has a station per effect, including:

- rain with splash sub-emitters;
- a trail on a Follow Spline rider;
- embers rising from a crate's own surface.

In play:

- **Rain:** about 210 drops alive instead of 350, because they die on the ground and set off about 350 live splash droplets.
- **Sparks:** stretch along their motion and stay above the ground.
- **Light:** the campfire and explosion lights bloom on the ground.
- **Frame time:** a steady 16.7 ms with every station running.

The editor previews every effect live and replays one-shots.

## Tests

- `particles.test.ts` is rewritten to cover:
  - effect resolution, including old emitters;
  - sanitizing, gradients and curves;
  - emission evenness, bursts, delay and prewarm;
  - every shape, including mesh surfaces;
  - trails and inherited velocity;
  - forces, turbulence and orbit;
  - bounce, die-on-hit and sub-emitter events;
  - `emitAt` and render values;
  - sorting, ribbons, the registry, the nodes and the script commands.
- Targeted run: 22 files, 322 tests passing.
- Typecheck, strict typecheck and diagnostics coverage pass.

author: new1direction
body:
The control room's slow reads used to run while a page waited, holding the cache lock, so every request queued behind them. These are the code surface, the supplier map, a year of git history for owners, and every file for compliance evidence. Every minute or five, a page took seconds.

## What changed
- **`background_scans.py`**: a scanner thread runs the four scans on their intervals (60 s for code and suppliers, 300 s for owners and compliance), and sooner when the repository changed.
  - Pages read the last committed result and **never wait**.
  - The one exception is the very first request, which waits for the first result, so nothing is shown empty just because it's still being read.
- **A finished scan is not automatically kept.** This is the prepare/commit check again, as in the stale-view work. Each scan fingerprints the repository (every file's path, size and modification time, plus git's HEAD, index and packed-refs) before it starts and after it ends.
  - If the fingerprint changed, the result was read while files moved, so it is **discarded** and the scan re-runs. The last good result stays in place meanwhile.
  - A repository that never holds still is retried 3 times, then left to its interval rather than spinning.
  - Errors are results too: reported, never retried in a tight loop.
- **`/api/scans`** reports, per scan: when it last committed, the revision, the duration, runs, discarded runs, any error, and whether it still describes the repository as it is now.
- `--bundle-only` runs one synchronous pass, so the golden fixtures exercise the same scan code.
- Discovery stays on the request path: it's 0.08 s with the Rust engine.
- Packaging (`install.py`), CI paths and `operating-picture.md`.

## Verification
- `python -m unittest discover -s tests`: 781 tests pass. The new `tests/test_background_scans.py` uses a scripted fingerprint and a fake clock, so each property is deterministic:
  - a result commits only when the revision held still;
  - a change during the scan discards it, keeps the last good result, and re-runs at once;
  - a repository that never holds still → 3 retries, then back off;
  - the interval applies, with an early re-run when the repository changed;
  - an error is recorded as a result;
  - the first request waits for the first result, and later ones return immediately;
  - `revision()` follows files and git but not `node_modules`;
  - end to end: all four scans commit, report no error, describe the current repository, and the first request gets its result.
- **Golden fixtures unchanged:** `golden.py check --require-rust` → 18 OK. The answers are identical; only *when* they are computed moved.
- **Measured on documenso** (about 3,000 files, 720 commits in a year): old `main` and this branch ran side by side, polled every 2 s for 75 s across the cache expiry:

  | | first load | slowest answer after it | median |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | main (Rust discovery, the default) | 6.9 s | **4.24 s** | 0.03 s |
  | this branch (Rust discovery) | 5.7 s | **0.19 s** | 0.03 s |
  | main, Python discovery | 7.0 s | 4.02 s | 0.03 s |
  | this branch, Python discovery | 7.1 s | 1.28 s | 0.03 s |

  The remaining 1.28 s with Python discovery is that discovery's own cost (0.42 s) plus contention with the scanner thread.

author: soumilb7
body:
## Why

Blind benchmark on 8 of Soumil's own clips (truth = his blind picks, 363 words):

| Labeler | WER |
|---|---|
| gpt-4o-transcribe (the current label model, randomly truncates) | 13.5% |
| Turbo, as Slive typed it | 4.4% |
| gpt-transcribe + Custom words + context | 2.8% |
| OpenAI whisper-1 | 1.7% |
| **Consensus of gpt-transcribe, whisper-1 and Slive's typed text** | **1.4%** |

## What

**Backend: `POST /label_consensus`** (`flowy/label_consensus.py`)
- gpt-transcribe (`languages[]=en`, Custom words as `keywords[]`, generic context plus the Vocabulary sentence) and whisper-1 (`language=en`) run in parallel on a 16-bit copy of the clip.
- The label is the medoid of those two plus Slive's typed text. Ties go gpt-transcribe > whisper-1 > typed. When candidates say the same words, the best-formatted text wins.
- Typed text is never a label on its own; if one API fails, the other API's text is used.
- 429/5xx/timeouts retry 3× with backoff. A rejected key or exhausted quota is a distinct fatal error.
- Returns `text`, `chosen`, `agreement` (0–1), `candidates` and `prompt`.

**App: "Best — 3-way consensus" recipe, first in the Ground truth picker**
- **Label everything · N clips · ~$X · ~Y min** covers every clip with audio and no hand label whose label isn't already consensus, so old gpt-4o/gpt-audio labels get upgraded.
- New `LabelRun` engine (singleton): the run continues when you leave the Data page or close Settings.
  - 4 clips in flight; a failed clip doesn't stop the run ("Retry N failed").
  - A key, quota or dead-backend error stops it with a clear message.
  - Stop, then Label everything again, resumes the run.
  - The Mac stays awake while it runs.
- Labels get the Custom-words spelling pass (`VocabularyCorrector`) and are tagged `consensus · <chosen>`. `llmAgreement` is stored, and rows below 0.8 surface under "needs a look".
- `finalText` (hand labels) is never touched.
- Index writes are coalesced (≤1 rewrite per 2 s, flushed at run end, on Stop and on quit). Same JSONL format; `llmAgreement` is omitted for other labels.
- The other recipes keep working through the same engine.

## Tests

- Backend pytest 96/96, including the new `test_label_consensus.py`: medoid, tie-break, fallback, auth/quota mapping, hotword parsing.
- Swift release build is clean; `--self-test` 325/325.
- Live check: the backend labeler on the 8 bench clips scored **1.4% WER** against the blind truth (agreement 0.90–1.00).

## Notes

- Add frequent missing terms (e.g. "z-docs") to Custom words. A speaker description in the Vocabulary context sentence also helps gpt-transcribe.
- Follow-up: when whisper-1 or the typed text wins on slightly different words, the label can come back lowercase without punctuation (2 of 8 clips here). A formatting-transfer step would keep the label style consistent.
- Estimated cost is about $0.0105 per audio minute.

author: nicoputten
body:
Nico ("Yes, fix now"): the Discord page's test posts still showed the old text board, because the bot's samples carry no site image. The site now draws sample pictures with the same renderer as the real ones and the bot's own made-up names (Test Friend, Another Test, Testy McTestface).

## The images
Fixed ids, behind the bot token like every card (`GET /api/bot/v1/cards/sample-<name>.png`; an unknown name is `404`):

| id | Size | What |
|---|---|---|
| `sample-board` | 800 × 560 | the daily board: a real day's five columns, Test Friend with three done, Another Test a PvP Virgin |
| `sample-feat-big` | 800 × 400 | Testy McTestface, Stone Guard, rank 6, first in the group (the bot's feat sample) |
| `sample-feat-strip` | 800 × 240 | Testy McTestface, first blood (with the designer's PvP icon once #136 is in) |
| `sample-recap-header` | 1200 × 400 | Warmonger, Testy McTestface, 12 honorable kills |
| `sample-recap-zone` | 800 × 450 | Bloodbath zone, Stranglethorn Vale, 12 kills, with the map credit |

## The contract (`docs/BOT-API.md`, under `test`)
The `test` event's `data` gains `images` per kind, so the bot needs no URL knowledge:
- `doomsday`: `{ board }`
- `feats`: `{ feat, strip }`
- `recap`: `{ award, zone }`
- `posts`: none

It's optional within v1: an older bot ignores `images`.

**What the bot must read (its follow-up):**
- `images.board`: the board embed's image, instead of the text table
- `images.feat`: the feat post's card; `images.strip` is optional, for a strip
- `images.award` and `images.zone`: the award embed's image and the stat card's map

Each one is fetched like a real card and attached as a file.

## Tests
`tests/server/sampleCards.test.ts`:
- every id a test event names resolves
- every sample renders a PNG of its size, without a BattleTag
- an unknown name gives nothing

`npm run lint` and `npm test` pass. No site screen changes.

author: wabarurse
body:
Updating Orca replaced the executable but left existing orchestrator daemons running old code. The inspected sessions still loaded `ef24e49` even though the installed binary was `a0a4ce6`, so they also missed the per-project account selection already merged in #168. Separately, a large conversation could repeatedly exhaust the whole-job summary deadline after switching to a smaller model.

- After a successful global `orca pull`, invoke the newly installed binary to schedule daemon reloads. A detached helper queues stops between turns, waits without force-killing, and verifies the replacement build. Durable project-scoped handoff records recover interrupted reloads; concurrent updates serialize. `orca reload` retries activation without rebuilding.
- Detect client/daemon build mismatches before accepting new messages or model/context commands. Preserve conversations and queued input; leave active workers/reviewers running and explain when the TUI needs reopening.
- Time out each summary request instead of the entire multi-part job, reuse completed unpublished summaries, and back off repeated failures. Cancel stale summary work and reset backoff when account, model, or context window changes. Bound each source part to the selected model's input budget.
- Attach the selected non-secret account identity and sanitized HTTP status to model failure diagnostics. Verify named profiles load without a default login; keep explicit account selection and no automatic account fallback.

The rolling deadline/reuse work incorporates Richard Huang's existing unpublished commit `12cc8e9`, preserving its authorship. Open PRs #173–#175 address other features; this builds on the merged account fix rather than duplicating it. A few existing tests had stale transcript/status and history-read expectations; the failures were reproduced on unchanged `a0a4ce6` and the assertions now match current behavior. Removed one unused barrel type export to restore the existing organization limit.

Validation: `bun run check`, `bun run build`, 362 passing tests across 27 selected suites (each suite in an isolated process/home), compiled CLI/runner and detached-helper checks, plus an isolated real daemon-to-tmux restart into the newly built executable. No live user session was restarted and no real provider requests were sent. The entire repository test suite was not run.

First upgrade from an older updater: after merging and pulling this version, run `orca reload` once, then reopen TUIs. Subsequent pulls schedule activation automatically. Running workers/reviewers finish on their loaded builds; newly launched agents use the installed binary. Progress and failures are recorded in `~/.orca/.runtime/updates.log`. Incompatible storage/protocol upgrades still require the release's offline procedure.

author: criew
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"criew"} -->
_Requested by **Christoph** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01FeRCSnbPwBFFkXBcNTDM2Z?thread=cmsg_01FeRCSnbPwBFFkXBcNTDM2ZWxPtWnryQQso9uK2iCS5zf)_

## Zusammenfassung

Eine Dropbox-Bibliothek kann jetzt **Team-Ordner** aus `team/namespaces/list` als Umfang wählen, auch solche, die kein einzelnes Mitgliedskonto sieht. Dazu gibt es eine zweite Art von Dropbox-Zugang: die **Team-App**.

**Anmeldung (Zugang)**
- Neue Vorgabe `teamApp` am Zugang, nur am Zugang setzbar (`onlyOnProfile`). Sie wird als „Team-App (Zustimmung einer Team-Administration)“ angezeigt.
- Ein zweites OAuth-Anmeldemuster ist nicht möglich, weil der SPI je Anmeldeart genau ein SignIn kennt. Darum ist die Team-App eine Vorgabe.
- Neuer SPI-Haken `SourceConnector#signInScopes(ConnectorData profileDefaults)`. Mit ihm fragt die Zustimmung unter einer Team-App zusätzlich `files.team_metadata.read`, `team_data.member` und `team_info.read` an.
- Eigene Scopes eines Zugangs haben weiter Vorrang.
- Wenn sich die effektiv angefragten Scopes ändern, gilt das in `ConnectionProfileService.plan` als geänderte Registrierung.
- Festgehalten in ADR-0038, Entscheidung 7 („Scopes aus einer Vorgabe“).
- Neuer SPI-Haken `SourceConnector#checkProfileScopes(String, ConnectorData)` (Standard: ohne Wirkung). `ConnectionProfileService.validate` ruft ihn beim Anlegen und Ändern eines Zugangs mit eigenen Scopes. Dropbox lehnt eigene Scopes einer Team-App ab, denen ein Team-Scope fehlt; der Zugang wird dann nicht gespeichert.

**Ordnerauswahl**
- Unter einer Team-App listet `browse` die Namespaces vom Typ `team_folder` (bis 10 Seiten, danach `cutAt`). Der Schlüssel ist die Namespace-ID.
- In der Einrichtung zeigt die Zeile „Verbindung“ statt des Schalters „Teambereich lesen“ einen Hinweis.
- Der Umfang nutzt den vorhandenen `ScopePicker` mit einer flachen Auswahlquelle. Von Hand lässt sich eine Namespace-ID aus Ziffern eintragen.
- Gespeichert wird `sourceSettings.teamFolders: [{id, name}]` mit 1 bis 50 Einträgen. Ein Team-Ordner ohne Team-App wird abgelehnt, ebenso Ordnerpfade oder ein Team-Bereich unter einer Team-App.

**Lesen**
- Je Lauf einmal `team/token/get_authenticated_admin` (liefert die Admin-`team_member_id`) und `team/namespaces/list`.
- Danach liest OPAA jeden Team-Ordner mit `Dropbox-API-Path-Root: {".tag":"namespace_id","namespace_id":"…"}` und `Dropbox-API-Select-Admin`.
- Die Identität im Team-Ordner ist `dropbox:ns:<id>/<path_lower>`. Ein Team-Ordner, der fehlt oder kein Team-Ordner ist, ist nicht erreichbar; der Bestand bleibt.
- Weist Dropbox das Token einer Mitglieds-App an einer Team-Route mit 400 ab, meldet OPAA: „Dropbox nimmt die Zustimmung nicht als Team-App an; die Quelle muss von einer Team-Administration neu verbunden werden.“
- Nur die Klartext-400 „access token you provided is for …“ ergibt diese Meldung; andere 400er bleiben die allgemeine Meldung.
- Fehlt der App ein Scope (`missing_scope`), nennt die Meldung den Scope, den Dropbox in `required_scope` angibt.
- Bricht die Team-Ordner-Liste mit `has_more` ohne Cursor ab, endet das als vorübergehender Befund statt als Fehler.
- Verbindungstest: ein Befund je Team-Ordner, mit Namen. Die Kontoanzeige nennt die Team-Administration.
- „Original öffnen“ funktioniert auch für Dokumente in Team-Ordnern.

**Weiteres**
- Fakten-Manifest `compliance/manifest/outbound.yaml` (ADR-0052) nachgezogen: `source-dropbox` liest mit einer Team-App als Team-Administration. Das Token könnte jedes Mitglied lesen, OPAA liest aber nur die gewählten Team-Ordner.
- Handbuch `konnektoren/dropbox.md`: neue Abschnitte 1 und 2.1, außerdem Abschnitte 3, 8, 9 und 11. Übersicht in `konnektoren/README.md` angepasst.
- Keine Änderung an der OpenAPI-Spec: `sourceSettings` ist ein freies Objekt, und `browse` ist typneutral.
- Keine Flyway-Migration.

## Zugehörige Issues

Closes #2472

Teil von Epic #2146.

## Art der Änderung

- [ ] Bugfix
- [x] Neues Feature
- [x] Dokumentation
- [ ] Refactoring
- [ ] CI/Build

## Wirkung auf Daten und Behördenunterlagen

- [ ] Neue oder geänderte personenbezogene Daten oder Protokollereignisse
- [ ] Neue Sichtbarkeit: Daten werden für weitere Rollen oder Personen sichtbar

body:
## What and why

First step of the slice for #250: the design prompt for the driver's arrival and the unreachable customer (`docs/design/prompts/18-driver-arrival-and-unreachable.md`). The technical lead answered on #250 that leaving these steps out was not on purpose: FR-038 (P0) and acceptance test T-25 make the driver record two contact attempts and wait the full 10 minutes before a job can fail, and the backend and contract already do it. The app cannot, because the customer step records arrival, start of unloading and end of unloading in one tap, so there is no moment in which the driver has arrived and is waiting.

The prompt covers the arrival step (U1, U2), the attempts and the wait (U3, with a confirm sheet U3-S), the failed outcome (U4) and the problem report entry (U5), for the rider and the driver app, with the honesty rules and a screen-to-endpoint table. It follows the format of prompt 17.

The PR also lists the gap, with the pilot fallback (the "Customer not reachable" problem report and the dispatcher's "Fail delivery"), in `docs/process/linking-handoff.md` and `docs/features/partner-app.md`, as the lead asked.

Refs #250 (does not close it: the design, G2, adapters and screens follow)
Lane: C · Rider and driver jobs

author: dtodorowa
body:
Closes #547

## Summary

```diff
 packages/civicos/src/lib/
 ├── services/
-│   └── session.svelte.ts    # cache + comhairle writes + landing error + setApi()
+│   ├── session.svelte.ts    # cache only, no API client
+│   ├── join.ts              # join, enterCampaign, signUpForUpdates
+│   ├── profile.ts           # saveProfile, saveDemographicResponse
+│   └── participant.ts       # + knownParticipant(): server answer, else cache
 └── utils/
+    └── poll-checkpoints.ts  # resumeProgress / recordVote, lifted from poll/+page.svelte
```

The participant is settled once, in the `[campaign]` layout load. That load also builds the `joinContext` that every write takes:

```diff
 [campaign]/+layout.ts
   session.useCampaign(campaign.id, preview)
+  knownParticipant = knownParticipant(server answer, cache)   # userId, zipCode, isReturning
+  joinContext      = { api, conversationId, preview }
```

The four callers that each decided between the server answer and the cache now read the result:

| Caller | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `CampaignLanding` isReturning | `participant?.zipCode \|\| (!resolved && session.hasSession)` | `knownParticipant.isReturning` |
| `CampaignLanding` zip seed | `participant?.zipCode \|\| session.zipCode` | `knownParticipant.zipCode` |
| `poll` Polis xid | `participant?.userId ?? session.userId ?? random` | `knownParticipant.userId ?? random` |
| `events/[slug]` isRegistered | server answer, else `session.isRegisteredForEvent` in the component | same rule, in `+page.ts` |

The four email signup sites (landing join, landing email, `EmailPanelContent`, events list) all go through `join.ts`. `setApi()` is gone, which drops one of the two ordering rules. `useCampaign()` stays: the session still needs to know which Campaign's record is current.

## Evidence

- New tests: `poll-checkpoints.test.ts` (12), `join.test.ts` (9), `knownParticipant` in `participant.test.ts` (5).
- `vitest --project server`: 235 passed.
- `pnpm --filter civic-os check`: 3 errors, the api-client zod floor.
- `pnpm --filter civic-os lint`: clean.
- `/utah` renders on the dev server.
- Not clicked through end to end. I had no local comhairle, so join, the checkpoints and the email signups were not exercised against a real backend.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way

No storage keys or data shapes change. A revert restores the old module.

**Blast Radius:** participant flow

Joining, the poll's checkpoint pauses, About You saves and every email signup go through new code. Behaviour changes on purpose in two places:

- Email signup creates a guest account only when nobody is signed in. The landing page used to check for a zip too, so an email-only participant who signed up again got a second guest account. The events list used to send the signup with no account behind it for a visitor who had not joined; it now joins them first, like the landing page does.
- `invalidate('civicos:participant')` now runs only after a join that succeeded. The landing email path used to run it after a failed join too.

author: bi-metrik
body:
## Qué hace

Los registros nuevos de Valida autoservicio aceptan los **Términos de Uso v2.2**, el texto de Emilio que aprobó Mauricio el 2026-10-29 (`proyectos/metrik/valida/docs/legal/terminos-valida-v2.2-autoservicio.md`). Los Términos ahora dicen lo que el código ya hace desde #1322: si el pago se reversa, el plan se cierra en el acto.

Cambios de texto (son los únicos que hay entre la v2.1 y la v2.2):
- encabezado: «Versión 2.2»;
- 3.6: frase final nueva, «Si un pago ya hecho se reversa, aplica la cláusula 11.3.»;
- 11.2: «por falta de pago **o por reversión del pago**»;
- 11.3 nueva: «Reversión del pago».

## Archivos

- `src/lib/valida-registro/terminos-plan.ts`: `PARTE_I_ORDEN` (encabezado) y `PARTE_II_TERMINOS` al texto v2.2, `version: 'v2.2'` y nota de la v2.2 en el comentario de cabecera.
- `src/lib/valida-registro/terminos-plan.test.ts`: huella nueva de la Parte II (`2c3e137b…f532`, 30.433 caracteres) y una prueba nueva para 3.6, 11.2 y 11.3.
- `condiciones.test.ts` y `cobro-registro-e2e.test.ts`: lo que guarda un registro nuevo pasa a `terminos-auto-2.2` / `v2.2`. Los fixtures de filas ya guardadas con `2.0`/`2.1` no se tocan.
- Nota de memoria de Max.

**Copia literal comprobada.** Un script compara el .md, del título a la 16.6, contra `PARTE_I_ORDEN + separador + PARTE_II_TERMINOS`. Antes del cambio, el código coincide letra por letra con la v2.1 (misma huella que fijaba la prueba). Después, coincide letra por letra con la v2.2. No se cambió ningún otro texto legal.

## SQL

**No hay SQL ni migración.** Un cliente nuevo queda en la v2.2 sin filas a mano:
- el registro guarda `terminos_version`, `terminos_texto` y `terminos_sha256` en `valida_registros` a partir de `TERMINOS_PLAN`;
- al activar, `valida_activar_autogestion` crea la fila de `documentos_contractuales_versiones` (alcance `cliente`, por `suscripcion_id`) con esa versión.

Una pestaña de registro que se cargó antes del deploy manda `terminos-auto-2.1`. El servidor la rechaza por versión desactualizada (`registro-servidor.ts:148`), que es lo que ya pasa con cualquier cambio de versión.

`permiteCobroAlConfirmar` solo mira la versión de las Condiciones (siguen en 2.1), así que el cobro al confirmar no cambia.

## Los clientes que ya aceptaron la v2.1: la re-aceptación NO está resuelta

La 13.1 de autoservicio exige dos cosas: aviso al correo con 30 días y nueva aceptación. Mientras el cliente no acepte, **rige la v2.1**. Este PR no toca a esos clientes. Esto también incluye a los que están hoy en prueba: aceptaron la v2.1 en el registro, y su activación registra la v2.1.

ONE tiene un flujo de modificación por aviso (`20261007150000_terminos_modificacion_por_aviso.sql`, `modificacionesPorAceptar` / `cubiertaPorAviso` en `src/lib/valida-api/terminos.ts`, `avisoModificacion` en `src/app/(app)/valida/page.tsx`, `src/lib/valida-cda/modificacion-terminos.ts`). Se hizo para la v1.4 de los CDA y **no alcanza tal cual**:

1. **El efecto legal es el contrario (bloqueante).** En los CDA, la 13.1 dice que el cambio rige «lo acepte o no», y así lo dicen `textosAvisoModificacion` y `textoQuienAceptaModificacion`. En autoservicio, sin aceptación no rige. Publicar la v2.2 con `rige_por_aviso = true` le mostraría al cliente un texto falso. La mecánica de la base sí sirve: la versión por aviso no pausa a quien aceptó la anterior, la designada la puede aceptar desde la publicación, y el soporte por `suscripcion_id` llegó en `20261016100100`. Lo que falta son textos del aviso propios de autoservicio (o un modo «por aceptación»), escritos por Emilio y pasados por Vera. Complejidad: **baja-media** (textos según el slug, más pruebas de render).
2. **Falta el correo de aviso con 30 días.** El flujo de los CDA avisa solo en la plataforma (`avisos_modificacion_vistos`). La 13.1 de autoservicio dice «aviso previo al correo del Cliente». Hace falta un envío por Resend al correo de notificaciones de la Orden, con constancia (id del envío, fecha) y sin duplicados. Complejidad: **media**.
3. **Falta el documento v2.2 de cada empresa.** Los Términos de autoservicio llevan la Orden (Parte I) de cada empresa. Por cada suscripción viva en v2.1 hay que armar el v2.2 lleno (su Orden más la Parte II nueva y su huella), generar el PDF, subirlo sin upsert e insertar la fila con `suscripcion_id`, `rige_por_aviso`, `reemplaza_version_id`, `publicada_at` y `vigente_desde` ≥ publicación + 30 días. Esto pide un script de publicación con ensayo, como `sql/valida-cda/2026-10-07_terminos-v1.4-por-aviso.sql`, pero generado por suscripción. Complejidad: **media**.
4. **Falta una prueba de punta a punta.** Hay que probar que la designada de una cuenta autoservicio (`aceptante_designado_id` = quien se registró) acepta la v2.2 por la plataforma sobre una suscripción, y que la constancia queda bien en `aceptaciones_terminos`. Hoy no está probado para autoservicio. Complejidad: **baja**.

**Tensión legal abierta (para Emilio, no es de código).** Desde #1322 el corte por reverso aplica también a clientes con la v2.1. Su contrato no tiene la 11.3, y la 11.1 pide aviso previo para suspender por falta de pago. El frontmatter de la v2.2 trae otra nota: la terminación a los 30 días de suspensión (11.2) no está construida en ONE para ningún caso.

Consulta de solo lectura para saber a cuántos alcanza (la corre la sesión principal):
```sql
select d.version, count(*) from public.documentos_contractuales_versiones d
 where d.slug = 'terminos-uso-valida-autogestion' and d.suscripcion_id is not null
 group by d.version;
select terminos_version, estado, count(*) from public.valida_registros
 where terminos_version is not null group by 1, 2;
```

## Verificación

- vitest de `src/lib/valida-registro`, `valida-api`, `valida-cda`, `suscripciones-producto`, `src/app/(app)/valida` y `src/app/(marketing)/valida`: 59 archivos, **887/887**.
- eslint de los 4 archivos tocados: limpio.
- `tsc --noEmit`: ningún error en lo tocado. Los únicos errores locales son de paquetes que faltan en el `node_modules` del checkout principal (`ai`, `@ai-sdk/anthropic`, `happy-dom`) y no tienen relación con este cambio. El typecheck de CI es el que vale.

No se mergea desde aquí. No toca la base.

author: lucasmagalhaees
body:
## O que muda

A IA passa a guardar memória de acusações, defesas e contradições, manter blefes coerentes e fazer campanhas antes de votar. Os NPCs ganham falas por personalidade e contexto, inclusive sobre votos anteriores. Governos consideram maioria provável e próximas presidências.

O caderno permite marcar suspeitos e guardar motivos privados como fato observado ou palpite, separados da ata pública. Acusações têm feedback visível; o fim destaca até três momentos decisivos. Investigação usa lupa, eliminação usa arma estilizada com recuo, clarão e fumaça. O card Sim brasileiro fica apenas verde e amarelo.

## Por quê

Pedidos da pessoa para melhorar IA, UI/UX, influência social e clareza das consequências. Preserva a main e as mudanças do PR #36.

## Interpretações que precisei fazer

- Notas são privadas, limitadas a 280 caracteres por motivo e nunca entram na View dos NPCs. “Fato observado” é uma classificação da pessoa, não uma confirmação de papel.
- Campanhas têm até duas falas de NPCs, uma por NPC, e não bloqueiam voto humano. As falas influenciam crenças, respeitando a informação de cada lugar.
- Reações e feedback não revelam segredos. A arma não mostra ferimentos; áudio e movimento reduzido respeitam as opções existentes.
- As falas são escolhidas pelo histórico público, sem rede, modelo de linguagem ou sorte extra. Consultar uma fala antiga não a modifica.
- Decisões D30–D34 documentadas. Nenhum merge ou deploy está incluído nesta tarefa.

## Testes existentes que mudei

- Os testes de turno agora permitem campanhas antes da votação e verificam o retorno à votação humana ou automática.
- O caso de repetição verifica a perda moderada e limitada de credibilidade do acusador, sem converter repetição em prova contra o alvo.
- E2E confere motivos privados, persistência, texto escapado, feedback e as animações de poderes.
- A checagem de fala do NPC usa seu autor no histórico e no log, pois as frases não são mais limitadas a “Confio em”/“Desconfio de”.
- A passagem pela votação também é verificada no momento do clique, com os dois botões e contraste mínimo: evita perder essa observação quando bots a tempo zero mudam de fase.
- O primeiro rascunho falhou por essas duas checagens antigas. A medição do CI já estava em 97,1% das funções e 97,7% do código. Nenhum mínimo foi reduzido.

## Evidência

Saída completa de `scripts/verify.sh` (ambiente com PYTHONPATH e PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH em /tmp):

```
ok     types      
ok     build      ✓ built in 239ms
ok     docs       216/216 documentation claims hold
ok     core       258/258 checks passed without a browser
ok     unit       258/258 checks passed
