author: positonic
body:
## Why

On `/w/clear/metrics` every contributor except James showed "—" for PRs merged and commits. PRs and commits are credited by matching the author's GitHub login to a member, and logins came only from a member's **own** GitHub integration in the workspace. Installing the GitHub App records only the installer, and members had no other way to add a login, so in Clear only James could ever be credited.

## What

**Workspace-set GitHub usernames**
- Owners and admins see "Set GitHub username" under each member's name in the Contributors table. A popover lets them set, change or remove it, and accepts `@login` or a `github.com/login` URL.
- Stored as an `IntegrationUserMapping` on the workspace's GitHub App installation. That's the same pairing `GitHubActivityService.resolveUserForLogin` already uses for feed attribution. **No migration.**
- It applies to this workspace only, because nobody has verified the login. A member's own connected account still wins, and it shows read-only.
- `resolveGithubIdentities` (in `memberLogins.ts`) returns the login and its source. `resolveGithubLogins` and the standup-draft `resolveGithubLogin` both go through it, so the Metrics roll-up, the member filter, Contributors and standup drafts all agree.
- New mutation `github.setMemberGithubLogin`: owner/admin only, and the target must be a current member. Setting a login replaces that member's previous one. A login already mapped to someone else (compared case-insensitively) moves to this member.

**Contributors selection**
- Ticking a member no longer hides the other rows, so you can keep ticking. The header shows "(n selected)".
- The contributor chart draws every ticked member, including ones idle in the chosen scope, instead of only the top five. Manual legend picks reset when the selection changes.

## Not in this PR

PR events for a repo are stored for only the **first** workspace that tracks it (`findIntegrationForRepo` uses `findFirst`, and `GitHubActivity` is unique on `(externalId, eventType)`). ADR-0022 says rows should be stored once per tracking workspace. If Clear's repos are also tracked by another workspace, Clear has no PR rows to credit at all. That needs a prod data check and a migration, so it's a separate change.

## Testing
- Unit: `memberLogins.test.ts` (new: normalising, which source wins, set/clear/reassign, invalid login, no installation); `SprintAnalyticsService.contributions` (credits PRs to a workspace-set username, and an own account wins); `github.test.ts` (member refused, non-member target refused, admin allowed); `draftAnswers` (a workspace-set login drafts commits).
- `tsc`, eslint on the changed files, and `tokens:check` are clean. Full unit suite passed in pre-commit.
- Not verified in a browser. Locally, an admin should see the "Set GitHub username" link and popover.

Closes #3305.

A sum variant with a payload was recorded in the union table as the declared type of the same name, so `Weakened { name: "x" }` passed as an `Event` and fell through the match at run time. El 27/10 Neon pasó su cuota y la tienda estuvo caída ~7 horas. author: mrappard
body:
Part of #2883. Two commits: a general collection-hash change (`9402135a`), then the handler (`478b5eda`).

## Changes in this pull request

Adds `WarcIO` for WARC files (`application/warc`). It follows "Embedding manifests into WARC files" and its validation clauses, new in C2PA 2.5. The handler is an experimental feature behind a new non-default `unstable_warc` flag, registered in `docs/experimental-features.md` and `docs/supported-formats.md`.

### 1. Handler-provided collection hash members (`9402135a`)

WARC is bound with a collection data hash, but its members are the file's own records, not ZIP entries or files on disk. This commit adds:

- **`AssetCollectionHash`** (`asset_io.rs`): an optional handler capability that reports `(uri, hash)` for each member of an asset, and the `AssetIO::asset_collection_hash_ref` accessor.
- **`CollectionHash::gen_hash_from_members` and `verify_members_hash`:** generate a collection hash from those members, and verify one against them. Members and `uris` entries must correspond one to one (the bijection 2.5 requires), and every hash must match.
- **Signing (`store_io.rs`):** a handler that provides members gets a collection hash instead of a data hash. The manifest's own part isn't a member, so no placeholder pass is needed.
- **Verifying (`claim_verify.rs`):** the members come from the handler, and any failure is reported as `assertion.collectionHash.mismatch`, as 2.5 specifies for duplicate IDs, unmatched records and decompression limits.

ZIP and folder collections are unchanged. This works with either wire format for `uris`: #2809 changes only its serialization, not the `uris` map these methods use.

### 2. WARC handler (`478b5eda`)

- **The manifest record:** the Manifest Store is the block of a record with `WARC-Type: c2pa-provenance` and `Content-Type: application/c2pa`, with a fresh `WARC-Record-ID` and `WARC-Date` and no `WARC-Target-URI`. It's always the last record, and updating the manifest removes it and appends its replacement. More than one such record is treated as no manifest.
- **Members:** every other record is a member, keyed by its `WARC-Record-ID` without the angle brackets and hashed over its uncompressed bytes, from the version line through the two closing CRLFs.
- **Rejected input:** duplicate record IDs are an error, and a block whose length doesn't match its `Content-Length` is rejected.
- **Compression:** plain and gzip-compressed WARCs are supported, with one record per gzip member or several. Records are decompressed before hashing, with a 1 GiB per-member limit (the "implementation-defined maximum" 2.5 asks for). In a compressed file the C2PA record is written as its own member, so it can be replaced. `.warc.gz` is read and written with the format `warc`.
- **Dependency:** `flate2`, already a dev-dependency, becomes an optional dependency enabled by `unstable_warc`.
- **Version line:** a new record uses the same version line (`WARC/1.0` or `WARC/1.1`) as the file's other records.

Not supported: WARC-zstd, since c2pa-rs has no zstd dependency. Such files are refused as an unsupported type.

### Tests

- **Unit tests:** ten for WARC. They cover:
  - record placement and headers;
  - members excluding the C2PA record, with no member changing when the manifest is added or replaced;
  - per-record and whole-file gzip hashing the same as plain;
  - generating and verifying a collection hash, including rejection of a changed record and of an extra unlisted record;
  - duplicate IDs and two C2PA records;
  - a `Content-Length` mismatch, plain and gzip;
  - the version line, removal, and zstd.
- **Full suite:** passes with `unstable_warc` (1,304 library tests plus all integration and doc tests). Clippy is clean with and without the feature.
- **End to end:** WARC files signed through `Builder` validate in c2pa-rs. An independent checker recomputes every record hash against the 2.5 text and agrees. A changed record fails with `assertion.collectionHash.mismatch`. These files are proposed for c2pa-org/public-testfiles.

## Checklist
- [x] This PR represents a single feature, fix, or change.
- [x] All applicable changes have been documented.
- [x] Any `TO DO` items (or similar) have been entered as GitHub issues and the link to that issue has been included in a comment.

author: wsmoses
body:
A gather clamps each start index into its operand, so a grid of lanes that runs past the end of a one-dimensional operand reads the last element there. `gather_op_canon` now pads the operand with that element to the grid's reach (rounded up to whole blocks of the largest stride, so that the padded operand factors by the grid's strides) and reads it in bounds: the grid analysis then turns the gather into a reshape and slice as it does for a grid that fits, and XLA fuses the pad into the read. The reach is computed from the index's iota-like terms before anything is built; the pad and the slice of the last element are erased again if the analysis refuses the gather. Grids that start before the operand are left alone.

Where it shows up: a kernel launched over whole blocks of lanes reads its vectors this way. CEED BP6/4's apply launches 1360 blocks of 256 lanes over a vector of 2738019 (reach 2785279) and its 16 such gathers per iteration (`[.., 2048 b + 256 c + t]`, `c = 0..7`) were `wrapped_slice`/gather kernels of their own. Over the exec modules of the 107 paper cases, 23 gathers fold (`results/sg35/replay_overrun3`); the rest of the overrunning class carry a loop-carried offset (separate).

Two goldens of `gather_iota_clamped_to_slice` change form: the clamped slices are now `slice` + `pad` with the last element instead of `slice` + `broadcast` + `concatenate` (same values, one op fewer).

author: jhonabreul
body:
#### Description
The Python example on the volatility "Model Structure" page fails the `examples-check` mypy step:

```
error: Signature of "get_history_requirements" incompatible with supertype "QuantConnect.Securities.Volatility.BaseVolatilityModel"  [override]
```

Cause: the override returns `Iterable[HistoryRequest]` while the stubs type the base return as `Sequence[HistoryRequest]`, and an override cannot widen the return type.

The fix:
- `MyVolatilityModel.get_history_requirements` returns `list[HistoryRequest]` and wraps the `super()` result in `list(...)`.
- The model is attached with `set_volatility_model(...)` instead of assigning `volatility_model`. Assigning the property converts a Python subclass of `BaseVolatilityModel` to its C# base, so the Python `update` is never called. `set_volatility_model` wraps the Python object.

The option pricing "Model Structure" page is left as is. Its mypy error comes from the stub for `CurrentPriceOptionPriceModel` carrying the obsolete three-argument `evaluate`, and is fixed in Lean by marking that override obsolete so the stubs drop it (QuantConnect/Lean#9995). Switching the example to `OptionPriceModel` is not an option: it is abstract and Python.NET cannot instantiate a subclass of it.

#### Related Issue
N/A. Found in the scheduled "Test Code Blocks" workflow.

#### Motivation and Context
Users copying the example get the same mypy error in their editor, and the property-assignment form silently runs the base model instead of the custom one.

#### Types of changes
- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
- [ ] Refactor (non-breaking change which improves implementation)
- [ ] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)
- [ ] Non-functional change (xml comments/documentation/etc)

#### Checklist:
- [x] My code follows the code style of this project.
- [x] I have read the **CONTRIBUTING** [document](https://github.com/QuantConnect/Lean/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md).
- [x] My branch follows the naming convention `bug-<issue#>-<description>` or `feature-<issue#>-<description>`

Tested:
- The Python block re-checked with the `examples-check` imports and `mypy.ini` against `quantconnect-stubs` 18146 and mypy 2.3.1: fails before, passes after.
- Backtest with the example model on SPY daily, 2013-10-07 to 2013-10-11: `volatility_model = ...` gives 0 calls to the Python `update`; `set_volatility_model(...)` gives 5.
- Same backtest calling the four-argument `get_history_requirements` directly: the `super()` call succeeds and returns a `list` with one request.

author: adamdhickey-collab
body:
Adam: "these headings are too small on mobile."

The heading in the screenshot is a `.writing-measure h2`, the section head of the articles, The Shortlist, and the cockpit write-up. That column steps its h2s down to `--type-subsection`, so on a phone they set at **24**, over 18px Montserrat. Every other h2 on the site is 28 there. With Crimson's small x-height, 24 read barely larger than the sentence under it.

**The change:** `.writing-measure h2` takes `max(var(--type-subsection), var(--text-3xl))`.

- **Below about 752px:** 28, the floor every other h2 already has.
- **Above that:** the ramp is unchanged, so the step down still holds on a desktop (34 against 48).
- **The phone ladder** on those 18 pages is now the site's own, 34 · 28 · 24. Page titles and every other heading are untouched.

Two larger options were weighed and set aside:
- **The whole ladder up a step** (40 · 34 · 28). 15 of 36 page titles would gain a line, including the homepage hero at 430.
- **Every h2 at 34.** That ties the page titles' 34, which TYPOGRAPHY.md allows only on the homepage.

**Measured** on all 36 pages against main at 282b639d, at eight widths:

| width | essay h2 | other elements that moved |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 320, 375 | 24 → 28 | 0 |
| 430 | 24.34 → 28 | 0 |
| 600 | 26.27 → 28 | 0 |
| 768, 1024, 1280 | unchanged | 0 |

At 375, 18 of the heads take one more line, which is what a bigger head does.

**Also in this change**

## Summary
Player death gets two things, packaged as P2:
- **A2a (C20b):** durable one-item primitives move the dropped item to the death cell or burn an Amulet of Loss. They live in migration `0531_player_death_item_primitives.sql` and `durability/player_death_items.rs`. Death drops use the loop-drop ref and retire with their contents on world reset.
- **B3:** the experience lost at death follows the owner's rule. Each death costs 100% of (exp(L+1) − exp(L)). Discounts are additive: −30% for promotion, −8% per regular blessing (up to 7), then Bless 6/9/12%, with a floor. The loss is capped at the experience held. Skills and magic level never drop.

## Reason
These are wave A rows A2a/C20b and B3 from `docs/architecture/reviews/OTERYN_GAME_CRYSTAL_REAUDIT_2026-10-28.md`, plus the owner's decision on death experience loss.

## Scope
- Migration `apps/game-server/migrations/0531_player_death_item_primitives.sql` (new).
- `crates/gameplay/durability/src/durability/player_death_items*` (new), `item_decay_retire/world_reset_cause/death_contents.rs` (new), `world_reset/ground_step.rs`, `item_mint_audit.rs`.

C20a/C20d/W23 and the death UI are out of scope. Skill and magic-level loss are not added. The audit ledger is not edited (one docs PR per wave).

## Risk and security impact
- Persistence: new SQL functions for death drops and the amulet burn, plus world-reset retirement of death contents. A wrong guard could lose or duplicate items; the primitives are covered by PG cases in `authority_cases/player_death_item_primitives.rs`.

author: ericdelorefice
body:
Agentic

## Summary

Refs #622. This is option 1 from the thread: roll up at read time, no schema change. You said you weren't sure about either approach, so this is meant to give us something concrete to look at. If it isn't the direction you want, I'm fine dropping it or moving to option 2.

`throughput_timeseries` takes an optional `bucket: timedelta`, on `InsightsService` and on both repository adapters. The default stays one minute, so the dashboard and `overview()` get the same rows as before.

```python
hourly = await insights.throughput_timeseries(last=timedelta(hours=24), bucket=timedelta(hours=1))
```

## Change

- `build_throughput_timeseries_query` uses `date_bin($2::interval, created, TIMESTAMPTZ '2001-01-01 00:00:00+00')` in place of `DATE_TRUNC('minute', created)`. `date_bin` needs Postgres 14, the oldest version in the CI matrix.
- The in-memory adapter floors `created` to the same buckets from the same origin, so the two adapters agree.
- `InsightsService.throughput_timeseries` raises `ValueError` for a bucket under one second or one that isn't a whole number of seconds. The rows are per second, so a 1.5 s bucket would put some seconds in the wrong bucket. The check is only in the service, like `clamp_window`. The repository methods trust their caller, so a zero bucket passed straight to `Queries` gets Postgres's own "stride must be greater than zero" error.
- With no bucket, the service calls the repository with the window only, as `overview()` does, so a custom repository written against the old signature keeps working.
- `RELEASE.md` Added entry, and one line in the insights API example in `docs/integrations/web-dashboard.md`.

Known gaps, so you can say where you want this to go:
- This doesn't reduce the number of stored rows, which is the volume part of the issue. That would be your option 2 (fold older rows into a coarser table and union on read). Happy to do that as a follow-up if you want it.
- `InsightsService` still caps the window at 24 hours (`MAX_WINDOW`), so hour buckets there give at most 25 points, the first one partial. The repository method has no cap. I left the cap alone.
- Buckets are aligned to UTC. `DATE_TRUNC` used the session time zone. For minute buckets that's the same result. An hour bucket in a session at UTC+5:30 now lines up with UTC hours, not local ones. In the issue I wrote the origin without a zone; I pinned it to UTC so buckets don't move with the session.

## Testing
- [x] `uv sync --frozen && uv run ruff check . && uv run ruff format . --check && uv run lint-imports && uv run mypy . && uv run pytest` passed (PostgreSQL 16.2 through `EXTERNAL_POSTGRES_DSN`, Python 3.12): 1591 passed, 10 skipped, 2 xfailed, with the change on top of current main (922b407).
- [x] Additional testing steps: `test_throughput_timeseries_bucket_matches` in `test_adapter_parity.py` stores the same per-second rows in both adapters (on and either side of minute, 15-minute and hour edges) and checks both against the expected buckets for the default, 15 minutes, 1 hour and 1 second. A second test checks the two agree for 7-second and 1-day buckets, which don't divide an hour. On main the non-default cases can't run, since the parameter doesn't exist. So I also put `DATE_TRUNC('minute')` back in the SQL, and separately the old minute floor in the in-memory adapter: each makes 3 of the 4 cases fail, and the default case still passes. Moving the in-memory origin to 1970 fails the 7-second case. `TestCheckBucket` covers the validation, that the service passes the bucket through, and that a repository with the old signature still serves the default.

## Checklist
- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guide](../CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [x] I have added or updated tests
- [x] I have updated documentation if necessary

author: farhadnuri
body:
## Summary of Changes

This PR introduces core academic features and key bug fixes across the Admin, Teacher, and Student/Guardian portals:

### 1. 📅 Routine & Timetable System
- **Model**: Added `Routine` schema supporting day-by-day periods for both classes and teachers.
- **Admin Management**: Full CRUD endpoints (`/api/admin/routines`) to create, update, and manage timetable schedules.
- **User Portal**: Added `/api/user/routine` endpoint for students and teachers to retrieve their active schedules.

### 2. 📝 Homework Submissions & Grading
- **Model**: Created `HomeworkSubmission` schema tracking uploaded documents, links, comments, and submission timestamps.
- **Student Submission**: Added `/api/user/homeworks/:id/submit` with file upload support (via Multer/Cloudinary) and deadline enforcement.
- **Teacher Review**: Added `/api/teacher/homeworks/:id/submissions` endpoint for teachers to review submissions and see completion statistics.

### 3. 📊 Subject-Level Gradebooks & Publishing Lockdown
- **Multi-Subject Gradebooks**: Refactored Gradebook schema and controller to allow multiple subject sheets per class.
- **Admin Publishing Lock**: Teachers are now restricted from modifying gradebooks that have been officially published by Admin.

### 4. 👨‍🏫 Teacher Context & Course Sync Fixes
- **Course Sharing Fix**: Fixed class-course synchronization so assigning a curriculum subject to one section (e.g. Class 8 Section A & B) does not unlink it from other classes.
- **Teacher Portal Enrichment**: Automatically enriches teacher classes and attendance sections with `mySubject`, `myCourseCode`, and assigned course metadata.
- **Course Catalog Details**: Added `/api/user/courses/:id` and enriched student/guardian course listings with teacher profiles and enrollment numbers.

body:
Folge zu #54: Auf dem Android-Handy erscheint bei `Notification.requestPermission()` weiterhin keine Abfrage. Auf https://whatpwacando.today/notifications funktioniert es – die Seite fragt über `registration.pushManager.subscribe({ userVisibleOnly: true, applicationServerKey })`.

## Änderungen
- Auf Android fragt die App jetzt ebenfalls über `pushManager.subscribe()` und kündigt das Abo sofort mit `unsubscribe()`. Erinnerungen laufen weiter nur lokal.
- `applicationServerKey`: fester öffentlicher P-256-Schlüssel (ohne privaten Schlüssel – es wird nie etwas gesendet); gegen echtes Chromium geprüft (gültiges Format).
- Andere Plattformen unverändert (`Notification.requestPermission()`).
- **Datenschutz-Ausnahme:** Chrome meldet die App beim Abo kurz bei seinem Push-Dienst (Google) an. In Hilfe (de/en) und AGENTS.md offen erklärt; vom Nutzer so freigegeben.
- **Diagnose kopieren** (Ende der Hilfe, Abschnitt „Fehlersuche“): kopiert Browser, Status der Berechtigung (`Notification.permission`, `permissions.query`, `pushManager.permissionState`), Service Worker und ein Protokoll der Schritte (Abfrage, Push-Abo, Benachrichtigungen, JS-Fehler) – ohne Erinnerungstexte.

## Tests
Android: Abfrage über Push-Abo, Abo sofort gekündigt, Test-Benachrichtigung; sofort abgelehnt → Hinweis; andere Plattformen ohne Push-Abo; Diagnose (Inhalt, Schritte, keine Erinnerungstexte). `npm test`: 372 bestanden.

author: ktysne
body:
## 概要

状態ファイルを同じリポジトリのすべての worktree で共有し、`comment --outcome` の記録時に、レビューの記録が無い往復の結論を止める。
スタックの 1 段目で、base は `main` である。
Closes #106

## 背景・目的

状態ファイル `.cross-review-state.json` は、コマンドを実行した worktree のルートに置かれていた。
レビューと `comment --outcome` を別の worktree で実行すると、同じブランチの往復の数と結論が別々のファイルに分かれる。
agent-cockpit は、収束した PR を「結論が未記録」と表示し、記録した側のセッションにも警告が出なかった。

## 変更内容

- 状態ファイルの置き場を、checkout のルートで `git rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-common-dir` を実行した結果の下の `cross-review-state.json` にした。
  同じリポジトリの worktree は、どこから実行しても同じファイルを読み書きする。
  git が使えないときは従来の `<root>/.cross-review-state.json` を使う。
  環境変数 `CROSS_REVIEW_STATE_DIR` で置き場を差し替えられる(テストの隔離に使う)。
- 書き込みを `updateState` に一本化した。
  `cross-review-state.json.lock` を排他で作ってから読み直し、一時ファイルへ書いて rename で置き換える。
  ロックは pid などを書いたらすぐ閉じる。fd を開いたまま消すと、Windows で名前が削除保留で残り、ほかの書き手が取れなくなるためである。
  30 秒より古く、持ち主の pid がいないロックは放棄されたとみなし、一意な名前へ rename してから消す。
  読み手はロックを取らなくてよい。
- worktree の旧ファイルは、書き込む系のコマンド(レビュー、`state --mark` / `--reset`、`dismiss`、`comment --outcome`)がロック内で取り込み、共通ディレクトリの `cross-review-state.imported/` へ移す。
  統合の規則は `mergeStates` で、`lastTriage` は `round` と独立に `lastTriage.round` の大きいほうを残す。
  `round` の大きい側の記録をまるごと残すと、Issue の表の例(レビュー側に往復、本体側に結論)で結論が消えるためである。
  表示だけのコマンドは取り込まず、未取り込みの旧ファイルがある旨を警告する。
- `comment --outcome` は、本文の生成と投稿の前に、そのブランチの `round` が記録する往復より小さければ終了コード 1 で止まる。
  止まるときは、状態ファイルのパスと、`node tools/cross-review.js state` で記録を確かめてから実行し直す手順を示す。
  意図した記録なら `--allow-round-mismatch` で検査を外せる。
  `lastReviewedSha` が HEAD と違うときは、両方の短縮 SHA を添えて警告する。
- 契約 `docs/contracts/cross-review-state.md` に、置き場の解決手順、ロックの方式、旧ファイルの扱い、同じリポジトリでの新旧の CLI の混在は非対応であることを書いた。
  統合規則の検証データを `contracts/cross-review-state/merge/` に足した。
- 移行ノート `docs/migrations/2026-10-shared-state.md` と、計画の資料 `docs/handover/2026-10-30-review-state-followups.md` を足した。

## 影響範囲

- 状態ファイルの JSON の形は変えていない。置き場だけが変わる。
- 既存の worktree ごとの記録は、次に書き込む系のコマンドを実行したときに共有のファイルへ取り込まれる。
- 状態ファイルを読む agent-cockpit は、共有のファイルを読む版(ktysne/agent-cockpit#717)へ更新するまで、取り込み後の記録を読めない。
- 同じリポジトリの worktree で新旧の CLI を混ぜると、旧版が旧ファイルを作り直し、`state --reset` した記録が再取り込みで戻ることがある。

## 改修後に行った確認内容

- `npx vitest run`: 942 件すべて通過。
- `npx eslint .`: 指摘なし。
- テストの前後で、このリポジトリの git の共通ディレクトリに `cross-review-state.json` とロックが作られていないことを `ls` で確かめた。

## 確認して欲しいポイント

- 2 つの worktree を持つリポジトリで、一方でレビューを実行し、もう一方で `comment --round <N> --outcome converged` を実行すると記録できること。
- レビューを実行していないブランチで `comment --round 1 --outcome converged` を実行すると、終了コード 1 で止まり、手順が示されること。
- 旧ファイルがある worktree で `state` を実行すると警告が出て、`state --mark` などの後に旧ファイルが `cross-review-state.imported/` へ移ること。

## 備考

- 導入先のリポジトリへの同期はこの PR では行わない。
- 判定から rename までの間にほかのプロセスがロックを取り直すと、新しいロックを奪う余地が残る。ロックが 30 秒より古いことが前提で、起きる確率は低いので対象から外した。

author: zoroyihan7
body:
## Summary

Stacked on #183 (base is its branch, `claw158-a2a-peer-allowlist`; GitHub retargets this to `main` when #183 merges). #183 made `a2a_call` reach only operator-configured peers and send no user key. This PR makes it a usable A2A client, **off by default** behind `A2A_CLIENT_ENABLED` (the tool is not offered, and a call is refused):

- **Endpoint from the card.** A peer is called at the card's JSONRPC 1.0 `supportedInterfaces` entry (cached by `ETag` / `Cache-Control`), not at a guessed `<base>/a2a` (the official `a2a-python` helloworld serves JSON-RPC at `/`). The endpoint must be on the origin the operator wrote down, so a card cannot carry the credential to another host.
- **Identity.** An entry with `audience` is called as the session's user: Brain exchanges a short-lived token (`user_id:<owner>`, RFC 8693) at primus-identity; the token stays in the Brain process, never in the model context or sandbox. An entry with `auth_env` keeps the operator service credential. Both in one entry, or an unknown key (a misspelt `audience`), is refused. Entries carry an optional `owner`, so per-user peers can follow without changing callers.
- **Structured result** `{state, task_id, context_id, text, artifacts, input_required?}`; `mode` gains `get` and `cancel`; `context_id` continues a conversation.
- **input_required** (and a structured approval request) is surfaced to the model; an `allow` answering a peer's approval request is held for the user through the existing approval gate (a peer's text cannot talk the model into approving).
- **Timeouts.** A streamed call stops waiting after 120 s without an event or 600 s in total (or when the run's remaining budget is nearly spent) and returns `state=working` + `task_id` instead of failing; the peer's task keeps running.
- **Stop** sends `CancelTask` to the peer (a restart abort does not).

Not in this PR: the server side (A2A inbound context/task model, `INPUT_REQUIRED` mapping), `D7`, per-user peers (the field is reserved only).

## Linked issues

Stacked on #183.

## Type of change

- [x] New feature
- [ ] Bug fix
- [ ] Refactor / internal change
- [ ] CI / build / tooling
- [x] Docs

## Affected components

- [x] Claw (api / brain / hands / protocol / utils)

## Testing

Unit and integration (real HTTP peers, a real RFC 8693 client against a local token endpoint), from `claw/packages/brain`:
`npx tsx --test test/a2a-client.test.ts test/a2a-client-result.test.ts test/a2a-client-tool.test.ts test/a2a-client-off.test.ts test/a2a-hitl-scope.test.ts test/a2a-peer-registry.test.ts` -> 64 pass, 0 fail. The whole brain suite (`tsx --test`, one process at a time): 3010 tests, 3008 pass, 0 fail, 2 skipped. `tsc --noEmit` clean. A peer that echoes the credential it was sent (into an artifact, status message, error or card; as is, base64, URL-encoded; short or long) never reaches the model: it is scrubbed (found by the codex review, fixed in two follow-up commits).

Real cross-agent run on a local stack (Postgres, NATS, fake LLM, Claw A brain + API with `a2a_call` on, a second Claw B API + brain). The caller is Claw A's brain through the normal chat path (user message -> agent loop -> router -> `a2a_call`); the fake LLM issues the tool calls. 20 of 20 checks pass:

| Peer | Checked |
|---|---|
| official `a2a-python` 1.3.0 `helloworld` sample, unmodified (non-Claw) | completed answer; the sample logged `POST /` and never `/a2a` (card-based endpoint) |
| helloworld-derived scripted agent (same SDK/routes, scripted executor) | `input_required` with the question; the answer on the same `task_id`/`context_id` completes; structured approval request surfaced, the `allow` is **held** (`permissionRequest`, peer receives nothing before the decision), user yes -> peer completes, user no -> peer never answered; no event for 8 s -> `state=working` + `task_id`, `get` reads it, `cancel` cancels it; user **Stop** in Claw A -> `CancelTask`, exactly that task `CANCELED` on the peer |
| second Claw (B), operator service credential | completed answer; **Stop** in A -> B's task `CANCELED` |
| identity peer (fake RFC 8693 endpoint) | peer saw `sub` = the session owner, `aud` = the peer, `act.sub` = `claw-brain`; the token is not in the tool result or the Brain log; revoked binding -> clear error, nothing reaches the peer |

Not verified: the exchange ran against a stand-in for primus-identity (same RFC 8693 shape, unsigned token), not primus-identity itself, and not against a Claw peer that verifies identity JWTs; `input_required` against a Claw peer (the inbound `INPUT_REQUIRED` mapping is the server side, not here); after a Stop, B's legacy server flips `CANCELED` back to `COMPLETED` when its LLM answers (server side, pre-existing).

## Checklist

- [x] PR scope is focused; unrelated changes are split out
- [x] `lint` and `build` workflows pass (all checks green on 5b36c6c3)
- [x] No secrets, credentials, or internal endpoints committed
- [x] Breaking changes documented above (migration path if any): `a2a_call` is off until `A2A_CLIENT_ENABLED=true`; the result is JSON instead of text; the unused `skill` parameter is gone; the "A2A Auth" prompt line is omitted while the tool is off.

author: finngi
body:
## Summary

tics 0.2.0 gives each finding and file an AI-style score. The beta-binomial model counts opportunities occupied by each pattern, caps a rule's evidence and accounts for absent patterns. It is fitted on 146 human texts from before ChatGPT and 438 model answers to the same prompts. Two new rules cover bold paragraph labels and stock section labels.

Terminal output groups findings by file, with the score, source line, underline and fix hint. Piped output defaults to `--format compact`; `--json` is shorthand for `--format json`. Tests pin the compact and JSON output contracts.

Directory walks respect parent and nested `.gitignore` files. Explicit file arguments still scan ignored files. Hidden directories, `target/` and `node_modules/` stay excluded from walks.

Held-out, prompt-grouped AUC is 0.808 (95% interval 0.770–0.846). Length and layout differ across this corpus, and per-finding and section scores have not been validated separately. Scores measure writing patterns; they cannot establish authorship. DESIGN.md and calibration/ have the method and results.

## Validation

- `mise x -- cargo fmt --check`
- `mise x -- cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- `mise x -- cargo test --locked`: 99 tests, including Rust/Python parity and output contracts
- Release performance: both 1 MiB cases under 1 second
- Real msbx docs scan excludes generated `docs/book/`
- README, DESIGN and CHANGELOG pass `tics --min-confidence 0.5`

This branch is 0.2.0; merge and release still need the owner's approval.

author: thehalfmoon
body:
**Inert pre-activation engineering, category A5** (shutdown, cleanup, recovery and crash regression tests) of the SG-000115 amendment (#526, merged). A1–A4 are merged and this PR is rebased onto main. This is not an activation and adds no capability.

### What
`crates/orcel-browser-host/src/unix_cleanup.rs`:
- **`sweep_held_profile(hold, path)`** deletes a profile only through its A3 hold:
  - It first verifies the path still names the held directory.
  - It deletes the contents relative to the held descriptor (`openat` with `O_NOFOLLOW | O_DIRECTORY`, then `unlinkat`). Symlinks are removed as links and never followed.
  - Depth (64) and entry count (100,000) are bounded. Hitting a bound fails closed and leaves the rest in place.
  - The lock file is removed last, while still held, and only after re-checking that its name still names the locked file. The directory itself is removed with `rmdir` after a fresh verify.
- **`recover_stale_profile(path)`:** if no live process holds the profile (a crashed holder's `flock` died with it), the profile is stale and removed. A profile with a live holder is left untouched. A live lock is never unlinked.
- **A3 changes:** a crate-private `root_fd()` accessor is added, and A3's own scan exempts this sibling test-only module.

### Tests (Unix CI legs)
- A whole profile is removed.
- Links inside the profile are removed and never followed: an outside file stays intact.
- The depth bound fails closed, leaving the rest in place.
- A swapped profile is not removed: another directory's content is untouched.
- A fixture `python3` process holds the lock: recovery reports `InUse` and touches nothing. After a `SIGKILL`, recovery reports `Removed`, and then `Absent`.
- An unsafe (0755) profile is refused.
- A source scan.

### Why it is inert
- **Build-time exclusion:** `#[cfg(all(test, unix))] mod unix_cleanup;`. No release build contains it.
- **No production caller:** `leftovers.rs`, `profile.rs` and `worker_launch.rs` are unchanged, and launch stays refused.
- **Test processes:** fixture processes only. No browser is started.

### Open for activation (not decided here)
- **An orphaned engine.** Recovery cannot yet tell whether an engine process is still using the profile. The lock is `O_CLOEXEC`, so an engine never holds it. If the host crashes while Chrome or Edge keeps running, recovery would call the profile stale and delete it under the browser. Activation must first establish that no engine process uses the profile, via the A2 process tree or the engine's own `SingletonLock`. **Recovery is not safe against a live, orphaned browser until then.**
- **A same-user window.** Between the lock check and the unlink, or while contents are cleared, a same-user process could swap the lock and let a second holder in.
- The final `rmdir` is by path, after a point-in-time verify.
- Coordination with the engine's processes (A2) before and during a sweep.

### Evidence
Clippy `-D warnings` is clean for `x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu`, `aarch64-apple-darwin` and Windows.

### Review
Security review: two rounds, ending APPROVE WITH NITS, with every nit fixed. The SG-000085 spawn-allowlist entry for `unix_cleanup.rs` was recorded with A2 (#529) and is guarded to the Unix-test-only declaration.

Three changes across two tools. There are no new npm, Go or Rust dependencies, and no release workflow changes.

### Copy: RCJ import and export in the desktop app, `4ec284e` and `9f7110f`

- **Import RCJ:** opens a native file dialog and reads the file through `internal/rcj` with its limits. The full explanation is shown before anything loads: encoding, paths, filters, errors, warnings, and every switch with its catalog help.
  - Unknown, stray, hidden, destructive and not-enabled switches are flagged and never dropped.
  - Loading into the designer needs a click, plus an acknowledgement checkbox when anything is flagged.
  - Nothing is saved or run on import. File values are inserted with `textContent` only.
- **Export RCJ:** shows the exact text first.
  - A job with errors is refused, so `/REG` is never written.
  - You can pick the encoding: automatic (the default), UTF-8 or UTF-16.
  - The file is written through `private.WriteNewBytes`: owner-only, never replacing an existing file. The dialog repeats the `robocopy /JOB:FILE /QUIT` hint.
- `rc1.md` and design sections 9.2 and 9.4 are updated.

### Readout: open linked documents in their default app after a confirmation (RD16), `d82322c`

- A relative link to a non-Markdown file is resolved in Rust against the open document, using the existing `resolve_target` rules.
  - Additional refusals: any `:` (drives, `file:`, alternate data streams), UNC paths and control characters.
  - Without an open folder, the target must be in the document's own folder.
- **Allow-list (opens after one confirmation):** pdf, png, jpg, jpeg, gif, webp, txt, csv, log, docx, xlsx, pptx, odt, ods, odp, rtf, json, xml, yaml, yml.
  - Programs and scripts (an extended list, plus any name without an extension) are refused with "Readout does not run programs".
  - Every other type is refused, including html, svg and macro-enabled Office files.
  - The type is checked on both the written name and the canonical name, so a symlink cannot turn a program into a document.
- **Confirmation dialog:** shows the full path and the file type, with Cancel as the default. On Open, Readout runs the full check again and requires the confirmed path to match. It then opens the file through the existing `tauri-plugin-opener` (`ShellExecuteExW` on Windows, with no arguments and no shell).
- The browser build is unchanged.

### Readout: browser UI suite in CI (RD5), `d70215c`

- `readout/uitest/` runs Playwright Chromium against the built web bundle, served locally. There are 17 scenarios, each run in dark and light:
  - open and render;
  - a byte-faithful save round trip (BOM, CRLF, no final newline);
  - Save as;
  - drag and drop;
  - dividers (mouse and keyboard);
  - folder mode and folder search;
  - toolbar accessibility and themes;
  - callouts, outline, mixed line endings and Convert, and Copy as rich text;
  - recent files;
  - a CSP self-test and a hostile document;
  - the desktop title bar, through a harness page.
- Each scenario fails on any console error, failed request, outside request or CSP violation.
- New CI job `web-ui` on ubuntu-24.04. Chromium is installed exactly as Scanner's `ui` job does it (`playwright@1.56.1`).

## Validation

All of these passed locally, on the integrated branch:

- **Readout:** typecheck and 297 tests, plus `npm run build`; the UI suite at 34 of 34 (Playwright 1.63 locally); `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy -D warnings` and `cargo test` (48 tests).
- **Copy:** gofmt; vet for Linux and `GOOS=windows`; `go test -race` in root and `app/`; the UI suite in dark and light; the unsigned Windows cross build plus `check-pe.sh`.
- **Shared:** the palette check.

## Needs real Windows

- **Copy:** the native open and save dialogs, the owner-only DACL, and `robocopy /JOB:file /QUIT` on exported files (the open items in `rc1.md`).
- **Readout:** `ShellExecuteExW` opening a PDF or docx, and junctions or symlinks pointing outside the folder.

## For review

- **Readout:** the confirmation is drawn in the WebView so Cancel can be the default (the native dialog cannot do that). A compromised WebView could still open only allow-listed files reachable from a granted document, and only by naming the confirmed path.
- **Readout:** `csv` is on the allow-list; Excel's own formula protections apply.
- **Copy:** the acknowledgement checkbox appears only when something is flagged.
- **RD5:** the suite has not been run locally against Playwright 1.56.1; CI will run it.

author: mdolce75
body:
Closes #127

En Java 21, esperar red o base dentro de un `synchronized` fija el hilo virtual a su núcleo; con los 2 núcleos del servidor, dos esperas así cuelgan la app (como pasó en #118). Se cambian todos los `synchronized` que quedaban por `ReentrantLock`:

| Dónde | Qué esperaba adentro | Cambio |
|---|---|---|
| `ExchangeRate.current()` | DolarAPI | Lock con `tryLock`: mientras uno consulta, los demás siguen con la cotización anterior (sin esperar). |
| `ReportQuota.consume()` | El pedido completo (base) | Un lock por usuario que sale del mapa cuando nadie lo usa: el mapa ya no crece sin límite. |
| `SampleReport` | Armar el PDF de ejemplo (escudos) | `ReentrantLock`. |
| `ReportService` / `PlayerReportService` (`onReady`) | Guardar en el historial (base) | `ReentrantLock`. |

**Tests** (corren con `-Djdk.virtualThreadScheduler.parallelism=2`, ya en el pom):
- `ReportQuotaTest`: 8 usuarios pidiendo a la vez, esperándose dentro del pedido, entran todos; **con el `synchronized` de antes este test se cuelga** (lo probé). Los pedidos del mismo usuario van de a uno, y al terminar no queda ningún lock guardado.
- `ExchangeRateTest`: con DolarAPI lenta, los demás reciben la cotización anterior al instante.

`mvnw clean verify` pasa.

author: nepreby
body:
## Summary
Fixes #97

Prevents consumers from exploiting stale, low-multiplier performance certificates during `lease_renew` when a provider has repriced or published a newer active certificate.

## Changes
1. **Core Types (`core/types.go`)**:
   - Added `Hash string` to `CertificateInfo` to preserve canonical certificate identity.
2. **Ledger Configuration (`core/ledger.go`)**:
   - Added `CurrentCertificateFn func(provider string) *CertificateInfo` to `LedgerConfig` and `currentCertificateFn` field to `Ledger`.
   - Added `SetCurrentCertificateFn` helper for runtime and harness overrides.
3. **Lease Renewal Currentness Gate (`core/lease_renew.go`)**:
   - In `validateAndAddLeaseRenew`, resolves the provider's active current certificate via `currentCertificateFn`.
   - Enforces that `b.CertificateHash` matches the provider's current certificate (`currentCert.Hash`).
   - Asserts that the certificate price multiplier is not lower than the provider's current rate (`cert.PriceMultiplierMilli >= currentCert.PriceMultiplierMilli`), preventing underpayment and forced sub-market renewals.
4. **Node Integration (`node/perf.go`, `node/node.go`)**:
   - Updated `certificateInfoByHash` to populate `Hash`.
   - Implemented `certificateInfoByProvider` querying `GetCertificateByProvider` (returning the latest unexpired valid cert).
   - Wired `CurrentCertificateFn` into `LedgerConfig` during node startup.
5. **Regression Tests (`core/lease_renew_cert_test.go`)**:
   - Added unit test verifying that renewals attempting to use unexpired but stale certificates with outdated multipliers are strictly rejected.

Payout / Reward Address (USDT - TRC20): `TMqmJjRgVS21NL2eFtfyHciTxvE4BqGmEv`

author: judell
body:
Jon's Claude (Bram 0.8.0, main thread, Opus 5.5, macOS, Tuck) speaking from the XMLUI project (github.com/xmlui-org/xmlui):

## The bug

Site search returned `https://www.xmlui.org/docs/wrap-component/bigcalendar` for a page served at `https://www.xmlui.org/docs/guides/wrap-component/bigcalendar`. `staticSearchData` (`website/utils/index.ts`) built each result's path from the content file's location. For 28 pages, that differs from the route in `website/src/Main.xmlui`:
- the wrap-component guides, 14 including their overview;
- 15 pages served under `/docs/guides/` (`forms`, `layout`, `scripting`, `routing-and-links` and others).

Another 16 search entries came from content files that no route serves.

## Changes

- **`website/utils/index.ts`:**
  - `DOCS_ROUTE_PREFIXES` maps content paths to their real routes for every search result.
  - `DOCS_SEARCH_EXCLUDED` leaves out the 16 route-less files: stale `xmlui-animations`, `xmlui-pdf` and `xmlui-spreadsheet` copies, `test.md`, `news-and-reviews.md`, `reference-extensions.md`, `themes.md` and `wrap-component/grid-layout.md`. The files themselves are kept.
  - Both tables are maintained by hand; a comment says to keep them in step with `Main.xmlui`.
- **Hard-coded links.** Old `/docs/<guide>` and `/docs/wrap-component/…` paths now go to `/docs/guides/…`. Also fixed:
  - a doubled `/docs/reference/docs/reference/…` prefix;
  - `/docs/components/*` → `/docs/reference/components/*`;
  - `/docs/reference/components-intro` → `/docs/components-intro`;
  - `/docs/theming` → `/docs/themes-intro`;
  - the Backdrop link, now pointing at its `xmlui-website-blocks` page;
  - the sample CSV download path;
  - an absolute `docs.xmlui.org` link.
- **Missing how-tos:** four links now point at existing how-tos that cover the same ground. Links to 7 how-tos that don't exist, and to Accordion and GridLayout, keep their text with no link.
- **Generated reference pages** are fixed at their sources: `xmlui/src/components/*/*.md` and the `xmlui-docs-blocks` docs.

## Checked

- **Search paths:** a script recomputes every docs search path and checks it against the routes in `Main.xmlui`. 44 mismatches before, 0 after, across 467 entries (483 before exclusion).
- **Build:** the website builds with the CI command, `npx turbo run build-ssg --filter=xmlui-website`. The built search index contains `/docs/guides/wrap-component/bigcalendar`, and the old path 0 times.

## Not in this PR

- The 7 missing how-tos, now plain text in some "Related" lists: write them, or remove the entries.
- The 16 route-less content files: delete them, or give them routes.
- `build-ssg` rewrites tracked files, such as generated reference docs and `reference/extensions/**`. That may deserve its own issue.

author: aliaska-varieva
body:
## Problem
`BaseGlobalExceptionHandler` logs every `BaseException` at ERROR with a full stack trace, including 4xx ones (`NotFoundException`, `BadRequestException`, conflicts). Missing header, method-not-supported and media-type errors are logged the same way.

A caller asking for an unknown id therefore shows up in logs and alerts as a server fault. Example on prod (`openframe-saas-management-api`): `NOT_FOUND: Device … not found` logged at ERROR with its stack trace.

## Fix
| Case | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `BaseException`, 4xx | ERROR + stack | WARN, message only |
| `BaseException`, 5xx | ERROR + stack | ERROR + stack (unchanged) |
| Missing header (400) | ERROR + stack | WARN, header name |
| Method not supported (405), media type not supported (415) | ERROR + stack | WARN, message only |
| `IllegalArgumentException` (400) | ERROR + stack | WARN + stack (our own code throws it too, e.g. a bad UUID in stored data) |

Response bodies and statuses are unchanged; only log levels change.

## Tests
- New `BaseGlobalExceptionHandlerLoggingTest` (the module's first tests) checks level and stack trace per case.
- `openframe-external-api-service-core` `GlobalExceptionHandlerTest` still passes (20).

## Follow-up
After the lib release and bump, the `NotFoundException` handler added in openframe-saas-shared#2782 (management-api) duplicates this and can be removed.

## Summary
- VP9 is gone: the video encoding (WLSV) is H.264 from `h264.rs`, VA-API where the host has an encoder and libx264 otherwise, at the daemon's fixed dial (`QUALITY = 90`, QP 18). The walk paces the frame rate alone (`QualityWalk::frames`); per-frame QP is the roadmap's next step.

## What it brings

- **Markers on the page of a Resource:**
  - the Level (K5.2, 3.3.3);
  - the grain (2.3.5, 1.2.2, 1.2.1);
  - the model type (2.3.6);

  - after the pointer rests on the marked text for a second (passing over opens nothing);

- **"Understand what is happening here"** under every Message Data Hub writes: the card its type names, which opens inline with "I understand it". For now that means the Registration (K5.1), the changed description (K3.4) and the change since the Confirmation (4.3.2).

author: gabox280
body:
## Summary
Hardens the NexusSIEM Phase 1 security baseline.

### Changes
- Removed shell interpolation from firewall commands in the IDS and SSH defender; added IP validation, timeouts, and explicit subprocess error handling.
- Removed the localhost authentication bypass from `POST /api/alert`; the endpoint now requires a separate `NEXUS_ALERT_TOKEN` Bearer token.
- Firewall blocking now requires an explicit `block_ip: true` and `level: "CRITICAL"`, validates the target IP, and reports the action result.
- Dashboard binds to `127.0.0.1` by default; remote binding requires explicit `NEXUS_HOST` configuration and should sit behind HTTPS.
- Reworked UFW hardening to preserve existing rules instead of running `ufw reset`, and only opens web ports when explicitly requested.
- Updated deployment documentation for secrets, tokens, safe exposure, and least-privilege firewall permissions.

### Validation still required
- Run Python syntax checks and the application in a disposable Linux VM.
- Verify sensor integrations with the new Bearer token.
- Test API rejection cases and firewall behavior without affecting a production host.
- Verify sudoers configuration and UFW behavior on the target distribution.

This is intentionally a draft PR until runtime validation is completed.

author: ryansaxe
body:
Node's security release of October 21, 2026 shipped 22.23.4, 24.22.1 and 26.12.1. pair now refuses a Node release older than the floor of its line, and a line it does not support.

## What changed

- `engines.node` is `^22.23.4 || ^24.22.1 || >=26.12.1`, one floor per supported line. `requireNode()` in `src/shared/settings.mjs` reads the floor of the running Node's line from it. `pair check`, `pair start`, the hub and every command that opens a session call it. `pair build`, `pair diff` and `pair guide` do not, and still run on any Node.
- Below its line's floor:
  `pair: Node 26.7.0 is missing security fixes that Node released in 26.12.1. Update Node to 26.12.1 or newer.`
- On a line with no floor, such as 25 or 20:
  `pair: Node 25.8.2 is not supported. Use Node 22.23.4 or newer in 22, 24.22.1 or newer in 24, or 26.12.1 or newer.`
- The `pair check` node line names the running line's floor: `26.13.0, and pair needs 26.12.1 or newer on Node 26`. `pair check` refuses before it prints that line on an unsupported line, so that case prints the refusal above.
- CI tests each floor and the latest release of each line: `22.23.4, 22, 24.22.1, 24, 26.12.1, 26`. macOS and Windows move from 24 to 26, the current LTS since October 28.
- The README, the install page, the contributing page and `guide/setup.md` name the three floors. The release steps in `docs/contributing/README.md` say to raise the floors before each release.

## Before this merges

- The develop ruleset requires `test (22.0.0)` and `test (macos-latest, 24)`, which no longer run, so the PR cannot merge until the ruleset names the new jobs. The main ruleset also requires `test (22.0.0)`.
- Once this is in develop and the linked clone pulls it, every session command and `pair check` on a machine with Node 26.7.0 refuse until Node is updated to 26.12.1 or newer.

## Verification

- `node --test` on Node 26.13.0: 286 pass, 0 fail. `npx --yes prettier@3.9.6 --check .` and `npx --yes eslint@10.11.0 .` pass.
- `npm run test:browser` on Node 26.13.0: 84 pass, 1 fail, 12 skip (WebKit on macOS 14). The failure, `selecting diff text starts a thread in its line annotation`, fails the same way on `origin/develop` on that machine, where headless Chrome cannot reach esm.sh. CI's browser job passes it.
- A new test in `tests/shared/settings.test.mjs` runs `pair check` from a copy of the package with `engines.node` rewritten around the running Node, and checks the floor line, the later-line case, both refusals and the exit status.
- `node src/cli.mjs check` on official Node binaries: 26.7.0, 22.23.3 and 25.8.2 refuse with the messages above, and 22.23.4, 24.22.1, 26.12.1 and 26.13.0 pass. A scratch hub on 26.13.0 started a session, and `status` on 26.7.0 against it refused.

author: moritzbrantner
body:
Part 3a of #145 (owner-approved split of part 3 into 3a/3b/3c; only 3c closes #145): exploration waystones and the Seam Test zone pair.

- **Waystones:** one global network (`mmorpg_core::WAYSTONES`: Greyhaven Outpost, Seam Test West, Seam Test East). Content binds the stones that stand in it. A living player within 8 m of a stone unlocks it for good; unlocks are stored on the character record, in canonical state and in the self flags.
- **`UseWaystone` command (tag 30):** instant travel between unlocked stones of the same zone. Refused in combat (new error 36), in a corridor (35), and toward a locked, unknown or current stone (new error 37). Travel to a stone in another zone is also refused with 37 until part 3b wires hosts to the fenced transfer.
- **Seam Test West/East (zones 901/902):** small flat zones joined by one walking seam; each zone's waystone sits away from the seam. Hosts now pick content by zone ID (`content_for_zone`). Greyhaven's geometry is untouched; its existing outpost waystone only gains the binding.
- **Clients:** a waystone panel in the native (egui) and browser clients. The browser gets `waystoneAt` and `waystoneNames` from WASM.
- **Docs:** ADR 0007 and PROTOCOL.md updated.

Defaults picked: discovery and use reach 8 m, no cast or cooldown, stone IDs 1–3, arrival 2.5–3 m north of each stone. Unlocks travel in the self flag byte's six spare bits, so the network holds at most 6 stones until a wire change.
Format: new protocol ID (fixtures re-recorded). New random `CHARACTER_RECORD_SCHEMA_VERSION` token, so stored characters of the old schema are refused (no migration). Greyhaven's content revision changes.
Ran: fmt; clippy on core/protocol/client/game-server/wasm/scenarios; `scripts/rerecord.sh`; core `waystones` + `handoff`; game-server lib + `host_transfer`; characters `store`; web `tsc --noEmit`; bun command-wire, replication, waystone-panel, local-zone-wasm and combat-presentation tests.
Not verified: the panels in a running client. Not done here: cross-zone travel, the seam handoff in live hosts, client rendering of the test zones (3b/3c). Gap for 3b: the test zones bind no quests, so a character carrying Greyhaven quest state fails the destination's record validation.

Part of #145.

body:
The design session's answers on M4 slices 1 to 3 that change the app. Its spec and technical design changes are in #158. #112's change gets its own pull request.

## What's in it

- **Saturation keeps colors outside Display P3.**
  - The appendix now says components below 0 come from wider-gamut originals, and that every operation accepts them (seura-photos/edit-format#5, as reviewed).
  - Saturation, from #157, clamped them at 0, which would have clipped such colors. It now keeps them, and can make them, since a vivid color made more so can go below 0.

- **Revert's confirmation names other apps' edits (EDT-10).** When the photo has operations Seura can't edit, it adds "Edits made in other apps are kept." The Editor learns this with the undo labels, which follow every change.
- **Leaving before answering "Keep yours or load theirs?" (FIL-3)** keeps the other version, as built, and now says "Your changes to this photo since it changed elsewhere weren't kept."
  - Changes made after the notice appeared were already saved onto the other version, so they stay; what isn't kept is the user's version from before it.

- UI format, lint, build and tests pass (165), with tests for the revert note and the message.

- The render check in the real web view on Windows: largest difference 0 on WebGPU and WebGL2.

author: paudley
body:
## Summary

Move the complete generic action-receipt persistence path to native PurRDF JSON: receipt digests, envelope publication, typed readers and both garbage-collection reads. Preserve recursively sorted compact digest input, declaration-order pretty envelope bytes, schemas, identity domains, bounds, locks, atomic publication and integrity checks. Principles 4 and 7.

Wire all nine first-party payload types through the same native path. Reuse the existing slice-verdict and build-identity owners; add complete owners for source exports, corpus artifacts, documentation receipts and pipeline receipts. Replace unit payloads with an owned null-only type. Hydration preserves stored fields without constructor normalization. New readers of named records require their declared fields and reject duplicates, unknown fields and positional records; unsigned schema/count tokens reject signed zero and other noninteger forms.

Remove the old generic receipt Serde implementations and recursive JSON sorter. Selector loading, executable receipts, artifact-content codecs and the separate stage-specific digest retain their existing active owners. No alternate native store API, fallback or cache-version change is introduced.

## Validation

Before replacement, two existing controls captured complete original scalar and structured envelopes and their actual digests. The literal 746-byte and 829-byte references are unchanged; the existing publish/read and canonical-GC controls now compare complete stored bytes and actual receipt digests against them.

All-target warnings-denied checks passed for action-cache, bundle-import, docs-model, docs, pipeline, slicetest, validation and the developer CLI. Independent design and complete source review passed. Formatting, whitespace, prose and complete-source publication scans passed. All 25 existing action-cache library controls passed on final source, with no skipped cases and a 0.115 second summary. Helper hygiene passed after replacing the duplicated envelope writer and fixture hex loop with existing shared owners. The two affected owners passed all-target warnings-denied checks again after that cleanup. Normal signed commit hooks passed.

This verifies the inspected first-party payload contract. Arbitrary external numeric-payload parity is unverified. Full CI is explicitly waived; no local optimized producer, canonical corpus or fixture production, synchronization or full gate ran. Authenticated corpus, installed/browser/release and performance acceptance remain open.

Part of #1776. The parent remains open for its remaining JSON owners, selector/executable paths, dependency removal and full acceptance.

author: mvanslobbe
body:
The generic UTF-16 validator (`src/generic/validate_utf16.h`, used by haswell, westmere, lsx, lasx and ppc64) gathers the high bytes of two registers into one byte register. It then kept only the low 16 mask bits and advanced 16 code units per iteration. On haswell and lasx the gathered register holds 32 code units, so half of every load was thrown away.

The step size and the mask type now come from the register width: 32 units and a `uint32_t` mask on 256-bit targets, 16 units and a `uint16_t` mask on 128-bit targets as before. The loop also starts as soon as one full step fits; before, it needed room for two, so short inputs went to the scalar tail.

### Results

Setup:
- CPU: i7-12700H, pinned to one P-core.
- Each number is the change in ns per call against master: minimum over 3 alternating rounds of 25 samples.
- Functions: `validate_utf16le`, `validate_utf16be`, `validate_utf16le_with_errors`.
- Inputs: the 9 unicode_lipsum UTF-16 files (geometric mean), plus prefixes of the Chinese and Emoji files of 64, 256 and 1024 code units.

| kernel | input | GCC 13 / 15 / 16 | Clang 14 / 18 / 22 |
|---|---|---|---|
| haswell | full | −49 .. −52% | −42 .. −48% |
| haswell | 64–256 units | −52 .. −86% | −63 .. −90% |
| haswell | 1024 units | −48 .. −58% | −52 .. −68% |
| westmere | full | −9 .. +4% | −20 .. −28% |
| westmere | 64–256 units | −4 .. −74% (one row +14%) | −21 .. −73% |
| westmere | 1024 units | +3 .. −33% | −11 .. −32% |

On westmere, GCC is flat to +4% on full-size BE input. The hot loop has the same instructions as master; GCC places one extra `mov` in the loop exit. I tried `end - input >= N` and a strict `<` instead, and neither helped. The +14% row is GCC 13, `with_errors`, Emoji, 256 code units; it showed −18% in an earlier run, so it looks like code layout.

### Testing

- ctest passes with GCC 13 and 16 and Clang 14 and 22. The tests cover every implementation the CPU supports, including westmere.
- A differential test compares `validate_utf16{le,be}[_with_errors]` against the fallback implementation on random inputs dense in surrogates, with lengths 0–300. It found no mismatches on haswell and westmere (300k cases), or on lsx, lasx and ppc64 under qemu (50k cases each). Advancing by `N` instead of `N - 1` is caught at once.
- LoongArch ctest under qemu 8.2: master and this branch fail the same 13 utf8-conversion and base64 tests. All UTF-16 tests pass.

### AI disclosure

I did this work with Claude (an AI assistant). It helped find this spot with a custom clang-tidy check, read the generated assembly, write the benchmark and the differential test, and draft the patch and this description. I reviewed the patch and the text, checked the results, and I'm happy to answer questions about any of it.

author: davidboone
body:
clod gemini [ARGS] runs Gemini CLI, which installs from the
@google/gemini-cli npm package into the home on first run and updates
itself, as Codex does. It runs with --yolo unless the arguments choose
an approval mode (--approval-mode, --approvalMode, -y or --yolo) or
start with a subcommand (mcp, extensions, skills, hooks, gemma, and
their aliases), which Gemini would otherwise take for a prompt. It runs
with GEMINI_CLI_TRUST_WORKSPACE=true unless the environment sets it, as
Gemini CLI drops YOLO to default approval in a folder it doesn't trust;
trusted, it also loads the project's .gemini/settings.json, which
docs/security.md says.

The entrypoint composes the container's and the shared config's
instructions into its global ~/.gemini/GEMINI.md, in the clod:begin/
clod:end block Codex's and OpenCode's files get, keeping the user's own
text outside it. clod home gains a GEMINI column, from
.gemini/oauth_creds.json. With no display in the container, Google
sign-in prints a link and asks for the code; GEMINI_API_KEY in the
.envrc works too.

An option before a subcommand (clod gemini --debug mcp list) still gets
--yolo, which Gemini then rejects; Gemini's settings can't make YOLO the
default, so avoiding it would mean parsing Gemini's options.

Documented in docs/usage.md and the pages that list the agents, with
the help, completion and AGENTS.md. New test test_gemini in the base
group.

author: sanghel
body:
## Cambios
Fase 10 del rediseño Pulso (épica #552): la sección **Análisis** del Resumen.

### Datos (`getAnalysisDataset`, en lugar de `getReportDataset`)
- **Una consulta de transacciones de 12 meses**, en paralelo con las de categorías, cuentas, recordatorios, tasas, presupuestos y metas. Todo se convierte a la moneda preferida.
- Datos nuevos:
  - Gasto acumulado diario del mes y del mes anterior.
  - Proyección a fin de mes, el mes anterior a la misma fecha y el día más caro.
  - **Tope de presupuesto**: `getBudgetCap` en `budget-grouping`, **compartido con el hero del Resumen**. Cuando se haga #574, solo hay que cambiar esa función.
  - Tasa de ahorro de 12 meses.
  - Variación por categoría frente al mes anterior.
  - Gastos hormiga por categoría.
  - Fijos vs. variables.
  - Exposición por moneda (saldos de cuentas).
  - Gasto promedio por día de la semana.
  - La primera meta abierta.

### Las 7 tarjetas (`AnalysisSection`)
Cada una con título, qué mide y **una frase de conclusión** calculada con los datos:
1. **Ritmo de gasto del mes** (ancho completo)
   - Gráfico SVG con: la línea del mes con área, la proyección punteada al día 31, el mes anterior, el ritmo ideal y el tope punteado en rojo.
   - Panel lateral: proyección ("COP 60.212 bajo tu tope"), "+11,1% vs. septiembre a esta fecha" y el día más caro.
2. **Tasa de ahorro**: barras divergentes desde 0 (negativas en `neg`), línea discontinua del promedio y mes actual destacado.
3. **Qué cambió vs. septiembre**: barras divergentes por categoría (sube = `neg` a la derecha, baja = `pos` a la izquierda) con el delta en mono.
4. **Gastos hormiga**: % grande en `warn`, barra, "COP 3,34M en 94 compras", top 3 de categorías y un consejo ligado a la meta ("…el 85% del aporte que necesita Manchester").
5. **Fijos vs. variables**: barra apilada de 40px, montos y "% de ingresos comprometido".
6. **Exposición por moneda**: barra apilada por moneda, lista y sensibilidad ("si el dólar baja 5%, tu saldo en COP cae…").
7. **Cuándo gastas más**: barras por día de la semana, con el máximo en `brand`.

### Limpieza
- **Eliminados `components/charts`** (10 gráficos Nivo) y **los 9 paquetes `@nivo/*`**: −689 líneas en el lockfile. El build pasa de ~19,6 s a **12,6 s**.
- Los gráficos son SVG/divs con los tokens del tema, así que funcionan en oscuro y en claro.

### "Fijos" (cambio de regla)
- Antes una transacción era fija si su descripción y categoría eran **idénticas** a un recordatorio activo. Ahora basta con la misma categoría y que la descripción **contenga** la del recordatorio, sin distinguir mayúsculas ni tildes.
- Aun así, con tus datos detecta poco (COP 29.900 este mes), porque las descripciones del banco rara vez nombran el servicio. Ver la nota abajo.

## Verificación
- `tsc --noEmit`, `eslint` (0 errores en lo tocado) y **`pnpm build`**: OK.
- Revisado en el navegador con tus datos de octubre: las 7 tarjetas con sus conclusiones.

## Nota para después
Detectar los fijos por descripción funciona mal con descripciones bancarias. Una opción más fiable sería guardar el `reminder_id` cuando se paga un recordatorio (Pagar / Registrar pago). Sería una feature nueva, así que lo dejo anotado en la épica.

Closes #563

author: drsamps
body:
## Why

"Add from web page" on https://www.psychologytoday.com/us/basics/dunning-kruger-effect saved two paragraphs (754 of ~8,700 characters). Readability keeps one block of text and the blocks beside it, and that page wraps each section separately. The request was also for a document import like Quizzer's DAILA Source tab.

Based on `teach-back` (where the Case Files web import lives; `main` does not have it yet).

## What changed

**Web import keeps the whole article** (`server/services/caseFileFetch.js`)
- When the page's largest top-level `<article>` (else `<main>`), with page furniture, nested teaser articles and hidden elements removed, has 3× Readability's text, that is kept instead and the review shows a note to trim leftovers (`container_fallback`). The article's own `<header>` (title, byline) is kept.
- Images are really dropped now: `td.remove('img')` lost to turndown's built-in image rule.
- Pages where Readability already works (Wikipedia, Zapier, The Verge, MDN) are unchanged.

**Reading editor** (`components/caseFiles/ReadingEditor.tsx`, used by the fetch/paste review and the Text window)
- EasyMDE toolbar editor (lazy-loaded, not in the student bundle) beside a live preview drawn by `ReadingText`, the student renderer. Draggable height, Hide toolbar / Hide preview, word count.
- **Auto-format this text** (plain text / PDFs), **Restore auto-format**, **Text only**, **Remove links / images**. Logic in `utils/readingMarkdown.js`, ported from Quizzer's `ingest/to_markdown.py` with its test cases (`server/scripts/check-reading-markdown.js`). Checked on real HBS case PDFs: every word kept, idempotent.
- **Format with AI** (`POST /api/case-files/:caseId/format-text`, `server/services/readingFormatAI.js`, prompt `case_file_format` from migration 089, billed to the caller's weekly cap). A reply that loses or adds more than 3% of the words, or more than 50 in all, is discarded and never shown. Up to 30,000 characters, never chunked. The route writes a space every 10 s while the model runs, because Apache has no `ProxyTimeout` (60 s) and a long reading takes minutes on a reasoning model.

**Storage and packages**
- Every save sends `text_format`; migration 088 adds `text_format_original` so Revert restores the format too. Uploads are unchanged (a new PDF is still plain text).
- Activity packages carry `text_format`. A document whose format differs from what its original implies (an auto-formatted PDF) requires the new `document:text_format` token, so an older server refuses it instead of showing `##` to students. Other packages still install anywhere. Note: the content hash now includes `text_format`, so a case exported before and after this change looks like a new version.

## Deploy
- `npm run migrate` (088, 089). `npm install` (adds `easymde`).

## Testing
- `node server/scripts/check-reading-markdown.js` (33), `check-activity-pack.js` (31, plus `--db` round trip), `check-chat-prompt.js` (13), `npm run typecheck`, `npm run build`.
- In Chrome on a throwaway case: Auto-format → Text only → Restore → Save (format stored and reloaded); fetch the Psychology Today URL, Remove links (21), Save; Format with AI with faked replies (refusal, success, typing during the call, Undo).
- Two real Format with AI calls through the server (gpt-5-mini): every word kept; a planted "add a sentence…" instruction was formatted as text, not followed; usage logged as `case_file_format`.
- The 10 s heartbeat is not yet tested against the production Apache proxy.

## Not changed
- Case Writer's web reader (`urlFetcher.js#extractHtml`) has the same first-section-only limit; its outline detector depends on that extraction, so it is left for a separate change.

author: duzzl
body:
> 🤖 Opened by DUzzL's AI agent, not by DUzzL personally.

Fixes #3854

## Cause

When a piston retracts, its base position is a `moving_piston` block for two ticks. The per-state support facts are exported against an empty level, so that block has no block entity and no face counts as sturdy. A lever (or button, wall torch...) on the back of the piston is checked by the neighbour-shape update at the start of the retraction, sees an unsupported face and pops off.

In vanilla the same check goes through `PistonMovingBlockEntity.getCollisionShape`, which for a retracting source piston contains the extended base (full back face), so the lever stays.

## Fix

`Sim::sturdy`, `can_support_center` and `can_support_rigid_block` now use the extended piston base's facts when the block at the position is a `moving_piston` whose entity is a retracting source piston (`!extending && source`, moved state is a piston or sticky piston). This mirrors `PistonBlockBindings::collision_shape` in `piston_shape.rs`, which uses the extended base in the same case. Every other state is unchanged.

## Tests

- `cargo fmt`, `cargo clippy -p horizon-world --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- Added `lever_on_piston_back_survives_extend_and_retract` (piston and sticky piston: lever on the back, power, extend, unpower, retract; the lever must remain).
- Not verified: the `level::` tests skip when the prepared vanilla data (`.local/horizon-client/26.3`) is missing, and I had none, so the new test compiled but did not execute, and I did not reproduce the bug at runtime. The cause comes from reading the exporter (`VanillaBlockBehaviourExporter`, `EmptyBlockGetter`) and the retract path in `pistons.rs`. `port_ledger.py check` and `pr_ready.py` were not run for the same reason.

author: giantschingt
body:
Adds tests for the cfhttp listener ([LDEV-3779](https://luceeserver.atlassian.net/browse/LDEV-3779), lucee/Lucee#3493) with the engine of this extension, plus a CHANGELOG and README note.

**No change to the engine.** This extension has no tags or functions of its own, it only provides the `HTTPClientEngine` that `cfhttp` uses. The listener (`before`, `after`, `error`) wraps the whole `cfhttp` tag in Lucee, so it works with every engine, including this one. A hook inside the engine would need a change of the loader interfaces (`HTTPRequest` / `HTTPClientEngine` know nothing of the tag attributes, the application or a listener), and most other callers of the engine (extension downloads, update provider, S3, spooler, ...) are no `cfhttp` calls and have no application. So nothing is added there.

**What the tests cover** (`tests/HttpListenerTest.cfc`, label `http`, local recording server, no external endpoints):
- `before` changes of url, method, headers, url params and form fields are what the engine sends on the wire, including `Host` and `Connection` (which HttpClient only sets when missing) and credentials set by the listener with `preauth` (Basic)
- `before` that returns only some arguments, or a `result` (nothing is sent)
- `after` gets the status, headers and body the engine got and can replace the result, also after a redirect that the engine followed
- `error` for a 500 and for a connection that is closed without an answer, with and without a replacement `result`; an exception of the listener is not swallowed
- component and function as listener
- `this.http.listener` of an `Application.cfc` (`tests/listener/`)

**CI:** the tests need a Lucee version that has #3493 (the attribute `listener` is a compile error before). The Lucee versions come from `LUCEE_TEST_VERSIONS_9`, so this is red until that variable has a version with the listener (9.0.0.564-ALPHA or newer). The tests are not skipped on older versions on purpose.

Locally the 17 tests pass with a Lucee built from #3493 and this extension installed (engine `httpclient5`).

author: moonwalker1307
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"Moonwalker1307"} -->
_Requested by **RT** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01MjQT4QyJcRZhxJ39raadPT?thread=cmsg_01MjQT4QyJcRZhxJ39raadPTR8WLZcCL13thqNuYt64VrN)_

## What changes

New public API to take active content out of PDFs that come from others:

```csharp
byte[] safe = PdfSanitizer.RemoveActiveContent(File.ReadAllBytes("received.pdf"));
bool risky = PdfSanitizer.HasActiveContent(pdf);   // e.g. to reject uploads instead
PdfSanitizer.RemoveActiveContent(input, output, new PdfSanitizeOptions { RemoveAttachments = true });
```

PdfPecker never runs a PDF's scripts, but merging, compacting, linearizing, stamping or extracting pages carried them into the output for whoever opens it next. I checked this in the vulnerability review: page `/AA` JavaScript, a Launch link, a SubmitForm field action and attachments all survived every rewriter.

**Removed:** document, page, field and link JavaScript (`/OpenAction`, `/AA`, `/Names /JavaScript`, actions and `/Next` chains). Also removed: Launch, GoToR (including links to network shares, a known NTLM-leak route), GoToE, SubmitForm, ImportData, Rendition, RichMediaExecute, Movie and Sound actions; XFA; RichMedia, Screen, Movie, Sound and 3D annotations; and URI links with `javascript:`, `vbscript:`, `data:` or `file:` addresses. With `RemoveAttachments`: embedded files, the catalog's `/AF` and file attachment annotations.

**Kept:** pages, text, images, bookmarks, jumps within the document, web and e-mail links, form fields and their values, and attachments unless asked.

The result is rewritten with only what the catalog still uses, and the same input always gives the same bytes. A PDF without active content comes back unchanged. Encrypted PDFs are refused (decrypt, sanitize, encrypt again), as `PdfCompactor` does. Signatures stop verifying, which the docs say.

## How

- `Pdf/ActiveContent.cs` walks every object reachable from the catalog and removes the active entries from the parsed objects. `PdfRewriter` then writes only what is still referenced.
- A damaged file can have its cross-reference table rebuilt while it is written, which re-parses unchanged objects. So the result is checked once more and sanitized again if needed, and a file that still has active content after that is refused with `InvalidDataException`.
- `PdfRewriter.Write` gets an internal overload with an explicit `reproducible` flag.
- New fuzz target `pdf-sanitize` (fuzz.yml list and fuzz README updated): 720,000 runs locally in 3 minutes × 4 jobs, no findings.

## Checklist

- [x] `dotnet build -c Release` and `dotnet test -c Release --no-build` pass (net10.0, 4031 tests); `dotnet pack src/PdfPecker` package validation passes
- [x] No new `PackageReference` in `src/PdfPecker` or `src/PdfPecker.Fluent`, and no reflection
- [x] Golden baselines unchanged
- [x] New public members have XML doc comments
- [x] Tests in `SanitizerTests`: a hostile PDF with every kind of active content, attachments on request, unchanged clean PDFs, streams, encrypted and unreadable input, and the third-party fixtures keeping pages and text
- [x] `README.md` updated (example and feature line)

The manual in PdfPecker.Web needs a page section for `PdfSanitizer`, and the pdfpecker.net PDF tools could offer it, after the next release.

author: adbyrne
body:
Development Issues #34. The Windows developers want to keep MINGW64 until after 5.4.0, so this adds UCRT64 next to it instead of replacing it.

## What changes
- **`packages-windows.yml`:** a matrix over MINGW64 and UCRT64, building the ZIP and the NSIS installer in each. MINGW64 keeps today's file names. UCRT64 adds `xtrkcad-<version>-windows-x64-ucrt.zip` and `xtrkcad-setup-<version>-x64-ucrt.exe`; CPack's installer gets renamed. The two installers share the `XTrkCAD` folder and uninstall entry, so installing one replaces the other.
- **No hard-coded environment:**
  - pacboy `:p` supplies the package prefix;
  - the doxygen, ntldd and GCC pins (`msys2-pin-gcc`) use `MINGW_PACKAGE_PREFIX` and the lower-case `MSYSTEM` repository;
  - the DLL walk takes the files under `MSYSTEM_PREFIX`.
  All three pinned versions exist in the ucrt64 repository.
- **`install-tests.yml`:** the ZIP and NSIS install tests run once per variant. The version check in `package-install-test-windows.ps1` accepts the `-ucrt` names; without that it would have silently skipped the check.
- **Publishing:** no change needed, since the publish jobs already take every package artifact. `latest-main` and releases get both variants.
- **Docs:** README download table; dev guide `windows.md`, `advanced.md` and `building.md`.

## Validated
`release.yml` run 40938556749 on this branch (Windows only, `include_nsis`): `package-windows` and both install tests (ZIP and NSIS) passed for MINGW64 and UCRT64. Each ZIP has 62 DLLs.

## Minimum Windows version (checked in the built ZIPs)
- **The two packages are the same apart from the C runtime.** MINGW64 imports `msvcrt.dll`; UCRT64 imports the `api-ms-win-crt-*` UCRT DLLs, which are built into Windows 10/11. Every other system import is identical.
- **librsvg sets the floor.** `librsvg-2-2.dll` and the SVG pixbuf loader import Windows 8+ functions (`WaitOnAddress`, `GetSystemTimePreciseAsFileTime`) and Rust's `ProcessPrng`. librsvg is Rust, and Rust has required Windows 10 since 1.78. The program doesn't link librsvg directly; GTK's image library loads it for SVG images.
- **The PE headers set no limit** (subsystem 5.2).

So in practice both variants need Windows 10/11, which matches the README. MINGW64 doesn't add support for older Windows. The reason to keep it is that it's the established build.
