body: Closes #125 ## Summary A visual polish pass, checked by looking at it: a script now screenshots every page, and the UI was fixed against those pictures. - **Screenshots.** `pnpm --filter @stash/web screenshots` boots the api under `alchemy dev` (stage `screenshots`, no credentials, no cloud), seeds synthetic data and a web session through two new dev-only routes (`POST /_smoke/seed`, `POST /_smoke/session`, live only when `SMOKE_ROUTES` is on), runs Vite against it and captures 6 views × 2 themes × 2 widths with headless Chromium (Playwright from the catalog) into `docs/screenshots/` (24 PNGs). It exits 1 if a page scrolls sideways (`document.documentElement.scrollWidth > width`) or a visible button or link has no accessible name. - **Two bugs that made the deployed UI look broken** (found from the screenshots): - The web api client sent `traceparent`/`b3` (Effect's HttpClient default), which the api's CORS doesn't allow. Every cross-origin preflight failed, so pages showed their error state. Propagation is now off in `withSession`, with a regression test. - `apps/web/src/styles.css` didn't list `@stash/web-search`, `-settings` or `-auth` under `@source`. Tailwind never generated the classes only those packages use, which is why Settings looked cramped (no section gaps) and search highlights were browser-yellow. A test now checks every feature package with templates is listed. - **Spacing and page header.** `docs/design.md` gains "Layout rules": a 4/8/12/16/24/32/48 scale, a `` (20px/600 title plus a mono line of counts) on every page, rows ≥44px, and centred empty/error states with an explanation line and an action (Retry, Clear filter, Add a device). - **Header.** The header matches the content's width and padding. The right side is one cluster: a sync dot plus mono `online`/`offline` with a tooltip, Search ⌘K, a theme menu (System/Light/Dark radio items), and an account menu (Settings, Sign out) that replaces the separate logout icon. Every icon-only control has an `aria-label` and a `title`. - **Phone (390px).** The nav becomes a bottom bar above the home indicator, the header keeps only the cluster's icons, row metadata wraps under the title, shortcut footers are hidden, and no page scrolls sideways. ## Screenshots Synthetic data only (`example.com` URLs, invented titles and devices). The viewport grows to the page's height before each capture, so the phone's bottom nav sits at the bottom as on a screen. body:
## Summary

- Adds `text`, the Transcript as plain text, and `language`, the language spoken for the longest total time, to the Transcribe Audio output. The Jobs API has no full-text field, so the integration builds them from the Segments.
- Without timestamps, Segments flow into paragraphs. A new paragraph starts after a sentence ends, when the Speaker changes, and around non-speech sounds such as `[music]`. Silence is left out.
- Adds an "Include Timestamps in Transcript?" option that puts every Segment on its own line, such as `[0:04] Speaker A: ...`.
- Keeps `output` unchanged, so existing mappings still work. The JSON copy stays the job as the API sent it.
- Builds the Sample per call instead of by mutating a shared object. It keeps the request fields the API echoes back and drops the undocumented `seek` field.
- Labels the output fields and ends the action description with a period, as check D021 asks.

Labels and help text come from Gemini 3.8 Flash (High) through the copywrite skill.

## Verification

```text
$ pnpm test
      Tests  39 passed (39)
$ zapier-platform validate
 Only the expected C002/C003 notices for Hotwords and Prompt, plus D028 and D003
```

On snapshot `0.0.0-text`, run remotely through Zapier's servers:

- **25-second clip with audio labels and timestamps.** `performResume` returned `language: "en"` and `[0:00] Hey everybody.` followed by `[0:01] Um, so today's video is gonna be...`.
- **25-second clip with speakers and timestamps.** It returned `[0:00] Speaker A: Hey everybody.` and so on.

author: marianoalvarosaiz
body:
https://liferay.atlassian.net/browse/LPD-108839

Supersedes #4156, with the review from @LuisOrtiz89 applied, and #4134.

## What Is Being Fixed

Adding a virtual instance through `POST /portal-instances/batch`, which the Virtual Instances UI also uses, sent "The instance X is ready to use." from `PortalInstanceResourceImpl.postPortalInstance`, inside the batch item's transaction. The instance is initialized later, in the commit callback that `CompanyLocalServiceImpl.checkCompany` registers, so the notification arrived up to ~20 s before the instance was usable. When an exception escaped `registerCompany` or `initCompany`, the user was still told the instance was ready.

## How It Is Being Fixed

The batch import task runs on an executor thread with no surrounding transaction, and each item commits its own transaction, which runs the instance initialization synchronously on the same thread. By the time the task reaches COMPLETED or FAILED, every committed item has finished initializing its instance.

`PortalInstanceImportTaskPostAction` records each instance a CREATE task adds, and `PortalInstanceBatchEngineImportTaskExceptionHandler` drops the record of an item that failed, so an instance is never reported both ready and failed. A `BatchEngineImportTask` model listener, scoped to `PortalInstance` tasks, sends the Add notification when the task reaches COMPLETED or FAILED. An instance in `PortalInstancePool`, whose `add` is the last step of the initialization, is reported as ready, and one missing from it as "The instance X was created with errors.", reusing the messages and notification handler change from Luis.

The fix stays in `headless-portal-instances` and `portal-instances-web`, with no new transaction callbacks, no changes to `portal-impl` or `portal-kernel`, and no API changes.

In a batch with several instances, each success notification waits until the whole task finishes; the Virtual Instances UI adds one instance at a time. Listener failures that `PortalInstanceLifecycleListenerManagerImpl` only logs still leave the instance in the pool, so they are reported as ready; returning the result instead of only logging it is LPD-109767.

Pi ruling (b) on task k17205kc0zy1qfvq20yw35rvzs8ah4jv: on an `evidence:` line of `send_message`, a live-state literal (PR state, task status, npm dist-tag) is REFUSED when that same line carries no command, even if the state is true. Header comment of `fresh-state-guard.ts` says how.
- 4 existing tests rewritten to carry a command line (they used a bare literal, now refused by design).

author: luxeonn
body:
## 🎯 Miért készült?
A kézzel írt getter/setter/konstruktor boilerplate és az ismétlődő objektumleképezések következetes kiváltása Lombok `@Getter`/`@Builder`/`@NoArgsConstructor` annotációkkal és MapStruct mapperekkel úgy, hogy az API, az adatbázis és az üzleti logika változatlan marad.

## 🛠️ Mit módosít / Mit javít?
- **Lombok 1.18.42** + **MapStruct 1.6.3** (+ `lombok-mapstruct-binding`) a Gradle buildben.
- **`@Builder` és setter-elimináció:** 19 modell-, DTO- és entitásosztály kapott `@Builder` támogatást (`@Builder.Default`-tal, illetve konstruktor-szintű `@Builder`-rel a normalizáló konstruktorokon, `toBuilder = true`-val a copy-update helyeken). A csak olvasható DTO-król és értékobjektumokról (`MarketStatsDto`, `PriceDropItemDto`, `PortalStatusDto`, `DashboardResponseDto`, `PortalSource`, `PriceInfo`, `PropertyDetails`) a `@Setter` teljesen lekerült. A portálparserek, a `ListingNormalizer`, a `PropertyParser`, a `MarketAnalyticsEngine`, a `SearchResultAggregator`, a `SearchExecutionEngine` és a `DashboardPresentationService` setter-láncok helyett buildert használnak.
- **Teljes MapStruct lefedettség (`JpaEntityMapper` & `PresentationMapper`):**
  - `JpaEntityMapper` (`componentModel = "spring"`, `unmappedTargetPolicy = ERROR`): a korábbi kézi `toItem`, `toItems`, `toProperty` és `toEntity` mezőmásolásai is MapStructra kerültek (`@BeanMapping(builder = @Builder(disableBuilder = true))`, `@AfterMapping`, `@MappingTarget updateEntityFromItem`), a meglévő `toSourceListing`, `toListingObservation`, `toPriceHistoryEntry`, `toStatusLogEntry` és `create*Entity` leképezések mellett.
  - `PresentationMapper`: MapStruct mapper a `PortalScrapeResult -> PortalStatusDto`, `(SearchResult, MarketStatsDto, List<PortalStatusDto>) -> DashboardResponseDto`, `IngatlanItem -> PriceDropItemDto` és `IngatlanItem -> SourceListing` konverziókra.
- **Konvenciók és tesztek:** frissített `AGENTS.md` irányelvek; célzott mapper unit tesztek a null/fallback ágakra.

## 🧪 Tesztelés és Ellenőrzés
- `./gradlew check bootJar` ✅ (Checkstyle 0 hiba, teljes tesztkészlet zöld, JaCoCo ≈ 86.7%)
- A frontendet és az OpenAPI szerződést nem érinti.

## 🛡️ Thematic Agent Approval Gate
- [x] **fullstack-architect**: [NO_FINDING] - Réteghatárok, JSON szerializáció és JPA entitás-szemantika változatlan maradt a `@Builder` és MapStruct refaktorálás mellett.
- [x] **scraper-security-engineer**: [NOT_APPLICABLE] - Portál-lekérdezési és hálózati biztonsági logika nem változott, csak az `IngatlanItem`/`PriceInfo`/`PropertyDetails` példányosítás lett builder-alapú.
- [x] **quality-devops-engineer**: [NO_FINDING] - Checkstyle, tesztek és JaCoCo lefedettség (86.7%) a helyi és CI futtatáson egyaránt megfelelnek.

Closes #322

author: montana
body:
Closes #1255.

## What was wrong

Building a `Simulator` with the analytical Jacobian (the default) took exponential time for a compartment whose size is read through a diamond of rules, `r_i := sin(r_{i-1}) + cos(r_{i-2})`.
- The dilution term's rate law is 92 characters: `-Sn·(d cv/dt)/cv`.
- Written out with its functions, it is 56 thousand characters at 12 rules, 1.5 million at 18 and 12 million at 22.
- #1124 collects a diamond of sums (`r_{i-1} + r_{i-2}`), but not this one, so it falls back to writing the text out.
- The derivative is as long. Deriving it, checking it and printing it cost the build:

| rules | main | `jacobian="fd"` |
|---|---|---|
| 12 | 3.1 s | < 0.01 s |
| 14 | 10.9 s | |
| 18 | 57 s | |
| 22 | 110 s | |

Past about 16 rules, main often ends on the finite-difference Jacobian anyway, after paying for it. Measured at 18 rules, beside a running suite: 28.7 s (25.6 s with `codegen=True`), then `declined: the build-time derivation exceeded its 20.0s budget`.

The GH #95 budget did not stop the cost, for two reasons:
- it is checked only before each `sp.diff`, and most of the time went after, walking and printing the derivative (19.5 M nodes traversed at 12 rules);
- the native saturable path runs first and wrote the text out with no memo (492,581 recursive `_inline_functions` calls at 22 rules).

## The fix

A rate law past the inlining limit that does not collect now declines the analytical Jacobian before anything is written out.
- **The check:** `_inlined_for_derivation`, in front of both derivation paths (`differentiate_rate_law` and the native `differentiate_rate_law_native`).
  - The limit is the existing `_INLINE_TEXT_LIMIT`, 20,000 characters written out, past which #1124 already tries `_compact_inlined`.
  - The predicted length comes from the existing `_inlined_length`, which costs nothing.
  - A law that collects shorter is derived from its collected form, as before. One under the limit is untouched.
- **The decline** has its own census kind, `written_out`, and names the law and its length.

**After:** 0.02-0.03 s at any depth (12, 18, 22, 30 rules), and the run is bit-identical to `jacobian="fd"`.

**Why declining is the right answer here, not a loss:** a derivative this long costs every Newton setup more to evaluate than differences of the right-hand side do. It is the same bet GH #95 makes, decided from the length instead of after the time is spent. On the three corpus models below that kept a complete analytical Jacobian, it bought neither run time nor accuracy:
- BIOMD0000000385 ran 0.28 s analytical against 0.14 s FD, in the same 177 steps;
- BIOMD0000000628 ran 0.098 s against 0.03 s. Against a tight reference (rtol 1e-12), both are 4e-4 off at default tolerances: 4.05e-4 analytical, 4.36e-4 FD. The two tight runs agree to 6.5e-12.

## Measured: the corpus, main against this branch

Real builds of 1,500 models (1,323 BioModels and 177 `.net`), 1,463 of which build on both sides. All runs used `codegen=False`, because the codegen cache key hashes bngsim's Python sources, so this branch compiles every model cold; the compile is not what this changes.

- **1,454 models keep their status, and 1,452 of them end bit-identical.** The other two (BIOMD0000000472, 473) differ by 4e-15 and 3e-17 with codegen on and are identical with it off.
- **9 change status:**

| model | main | this branch | build | answer |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| BIOMD0000000246 | declined: **budget** (20 s spent) | written_out | 30.7 s → 0.06 s | identical |
| MODEL1006230049, -053, -077 | declined: budget | written_out | 20 s → 5.0-6.3 s | identical |
| MODEL1006230090 | declined: budget | written_out | 20.0 s → 1.9 s | its run fails on both (SimulationError) |
| BIOMD0000000385 | complete | written_out | 9.6 s → 0.29 s | 4e-15 |
| BIOMD0000000628 | complete | written_out | 18.1 s → 0.05 s | 1.7e-4, within the integration error above |
| MODEL1006230100, -112 | complete | written_out | 1.0 s → 0.6 s | their runs fail on both (SimulationError) |

## Tests (`test_jacobian_written_out_decline.py`, 9)

| test | on main |
|---|---|
| the issue's model at 12, 18 and 30 rules builds in under 2 s, declines `written_out`, and runs bit-identically to `jacobian="fd"` | **fail** (3.1 s, 57 s, minutes) |
| the same with `codegen=True` | **fail** (25.6 s at 18 rules, then a budget decline) |
| neither path writes the law out (`_inline_functions` patched to raise), at 30 rules | **fail** |
| `written_out` is a census kind | **fail** |
| controls: 10 rules (18 thousand characters) keeps its analytical Jacobian; #1124's sum diamond past the limit gets its collected form, not a decline | pass |

The existing `test_jacobian_diamond_of_rules.py` (#1124) passes unchanged.

## Mutations

| mutant | fails |
|---|---|
| G1: the law is written out instead of declined | the 12-rule build |
| G2: the native path writes it out (as on main) | the 30-rule build (3.5 min) |
| G3: the decline filed under `budget` | the kind test |
| G4: the limit 100× higher | the 12-rule build |

## Checked

- **Full suite:** 16,760 passed, 138 skipped (on a core built at this commit). `pre-commit run --all-files` and `sphinx -W` are clean.

## Not in this PR

- **The chain-rule derivation the issue sketches**, differentiating through the rules by name. That would keep an analytical Jacobian for these models, but its derivative would have to reference intermediate values the emitters cannot yet hold.
- **Other places that inline a law as text** (`_codegen.py`'s RHS paths, `_switch_sensitivity`). They are not in the default build path this issue measures.

author: adampingel
clansty
body:
Model: deepseek-v4.1-flash

## Problem and resulting behavior

The interface has had gettext plumbing since #37, but no catalogue ships, so the interface is English everywhere. On top of that, several labels could not be translated even with a catalogue installed, because they were assembled from bare string literals and so were neither extracted into the template nor translated at runtime:

- the context menu's Terminal and Open with entries: `application_items` in `window/context_menu/entries.rs` selected `Open in Terminal` / `Open containing folder in Terminal` / `Open folder with…` / `Open with…` into variables and passed them to `item()`, which does not translate, and two of those four were not in the template at all;
- the sidebar's section menu: `section_item` in `window/sidebar/menu.rs` built `{verb} section “{name}”` from the bare verbs `Hide` / `Show`;
- the sidebar's Home, This PC, Network and Recycle Bin rows (`fixed_entry` kept the label as it came);
- the details pane's folder type (`kind: "Folder"`);
- the folder-size texts `Scanning…`, `Unavailable`, `Not scanned` and `Calculating…`, and the `1 file` / `1 folder` singular counts with their `, ` separator;
- the Permissions page's Owner and Group rows;
- the Default apps buttons `Enable` and `Apply now` (`Apply now` was not in the template);
- the About page's group headings, button labels and build description.

This pull request adds `native/po/zh_CN.po` (1987 messages, `nplurals=1; plural=0;`), takes those literals through `gettext`/`gettext_static`/`message_id` so that extraction and translation both reach them, and regenerates `native/po/openxplorer.pot`.

With the catalogue installed — `share/locale/zh_CN/LC_MESSAGES/<package>.mo`, which `package_data.py` already installs from `native/po/*.po` — a zh_CN desktop shows the interface in Chinese. Without it nothing changes: every new call falls back to its English message id.

The catalogue's name is the gettext domain, and each packaging channel now keeps its own, named after its package: `openxplorer.mo` for the stable app and `openxplorer-native.mo` for the preview. Both packages install into the same `/usr/share/locale`, and neither dpkg nor RPM lets two packages own one file, so a shared name would stop a machine with the preview installed from installing the stable package. `ox_core::i18n::install` takes the domain from its caller, `crates/ox-app/src/config.rs` picks it from the application ID the build already sets, and `package_data.py` names the file from the same channel.

## Validation

Run on Arch Linux with Rust 1.97.1 and GTK 4; the GTK runs used a disposable `HOME`, `XDG_*` set and `xvfb-run` with a private D-Bus session, never the live desktop.

- `python3 native/tools/i18n.py check` — template and generated UI table match the sources.
- `python3 native/tools/test_i18n.py`, `test_package_data.py`, `test_package_i18n.py`, `test_package_recipes.py`, `test_flatpak.py`, `test_build_deb.py`, `test_release_publication.py`, `test_check.py` — pass. Two of their cases are new here: one checks that each channel's catalogue is named after its package, the other that the domains in `crates/ox-app/src/config.rs` are the channels' package names.
- `python3 native/parity/check.py` — exits 0.
- `cargo fmt --manifest-path native/Cargo.toml --all -- --check` — clean.
- `msgfmt --check native/po/zh_CN.po` — no errors.
- `cargo test -p ox-core` — 989 passed, 2 failed; both failures reproduce on an unmodified checkout here (the clipboard test against the Python app and the trash monitor test), so they are environmental.
- `cargo test -p ox-app --lib properties::`, `window::sidebar`, `window::details_pane` — pass.
- `cargo test -p ox-app --lib settings_page::` — 31 passed, 55 failed, with exactly the same counts on an unmodified checkout; those tests collide on the private session bus when they are not run through `check.py`.
- Manual screenshots, read by me: the main window, all seven Settings pages, the folder, file and sidebar-section context menus, both Properties tabs and the keyboard-shortcuts window are Chinese.
- Both builds rendered with `LANGUAGE=zh_CN.UTF-8` and the staged catalogue: the preview reads `openxplorer-native.mo` and the stable build `openxplorer.mo`, both in Chinese. As a control, the preview binary with only the stable channel's `openxplorer.mo` present stays English, so it cannot read the other channel's file. Staging both channels through `package_data.install` for the Debian and FHS layouts and diffing the payloads, they now share no path at all.
- Arch recipe: `makepkg` builds the package and it installs beside the previous one; the installed program renders Chinese from `/usr/share/locale/zh_CN/LC_MESSAGES/openxplorer.mo`. The Debian, RPM and Flatpak recipes were not built.
- `python3 native/tools/check.py` — the inventory checks, the drawn-icon guard, rustfmt and the tool tests pass. It then stops in the Clippy stage, on `clippy::duration_suboptimal_units` (`Duration::from_secs(60)` should be `from_mins(1)`) in five `ox-core` files this change does not touch: the local Clippy 1.97 has the lint, the pinned one does not. The changed files raise nothing. Running the driver's test stage on its own (`check_rust_tests`, the same isolation) passes every executable and the doctests except five, which fail in this container and fail the same way on an unmodified `main`: `display_scale` (its snapshot render aborts, "the snapshot at scale 1 failed: signal: 6"), `launch` (`launches_share_one_instance_that_quits_and_restarts_on_request`), `location_fixture_drift` (`smb://[V1.x]/` is parsed differently from the committed Python fixture here), `ops_recycle_bin` (exit 101) and the `ox_app` executable (SIGABRT).

Not run: the Debian, RPM and Flatpak package builds, and the two real Debian packages installed side by side (no root here).

## Compatibility and release impact

No persisted path, DBus name, keyring schema or MIME handler changes. Desktop entry and metainfo keys stay English, so nothing in `package_i18n.py` is affected. The only new installed file is the catalogue, built from `native/po/zh_CN.po` by the existing packaging step. The template gained five messages (`Apply now`, `Updates`, `Read license & source information`, `Open containing folder in Terminal`, `Open with…`) and lost none. All examples in the comments are the upstream ones; no private paths or shares are included.

body:
Closes #171 (PR 2 of 2: the screens; the API came in #208). Owner decisions 1a–5a, 2026-10-29. No API change and no migration.

## What changed

- **Cash Drawer on POS (1a).** A tab next to POS Terminal and Sales History, where the cashier:
  - opens a session with a float (0 allowed);
  - puts cash in (float top-up, other) or takes it out (bank drop, petty cash, other), with a reason;
  - closes with a blind count, then sees the result (Z number, over or short) and prints the Z report.

  Nothing shows what is expected while the session is open. A badge by the tabs says "Cash session open" or "No cash session".
- **Cash Sessions page (2a).** Under Finance, for Admin, Manager and Finance_Officer.
  - The branch's sessions, filtered by status. A session opens with its X report (open) or Z report (closed).
  - An Admin or Manager accepts a count beyond the limit with a reason ("Accept count"), or closes a session left open ("Close for …").
  - The review notification opens the session.
- **Printing (3a).** The X and Z reports print with the float, expected, counted, variance, totals by kind and method, the movements, and lines for "Counted by" and "Checked by".
- **Settings (4a).** A Cash tab with Require Cash Session and Cash Variance Limit, set per branch like the others.
- **Cash refused (5a).** Where the branch takes cash only with a session and none is open, a banner on the terminal says so, with "Open cash session". A cash sale refused for that reason brings the same button.
- The README says where the screens are.

## How it was verified

- **Tests first.** These failed before the change (every mocked answer checked against its contract):
  - `CashSessionsFeature.test.tsx`: 10 tests;
  - one Settings test;
  - two POS terminal tests.

  They cover opening, cash in and out, the blind count and Z report, the list and report, accepting and closing by a Manager, the menu, the notification, the settings, and the refused sale.
- **Checks.** Lint 0 problems; web typecheck clean; web tests 421 passed (51 files); web build passes.
- **Fresh install** with `npm run db:demo`, through the screens with Playwright (ALL OK):
  - the admin finds both settings under Settings → Cash; with the setting on, Sara sees the banner and opens with 0 from it;
  - Sara sells Dune for cash (recorded on her session) and takes out 5 for tea;
  - she sees no expected amount, neither on the tab nor in the count; she closes 1.00 short and prints the Z report;
  - the admin opens it under Cash Sessions with the expected amount and the petty cash;
  - `db:check` passes 24 rules with 0 errors.

## Summary

RiskGate inspections done in GoCanvas can now be loaded, read, and reported on in the portal, with their photos. Along the way, every file in object storage gets one record.

- **Risk inspections:** GoCanvas form definitions are imported per operator; their sections become zones. Submissions are parsed into typed zones, materials, and a RAMP summary, with every response kept as sent and anything unreadable listed in `parse_warnings` (older submissions use options and formats the current form no longer has). author: jayadelson
body:
## Summary
- New **Linux** workflow on every PR, every push to main and on manual dispatch:
  - amd64 and arm64 (u18): build and test; arm64 runs natively.
  - armhf (u12): cross-compiled, build only.
  - The Python wheels are built in a separate job.
- Each architecture runs the release's own `scripts/linux-build.sh` in the release builder image. It then checks the release file names and that the library was built for that architecture, so CI builds what ships.
- Building the test suite on Linux for the first time exposed several Linux-only problems; they are fixed here.

## Details
- **Production builds:**
  - A merge to main builds production with the encryption secret, exactly as a release does. A broken release build therefore shows up on the merge, not on release day.
  - Pull requests (forks get no secrets) build the same packages non-production. `scripts/build-core.sh` now takes `SCORBIT_SDK_PRODUCTION` from the environment and still defaults to ON.
  - The release workflow now sets ON explicitly.
- **Tests:** `scripts/linux-test.sh <arch>` builds `tests/` in the builder image with that architecture's toolchain, and runs ctest when the architecture is the machine's own. It builds Debug, since the suite compiles the SDK with `-Werror`, and at Release optimisation GCC reports a stringop-overflow false positive inside Boost's `sha1.hpp`.
- **Runners:**
  - GitHub-hosted by default, switchable through the `RUNNER_AMD64` / `RUNNER_ARM64` repository variables.
  - Pull requests from forks always get the hosted default, so a self-hosted runner never runs untrusted code.
  - Checkout does not persist credentials into the mounted workspace.
  - Only PR runs cancel each other; every run on main completes.
- **Found by the first Linux build of the suite:**
  - Static dependencies were not PIC (`tools.cmake` only sets it for a top-level project), so the shared SDK could not link. Fixed in `tests/CMakeLists.txt`.
  - munit needs `librt` on u12's glibc (before 2.17).
  - Catch2 tried to run cross-built binaries to list their tests; discovery now happens when ctest runs.
  - The updater tests reached the Linux remount code with a fake path. Remounting is now a pair of protected virtuals on `Updater`, which the tests override, so they never touch the host's mounts.
  - The gzip download-limit test needs a libcurl built with zlib, and the Linux builder's is not. It is skipped there, and reported as skipped. The SDK never asks for compression, so this only matters for a server that compresses unasked.
  - The worker "post does not block" bound was 3 ms and failed at 3.8 ms under load. 50 ms still proves posting does not wait for the 100 ms task.
- The disabled template workflows (MacOS, Install, Style, Documentation) are left as they are.

## Testing Notes
I ran everything locally in `dilshodm/gcc-builder:8`, the image `DOCKER_RELEASE` pins:
- **arm64:**
  - `SCORBIT_SDK_PRODUCTION=OFF ./scripts/linux-build.sh arm64` produced all four release-named packages plus encrypt_tool. `file` reports the library as `ARM aarch64`.
  - `./scripts/linux-test.sh arm64` ran the full suite natively: `100% tests passed, 0 tests failed out of 525`, with the gzip test skipped.
- **armhf:**
  - `linux-build.sh armhf` produced the u12 packages. `file` reports the library as `ARM, EABI5`.
  - `linux-test.sh armhf` cross-built the whole suite.
- **Python wheels:** `make python python27` produced both wheel names the release uploads.
- **macOS:** a test build with Boost fetched by CPM passes all 525 tests, including the gzip test, which runs there.
- **Not run locally:** amd64 runs for the first time in this PR's CI. I couldn't run `clang-format` or `cmake-format` locally.

FIXES: SB-6104

author: kvaksrud
body:
Closes #31

Ports `api/gates/*` and `core/triggers/*` from 4.2.2.

## What changed
- **Registries instead of numeric ids.** Triggers and actions now live in two registries, `buildcraftreforged:trigger` and `buildcraftreforged:action` (`ActionManager.TRIGGER_REGISTRY` / `ACTION_REGISTRY`), synced to clients. Each `ModuleRegisters` has `triggers` and `actions` registers. Entries are named after the 4.2.2 field (`triggerMachineActive` → `trigger_machine_active`). The 4.2.2 unique tags still resolve through `ActionManager.triggers` / `actions`, for the P9 importer. Codecs and stream codecs are provided for saves, packets and data components.
- **Machine trigger: new "blocked" state** (plan 8.3). `TriggerMachine` now uses `State { Active, Inactive, Blocked }`. The new `trigger_machine_blocked` is driven by `IMachine.isBlocked()`, a default method that returns false. "Work Done" is false while a machine is blocked.
- **Inventory and fluid triggers** read `Capabilities.Item.BLOCK` / `Capabilities.Fluid.BLOCK`, so vanilla and other mods' blocks work too. They keep the 4.2.2 slot and tank logic. #23 and #24 aren't merged, so the triggers use the NeoForge handlers directly.
- **Parameters.** `TriggerParameter` uses `ValueInput`/`ValueOutput` with the `stack` key, plus `CODEC`/`STREAM_CODEC`. 4.2.2 never stored triggers in item NBT, so no data component is registered yet. #60 builds the gate item component from these codecs.
- `IMachine.allowAction(IAction)` is back, which resolves #21's seam. `IFillerRegistry.getActions()` is back (#34 is merged).
- Icons are GUI sprites (`buildcraftreforged:triggers/...`). I copied the 4.2.2 PNGs to `textures/gui/sprites/triggers/`. The blocked icon still needs new art.
- Docs: PORTING-NOTES section "Triggers and actions (#31)"; PARITY rows ticked *compiles* with the new ids, plus a row for the blocked trigger; BUGFIXES entry for the upstream triage (no fix applies).

## Tests
GameTests `trigger_registries`, `trigger_machine`, `trigger_inventory` and `trigger_fluid` run against a test-only machine block in the gametest source set (two item slots, a 4000 mB tank, `IMachine`) and a vanilla chest. They cover registry and tag lookups, codec round trips, every core trigger's states with and without parameters, and the default trigger and action providers.

`./gradlew build runGameTestServer`: build passes, all 8 GameTests pass.

author: psoldunov
body:
## Summary

Two SearXNG changes on one branch.

The web UI gets a custom theme. nginx injects a stylesheet into every page:

```diff
 search.theswisscheese.com (nginx, basic auth)
   location /        → SearXNG 127.0.0.1:8790
+    proxy_set_header Accept-Encoding ""     # sub_filter needs a plain body
+    sub_filter </head> → <link rel="stylesheet" href="/theme/theme.css?v=<store hash>">
+  location /theme/  → linkFarm "searxng-theme"
+    theme.css            hosts/bigtasty/modules/services/searxng-theme/theme.css
+    fonts/MonaSans.ttf   pkgs.mona-sans, MonaSans[wdth,wght].ttf
```

The theme overrides the simple theme's `--color-*` variables for light, dark and black. It sets Mona Sans, turns the search box into a pill with a round gold button, and replaces the hard-coded "SearXNG" wordmark with "The Search Cheese". The `?v=` comes from the store hash: store files have mtime 1, so browsers would otherwise keep an old stylesheet.

Agents search through SearXNG instead of their built-in web search:

```text
Claude Code  PreToolUse hook on WebSearch exits 2 and points at mcp__plugin_hm_searxng__searxng_web_search
Codex        web_search = "disabled"; the preamble names the searxng tools
pi           extensions/searxng-search.ts blocks web_search and source_check, points at the searxng MCP server
```

## Evidence

- **Before:** stock simple theme.
  **After:** a local preview, with SearXNG from the same nixpkgs pin behind a small proxy that injects the link the way nginx does. Screenshots of home, results, images, preferences and stats at 1440, 768 and 390 px, light and dark, are in `/tmp/searxng-preview/before/` and `/tmp/searxng-preview/after/` on the Mac. The search button measured as an exact circle in all 24 states checked.
- `nix eval` of BigTasty: the toplevel evaluates, and the `/` location renders as

  ```nginx
  proxy_set_header Accept-Encoding "";
  sub_filter '</head>' '<link rel="stylesheet" href="/theme/theme.css?v=jl8saywj2i4k"></head>';
  sub_filter_once on;
  ```

- The agent web-search commit has no test run here.

## Test plan

- [ ] Rebuild BigTasty, open search.theswisscheese.com in light and dark, run a search
- [ ] Network tab: `/theme/theme.css?v=…` and `/theme/fonts/MonaSans.ttf` return 200
- [ ] `/search?q=test&format=json` still returns JSON (sub_filter only rewrites text/html)
- [ ] Preferences still save
- [ ] Rebuild the Mac: Claude Code's WebSearch is refused with the SearXNG hint, and Codex and pi search through SearXNG

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way

Reverting and rebuilding brings back the stock look and the built-in search tools. No data or state changes.

**Blast Radius:** small

A stylesheet bug only affects the SearXNG web UI; the JSON API the agents call is untouched. SearXNG now sends uncompressed responses to nginx over loopback, and Cloudflare still compresses toward the browser. If the searxng MCP server is down, agents on this machine have no web search until it is back. Not checked: `nginx -t` on the real host, Firefox, right-to-left languages.

author: masterace572-prog
body:
## The two reports

> "It's not copying obb saying copy failed try again"
> "obb copied fail but when I manually pasted obb and launch game it shows launch failed game not available but the game launches"

Both were the app trusting a single answer where it should have checked reality.

### Copy

`AppManager.copyObbFolder()` read one folder, wrote into one folder, and passed
the caller only true/false — so `MAct` printed **"Copy failed. Try again."** for a
missing file, a folder it could not create, and a permission error alike.

- The search now covers the sandbox dir, `Android/obb/<pkg>`,
  `Android/media/<pkg>`, `Download`, `Downloads` and the storage root, taking the
  newest `main.<n>.<pkg>.obb` (or any `.obb` in a folder owned by the game).
- The GAME DATA card names the copy in use: **Ready · Android/obb**.
- An obb in the phone's own `Android/obb` counts as ready — the sandbox serves
  that path, which is exactly why a hand-pasted file starts the game. A write
  into the sandbox that fails is therefore not a failure.
- Real failures now show the reason (folders checked / path that could not be
  created / sandbox exception) in a dialog with **Retry** and **Launch anyway**.

### Launch

`obtainSplashLaunchIntent` returning null was treated as "the game is not
available", even though the game was opening. Now:

1. `obtainSplashLaunchIntent` → `startActivity`
2. else `launchAppWithSplash(ctx, pkg)`
3. else `getLaunchIntentForPackage`

then after 3.5 s it asks `isAppRunning(pkg)` and only prints *Launch failed*
when every path threw. A launch that was handed over but is still coming up says
nothing (and clears itself) instead of lying. The "container not ready" check no
longer blocks the launch either — it is logged.

## Checks

- `Build loader APK` **success** → release **`loader-50`**
  https://github.com/masterace572-prog/Kurrrrrro/releases/download/loader-50/xlox-loader.apk
- Resource pre-flight (ids, colours, drawables) clean; every Java file parses.
- `docs/LOADER.md` §4b rewritten to describe the lookup order and the launch
  fallbacks.

body:
Empresas passam a receber recursos e limites por uma única resolução: atribuição manual válida, assinatura Cakto verificada, teste grátis existente e ausência de licença. A Central de Administração de Clientes permite conceder ou remover planos com revisão, controle concorrente e histórico; assinaturas comerciais e sessões são preservadas.

O servidor aplica as permissões nas APIs, agenda, profissionais, IA, filas e envio final. A interface reutiliza os componentes e estilos existentes, atualiza o acesso sem logout e preserva dados excedentes no downgrade. Novas compras são impedidas enquanto houver atribuição manual ativa, inclusive se o checkout já estava aberto.

A migração aditiva 0050 exige backup privado verificado e aplica atomicamente a decisão autorizada: 9 empresas existentes no Essencial sem prazo e 1 espaço administrativo com acesso completo. Não altera status das empresas, não cria assinatura nem cobrança. O worker aguarda o marcador da implantação. A recuperação preserva a migração/auditoria e requer correção compatível para frente ou restauração controlada; a imagem antiga não deve ser promovida sem verificar sua compatibilidade com 0050.

Validação no commit final a6c7144: quatro jobs de planos aprovados, com 1013 unidades, 161 DOM, release/bootstrap PostgreSQL 2/2, PostgreSQL 171/171 e 120 cenários do painel real em Chromium/WebKit, seis dimensões e dois temas, além do smoke do catálogo. A regressão de agendamentos também passou: 195+43 cenários de banco, 436 contratos Node/QR, 24 cenários visuais e contenção limitada a 50 operações em voo (100/500/1000 tentativas, um vencedor por horário). Matrizes adicionais de consumidores passaram: 336 WhatsApp e 164 campos/acesso. Cobranças e saídas externas bloqueadas ou simuladas nos testes; nenhuma alegação de capacidade de produção.

Limites conhecidos: suporte prioritário ainda sem fluxo operacional; campanhas permanecem no modo de rascunho existente. ## Outcome

A lock containing runtime `split@1.0` and development-only `split@2.0 -> dev-child@1.0` now keeps the latter two packages development-scoped. Previously, name-only traversal promoted all three to runtime and the recorder accepted those incorrect rows.

## Scope

Only the classifier, recorder, and their tests change. This is a classification correction, not a new vulnerability or production-exposure finding.

Low: CI dependency-graph tooling only. Ambiguous/unresolved references now fail closed rather than assigning guessed scopes. The existing root-selection and dev/docs policy remain as before. body:
## Why

The lint config was the TanStack library preset, which has no React, accessibility, promise or security rules. This change keeps each plugin only if it found something in this repo or guards a real risk, such as the trading keys in browser storage.

## What changed

- ESLint 10 with typed lint through the TypeScript project service, plus typescript-eslint strict and stylistic, react-hooks, @eslint-react, jsx-a11y-x, the TanStack Query and Router plugins, better-tailwindcss, the Vitest plugin, regexp and no-unsanitized.
- Repo guards as core rules. Storage goes only through `src/trade/vault.ts`. Key libraries stay in `packages/trade`. `Math.random` is allowed only in the hub worker. Every `eslint-disable` needs a reason.
- `lint` and `verify` fail on any warning.

## Scope

- Fixes what the rules found: deprecated wagmi aliases, a ref write during render in the frame hooks, non-null refs in the trade queries (now `skipToken`), switches that hid union members in `default`, and a quadratic `/0+$/` in `fixed.ts`.
- Leaves out sonarjs, unicorn, react-refresh, eslint-plugin-security and `no-non-null-assertion`. Each was measured here and was mostly noise, or needed core refactors only to fit a number.
- knip, for unused exports and deps, comes in its own PR.

## Blast radius

Most of the diff is config. The runtime changes are in the frame hooks, the trade queries, the wallet button and Tailwind class names, and each one keeps the old behavior. Lint time goes from 5.5 s to 9.4 s. Most of the increase is the Tailwind plugin loading the theme and the typed rules.

- `pnpm verify` passes with 0 errors and 0 warnings, and all 121 tests pass.
- verify-tape on a testnet build: book, trades, depth and candles update, market and venue switches work, the wallet connects, Hyperliquid enable shows the expected deposit rejection, and the dYdX order shows the no-account error.

body:
The old prototype could not reproduce training: its data files were missing, the scaler was not saved, and live prediction substituted individual packet fields for flow statistics. This change replaces the executable path with a reproducible, resource-conscious flow-classification pipeline and an ordered plan for reaching a real deployment.

The new package provides official dataset acquisition with transfer/disk limits and provenance, full-stream bounded sampling, duplicate/conflict checks, a shared feature contract, training-only preprocessing, validation-only model/threshold selection, independent test and external-source evaluation, saved pipelines, strict batch prediction, and resource measurements. It compares SGD, histogram boosting, Extra Trees and optional XGBoost against a dummy. The README, audit, architecture, dataset research, evaluation protocol, operations runbook, 39-story Scrum backlog, work log and model card document both implemented work and remaining release gates.

## Measured results and limitations

- Downloaded and scanned 19,330,771 flows across NF-UNSW-NB15-v2 and NF-ToN-IoT-v2, retaining compressed archives totaling 192.64 MiB locally.
- The selected local histogram model reached 99.31% in-domain accuracy, 97.17% attack precision and 81.28% recall. Its test precision target failed. The initial laptop experiment used a sampled peak 347 MiB RSS, took about 60 seconds, and saved a 103,065-byte bundle.
- The frozen model failed transfer to ToN-IoT: 0.3314% attack recall, 29.94% precision and 1.3503% benign FPR. This evidence is retained prominently; the model must not be deployed.
- The next priority is global data auditing, source/capture-aware evaluation, feature ablations and development across multiple sources with a new untouched holdout. Live exporter parity, a bounded sensor, local shadow validation and operational release gates remain backlog work.

## Validation

- 24 focused local tests pass; lint and formatting checks pass.
- GitHub CI passes on Python 3.11 and 3.13, including synthetic smoke training: https://github.com/LahsenAitOiahmane/NetAttDetector/actions/runs/40967625888
- Real-data GitHub training succeeded at clean commit e0a8352, reproducing both source hashes, all split fingerprints, champion, threshold, final test metrics and external failure exactly: https://github.com/LahsenAitOiahmane/NetAttDetector/actions/runs/40966749037
- Actual saved-model prediction processed a 1,000-flow compatible export. Both analysis figures were visually inspected.

See reports/BASELINE.md and reports/evidence/ for detailed measurements. Large raw inputs and new model artifacts remain local or retained workflow artifacts. Historical modules and artifacts remain for reference. The final real-data workflow is manual-only. UQ commercial-use permission and the repository's source-code license remain owner decisions before product publication.

author: beidlat
body:
Besitzer: „Harmonizer als Audio-Effekt. Arp als MIDI-Effekt. Zusätzlich kann man Schleifen arpen … ausgefuchst, ganz im Myzel-Style … optisch ein Highlight … eine richtige Trickkiste“. Einzelheiten stehen in `dev/klang/sporenwerk.md`.

**Harmonizer** (`dsp/harmonizer.js`, `myzel-harmo`, FX-Typ `harmo`)
- **Stimmen:** drei, in der Tonart (Stufen ab der gehörten Tonhöhe) oder in Halbtönen. Dazu Formant halten, Breite und Schimmer.
- **Verfahren:** Phasen-Vocoder mit STFT 2048 und Hop 512. Beide Seiten laufen in einer komplexen FFT, alle Stimmen werden im Spektrum summiert. Die Verschiebung folgt Laroche–Dolson, die Tonhöhe kommt aus der Autokorrelation.
- **Prüfstand:** +7 Halbtöne auf 220 Hz ergeben −0,5 dB am Ziel, das Original liegt bei −120 dB. In C-Dur werden E zu G und C zu E.
- **Kosten:** `FX_COST.harmo = 7.5`, gemessen 6,5.

**Sporenwerk** (`arp/sporenwerk.js`, `arp/schleifen.js`, `arp/sporenwerk-ui.js`, Parameter `arp.*`)
- **Einbindung:** `onDown` übergibt gehaltene Töne an das Sporenwerk. Es spielt sie im Taktgeber-Raster über alle Ebenen, und was es spielt, landet im Humus.
- **Wuchsformen:** Auf, Ab, Pendel, Wie gespielt, Zufall, Hyphe, Spirale, Sporenflug, Pilzring, Wachsen.
- **Raster:** 1/4 bis 1/32, gerade, triolisch oder punktiert. Dazu Swing, Länge und ein euklidischer Ring.
- **Trickkiste:** Chance, Ratschen, Akzent, Höhe-Welle, Stimmen, Leiter-Wanderung, Mutation, 1–4 Oktaven, Halten, Würfeln.
- **Schleifen arpen:** Die Noten, die gerade in der gewählten Schleife (Fokus oder Platz 1–8) klingen, bilden den Akkord. Die Schleife kann dabei auf Wunsch still sein.
- **Panel:** Tab „Sporenwerk“ mit animiertem Pilzring, Hyphen, Sporen-Bursts, Mutations-Fäden und Notennamen.
- **Touché:** Der F12-Arp lässt dem Sporenwerk den Vorrang.

**Tests** (nur Chromium)
- neu: t-arp 8/8 (eigene Stimmen 0; 1/16-Raster genau 0,125 s bei 120 BPM; Ring 8/3; Ratschen; Terz; Schleifen-Quelle mit Stille und Rückkehr; Harmonizer klingt)
- grün: v2 func, sources, presets, smoke; mixfunc; mixui; fxret; t-hx-mixer 12/12, t-hx-ui 69/69, t-hx-abdruck 10/10

author: asuresh8
body:
`beta / mixed-version` failed on two main pipelines (runs 40911011596 and 40912351444) at `cargo xtask release fetch-previous`, before any test ran:
`xtask: gh api repos/komira-ai/kbf/releases/tags/v0.0.32: not found (HTTP 404)`

The tag v0.0.32 was pushed at 16:22:51Z, and its release was a draft until 16:35:24Z. GitHub answers `releases/tags/<tag>` for a draft with 404, and both failures fall inside that 12-minute window. Every push to main during a release cut fails the same way.

`release fetch-previous` now asks for the previous tag's release up to `--release-attempts` times, `--release-poll-secs` apart (by default 40 times, 30 s apart, about 20 minutes), before the missing release is the error it always was. Each wait prints a line saying so.
- The rule the verb keeps is unchanged: a tag whose release never appears is an error, not a step back to a lower tag (`a_tag_with_no_release_is_an_error_not_a_step_back_to_a_lower_tag` still passes).
- N-1 stays the release before N, so a run in the window waits for v0.0.32 instead of testing against v0.0.31.
- The fake gh gains a `draft-release:<tag>:<times>` fault: the first `<times>` GETs of that release answer 404.

Tests (crates/xtask/tests/release_fetch_previous.rs):
- `a_release_that_is_still_a_draft_is_waited_for_and_then_fetched`: two 404s, then the published release. It must be fetched as N-1 (`previous-tag` is that tag, binaries unpacked, three asks) and not stepped back to the lower tag.
- `a_release_never_published_is_still_an_error_after_the_asks`: with `--release-attempts 3`, the run is refused with the 404 after exactly 3 asks, and nothing is unpacked.
- Every test passes `--release-poll-secs 0`, so no test sleeps.

Locally `cargo test -p xtask --test release_fetch_previous` gives 33 passed, and `cargo clippy -p xtask --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean. Red-first: the test commit alone (the flags exist but do nothing) runs in kbf#1959, where the draft test must fail with the first 404.

body:
Tests that wait on a real process used a fixed 60 s window, or a 2 to 5 s budget for a single step. On a host loaded by other work every exec can cost ten times as much, so those tests failed under load and passed alone.

`tests/process_wait.py` times five bare interpreter starts once per test process. It divides the median by an idle baseline (0.025 s) and clamps the result to 1x to 4x. `AI_CLI_TEST_PROCESS_WAIT_SECONDS` still sets the observe window explicitly and wins.

- The ten test files that read `AI_CLI_TEST_PROCESS_WAIT_SECONDS` now call `process_wait_seconds()`.
- `test_session_begin_recovery.py`'s step budgets use `scaled()`.
- `tests/test_process_wait.py` covers the override, the idle floor, linear scaling and the cap. Removing the cap or the override makes the matching test fail.

The probe starts `sys.executable`, so it behaves the same on Linux, macOS and Windows.

Verified locally on a heavily loaded macOS host (load about 26 on 10 cores): the changed files ran 223 passed, 1 skipped.

author: tanimax
body:
## Pourquoi

Première étape de l'informatisation des annonces du dimanche, aujourd'hui préparées à la main sur PowerPoint. La plupart des annonces reviennent chaque semaine. Le secrétariat les saisit maintenant **une seule fois**, et les événements datés disparaissent d'eux-mêmes une fois passés.

## Ce qui change

**Page Communication › Annonces** (`/admin/annonces`, politique `ManageCommunication` : Admin et Secrétaire)
- Quatre types d'annonces, dans l'ordre où on les lit :
  - **Activité de la semaine** : un « quand » libre, par exemple « Mercredi soir de 19h00 à 21h15 ».
  - **Événement** : une date (et une date de fin si l'événement dure plusieurs jours) et une heure, par exemple « à 18h00 ». L'annonce n'apparaît plus une fois sa dernière date passée.
  - **Annonce pastorale** : permanente.
  - **Annonce externe** : l'invitation d'une autre église.
- Pour chaque annonce : un titre (« ce qui a lieu », en rouge comme sur les diapositives), des lignes de détail avec une étiquette (Sujet, Tél., Prédicateur, Horaire, N.B.) et un titre de section facultatif (par exemple « 2e jeûne annuel »).
- Une annonce est **archivée** plutôt que supprimée, et on peut la restaurer.
- Une annonce passée reste dans la liste avec un badge « Passée ».
- **Le thème du mois** (« Octobre : Mois d'actions de grâces ») s'enregistre pour le mois du dimanche à venir.
- La page indique combien d'annonces seront lues dimanche.
- Le bouton « Enregistrer » ignore les clics répétés, et les droits sont revérifiés dans chaque action.

**Code**
- Domaine : `Announcement`, `AnnouncementDetail` et `MonthlyTheme`. La règle `IsShownOn(dimanche)` dit si une annonce fait partie des annonces de ce dimanche.
- `AnnouncementTexts` écrit en français la première ligne en gras de la diapositive, par exemple « Samedi 31 octobre 2026, à 18h00 : » ou « Du vendredi 6 au dimanche 8 novembre 2026 : ». Il choisit aussi le titre de section : celui de l'annonce, « Annonce externe » ou le thème du mois.
- `AnnouncementService` : le catalogue, l'archivage, le thème du mois et `GetShownOnAsync(dimanche)`, qui servira aux prochaines étapes (les annonces du dimanche, puis l'export PowerPoint).
- `ChurchClock.UpcomingSunday`.
- Menu : la page Annonces s'ajoute au groupe Communication, avec son fil d'Ariane.

**Migration** `AddAnnouncements`, générée par `dotnet ef migrations add` : deux nouvelles tables, et les lignes de détail dans une colonne `jsonb`. Aucune table existante n'est modifiée.

## Tests

- `AnnouncementTextsTests` : les premières lignes en gras (un jour, plusieurs jours, sur deux mois ou deux années, « 1er »), le choix du titre de section, et la règle d'affichage jusqu'à la date.
- `AnnouncementServiceTests` :
  - l'enregistrement nettoie les espaces et ignore les lignes vides ;
  - la modification et le changement de type ;
  - chaque refus de validation ;
  - l'archivage et la restauration ;
  - la sélection des annonces d'un dimanche et leur ordre de lecture ;
  - le thème du mois : remplacé, puis supprimé quand on le vide.
- `AnnoncesPageTests` : la Secrétaire et l'Admin voient la page, et ce qu'elle affiche (premières lignes, thème, dimanche). L'École Dominicale est renvoyée vers la connexion.
- `ChurchClockTests` : le dimanche à venir, un samedi et un dimanche.
- `NavigationTests` : Annonces dans le groupe Communication et dans le fil d'Ariane.
- Dans le navigateur, `AnnoncesJourneyTests` : une annonce créée avec une rafale de 5 clics n'apparaît qu'une fois, puis on l'archive. Ce test échoue si on retire la protection contre les clics répétés (vérifié).
- En local, tout passe : 314 tests de l'app, 23 d'architecture et 32 dans le navigateur.

## Prochaines étapes

1. Les annonces du dimanche : préremplies avec les annonces en cours et les anniversaires du rapport Anniversaires, à cocher et à mettre dans l'ordre.
2. L'export PowerPoint à partir du modèle de l'église : 4:3, Calibri 36 pt, page de titre avec le bandeau.

author: rahul-sinha1908
body:
**Phase 2** of the content studio rebuild. Plan: https://claude.ai/artifact/9SaDvpvN1RzaCyS1Vm5De4

While the AI worked, the media section showed a bare spinner and "follow along in the chat" — so the one place the user had just acted went blank, and the only feedback moved to a panel they may not have been looking at.

## What it shows now

**The real step.** The backend already pushes a `status` frame naming each tool as it runs ("Designing your visual…", "Generating an image…", "Reviewing the design…"), and `AIChatPanel` already rendered it. This lifts it out through a new `onStatusChange` so the canvas can report the same work.

**The brief, echoed back** beside it — in the place it was typed, so you can see what you asked for without re-reading the chat to remember.

## Deliberately not a scripted progress list

The design reference drives its step list from a fixed per-approach script. I didn't build that. A sequence of reassuring steps that isn't tied to real work is a lie that gets found out the first time something is slow — and worse, it can't tell you *which* step is the slow one. These labels are the actual tool calls, so when image generation takes 40 seconds the screen says "Generating an image…" and that is true.

It falls back to generic copy between steps rather than blanking, since the status frame is empty in the gaps.

## Checks

`npx tsc --noEmit` clean. 7/7 suites, 85 tests. Not yet verified on dev — that's next.

PR_AUTHOR_SESSION_DECLARED: P4 Maintenance Lane a65c67bf

**Site main health** (StegVerse-org/.github#166, #167). Round 60 reported two non-green items on every Site main push run; root causes:

## 1. `verify-live-music` (StegMusic Live Verification) — real in-repo failure, repaired
The job fetches the public Pages files and compares each with required markers. The deployed files are byte-identical to the committed source (checked), so the failure is marker drift in `scripts/check_stegmusic_live_routes.py`, not a propagation or external problem. It has not passed on any of the last 100 runs. Three markers could never match:
- `assets/ecosystem-music-diagnostics.js`: `audible_output_confirmed: false` (with a space). The source is minified as `audible_output_confirmed:false`.
- `assets/ecosystem-music-media-transport.js`: `screen_lock_continuity_confirmed` never existed in that file (added with the check in 34f99179e). The source states the boundary as the human-confirmation text `Human confirmed playback continued while the screen was locked.`, which is now the marker; the claim `screen_lock_continuity_verified` stays false in the report.
- `ecosystem-chat.html`: `Ecosystem Node` was removed from the page on 2026-08-21 (9f50ba19d). The page's current Node surface marker `stegverse-node-continuity` replaces it; the `ecosystem-music.html` link marker is unchanged.
Nothing is suppressed: every other marker and the PASS/FAIL logic are unchanged, and the check still reads the public Pages URLs exactly as before (no fetch is added).

To keep it from recurring, `scripts/check_stegmusic_live_verification_contract.py` (run by `check_ecosystem_chat_application.py`, so on pull requests) now asserts offline that every marker in ROUTES exists in the committed source of its route. Against the old markers it fails with the three messages above; against the new ones it passes. A dry run of the repaired checker against the public Pages files gives `STEGMUSIC_LIVE_VERIFICATION_PASS`. The workflow runs only on a completed Pages deployment, so its own green run is observed on main after merge; it was not dispatched.

## 2. The skipped `validate` job — not a folded or dispatcher job, recorded
It belongs to `check-stegfin-phone-projection.yml` (a kept surface): `validate` carries `if: github.event_name != 'workflow_run'` and `observe-publication` carries a workflow_run `if`, so one of the two jobs is skipped on every run by design. NOT_SELECTED gating applies to dispatcher and folded groups only, so the job is recorded in its registry entry, with a proposed conforming resolution: carry the pull_request and push validation steps as a catalog group with the same path_filters and keep the file as the workflow_run-only observer. The workflow file is byte-unchanged.

No workflow is added or folded; Site stays at 97. author: roc-ops
body:
## What this changes

Four Edgecore supplies stated their input as a sentence. Each now states `attrs.input` as `ac` or `dc`, as the
library's other supplies do (for example `arista/7280r3-pwr-500-dc@1`), and keeps the sentence unchanged in
`attrs.input-note`:

| supply | before | after | `input` | `input-note` (unchanged) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `edgecore/csr310-psu-ac@1` | 1.0.1 | 1.0.2 | `ac` | `100 V - 240 V, 5 A` |
| `edgecore/csr310-psu-dc@1` | 1.0.1 | 1.0.2 | `dc` | `36 V - 72 V, 10 A` |
| `edgecore/agr-psu-ac@1` | 1.0.0 | 1.0.1 | `ac` | `100-120 V 12 A or 200-240 V 7.5 A, 50-60 Hz per PSU` |
| `edgecore/agr-psu-dc@1` | 1.0.1 | 1.0.2 | `dc` | `-40 to -75 VDC, 40 A max per PSU` |

Why: a consumer that reads a build's supply type reads `input` of the supplies fitted in a configuration's bays, and
accepts only `ac`, `dc` and `hvdc`. It read each sentence as "not stated", so neither build of the four devices was
recognised as AC or DC. Both supplies of each pair had to change for the pair to read.

Four devices take a patch bump, as the lock asked: the CSR310 (1.0.6 to 1.0.7), the CSR430 (1.0.7 to 1.0.8), the
AS7946-30XB (4.0.5 to 4.0.6) and the AS7946-74XKSB (4.0.5 to 4.0.6). No drawing, size, element, id, port or skin
changes.

Exports that changed: the comments of the four module types (`CRXT-T0T12BS`, `SPAACTN-03BG`, `AGR PSU (AC)` and
`AGR PSU (DC)`, in NetBox and Nautobot) and the "Drawing version" line of the four devices' device types (the AS7946
pair's four ordering codes under Arrcus, Edgecore and IP Infusion; the CSR310's `7315-27X-*` codes and the CSR430's
`AS7515-24X` under Edgecore and IP Infusion). 44 files in all, no other export.

This is a two-way change; its reach is four devices and four module types.

## Sources

- Edgecore CSR310 / AS7315-27X Cell Site Router Data Sheet, page 3: "DC Input: 36V -72V, 10 A" and "AC Input: 100V-240V, 5 A".
- Edgecore AS7315-27X Cell Site Gateway Quick Start Guide E112022-CS-R05, page 3, hardware specification: "DC Input 36 V - 72 V,
  10 A" and "AC Input 100-240 VAC, 50/60 Hz, 5 A maximum".
- Edgecore AGR400 (AS7946-30XB) data sheet R05 and AGR420 (AS7946-74XKSB) data sheet R03, page 3: "DC Input: -40 - -75V, 40 A,
  per PS" and "AC Input: 100V-120V, 12 A, per PS / 200V-240V, 7.5 A, per PS".
- Edgecore AS7946-30XB and AS7946-74XKSB quick start guides, page 4, hardware specification: "DC Input -40 - -75 VDC, 40 A max"
  and the AC input lines.

They print the sentences the supplies already carried.

## Left as it was

- Every figure.
- The CSR430 shares this supply part with the CSR310, but its own data sheet (page 3) prints a different pair: "DC Input:
  -44 - -60V, 15.5-9.6 A, per PS" and "AC Input: 100V-240V, 6.0-2.4 A, per PS". Its quick start says "36 VDC to 72 VDC PSU"
  (page 3) and "System Input Rating ... 36 - 72 VDC, 8.4-4.2 A" (page 4). This change does not reconcile them.
- `edgecore/csr440-psu-ac` and other supplies still state their input as text and are not changed here.
- `edgecore/agr110` and `edgecore/agr130` seat other supplies that already state `ac` and `dc`; their files and locks are
  untouched.

## How it was checked

- New `spec/tests/test_edgecore_supply_input.py`, run first against the unchanged contracts: 12 failed (the four tokens, the
  four kept sentences, and the four devices' configurations) and the 4 "nothing else about the supply moved" checks passed.
  After the change all 16 pass.
- `devicelock.py`: before the version bumps it named exactly the four devices and "at least a patch bump"; after them, 0
  findings. `--update` wrote exactly the four devices' lock files. `expand.py --check`: 2/2 in step with their layout.
- Lint: no error and no warning beyond the baseline; `lint-baseline.json` unchanged.
- Related suites (changelog fragments, psu inlet, module collisions, components catalogue, lock contents, lint baseline,
  module power, vocabulary, dc inventory, preflight): 194 passed, 5 skipped.
- Full build: 503 devices built and 503 listed in `devices.json`; 2276 components, none added or removed. The built
  contracts read `ac`, `dc`, `ac`, `dc` as in the table.
- Exports regenerated with the exporter and compared with a fresh export folder: no difference. Preflight passes.
- Renders of every view of the four devices, in each configuration (`ac` and `dc`; `dc-psu` and `ac-psu`), on this branch
  and on `main`: 72 SVGs and 80 other files. Their bytes differ only where they record the device version, the supply
  versions, the source hash and the supply's `input` attributes; with those removed, all 152 files are identical.

author: lavan96
body:
## Why

These are findings R3, S1, S2 and A1 of the 29 Oct key audit, which was read live from Mission Control's ledger:

- **R3 (High).** Two writers recorded Aurixa's money as `set`. `set` is the status a tenant's own key has, so its usage rates `byok` and is charged at nothing.
  - The email identity's Resend key is minted on Aurixa's Resend account. It reads `set` on all four clones that have one.
  - The Integrations broker recorded every write `set`. That covers an unchanged re-save and a paste of the platform's own value.
- **S1 (High).** `GITHUB_WEBHOOK_SECRET` is Mission Control's own GitHub webhook signing secret: `/hooks/github` trusts anything signed with it. It was a fleet row marked `inherit`, and is `inherited` on all five clones. No clone reads it.
- **S2 (High, part).** `VAPI_API_KEY` is Aurixa's organisation-wide Vapi key. It reaches every tenant's assistants and the prime's, and it is `inherited` on all five clones too. Mission Control's own design (`CLONE_VOICE_AUTOMATION.md` item 3, `cloneVapiCustody.pure.ts`) holds each clone's Vapi organisation itself and puts no Vapi key on a clone. No clone has ever logged a Vapi call: `vapi_call_logs` is empty on all five.
- **A1 (Low, part).** The TS rating mirror no longer matched the SQL. It rated `minted` and `federated` as `no_key`, where `record_api_usage_event` bills both. It also kept a failed call on a tenant's own key as `byok`, where the SQL calls it `error_call`.

## What changes

- **One authority for what an identity-written name is recorded as.** `settledLedgerStatus` returns `minted` for the Resend key and `set` for everything else. The mint, the hourly email audit (`identityLedgerFromListing`) and the provisioning planner's settled path all ask it. The hourly audit corrects a `set` row it finds, so no data migration is needed. Billing or absorbing email stays a rate-row decision.
- **The Integrations broker decides per name** (`integrationLedgerStatus`):
  - An unchanged save keeps a platform-paid record (`inherited`, `minted` or `federated`).
  - An unreadable record is left alone.
  - Mission Control's own value is `inherited`. It is compared as SHA-256 digests in constant time (`platformSecretValue.server.ts`).
  - Only a key the tenant brought is `set`.
- **`CONTROL_PLANE_SECRETS`** adds the GitHub webhook secret and the org-wide Vapi key to the `prime_only` class. Each has its own reason, given through `refusalFor`, so the Vapi refusal no longer talks about Supabase projects. As a result they are:
  - refused on both forward paths and by the Integrations broker;
  - recorded `withheld` by the provisioning planner;
  - removed from every clone by the half-hourly prohibited-secrets sweep. The sweep reads what each project actually holds and confirms the removal with a second read.
- **Provisioning asks the class.** Its fleet values came from every row marked `inherit` with no class check, so a `prime_only` name relied on its data row alone at provisioning. The planner now withholds every `prime_only` name.
- **`20261029230000`** sets the two fleet rows to `inherit = false`, so the forwarding page says the same thing as the code.
- **`resolveBillingReason`** now follows `record_api_usage_event` step for step. The new tests pin the drift cases.
- Docs updated: `prime-repo-api-usage-metering.md` (full status table), `CLONE_MANAGEMENT_TOKEN.md`, `THE_CLONING_ENGINE.md`.

| change | rows it will move |

author: christian-rogobete
body:
Before this change, the `Signer` trait and the keyring sign handle signed any 32 bytes a caller passed them. The network crate's public signing entry points carried no network check. A library caller holding a mainnet transaction hash could have the wallet's trusted signers sign it, although the documentation stated that signing refused mainnet. The transaction, Soroban, smart-account, and message domains shared one byte array type, so a caller could pass a message digest where the signer expected a transaction hash.

This change:

- Makes every ed25519 method of `Signer` take a typed payload: `TxSigningPayload` for transaction hashes, `SorobanAuthPayload` for Soroban address authorizations, `SmartAccountAuthDigest` for smart-account entries, and `MessagePayload` for SEP-53 messages. `Signer::sign_message` becomes required, and the inherent methods of `KeyringSignHandle` take the same types. Implementations sign the payload bytes, and callers build the payloads from an envelope, a tagged transaction, a preimage, or a message. This breaks the `stellar-agent-network` API for every `Signer` implementation and caller; the CHANGELOG lists the migration per method. The SEP-43 and SEP-53 signing functions keep their signatures.
- Refuses mainnet in the public constructors of the transaction, Soroban, and smart-account payloads. A mainnet transaction or Soroban payload exists only through the intent authorization. The Soroban one consumes the authorization, carries no public bytes, rechecks the authorization's freshness against the trusted clock right before signing and signs once.
- Binds an authorized mainnet payload to the signer key the authorization names. The payload types are neither Clone nor Copy, and the keyring, software, and hardware signers refuse a payload bound to another key. A caller-supplied signer callback cannot forward a mainnet payload to a key the authorization did not name.
- Keeps the raw signing primitives of the software and hardware signers private to the crate, with doctests that pin the visibility. The hardware message test asserts the exact Ledger input.

The lead chain ran green on this tree, with fmt, clippy with the feature set off and on, the Windows cross clippy, and rustdoc both ways. It also ran the workspace test pair off and on, the inbox renderer node test, feature discipline, the docs checker, the skill archive check, diff --check, and the release contracts. Twenty-seven mutation probes across the implementation and the two fold rounds failed under their mutation and passed after the restore. Among them: each trusted signer's binding check removed, the Copy derive restored, and the raw primitives made public. Codex reviewed the change, Codex folded the findings, Opus cross-checked the fold and Codex folded the cross-check findings.

author: w3-bounty
body:
## Problem and resulting evidence/behavior

Task/component ID and target release + SHA-256: **RE-005**, bincode-fork varint / integer-encoding boundary, node release **#94**, `artifacts/node/94/hl-node` SHA-256 `3b7179cd967d1b13b683e05debfc685ad4c750e918226402d5d575eff1c0459f` (91,774,280 bytes).

This PR adds a static, offline, reproducible evidence packet for how the fork's bincode varint layer encodes and decodes integers in #94 (one byte below 251, `0xfb` u16, `0xfc` u32, `0xfd` u64, `0xfe` error arm). It is narrowed to the varint layer, has pinned outputs and tamper controls, and cross-checks addresses with readelf and objdump. The binary is never executed.

Bounded claim: in #94, the 7 encode/size functions and the u64 slice decode fast path listed below implement the bincode varint wire rule, and the stated `.text` idiom scans find exactly the listed sites and no others. Nothing beyond that is claimed.

## Evidence and scope

Packet: `research/work-items/RE-005-bincode-varint/` (README, `varint-sites.json`, `decode-sites.json`, two objdump excerpt files, `MANIFEST.sha256`, `verify.py`). Tools: `tools/bincode_varint.py`, `tools/bincode_varint_decode.py` (stdlib only). Tests: `tests/test_bincode_varint.py`, `tests/test_bincode_varint_decode.py`.

**Observations**
- Encode/size side: 7 functions, bounded by #94's own `.eh_frame_hdr` FDEs (121,299 FDEs, cross-checked with `readelf`), each with exact anchor bytes and exact direct-call counts (3, 2, 25, 25, 75, 86, 87). Three panic `lea`s resolve through `R_X86_64_RELATIVE` relocations to `bincode-fork/src/enc/write.rs:78:9`.
- Encode-side scan coverage: a `.text`-wide scan for exactly three idioms finds **9** sites, all inside the 7 functions; the tool rejects any site outside them. Definitions (`IDIOMS` in `tools/bincode_varint.py`):
  - `cmp r32,0xfb` (`81 /7`, no REX.W), `jae`, then `cmp r32,0x10000` within 48 bytes: 3 sites;
  - the same with REX.W on both compares (`cmp r64`): 4 sites;
  - the specific SIB store `42 c6 04 0f fd` (`mov byte [rdi+r9],0xfd`): 2 sites.
- Looser patterns match more and the extras are **not claimed**: across `.text`, a bare `cmp r32,0xfb` (no REX) gives 5, any `cmp r64,0xfb` gives 27, and any `0xfd` byte store gives 3 (independent verifier's count). Named extras, checked with objdump and all outside the 7 pinned functions: `0x4587475` (`cmp ecx,0xfb`), `0x466bc4a` (`cmp edx,0xfb`), `0x3cd50ac` (`mov byte [r13+0x8],0xfd`).
- Decode side: 2 decoders pinned in full (`0x466bd10..0x466bdf5` with jump table `0x6f6ea8`, and the inlined copy `0x2558ee0..0x2559404` with table `0x3e5984`), including targets per tag and Locations `de/decoder.rs:93:13` and `de/impls.rs:499:20`.
- Decode closure: `.text` contains exactly **21** `add r32,-0xfb; cmp r32,3` tag dispatches in **16** functions, each preceded in its function by `cmp reg,0xfb`.
- Every recorded VA (encode and decode) is an instruction start as objdump prints it; for the 8 REX.B (`r8d..r15d`) dispatch sites that is the `0x41` prefix. A test checks every VA against objdump instruction boundaries.

**Inferences (not observations)**
- The function names are our labels; the binary has no symbols for them.
- The `*_vec` byte-swap arm looks like a compiled-in big-endian flag; `0x12` on decode looks like the `Ok` niche; the error-arm codes look like `InvalidIntegerType`-style expected/found codes. None checked against source.

**Dependencies and related work**
- RE-001 (#2, #5, function-boundary / unwind inventory): these addresses do **not** depend on RE-001 output; bounds come from #94's own FDEs. If RE-001 lands, its boundaries should contain these ranges exactly; that comparison is not in this PR.
- PR #8 (bridge encoder at `0x3c9a570` / `0x58f650`) is a different layer. Tests assert no pinned FDE or dispatch site lies in those functions, and this PR makes no bridge-encoding claim.

**What this does not claim**
- No gate change and no completeness claim for RE-005 as a whole.
- The decode slow reader path and decode widths other than the u64 slice fast path.
- Any serde/type-level mapping of which messages use which function.
- Any bridge (#8) behaviour, runtime behaviour, or other node releases (#115 is rejected by the tool).
- Source-level equivalence; names and enum meanings above are inferences.

## Validation

`make` is not installed on the box used, so each recipe's commands were run directly:

```sh
python3 -I -B tools/bincode_varint.py | sha256sum
# 7e7a06b035c5b223cfa4573b9f315e344db2207c88c967e8079b88a0093a7657  (varint-sites.json)
python3 -I -B tools/bincode_varint_decode.py | sha256sum
# 6da03736b718d6c7db769a0a1be7e9131a6229cea6b198dd85d535282be5a56f  (decode-sites.json)
python3 -I -B research/work-items/RE-005-bincode-varint/verify.py   # rc=0, both files OK
python3 -O -B research/work-items/RE-005-bincode-varint/verify.py   # rc=0, both files OK
python3 -I -B -m unittest discover -s tests                         # Ran 55 tests, OK
python3 -O -B -m unittest discover -s tests                         # Ran 55 tests, OK
```

Unchanged packet files: `objdump-excerpts.txt` `d4ac4801d3dedb823964a2ffcbb50b1034ea4a33411b19a1817f4da2271329de`, `decode-objdump-excerpts.txt` `6271d7c6badeb6f4e6bd0aabefafa0b756bf15b0c8f2ae352363a586a7a91701`. `MANIFEST.sha256` matches all four files.

Negative controls (all rejected): corrupted digest; truncated binary; node #115; swapped `0xfb`/`0xfc` marker and threshold immediates; FDE end off by 4; call count off by 1; idiom site outside pinned functions; swapped decode tag threshold, jump-table entries and load width; an extra dispatch site; an off-by-one VA (encode `0x27ab30b`, decode `0x2558fe2` and `0x466bd5b`) fails the objdump-boundary check. Identity baselines pass. Output is byte-identical under `PYTHONHASHSEED` 0, 1, 7 and 4242.

Repo-wide checks, run after the `pull` recipe steps (run directly: `git submodule update --init --recursive`, `git lfs pull`, `git -C references/can1357-hl lfs pull`). Submodules checked out at the pinned commits (`references/can1357-hl` 999556f6, `upstream/node` 405cc08b, `upstream/contracts` d7e66aa7, `upstream/block-importer` 703f10ed, `upstream/hyper-evm-sync` d0945c69, `upstream/order_book_server` 8b4f2379, `upstream/historical_data` 984357d3). Same results on this branch and on `origin/main` (6fb8631):

```sh
python3 tools/artifacts.py verify     # rc=0
# SHA-256 OK: artifacts/node/94/hl-node (and the other 7 pinned files)
# Valid signature: node/94/hl-node, node/115/hl-node, visor/captured/hl-visor
# Pinned upstream binary, signature and public key match.
python3 tools/verify_imports.py       # rc=0
# Verified 37 imported files and all pinned source repositories.
python3 tools/catalogue.py --check    # rc=0
# Catalogue and progress tables match pinned inputs.
python3 tools/reproduce.py            # rc=0
# Inventories, raw counts and refined item classifications reproduce the imported evidence.
# Refined counts: {'grounded': 822, 'drift': 60, 'notes': 116, 'late': 1, 'unanchored': 386, 'case': 11, 'partial': 56}
```

The catalogue is current with the RE-005 packet included, so no regeneration commit is needed.

## Progress / limitations

No gate change. Remaining gaps: decode slow path and other widths, type-level mapping, and the RE-001 boundary comparison. Provenance: all evidence derives from the public #94 artifact and binutils output; no third-party source is included.

author: ssidey
body:
## Summary

Spec 39 step 8b5-xxxvii (`specs/39-simulation-in-rust.md`, Step 8 split bullet): the routes and the perception held by the crate. Stacked on #667 (8b5-xxxvi).

**The routes.** GDScript no longer copies routes by hand.
- `SkirmishSquad.route` is now a view of the crate's route and code. It reads through the new `SquadRoutes` class, kept on the store.
- A squad reads the route kept for its code.
- When the crate makes a route itself (a re-routed group, or a pursuit's post route handed over unnamed), `SquadRoutes` builds it once from the crate's points and its corridor (`squad_route_half_width`). It names it by its object (`name_route`) so the code stays the same.
- The crate now keeps the post route's code as a pursuit begins (`Squads::post_route_code`). The squad takes that code up again back at its post. A post route set by `put_squad_pursuit` gets a fresh code there.
- `squad_put_route` with object 0 issues a route its own code.
- Removed: FormationOpening's `_pursued`, FormationOrders.apply's `enemy.route = quarry.route`, FormationPathing's `_follow`/`rerouted`, and FormationPursuit.mirror (with its two callers).
- A squad moved to another store now takes its route along (`SquadRoutes.carry`).

**The perception.** The crate keeps each squad's threat (`Squads::threatened`, set by `perception::keep` in the opening and in `perception_see`). `taking_step` reads it instead of being handed a list. GDScript sees it as `SkirmishSquad.threatened`. FormationTaking.step takes no perception, and FormationPerception.threatened is removed (its tests now read `squad.threatened`).

**Outcomes.** These should not change, with one possible exception. A pursuer back at its post now holds the code of the very route it held its post on. The old mirror gave it a route with the same points: its current one, its command's, or a new copy. Codes are only compared for equality, so this can matter only where two route objects share the same points. The digests in CI's `sim-checks` will show whether that happens. I did not add `outcomes-changed`.

## Tests

- gdUnit, red then green:
  - `test_skirmish_squad.gd`: `test_a_squad_reads_the_route_the_crate_holds_it_on`;
  - `test_formation_taking.gd`: `test_a_group_the_crate_saw_threatened_sends_none`. The existing crate-pass test now sets `line.threatened`.
- Cargo (810 pass locally, clippy clean):
  - `perception/tests.rs`: `keep`;
  - `opening/tests.rs`: each squad's threat kept, and the one-by-one comparison keeps it too;
  - `orders/tests.rs`: the post route's code kept;
  - `scrum/pursue/tests.rs`: the code taken up at the post, an unnamed post route issued one, and the squad placed on its own route with no about-face.
- Left to CI: `test_formation_perception.gd`, `test_scrum_pursue.gd` and the rest of the suite.

## Rubric checklist

- Static checks: function length, generic naming, ISP, dependency direction, helper promotion and id order pass. gdlint and gdformat are clean.
- `check_ocp_shotgun_surgery.py`: this is a stacked PR. Against its base (`origin/feature/routes-and-perception-in-the-crate`), it counts 16 pre-existing files modified (threshold 11). That is one cross-cutting change: the route becomes a view, its mirrors are deleted, and the threat column is added with its readers.
- `check_context_locality.py` (informational): 13 source files.
- design-check:
  - **Rules over cases:** general. A squad back at its post holds the route it held its post on; a squad reads the route the crate holds it on.
  - **Order:** codes are issued in order but only compared for equality, never ranked. `check_id_order` passes. The both-ways-round trials were not run in this session (no long runs); CI and `bench` can run them.
  - **Bounded:** no new loops. Each read of `squad.route` now makes one or two calls into the crate.
- Every Given/When/Then above has a test.

## Documentation

- Impact assessment: an internal refactor. Nothing a player or designer would notice, no data-format change, no new Decision.
- README: verified, no change.
- Changelog: N/A (an internal move of state into the crate; nothing a player or designer sees)
- Docs: N/A. No page in `docs/` names the removed functions. The step is recorded in the spec's Step 8 bullet.

### Cause
Connexion forwards route path parameters by name to view handlers without unpacking kwargs. The route `GET /api/pipeline-study-results/{pipeline_study_result_id}` is declared in the OpenAPI spec with a parameter named `pipeline_study_result_id`, but `PipelineStudyResultsView` inherited `ObjectView.get(self, id)` which only accepts `id`, resulting in a 500 TypeError.
